mapping.name: Aegis
mapping.description: On the continent of Meridia, a sickness that begins in a cabin at the edge of a forest village, and the cities that silence it.
pages:
# Welcome to Aegis

@[Meridia](entity:location/Meridia) is a continent of white stone cities, busy harbors and open roads. In the capital the guilds rule; in the harbors ships dock every season; in the forest villages timber is cut, bread is baked, watches are kept.

In the villages of the southern forest there is talk of a sickness. No one quite knows its name. Some call it the **Blight**.

## The feel of the world

The institutions you will face are cold, the past is dark. But life today goes on: cauldrons boil, linens are washed and hung out, the innkeeper writes up debts, an apprentice knows everything because no one ever asks her anything. Not everyone you meet has a secret. There are ordinary people too, generous ones who do their work well.

The world is a livable place. But things are going badly.

## The godless continent

Three hundred years ago King Lucian cut the bond between the gods and the people. Since that day Meridia has had squares instead of temples, work instead of prayer. Praying in the face of disaster is counted as helplessness; finding a solution is a virtue. See @[The Way of Will](entity:lore/The Way of Will).

The gods, though, did not leave entirely: @[they still whisper](entity:lore/The Gods and the Whisper).

## The guilds

In the capital, @[Lucid Triton](entity:location/Lucid Triton), six guilds sit in the Assembly and run the continent's affairs. See @[The Council and the Guild Assembly](entity:lore/The Council and the Guild Assembly).

# Rules of play

**Aegis is played with the D&D 5e rules.** The rules this world adds to 5e are written on two cards: @[Blight — Infection](entity:curse/Blight — Infection) and @[Rule Deviations](entity:lore/Rule Deviations). Everything else works as in the book.

## Sickness

Getting sick is not random. You roll when you touch a sick person, when you carry a corpse, or when you spend the night in a closed room with someone sick. Once the sickness score goes up, it does not come down.

## Lasting Wounds

Dropping to 0 hit points or losing half your hit points in a single attack calls for a wound roll. Wounds can be permanent. The DM reminds everyone of this rule before the first fight.

## Divine magic — read this first

In this world the gods are far away and a call being answered is **the exception.** Every attempt at divine magic rolls `d20 + Religion`: **19** in combat; outside combat, within the same hour, in order **18 → 20 → natural 20 only → impossible.** An attempt that fails spends the spell slot (and in combat, the action too). Numbers and scope: @[Rule Deviations](entity:lore/Rule Deviations).

> **What this means is plain:** **Cleric and Warlock are not playable classes on this continent.** Paladin is playable, but with a single oath: @[Oath of Will](entity:subclass/Oath of Will). Druid, Ranger and all arcane casters are not affected by this rule.

## Magic

- **In a city**, casting magic requires a guild license (@[Wizards' Guild](entity:lore/Wizards' Guild)). In a village, on the road and in a harbor, no one asks.
- **In the army**, casters are few and protected.
- **In a village**, magic is an oddity; even when it helps, it is foreign.
- **1st- and 2nd-level spells** get no extra rules. The extra rules begin at 3rd level.

## Story and characters

The story is not tied to any particular character. If a character misses a clue, the same information can be found somewhere else, from someone else's mouth.

# Character creation

Create your character however you like. There is a single condition:

> **Rumors of the sickness have, one way or another, set your character on the road to @[Silverwater](entity:location/Silverwater).**

## Classes

All of the SRD's classes are open, with two exceptions:

- **Cleric and Warlock are not played.** On this continent it is not possible to get something from a god or a patron whenever you want it (@[Rule Deviations](entity:lore/Rule Deviations)), and a character cannot be built on that roll.
- **Paladin is played with a single oath:** @[Oath of Will](entity:subclass/Oath of Will). Its power comes from the oath, not from a god; it opens at 3rd level, and nothing it grants requires a roll.

These two points are not a punishment; they are the world itself. No one at the table makes plans by trusting in a god.

This world's cards have four subclasses ready: @[Oath of Will](entity:subclass/Oath of Will) (Paladin) · @[School of the Bulwark](entity:subclass/School of the Bulwark) (Wizard) · @[Clockwork Soul](entity:subclass/Clockwork Soul) (Sorcerer) · @[Drakewarden](entity:subclass/Drakewarden) (Ranger; companion @[Drake](entity:animal/Drake)).

The characters do not need to know one another or arrive on the same day. The first meeting happens in Silverwater. You decide why your character is on the road; the DM ties that reason to the world.

## This world's backgrounds

In Meridia everyone who turns eighteen joins a guild, the army or the bureaucracy. This world's nine backgrounds come from these institutions:

@[Archivist](entity:background/Archivist) · @[Guild Member](entity:background/Guild Member) · @[Guild Scion of Rank](entity:background/Guild Scion of Rank) · @[Magic Guild Student](entity:background/Magic Guild Student) · @[Guild Agent](entity:background/Guild Agent) · @[Dockworker](entity:background/Dockworker) · @[Ship Captain](entity:background/Ship Captain) · @[Paladin Soldier](entity:background/Paladin Soldier) · @[Paladin Officer](entity:background/Paladin Officer)

Every background uses the standard 5e mechanics. It adds two things:

- **An item.** A seal, a tag, a hook or a ledger. The item opens certain doors for you in certain places; the background card says which.
- **A price.** Being recognized, being watched, being in debt, going when you are called. This is not a roll; it is how people look at you.

# Running the adventure

## The situation

The characters arrive in @[Silverwater](entity:location/Silverwater) (@[Arrival at the Village](entity:scene/Arrival at the Village)). The village is working, the sickness is talked about openly, and in @[The Cabin](entity:location/The Cabin) outside the village three sick strangers lie in bed. All three are about to pass into the last stage; no one knows this. You choose when they turn (@[The Dawn Turning](entity:scene/The Dawn Turning)).

This adventure is not a sequence of events. The cards give a situation, places and people; the table builds what happens. Scene cards say *"if this happens, it plays like this"*, not *"this happens"*.

## Where it opens up

- **The authorities.** The characters can take what they have seen to the Assembly in the capital or to the paladin castle at @[Votumar](entity:location/Votumar). The attitude of the people there is written on their own cards (@[Chasing the Rumor](entity:quest/Chasing the Rumor)).
- **Orvan's job.** The ships that go missing, the hard proof of the sickness, and who brought the three strangers across (@[Where They Came From](entity:quest/Where They Came From)).
- **The north.** The tribe that reads the sickness from nature (@[What the Stones Know](entity:quest/What the Stones Know)).
- **The passage paper.** The signature Orvan pays for in advance, and the paper's road from the desk to the signatory (@[Good Writ](entity:quest/Good Writ)).
- **Leaving the continent.** Two ways to board a ship, and the land that appears on the horizon (@[The Continent on the Horizon](entity:quest/The Continent on the Horizon)). The act ends there.

## Where the cards are

Every card likely to come up in a chain — places, NPCs, scenes, items, rules — is gathered chain by chain in the @[Index](entity:lore/Index).

## Which rumors, where

| Place | What is heard about the sickness |
|---|---|
| @[The Wharf](entity:location/The Wharf) | A lot; most of it true and free |
| @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr) | There are traces of it in the customs ledgers; whoever knows how to read them sees it |
| @[Cinervik](entity:location/Cinervik) | A lot; half of it made up |
| @[Argenfon](entity:location/Argenfon) | Spoken of with worry; every conversation ends with *"The Lord Commander will handle it"* |
| @[Lucid Triton](entity:location/Lucid Triton) | Little; the Assembly is silencing the subject |
| @[Votumar](entity:location/Votumar) | In whispers; no one says it out loud |
| @[Radenhall Courtyard](entity:location/Radenhall Courtyard) | No rumors; everyone there already knows |

Give the characters rumors from two different places. Let them see the contradiction for themselves.

## Where the secrets are

Everything the players should not know is in the cards' DM fields: **secrets** on location and NPC cards, **secrets** on quests, **tactics** on encounters.

Three questions are asked in this adventure but not answered: what the sickness is, on whose behalf the captain of the *Fate* carries, and who @[Lord Commander — Varhan](entity:npc/Lord Commander — Varhan) is. The answers are written on the relevant cards. Let the characters sense them; do not say them outright.

## Tomas

The Assembly may not listen, doors may close. In return an innkeeper writes up a debt, an old healer gives forty years of knowledge for nothing, a wharf apprentice tells everything. @[Silverwater](entity:location/Silverwater) can be saved.

# Glossary

Words you will hear on the first day of play.

**Meridia** — the continent you are standing on.

**The Beyond** — the continent on the far side of the sea. Its real name is @[Vorstrand](entity:lore/Vorstrand — What Is Known), but no one in Meridia uses that name.

**Lucid Triton** — the continent's capital of white marble.

**Council / Assembly** — people use both. The Council is the government the king founded; the Assembly is the six guilds sitting in that government's seats. See @[The Council and the Guild Assembly](entity:lore/The Council and the Guild Assembly).

**Guild** — an institution that runs one of the continent's trades: commerce, smithing, healing, law, architecture, magic. Six guilds sit in the Assembly.

**House** — a family that holds a guild's seal.

**Sealed · Registered · Unwritten** — a person's place before the guilds: those who write in the ledger, those written in the ledger, those in no ledger at all. See @[The Banner Register](entity:lore/The Banner Register).

**Names** — someone with two names (a name and a house) belongs to a house or a guild. Someone with one name serves. Someone known by a nickname has no seal.

**Countersignature** — the second signature that shows a piece of work was officially done.

**Blight** — the name the villagers give to the sickness they cannot name. See @[Blight — What Is Known](entity:lore/Blight — What Is Known).

The players read this card first. The source of the sickness, the hand that holds the captain of the *Fate*, and the identity of @[Lord Commander — Varhan](entity:npc/Lord Commander — Varhan) are not written here; they are all in the secrets fields of the relevant cards.

The heart of the adventure: the characters did not create these problems, but the problems are theirs now.

# Index

Every card likely to come up in a chain is here, chain by chain: places, NPCs, scenes, encounters, items and rules. Every name is clickable.

The adventure itself, its situation and how to run it: @[Aegis](entity:campaign/Aegis).

## Nine chains

**@[Chasing the Rumor](entity:quest/Chasing the Rumor)** — the rumor of sickness, @[Silverwater](entity:location/Silverwater), and taking what you have seen to an authority. The other two chains open from here. *Page 2.*

**@[Where They Came From](entity:quest/Where They Came From)** — the job of @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar): why ships go missing, and proof of the sickness that cannot be denied in the Assembly. The three strangers' trail goes cold at @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor). *Page 3.*

**@[Good Writ](entity:quest/Good Writ)** — the countersigned passage paper: a name in the cellar, a paper at the desk, a signature in the signatory's room. Orvan's offer pays for this signature in advance. *Page 4.*

**@[The Continent on the Horizon](entity:quest/The Continent on the Horizon)** — boarding a ship and leaving the continent: from @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr) with a good writ, or from @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor) with good money. The act ends when the second continent is sighted on the horizon (@[Land Ho](entity:scene/Land Ho)). *Page 10.*

**@[What the Stones Know](entity:quest/What the Stones Know)** — at the continent's far north, in @[Radenhall Courtyard](entity:location/Radenhall Courtyard), the tribe that reads the sickness from nature. *Page 9.*

**@[Night of the Tide](entity:quest/Night of the Tide)** — on some nights the drying racks of @[Argenfon](entity:location/Argenfon) are emptied. What is being looked for is not a thief but a **nest**, and this chain opens only for a table that stops at the village. *Page 8.*

**@[The Last Written Order](entity:quest/The Last Written Order)** — telling what you saw at @[Votumar](entity:location/Votumar). The one running the castle is @[Deputy Lord Commander — Aren](entity:npc/Deputy Lord Commander — Aren), and she holds an order. The @[Sealed Letter](entity:adventuring-gear/Sealed Letter) that leaves the castle opens doors in the capital. Its cards are in the Votumar list on page 2.

**@[The Missing Count](entity:quest/The Missing Count)** — the castle's storehouse count does not add up. The only job @[Forgemaster — Torvun](entity:npc/Forgemaster — Torvun) can give a stranger; it needs no background, and it is short. Its cards are in the Votumar list on page 2.

**@[The Masked Job](entity:quest/The Masked Job)** — in @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr), the @[Customs Governor](entity:npc/Customs Governor) has a masked job: taking a chest out of the cellar of a room a guild has set up in the harbor, then burning the room. *Page 11.*

Places that do not fit a chain are on page 5, character cards on page 6, rule and institution cards on page 7.

## Where the chains cross

- @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar) is in all three: the seat in the Assembly that does not deny the sickness, the man who can give the job, and the hand that can sign the passage paper.
- @[Questioning at the Cabin](entity:scene/Questioning at the Cabin) is both in the first chain and the first clue of the second — @[The Sealless Ring](entity:trinket/The Sealless Ring) is found there.
- If @[The Offer at the Door](entity:scene/The Offer at the Door) is made, it opens three chains at once: @[Where They Came From](entity:quest/Where They Came From), @[Good Writ](entity:quest/Good Writ) (signature in advance) and @[The Continent on the Horizon](entity:quest/The Continent on the Horizon).
- @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor) is the shared place of Where They Came From and The Continent on the Horizon; in both, the door is @[Admitted to the Harbor](entity:scene/Admitted to the Harbor).
- @[Customs House](entity:location/Customs House) is the shared place of Good Writ and The Continent on the Horizon: the paper is countersigned there too, and the ship is boarded from there (@[The Customs Wharf](entity:scene/The Customs Wharf)).
- @[The Open Sea](entity:location/The Open Sea) is the road both of the ships that do not arrive and of whoever leaves the continent: the question of Where They Came From, the water of The Continent on the Horizon.
- @[The Assembly Session](entity:scene/The Assembly Session) is one of the authorities in the first chain, and in the second chain the place where real names can be recognized.

- The ledger of the @[Customs House](entity:location/Customs House) also touches @[The Masked Job](entity:quest/The Masked Job): the bundle showing that the scale and the ledger do not match is in the cellar of the @[Military Law Chamber](entity:location/Military Law Chamber).
# Chasing the Rumor — cards

## Scenes

- **Silverwater:** @[Arrival at the Village](entity:scene/Arrival at the Village) · @[Questioning at the Cabin](entity:scene/Questioning at the Cabin) · @[The Dawn Turning](entity:scene/The Dawn Turning) → @[Dawn Clash](entity:encounter/Dawn Clash)
- **The authorities:** @[The Assembly Session](entity:scene/The Assembly Session) (capital)
- **Orvan's offer:** @[The Offer at the Door](entity:scene/The Offer at the Door)

## Places

- @[Silverwater](entity:location/Silverwater) · @[The Cabin](entity:location/The Cabin) · @[Goodbarrel's Hearth](entity:location/Goodbarrel's Hearth)
- @[Lucid Triton](entity:location/Lucid Triton) · @[Assembly Hall](entity:location/Assembly Hall) · @[Hall of Seals](entity:location/Hall of Seals)
- @[Votumar](entity:location/Votumar) · @[Watchtower Line](entity:location/Watchtower Line)

## NPCs

**Silverwater:** @[Duran](entity:npc/Duran) (head of the Council of Elders) · @[Umay](entity:npc/Umay) (healer) · @[Corvin](entity:npc/Corvin) (the man who goes down to the shore and brings back goods) · @[Milo Goodbarrel](entity:npc/Milo Goodbarrel) (innkeeper) · @[Halim](entity:npc/Halim) (the fourth stranger, upstairs at the inn)

**The Cabin:** @[Alton Leagallow](entity:npc/Alton Leagallow) · @[Merla Tealeaf](entity:npc/Merla Tealeaf) · @[Kromanna](entity:npc/Kromanna)

**The Assembly's six seats:** @[Rector — Quarion](entity:npc/Rector — Quarion) · @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar) · @[Head Journeyman — Adrik Ferrun](entity:npc/Head Journeyman — Adrik Ferrun) · @[Chief Physician — Caramip Kalender](entity:npc/Chief Physician — Caramip Kalender) · @[Registrar — Valen Custar](entity:npc/Registrar — Valen Custar) · @[Master of the Board — Perhun Mizan](entity:npc/Master of the Board — Perhun Mizan)

**Votumar:** @[Lord Commander — Varhan](entity:npc/Lord Commander — Varhan) (not at the castle for two months) · @[Deputy Lord Commander — Aren](entity:npc/Deputy Lord Commander — Aren) · @[Gate Commander — Nevra](entity:npc/Gate Commander — Nevra) · @[Forgemaster — Torvun](entity:npc/Forgemaster — Torvun) · @[Castle Clerk — Nerion](entity:npc/Castle Clerk — Nerion) · @[The Shore Siblings — Kessa, Bram and Tomas](entity:npc/The Shore Siblings — Kessa, Bram and Tomas) · @[Watch Captain — Drahan](entity:npc/Watch Captain — Drahan) · @[Tower Sentry — Vrask](entity:npc/Tower Sentry — Vrask)

## Items and what is known

@[The Black Fleet — What Is Known](entity:lore/The Black Fleet — What Is Known)

## Encounter

@[Dawn Clash](entity:encounter/Dawn Clash) — @[Turned Alton](entity:monster/Turned Alton) · @[Turned Merla](entity:monster/Turned Merla) · @[Turned Kromanna](entity:monster/Turned Kromanna); the generic form is @[The Turned](entity:monster/The Turned).

**Actions:** @[Claw Attack](entity:creature-action/Claw Attack) · @[Mighty Claw Attack](entity:creature-action/Mighty Claw Attack) · @[Leaping Bite](entity:creature-action/Leaping Bite) (the only action that infects).

**Symptom traits:** @[Knows No Pain](entity:trait/Knows No Pain) · @[Relentless Stride](entity:trait/Relentless Stride) · @[Fitful](entity:trait/Fitful) · @[Early Empowerment](entity:trait/Early Empowerment).

## Items

- @[The Sealless Ring](entity:trinket/The Sealless Ring) — in @[Kromanna](entity:npc/Kromanna)'s hidden pocket; the start of the second chain.
- @[Sherbet of Resistance](entity:adventuring-gear/Sherbet of Resistance) — the only protection in the healers' hands.

## Rule and institution cards

@[Blight — Infection](entity:curse/Blight — Infection) (Sickness Score) · @[Blight — What Is Known](entity:lore/Blight — What Is Known) (what the village knows) · @[The Council and the Guild Assembly](entity:lore/The Council and the Guild Assembly) · @[Order of the Silver Shield](entity:lore/Order of the Silver Shield) · @[Vorstrand — What Is Known](entity:lore/Vorstrand — What Is Known)
# Where They Came From — cards

The job of @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar): why the ships go missing, stopping it if need be, and hard proof of the sickness. The three strangers' trail is short; it goes cold at the harbor.

## Scenes

- @[Questioning at the Cabin](entity:scene/Questioning at the Cabin) — traces, and @[The Sealless Ring](entity:trinket/The Sealless Ring)
- @[Admitted to the Harbor](entity:scene/Admitted to the Harbor) — entry into @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor) with a guarantor
- @[The Assembly Session](entity:scene/The Assembly Session) — the only seat that recognizes the real names; an open road for a table that never went to the harbor
- @[What the Stones Know](entity:quest/What the Stones Know) — the druid's reading at @[Radenhall Courtyard](entity:location/Radenhall Courtyard); a possible piece of the proof

## Places

@[Border and Trade Guild Council Chamber](entity:location/Border and Trade Guild Council Chamber) (which ship did not arrive) · @[The Cabin](entity:location/The Cabin) · @[Silverwater](entity:location/Silverwater) · @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor) · @[The Wharf](entity:location/The Wharf) · @[Lucid Triton](entity:location/Lucid Triton) · @[The Open Sea](entity:location/The Open Sea) (the road of the ships that did not arrive)

## NPCs

**Those who open the way to the harbor:** @[Duran](entity:npc/Duran) (*"they came from the harbor"*) · @[Corvin](entity:npc/Corvin) (knows the way; if he dies, this door closes) · @[Kildrak Ferrun](entity:npc/Kildrak Ferrun) (the assay master who reads unstamped work)

**At the harbor:** @[Twine](entity:npc/Twine) (the harbor's goods ledger) · @[Mouse](entity:npc/Mouse) (the night the ship came) · @[Enamel](entity:npc/Enamel) (the hand that filed the ring) · @[Velvet](entity:npc/Velvet) (the guild's hand at the harbor) · @[Captain Caelynn](entity:npc/Captain Caelynn) · @[Captain Holg](entity:npc/Captain Holg)

**Carriers of the proof:** @[Halim](entity:npc/Halim) (witness) · @[Sindri](entity:npc/Sindri) (copy of the first declaration)

**In the city:** @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar) · @[Bargeman — Rüstem](entity:npc/Bargeman — Rüstem) (weighbridge slips) · @[Crane Master](entity:npc/Crane Master) (the @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr) wharf) · @[Captain — Maren](entity:npc/Captain — Maren) (the name of a ship that did not arrive)

## Item

@[The Sealless Ring](entity:trinket/The Sealless Ring) — the chain's only object; its lack of a stamp points to a workbench outside the guilds, that is, to the harbor.

## Institution cards

@[The Harbor Compact](entity:lore/The Harbor Compact) (what is a crime at the harbor) · @[The Banner Register](entity:lore/The Banner Register) (what unregistered means) · @[Border and Trade Guild](entity:lore/Border and Trade Guild) · @[Vorstrand — What Is Known](entity:lore/Vorstrand — What Is Known) · @[Courts of Honor](entity:lore/Courts of Honor)

The chain's payment is a signature, the countersignature on the passage paper — given in advance once the offer is accepted: @[Good Writ](entity:quest/Good Writ). The share of the house's inheritance comes when the job is done. The voyage that opens together with the offer: @[The Continent on the Horizon](entity:quest/The Continent on the Horizon).
# Good Writ — cards

The countersigned passage paper; in the language of the harbors, a *good writ*. Three steps, in the order of the paper's road.

1. @[Bargemen's Inn](entity:location/Bargemen's Inn) — a name and clothes in the cellar; for those who would board under their own name, skip it
2. @[In Line at the Passage Court](entity:scene/In Line at the Passage Court) — @[Countersign Desk](entity:location/Countersign Desk) (@[The Chancery](entity:location/The Chancery)), the paper and the preliminary approval
3. The signatory's room — @[Assembly House](entity:location/Assembly House) (the most crowded) · @[Border and Trade Guild Council Chamber](entity:location/Border and Trade Guild Council Chamber) · @[Customs House](entity:location/Customs House) (@[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr)): the countersignature. For Orvan's advance signature, @[The Offer at the Door](entity:scene/The Offer at the Door)

**NPCs:** @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar) · @[Corin Sancar](entity:npc/Corin Sancar) (the clerk who gives the preliminary approval) · @[Signatory — Selvi](entity:npc/Signatory — Selvi) (the Council Chamber's signatory, Orvan's papers) · @[Lamp](entity:npc/Lamp) (knows the way to the cellar) · @[Innkeeper — Aysel](entity:npc/Innkeeper — Aysel) (shows the stairs) · @[Needle](entity:npc/Needle) (a name and clothes in the cellar) · @[Bargeman — Rüstem](entity:npc/Bargeman — Rüstem) (the river road to Elymsyr) · @[Sergeant Krusk](entity:npc/Sergeant Krusk) (the law at the end of the corridor)

## Institution cards

@[The Banner Register](entity:lore/The Banner Register) (the trace the paper leaves) · @[Border and Trade Guild](entity:lore/Border and Trade Guild) · @[The Council and the Guild Assembly](entity:lore/The Council and the Guild Assembly) · @[Military Law Guild](entity:lore/Military Law Guild)

## Character tie

A character with the @[Guild Scion of Rank](entity:background/Guild Scion of Rank) background who is written onto a crew list under their own name is recognized at the wharf.

The ship the paper puts you on is a separate chain: @[The Continent on the Horizon](entity:quest/The Continent on the Horizon) (page 10).
# Places

mapping.name: Age of Will
mapping.description: Three hundred years that began on the day King Lucian cut the bond with the gods, as far as the people tell it.
pages:
# Age of Will

In every square in Meridia the same story is told: three hundred years ago King Lucian cut the bond between the gods and the people and left the people a single thing, **their own will.**

Since that day the continent has lived without gods. There are squares instead of temples, masters instead of priests, work instead of prayer. If a village falls sick, it first looks after itself. Asking for help is not a crime, but it is counted as a shortcoming.

## The burden of choosing

People could not bear the weight of choosing on their own, and they built new orders for themselves: guilds, ranks, ledgers. Today on the continent, @[The Steps of Service](entity:lore/The Steps of Service) decide who rises, and @[The Council and the Guild Assembly](entity:lore/The Council and the Guild Assembly) decides who makes decisions.

## The king

Lucian's name is spoken everywhere; he himself is seen nowhere. For three hundred years he has not come to the Council's sessions, and this bothers no one: the Council works without him too. In Votumar his words *"look to one another"* are still repeated every day.

## The unknown

No one knows what **really** happened three hundred years ago. Lucian left behind a great teaching, but almost no documents. The only place on the continent that keeps documents from that period is **Occulus**; the other archives keep only the teaching itself.

How the teaching is lived today: @[The Way of Will](entity:lore/The Way of Will).
mapping.dmNotes:
Every sentence on this card is true; everything missing is missing on purpose. The gap in history is not an oversight but the result of censorship.

Godlessness and the teaching of will keep people from asking for help. A merit system that does not see its own fault makes it possible for a sickness to be hidden. Do not tell the players this; play it as the institutions' silence.

mapping.name: The Gods and the Whisper
mapping.description: The gods did not leave; they gave up their existence, and only their whispers remain. Divine magic is still possible — but almost no one can do it, and those who can cannot do it every time.
pages:
# The Gods and the Whisper

The gods did not stop caring about people. They gave up their existence so that one single thing could be possible, and the only thing left in their hands is the ability to whisper.

Those who hear the whisper do not find it frightening. They describe it as the voice of someone who has a great deal to say but only the strength for a few words: tired, warm, brief.

Few hear it. No one has counted how many of the ten thousand people born in Meridia have heard that voice, because no one who would count took it seriously.

# Divine magic

**It works. And almost no one can do it.**

The overwhelming majority of people living on this continent **do not even try** to ask a god for something — and most of those who try get nothing in return. Even so, it is said there are those who do it: a woman cleansing the water at the head of a well, a priest closing a wound during a siege, someone stopping a fire with their voice. The stories are not lies. But every story happened **to someone else**, and the one telling it heard it from an acquaintance.

There are people who really can. Very few, and none of them has been able to build a countable pattern — because **having been answered once does not bring the next time.** The same person says the same prayer two days in a row; one holds, the other does not. Someone who asked for something and received it describes it not as an ability but as **luck**.

The rule is carried by @[Rule Deviations](entity:lore/Rule Deviations).

## Two consequences of this

**No one makes plans by trusting in divine magic.** An army does not leave its wounds to a priest, a guild does not tie its harvest to a prayer. All of Meridia's institutions were built on top of this absence: here the solution to a problem is always a person, a record or money.

**The paladin orders stopped asking.** The knights of Votumar take their power not from a god but from the oath they swore — and because that oath is sworn before witnesses and entered in the ledger, it stands the same way every morning (@[Order of the Silver Shield](entity:lore/Order of the Silver Shield)).

# Healing and the symbol

**Healing does not soothe.** Healing magic puts a weight on the body of both the caster and the one who receives it: a pressure in the bones, then a tiredness that does not pass. No one in Meridia describes being healed as something refreshing.

**A holy symbol is a tool.** Not an ornament; an instrument that focuses the divine. A priest who loses their symbol loses more than a component. But having the symbol does not bring the answer — it only carries the call.

## In the city

In Lucid Triton, someone who casts divine magic is seen not as someone working a miracle but as someone committing an irregularity. In the city there is no place where an answer from the gods could be written down.

But add this too: no one in this city has **seen** such a thing. Many have heard of it; no one has seen it. If it is seen once, it will be the only thing talked about in the city that day, and being talked about does not serve whoever did it.

Where faith lives, far from the city's eyes: @[The Silent Shrines](entity:lore/The Silent Shrines).
mapping.dmNotes:
**This card carries a table rule, and the rule is harsh.** Every attempt at divine magic rolls `d20 + Religion`; the numbers are in @[Rule Deviations](entity:lore/Rule Deviations). In practice this makes **Cleric and Warlock unplayable on this continent.** Tell the players this **before character creation** — a rule told after play has started is a price the player did not agree to.

A player who wants to play a Paladin has a separate, open road: @[Oath of Will](entity:subclass/Oath of Will). Nothing that oath grants requires a roll, because none of it is asked of a god.

The weight of healing and the symbol being a tool are narrative rules; they do not change the dice. The mechanical price is only in two spells and is written on the Blight card: whoever casts *Lesser Restoration* takes 1 level of Exhaustion, whoever casts *Greater Restoration* permanently loses one Hit Die.

If a character succeeds at casting divine magic, do not explain why the gods answered them. There is no reason; it held this round.

mapping.name: Blight — What Is Known
mapping.description: The sickness the villagers have named, but which no one knows the nature of.
pages:
# Blight — what is known

The villagers call it **the sickness**, some **the Blight**. Both words say the same thing: we gave it a name, we do not know what it is.

It seems to spread, it seems to make people ill, it comes before a physician like a disease. No one can say whether it really is a disease.

## Symptoms

1. First a slight cough, purplish-black veins as thin as a hair on the inner side of the joints, a metal taste in the mouth that does not go away.
2. Then a high fever, wounds that are slow to close, skin turning grey.
3. Later a purplish-black fluid seeping from the eyes and ears, breath growing short, and whispers coming from where no one is.
4. At last the skin hardens and flakes, the muscles contract against the person's will, speech falls apart.

And then consciousness shuts down.

## No two patients walk the same road

This is what wears out those who tend the sick the most. In one, tiredness comes to the fore; one is lucid for a moment, lost the next; one's body grows strong earlier than it should.

## How it passes

As far as is known, by contact: touching a sick person, spending a night in the same closed room with them. The sickness does not spread evenly; it is seen in one village and not in the village next to it.

## Treatment

There is no known treatment. The city's physicians call it *an advanced fever*. The villages' method is simple: **keep the sick apart, bring them their food, do not go inside.**

The only known protection against the sickness is the @[Sherbet of Resistance](entity:adventuring-gear/Sherbet of Resistance). The sherbet does not cure the sickness; it only makes it harder to catch.
mapping.dmNotes:
This card tells what the people know. The rules: @[Blight — Infection](entity:curse/Blight — Infection).

The sickness did not come to Meridia on a wind; it came with people from @[the Beyond](entity:lore/Vorstrand — What Is Known). No one the characters meet knows this.

The Blight is magical and tied to a source. Do not name, show or point to the source. The only way the characters can sense this is Arcana DC 13.

mapping.name: Vorstrand — What Is Known
mapping.description: The continent on the far side of the sea. No one in Meridia uses its name; everyone says "the Beyond".
pages:
# Vorstrand — what is known

The continent across from Meridia. You go by ship, you come by ship, and trade between the two continents has never stopped.

Its name is **Vorstrand**, but almost no one in Meridia says that name. People say **the Beyond**: *came from the Beyond, going to the Beyond, that's how it is in the Beyond.* It is used more like the name of a direction than the name of a place.

## In the harbors

On the wharf at Elymsyr the cloth, dye and spice of the Beyond are sold. Crews from the Beyond speak their own language; @[Elymsyr's interpreters](entity:npc/The Interpreter) carry their news to the continent.

## Those who come from the Beyond

Nothing about the past of someone from the Beyond can be verified in Meridia. The name they give, the trade they claim, the road they describe — all of it is their own word.

The only exception is the ledger of the @[Border and Trade Guild](entity:lore/Border and Trade Guild): the names of the Beyond's known free merchants are written in that ledger.
mapping.dmNotes:
The Blight was carried to Meridia from here. @[Alton Leagallow](entity:npc/Alton Leagallow), @[Merla Tealeaf](entity:npc/Merla Tealeaf) and @[Kromanna](entity:npc/Kromanna) came from here.

There is little on this card on purpose: the characters should not find a single verified piece of information about this continent.

mapping.name: The Council and the Guild Assembly
mapping.description: The continent's government: the Council the king founded, and the guilds that fill its six seats.
pages:
# The Council and the Guild Assembly

People say *"the Council decided"*, and they also say *"the Assembly met"*. Both mean the same six people sitting in the @[Assembly Hall](entity:location/Assembly Hall).

| | Council | Guild Assembly |
|---|---|---|
| **What** | The government the king founded | The board the guilds hold among themselves |
| **What it does** | Defines cities, levies taxes, appoints governors | Decides who will sit in which of the Council's seats |
| **Who sits** | The guilds fill its seats | Six guilds, six seats |

Everyone who speaks in the Council's name is really speaking in the name of a guild.

## Six seats

| Guild | House | In the seat |
|---|---|---|
| @[Wizards' Guild](entity:lore/Wizards' Guild) | No house; the Assembly appoints the seat | @[Rector — Quarion](entity:npc/Rector — Quarion) |
| @[Border and Trade Guild](entity:lore/Border and Trade Guild) | The Sancars | @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar) |
| @[Smithing and Labor Guild](entity:lore/Smithing and Labor Guild) | The Ferruns | @[Head Journeyman — Adrik Ferrun](entity:npc/Head Journeyman — Adrik Ferrun) |
| @[Alchemy and Healers' Guild](entity:lore/Alchemy and Healers' Guild) | The Kalenders | @[Chief Physician — Caramip Kalender](entity:npc/Chief Physician — Caramip Kalender) |
| @[Military Law Guild](entity:lore/Military Law Guild) | The Custars | @[Registrar — Valen Custar](entity:npc/Registrar — Valen Custar) |
| @[Architecture and Planning Guild](entity:lore/Architecture and Planning Guild) | The Mizans | @[Master of the Board — Perhun Mizan](entity:npc/Master of the Board — Perhun Mizan) |

## How decisions are made

Decisions are made not in session but before it, in the seat holders' own rooms. In session a decision is only announced, then sealed in the @[Hall of Seals](entity:location/Hall of Seals).

A seat holder who wants to object does not speak in session; they do not come to the session, or they withhold their countersignature.

## Signatories

Each guild has between five and ten **signatories** in the Assembly. They put down the signatures given in the guild's name: the seat holder decides, the signatory signs. The countersignature on a passage paper also comes from a signatory's hand. Signatories sit in **signatory rooms**, and a guild's rooms can be in different parts of the city (@[Countersign Desk](entity:location/Countersign Desk)).

## The king

King Lucian has not been seen at a session for three hundred years. The Council works without him too.

## Appointments

The Council appoints Elymsyr's @[Customs Governor](entity:npc/Customs Governor) and Votumar's Lord Commander — today @[Lord Commander — Varhan](entity:npc/Lord Commander — Varhan); that is to say, in practice, a guild does.
mapping.dmNotes:
If the characters ask *"which Council members take a share from the harbor?"*, the real question is *"which guilds?"*. @[Velvet](entity:npc/Velvet) on the wharf is a guild's man — and in Act 1 he is the second door that sends the characters to this hall (the first is @[Halim](entity:npc/Halim)).

The Council appointed the Lord Commander: whoever sits in that seat today was seated there by a guild, with its own hand, without realizing it.

mapping.name: The Banner Register
mapping.description: The Council's great ledger: who is sealed, who is registered, who is unwritten. How lines are opened, raised and erased.
pages:
# The Banner Register

The Council's great ledger. In Meridia a person's name, house, guild and rank are written in this ledger. The ledger belongs to the Council; the guilds hold the pen.

## Three classes

| Class | What it means | How they are known in the street |
|---|---|---|
| **Sealed** | Carries the seal of a house or a guild; writes in the ledger with their own hand | By two names: a name and a house |
| **Registered** | Is written in the ledger, but is not the hand that writes | By one name |
| **Unwritten** | Is in no ledger; either never entered one or was removed | By a nickname |

If someone unwritten disappears, no one writes it down anywhere.

## The seal

A seal is the authority to write in a ledger; a seal ring is the portable form of that authority. A sealed person wears their ring openly.

## Surnames

Halfling and dwarf surnames are family tradition, not houses. The ledger does not write these surnames as houses; behind a halfling surname there is no record to check.

## Outside the ledger

@[The Beyond](entity:lore/Vorstrand — What Is Known) is a single line in the ledger: *off-continent*. None of the people of @[Radenhall Courtyard](entity:location/Radenhall Courtyard) are written in the ledger, and no one there misses it.

# How the ledger works

## Who writes

In the city each guild keeps its own ledger. In the provinces there is a single pen: the @[Border and Trade Guild](entity:lore/Border and Trade Guild). A villager's name and the list of a load crossing the border come from the hand of the same guild's clerk.

## A line

A line has four boxes: **name · house · guild and rank · guarantor.** If the house box is empty, the person is sealless. If the guarantor box is empty, the line is not opened.

## How a line is opened

A person enters the ledger not by being born but by surety: at eighteen they are enrolled as an apprentice in a guild (@[The Steps of Service](entity:lore/The Steps of Service)), or someone written in the ledger stands guarantor for them. The guarantor also takes on the debts of the one they vouch for.

## How one rises

Rank changes with a master's signature, and becomes official with a countersignature. The wait between the two signatures is shortened with bribes. See @[In Line at the Passage Court](entity:scene/In Line at the Passage Court).

## How a seal is obtained

The Council does not give the seal; a house passes it on. That is why the number of the sealed does not grow; a seal only changes hands.

## How a line is erased

1. **Striking from the ledger** — the punishment the @[Courts of Honor](entity:lore/Courts of Honor) give for treason.
2. **Withdrawal of surety** — if the guarantor withdraws their hand, the line falls.
3. **Erasure for money** — removing a page as if it had never been written. This is a crime.

Erasure for money leaves two traces. **The guarantor's countersignature stays in the ledger**, because the signature is part of the column, not of the page. **The line's copy in the provincial pen stays**: the page goes to the city, the second copy does not.
mapping.dmNotes:
**Erasure for money has a price.**

**In Act 1, erasure for money does not come up.** The three strangers are written in no ledger: they never entered Lucid Triton's ledgers, because they never passed through customs; and the ledger of @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor) does not write people, only goods.

@[The Sealless Ring](entity:trinket/The Sealless Ring) in Kromanna's hidden pocket is a seal ring, but it was being carried hidden rather than openly, and its seal face had been filed off.

mapping.name: Wizards' Guild
mapping.description: The guild of licensed magic, the academy and teleportation. The Assembly's only seat without a house.
pages:
# Wizards' Guild

| | |
|---|---|
| **Business it runs** | Magic licenses, the academy, long-distance teleportation |
| **House** | None; the Assembly appoints to the seat |
| **In the seat** | @[Rector — Quarion](entity:npc/Rector — Quarion) |
| **Who it clashes with** | All of them; its knowing who goes where unsettles everyone |

The only seat in the Assembly without a house. For the other five houses, proof that a seat can be taken from a house.

## The academy

The guild's academy is in Lucid Triton: with its library, its study halls and its masters. In the city magic is a disciplined profession; students rise step by step at a master's side.

## The license

> Casting magic within city limits requires a **Guild License**. Unlicensed magic is the crime of *threatening public safety*.

This guild issues the license; the @[Military Law Guild](entity:lore/Military Law Guild) writes up the crime. The punishment is not prison: public service, a fine and a line in the record. Someone who carries that line in their record can never get a license again.

The license is only asked about in the city. In a village, on the road and in a harbor no one asks; at @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor) a license is a joke.

## Two forbidden schools

| Forbidden | Why |
|---|---|
| **Necromancy** | The cause of death is written by the @[Alchemy and Healers' Guild](entity:lore/Alchemy and Healers' Guild). Magic that raises the dead makes that declaration a lie |
| **Enchantment that controls the mind** | Meridia's teaching rests on will. Magic that takes away someone's will is a crime committed against the teaching |

Neither can be done even with a license. Someone caught working with these schools is struck from the ledger.

## Teleportation and materials

Long-distance teleportation goes only through this guild, and the guild knows who goes where. Rare spell components are found either with guild permission or on the black market. Details: @[Rule Deviations](entity:lore/Rule Deviations).
mapping.dmNotes: A license gives a caster character not a punishment but a relationship. The licensed are bound to a guild and go when called; the unlicensed have to be careful in the city. Do not play the rule as *"you can't cast magic in the city"*.

mapping.name: Border and Trade Guild
mapping.description: The guild of passage, customs and grain; in the provinces, the pen of every ledger. Its seal is in the oldest house, its money in none.
pages:
# Border and Trade Guild

| | |
|---|---|
| **Business it runs** | Passage, customs, tonnage, grain and prices; every ledger in the provinces |
| **House** | The Sancars |
| **In the seat** | @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar) |
| **Who it clashes with** | The @[Smithing and Labor Guild](entity:lore/Smithing and Labor Guild) (imported goods undercut the local workbench) and the @[Military Law Guild](entity:lore/Military Law Guild) (whose word counts at the border) |

This guild's clerk writes down both the load that crosses the border and the child born in the provinces. The price of bread is this guild's business too: grain is imported to the continent.

## The oldest seal, the emptiest purse

The Sancars' seal is the oldest in the Assembly, but they have no money. The guild's income comes not from property but from trade: when a ship is late or never comes, when the border gates slow down, when grain does not arrive, the guild grows poorer. The other five guilds' income comes from the city's own markets and budget.

## In the provinces

The customs of @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr) answer to this guild. That is why the customs governor is the richest official of the Assembly's poorest guild.

Archivists are this guild's provincial clerks.

## The passage paper

The way to board a ship officially is the countersigned passage paper; in the harbors this is called a **good writ**. The paper is collected from the @[Countersign Desk](entity:location/Countersign Desk) with the name and details already written on it. The countersignature is given by one of the guild's signatories, in one of three **signatory rooms**: the @[Assembly House](entity:location/Assembly House) (the most crowded) · the guild's own house, the @[Border and Trade Guild Council Chamber](entity:location/Border and Trade Guild Council Chamber) · the @[Customs House](entity:location/Customs House) in @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr).
mapping.dmNotes:
The sickness came in over the border, and the border's ledger belongs to this guild. That is why this is the only seat in the Assembly that believes in the sickness, and also the seat no one in the hall listens to.

The guild's preliminary approval desk is in the hands of @[Corin Sancar](entity:npc/Corin Sancar), and it was @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar) who sat him at that desk. It is also the point in the guild where the most bribes change hands. Orvan knows this; it has worked this way for thirty years.

mapping.name: Smithing and Labor Guild
mapping.description: The guild of metal, coinage, the assay stamp and the day wage. The continent's most crowded guild.
pages:
# Smithing and Labor Guild

| | |
|---|---|
| **Business it runs** | Metal, minting coin, the assay stamp, the day wage |
| **House** | The Ferruns, a dwarf house |
| **In the seat** | @[Head Journeyman — Adrik Ferrun](entity:npc/Head Journeyman — Adrik Ferrun) |
| **Who it clashes with** | The @[Architecture and Planning Guild](entity:lore/Architecture and Planning Guild) (who plans the work, who calls the workers) and the @[Border and Trade Guild](entity:lore/Border and Trade Guild) |

The continent's most crowded guild. Most of its members are not rich, but there are many of them.

## The smiths' market

In Lucid Triton's smiths' market the anvils start before sunrise and do not fall silent until the lanterns are lit. The street smells of coal smoke and hot iron; in front of the doors stand horseshoes, chains and blade edges left to cool.

## The assay stamp

A small strike that shows a metal's purity and which workbench it came from. Every jeweler and assay master has their own stamp. Which workbench each stamp belongs to is written in an index, and few people can read the index. One of them: @[Kildrak Ferrun](entity:npc/Kildrak Ferrun).

## Dwarves and metal

On the continent, metalwork, walls, armor and heavy mechanisms are mostly in the hands of dwarves. This is not a rule but a tendency; still, most of the names in the stamp index are dwarf names.
mapping.dmNotes:
The guild's knowledge is not with the rich but with the masters at the workbench. The master at the workbench is also easy to silence.

In the Assembly this guild's numbers did not drop, because the same workers are working two shifts and new names were written in place of the missing.

mapping.name: Alchemy and Healers' Guild
mapping.description: The guild of the physician's license, potions and the declaration of cause of death.
pages:
# Alchemy and Healers' Guild

| | |
|---|---|
| **Business it runs** | The physician's license, potions and alchemy, the declaration of cause of death |
| **House** | The Kalenders |
| **In the seat** | @[Chief Physician — Caramip Kalender](entity:npc/Chief Physician — Caramip Kalender) |
| **Who it clashes with** | The @[Wizards' Guild](entity:lore/Wizards' Guild); over who does the healing |

In the city, this guild writes down why a person died.

## Healing potions are scarce

In the city, healing potions are sold only at the benches of licensed physicians, and they are expensive. In the provinces they cannot be bought with money; they are made.

## Who can make them

A licensed physician, someone with druid knowledge, or someone who works with an alchemist's kit. They all need the same thing: **clean water** and the right herb.

The @[Sherbet of Resistance](entity:adventuring-gear/Sherbet of Resistance), the only known protection against the sickness, is made by the same hands.

## The healers' barracks

The guild's apprentices live and work in a stone barracks in Lucid Triton. The barracks' long corridors smell of camphor and vinegar; the steam of boiling cauldrons fogs the windows of the rooms. Declarations are first written out fair here, by the apprentices' hands. One of the apprentices: @[Sindri](entity:npc/Sindri).
mapping.dmNotes:
The Chief Physician had the sickness's declarations changed. A copy of the first declaration is with @[Sindri](entity:npc/Sindri); that copy is the document proving the sickness was known in the city.

This guild cannot say *"we don't know"*: admitting it does not know would tear down the claim on which its right to grant physicians' licenses rests.

mapping.name: Military Law Guild
mapping.description: The guild of the criminal record, policing authority and quarantine law.
pages:
# Military Law Guild

| | |
|---|---|
| **Business it runs** | The criminal record, policing authority, the law of quarantine and states of emergency |
| **House** | The Custars |
| **In the seat** | @[Registrar — Valen Custar](entity:npc/Registrar — Valen Custar) |
| **Who it clashes with** | The @[Border and Trade Guild](entity:lore/Border and Trade Guild); whose word counts at the border |

## Public order in the city

The army does not keep order in Lucid Triton; the authority rests with this guild. This guild writes up the crime, this guild hands down the punishment.

But the man standing watch in the street is not always this guild's man. Each guild has its own police in its own market. Who you complain to depends on where it happened to you.

Military Law has the final word, but it takes time to arrive, and by the time it does the matter is usually over.

## The crimes it writes up

This guild writes up the crime of unlicensed magic. Major crimes and treason go to the @[Courts of Honor](entity:lore/Courts of Honor).

## Quarantine

The authority to declare quarantine rests with this guild. By law, a quarantine requires martial law to come into force.
mapping.dmNotes:
The Registrar **has** the authority to declare quarantine, and for two seasons has not used it: the day he uses it, the responsibility becomes his too.

The Custars have money in the harbor. The real name of @[Velvet](entity:npc/Velvet) on the wharf is **Halet Custar**.

The guild is setting up a room for itself in @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr), on one of the upper terraces: the @[Military Law Chamber](entity:location/Military Law Chamber). A second eye beside the customs; the @[Customs Governor](entity:npc/Customs Governor) does not want it (@[The Masked Job](entity:quest/The Masked Job)).

mapping.name: Architecture and Planning Guild
mapping.description: The guild of building permits, waterways, district boundaries and the city wall.
pages:
# Architecture and Planning Guild

| | |
|---|---|
| **Business it runs** | Building permits, waterways, district boundaries, the city wall |
| **House** | The Mizans |
| **In the seat** | @[Master of the Board — Perhun Mizan](entity:npc/Master of the Board — Perhun Mizan) |
| **Who it clashes with** | The @[Smithing and Labor Guild](entity:lore/Smithing and Labor Guild); who plans the work, who calls the workers |

Where a district begins and ends, which way the water flows, is written in this guild's plans.

## Meridia's architecture

- **Large but on a human scale.** Buildings do not climb to the sky; they are large enough to live in comfortably and are made with the finest craftsmanship in stone and wood.
- **Monuments are statues of people.** There are no statues of gods in the squares: there are architects, engineers and soldiers whose names are unknown.
- **Lanterns.** At night the cities are lit meticulously with lanterns. A lantern gone out is counted a bad sign.
- **White stone.** @[Lucid Triton](entity:location/Lucid Triton) is built of white marble, @[Votumar](entity:location/Votumar) of white limestone.
mapping.dmNotes: For some time now the plan in the Master of the Board's hands has not shown the city correctly. The wall repairs have stayed on paper.

mapping.name: The Way of Will
mapping.description: The teaching left from the Age of Will, and its corruption that no one speaks of out loud.
pages:
# The Way of Will

The teaching left from the @[Age of Will](entity:lore/Age of Will). It has no temple, no priest, no prayer; it has squares, ceremonies and a founding text.

## Three foundations

**You are the master of your own fate.** Everything that happens to you is the result of your own choice. Praying in the face of disaster is helplessness; finding a solution is a virtue.

**Work well done.** Plowing a field well, forging a sword flawlessly, keeping a watch without fail. These are the teaching's greatest virtues.

**Order and the Text of Will.** The founding text left from the beginning. There is a copy in every square and in almost every house; it speaks of justice, honesty and endurance. No one has read it from beginning to end; everyone knows a few lines by heart.

## The corruption

No one says this out loud. The long peace has turned will from a labor every person spends every day into an abstract power:

| What the teaching asks | What happens today |
|---|---|
| Everyone uses their own will | Will is taken for a body of traditions that protects society |
| No one kneels to anyone | The people trust blindly in those they believe were chosen on merit |
| There is no god | There is no god, but there are plenty of ceremonies |

## Three readings in three places

- **Votumar:** there, Lucian's words *"look to one another"* are read as *"be one another's shield"*.
- **Radenhall:** there, the Way of Will is not a teaching but the law of nature.
- **Lucid Triton:** will is a rank; the countersignature tells whose word counts.

The faiths that remain outside the teaching: @[The Silent Shrines](entity:lore/The Silent Shrines).
mapping.dmNotes:
**The teaching's weak point is trust in the leader.** In @[Votumar](entity:location/Votumar) the people obey whoever sits in that seat not out of fear but because they truly trust them. Whoever sits in that seat does not need to persuade anyone. See @[Lord Commander — Varhan](entity:npc/Lord Commander — Varhan).

Votumar is where the teaching is lived most soundly, and that is why it is the place most easily exploited.

mapping.name: The Silent Shrines
mapping.description: The faiths that live outside the teaching in Meridia. They are not forbidden; they are ignored.
pages:
# The Silent Shrines

The old faiths did not vanish; they withdrew out of sight. The Council does not forbid them, and ignores them as long as they do not disturb public order.

| Faith | Where | What is done |
|---|---|---|
| **The old gods** | Back streets, cellars, the oldest houses, caves | Small altars to sea gods and harvest goddesses. Their names half forgotten |
| **The ancestors** | The place of honor in the house | The bust or weapon of an ancestor who achieved something great is displayed. The faith closest to the teaching: after all, it is a person being honored |
| **Nature spirits** | @[Silverwater](entity:location/Silverwater) and @[Radenhall Courtyard](entity:location/Radenhall Courtyard) | It is believed that nature has its own consciousness, and that runes are the language of that consciousness |
| **Blind luck** | @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor) | The forgotten god of sailors. Incense is burned in nooks, old symbols are carved into the rocks |
| **The Spirit of the Current** | @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr) | Before setting out, a sailor throws a piece of silver into the water. Everyone does it, no one talks about it |

## On the shore and in the village

The fishers of @[Votumar](entity:location/Votumar) quietly leave flowers on the shore and carve runes into the stones to calm the sea's anger; they do it at hours when the knights are not looking. In @[Cinervik](entity:location/Cinervik) a small altar to the old gods stands right beside a monument to Will, and no one is bothered. In Silverwater most doors carry a charm carved from wood; the village believes in the voice of the **Great Forest**.
mapping.dmNotes: A character who casts divine magic is not breaking the law but committing an irregularity. This card shows them the places in the city where they can breathe easy.

mapping.name: The Steps of Service
mapping.description: The rise that begins at eighteen: from apprentice to grandmaster, from private to officer.
pages:
# The Steps of Service

> Everyone who turns eighteen joins a **guild**, the **army** or the **bureaucracy**. Rising comes through achievement: *Apprentice → Journeyman → Master → Grandmaster*, or *Private → Corporal → Officer*. Blood ties have no official place.

## Consequences

**Idleness is shameful.** Unemployment is counted not as a misfortune but as a flaw of character. In Meridia an adult not bound to an institution has to explain themselves.

**Rising really happens.** The apprentice becomes a master, the private becomes an officer. But making the rise official depends on a guild's countersignature, and the countersignature comes quickly or slowly depending on whose side you stand.

**Houses.** *Influential family* is not an official title. It is the family whose children have been better prepared for the examinations for generations, that is, the family that holds a guild's seal.

## House and seal

A house is the family that holds a guild's seal, and the seal passes not by blood but by transfer: adoption, taking in a son-in-law, rarely purchase. A family that loses the seal stops being a house. That is why quarrels between houses are fought not with swords but with seals.

How the ledger works: @[The Banner Register](entity:lore/The Banner Register).

mapping.name: Courts of Honor
mapping.description: In Meridia a crime is committed not against a person but against the Common Will. The punishment for treason is being struck from the ledger and exile.
pages:
# Courts of Honor

In Meridia a crime is counted as committed not against a person but against **the Common Will**. Trials are swift, punishment certain.

| Crime | Where it is heard | Punishment |
|---|---|---|
| **Minor** | Guild court | A fine, compensation, a line in the record |
| **Major** | Court of Honor; the Council appoints the judge | Public service: river works, mines, hard labor on the border line |
| **Treason** | Court of Honor | Striking from the ledger and exile |

**Prison is not common.** Feeding and holding a person costs more than putting them to work.

## Treason

The punishment for treason is counted as heavier than death. The exile is also struck from the ledger and becomes Unwritten: their name is written nowhere, and whatever happens to them, no one makes a note of it anywhere.

## Police and court

The record and the punishment are written by the @[Military Law Guild](entity:lore/Military Law Guild); the police in the street are each guild's own men.

## Votumar

In @[Votumar](entity:location/Votumar), the **Laws of Honor and Oath** take the place of civil law. There even a minor crime can be counted *Treason against the Will*, and trials are swifter even than in the capital.

## Elymsyr

In @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr) the gravest crime is smuggling. Its punishment is lifelong hard labor on the river works.
mapping.dmNotes: Most of the people of @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor) are people who fled these courts: debtors, fugitives, those struck from the ledger. @[Enamel](entity:npc/Enamel) left her own name behind of her own will.

mapping.name: Order of the Silver Shield
mapping.description: Votumar's paladin order: heavy armor, giant tower shields, flawless discipline.
pages:
# Order of the Silver Shield

The paladin company of the castle of @[Votumar](entity:location/Votumar), and the most elite defensive unit of Meridia's army. Heavy plate armor, tower shields taller than they are, white cloaks.

## Drill

In the mornings the Order's paladins drill the shield wall in the castle courtyard: shields side by side, shoulder to shoulder, a wall that advances on a single command. During drill a single voice is expected to be heard, the voice of the officer giving orders.

## Being a shield

In the Order, Lucian's words *"look to one another"* are read as *"be one another's shield"*. A paladin's faith is bound not to an abstract power but to the comrade standing beside them.

Needless noise is frowned upon. *"Patient as the bay, upright as the castle"* is praise.

## The oath

In the castle it is not civil law but the **Laws of Honor and Oath** that apply. Even a minor crime can be counted *Treason against the Will*.

## Tag and seal

The Order's soldiers wear a @[Barracks Tag](entity:trinket/Barracks Tag) around their necks, its officers a @[Seal of Command](entity:trinket/Seal of Command) on their fingers. The tag is also used like a holy symbol.

A paladin who leaves the Order loses not only their title but also their food, their bed and their right of passage; and they must leave their tag behind.

## The people

The people who serve the castle are bound to the paladins by a deep bond. In @[Argenfon](entity:location/Argenfon) the paladins often come down to the village, chat with the tradespeople, join the festivals.

## The High Command

All administrative, judicial and military authority in the castle rests in a single office: @[Lord Commander — Varhan](entity:npc/Lord Commander — Varhan). The Council appoints the Lord Commander.
mapping.dmNotes:
Everyone in the Order is well-meaning, disciplined, and trusts a commander they love. Do not play the Order as an enemy.

Paladins are more resistant to the Blight's bodily symptoms: the symptoms of the Incubation stage do not show in them. Their scores and mechanics do not change.

mapping.name: Wardens of the North
mapping.description: The druid tribe that governs Radenhall. Decisions come not from a vote but from the cycle of nature and the sign of the runes.
pages:
# Wardens of the North

The druid tribe that governs @[Radenhall Courtyard](entity:location/Radenhall Courtyard). The tribe is led by the village elder, the eldest druid; the authority rests not on a vote but on the cycle of nature and the sign of the runes.

## In place of an army

- **There is no standing army.** Radenhall is guarded by tamed dire wolves, ravens, and protectors who can turn nature into a weapon.
- **A single narrow path.** There is only one road that comes down to Radenhall through the coastal mountains, and it is watched constantly. Meridia's army counts entering here a logistical nightmare, and does not enter.
- **There is little property.** Almost everything is shared. The tribe's people are mixed: people of every race and every gender who fled here from elsewhere. Their clothes are mostly made from plants; even what looks like cloth is woven from bamboo and similar plants.

## Stone and song

The ceremonies of harvest, birth and death are held around the Courtyard's runed stones. The tribe's history is written not in books but in songs; bards and healers are its most respected members. The houses are just outside the Courtyard, under the trees: wooden houses large and small; some on the ground, some up in the trees, some wrapped in vines strung between two trees.

## Runes

The Wardens believe less in gods than in the old powers beneath the earth and in the sky, and they count runes as the language of those powers. Here the Way of Will is not a teaching but the law of nature.

## Barter

Gold is hardly worth anything here. Healing herbs, runed stones and the @[Sherbet of Resistance](entity:adventuring-gear/Sherbet of Resistance) change hands. The sherbet's recipe is the tribe's knowledge.
mapping.dmNotes:
The knowledge that can read when nature has fallen sick is taught here. The +2 druids get on the Corruption Check is the result of this training.

The Wardens read the rot not from rumor but directly from nature, and they have known for months. No one came to ask.

mapping.name: The Harbor Compact
mapping.description: Hidden Harbor's unwritten law. Two grave crimes: telling where the harbor is, and boarding a ship without permission.
pages:
# The Harbor Compact

There is no written law at @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor). There is a spoken rule everyone knows, and its name is **the Compact**. The sentence someone who breaks the rule will hear is known: *"You broke the Compact."*

## Two grave crimes

1. **Telling outsiders where the harbor is.**
2. **Boarding someone's ship without permission.**

The punishment is permanent exile from the harbor. No one stands guarantor for an exile, and no one gets into the harbor without a guarantor.

## Threats

At the harbor a threat does not start a fight; word of it spreads. Prices go up for whoever made the threat, no one stands guarantor for them, doors close. The punishment is not a beating but loneliness; and someone alone cannot board a ship from this harbor.

Threatening with the Council does not work either: the Council knows about this harbor.

## Three fixed truths

1. **No one comes to help.** Whoever joins a fight gets the same punishment as whoever started it. The wharf watches.
2. **Running saves you, but it is expensive.** Whoever runs loses their guarantor. To get into the harbor again they have to find a new guarantor.
3. **Whoever kills, loses.** Someone who kills a person at the harbor can never enter this harbor again.

The harbor is still dangerous. No one is obliged to protect anyone.
mapping.dmNotes:
If a fight breaks out at the harbor, there is no ready-made encounter card. Improvise, and do not step outside the three fixed truths.

Tell the players the third truth in advance. @[Mouse](entity:npc/Mouse) tells it on the first day, for free.

mapping.name: Rule Deviations
mapping.description: The three rules this world adds to 5e: the price of resurrection, teleportation and distance, lasting wounds.
pages:
# The Calling Roll

*A rule added to 5e.*

> **When someone wants to cast a divine spell, `d20 + Religion` is rolled before the spell takes effect.** If the threshold is not met, the spell **does not happen** and the spell slot is spent anyway.

| Situation | Threshold |
|---|---|
| **In combat** — every attempt | **19** · a failure spends **the action too** |
| **Outside combat** — the **1st** attempt in that hour | **18** |
| the **2nd** attempt in that hour | **20** |
| the **3rd** attempt in that hour | **bare d20, natural 20 only** — Religion is not added |
| the **4th** and later in that hour | **impossible** — no roll is made |

The counter is hourly and single: attempts rolled in combat are written to the same hour. The hour starts with the first attempt.

## Whom it binds

**It binds:** all of the Cleric's and Warlock's spells, the Paladin's divine spells. Which spells count as divine: @[Divine Spell List](entity:lore/Divine Spell List).

**It does not bind:** Druid and Ranger (their power comes from nature, it is not granted), class features that are not spells, and everything that has been granted once — warlock invocations, the paladin aura, everything the @[Oath of Will](entity:subclass/Oath of Will) grants.

The distinction in a single sentence: **what is asked for anew with every use requires a roll; what has been granted once does not.**

Why it is so: @[The Gods and the Whisper](entity:lore/The Gods and the Whisper).

# The Weight of Death

*A rule added to 5e.*

*Revivify* and the resurrection spells above it **cannot be cast by spending a spell slot alone.**

> **A life for a life.** Before the resurrection begins, the price is chosen:
>
> - **The caster** permanently loses one **Hit Die**, **or**
> - **The one raised** permanently gives up one **ability score point**.

## The Resurrection Trial

Paying the price does not guarantee the result.

If the resurrection fails, the soul returns in one of three states:

| State | What it means |
|---|---|
| **Incomplete** | Something did not come back: a memory, a skill, a habit. The person does not know what is missing |
| **Corrupted** | It came back, but not the same. It says it is itself; those beside it cannot be sure |
| **Possessed** | What returned is not them. The DM knows this, the player does not |

# Teleportation and Distance

*A rule added to 5e.*

> **A teleportation spell of 4th level or higher gives the caster 1 level of Exhaustion.** Long-distance teleportation is **not possible outside the guilds.**

## Distance

On the continent news travels on horseback. A place two days away is also two days away politically.

> **Lucid Triton → Votumar:** **2 days** for a mounted courier.

The only institution that can shorten this time is the @[Wizards' Guild](entity:lore/Wizards' Guild), and it too knows who goes where.

## Rare components

The rare components of high-level spells are found either **with guild permission** or **on the black market**. The black market's address is @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor).

# Lasting Wounds

*A rule added to 5e.*

> **Trigger:** hit points **dropping to 0**, or taking damage equal to **half of maximum hit points** in a single attack.
>
> **Roll:** d20. A low result is bad.

| d20 | Severity | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **1–5** | **Permanent**; does not heal on its own, requires *Greater Restoration* | A limp (speed −10 ft) · loss of an eye · a hand that won't grip |
| **6–14** | **Long-term**; lasts weeks, shortened by care | A bone that hasn't knit · a deep cut · an ear that doesn't hear |
| **15–20** | **Temporary**; passes at the next long rest | Aching ribs · a swollen eye · a throbbing hand |
mapping.dmNotes:
**Use the resurrection rule as a threat.** An NPC saying *"I can bring them back, but it will cost me a Hit Die"* shows what kind of place this world is without any resurrection being cast.

**Tell the players about Lasting Wounds before the first fight.** A result of 1–5 can leave a character permanently lame; the players should know this in advance. The first place in the act where the rule may be needed is @[Dawn Clash](entity:encounter/Dawn Clash).

The Blight's effect on magic is on a separate card: @[Blight — Infection](entity:curse/Blight — Infection) (Corruption Check).

mapping.description: Which spells call for the calling roll: the SRD breakdown of the Cleric, Warlock and Paladin lists, and the spells that cannot be cast without the roll.
pages:
# Who triggers the roll

The rule itself is on page 1 of @[Rule Deviations](entity:lore/Rule Deviations); this card only answers the question of **which spell**.

> **It is not the spell that triggers the roll, but whoever casts it.** *Cure Wounds* from a Cleric's mouth calls for the calling roll; from a Bard's mouth it does not. The same line, the same slot, the same damage — the difference is that one was asked for and the other was learned.

That is why the lists below were drawn up **by class**, not by school. School is no use: the SRD's 168 divine spells are spread across **all** eight schools (the most crowded is Abjuration with 35, the least Illusion with 11), so there is no line saying "this school is divine".

| Class | SRD spells | Roll |
|---|---|---|
| **Cleric** | 105 | all |
| **Warlock** | 68 | all |
| **Paladin** | 34 | all — except those granted by the @[Oath of Will](entity:subclass/Oath of Will) |
| **Druid · Ranger** | — | **none** (the power comes from nature, it is not granted) |
| Bard · Sorcerer · Wizard | — | **none** |

Spells marked **°** are also on a non-divine list: if they come from that class, there is no roll.

**Why the Warlock is here.** Half of its list looks arcane (*Mage Hand*, *Counterspell*, *Fly*), and this is not a mistake: the warlock's roll comes not from the spell being divine but from the power being **granted**. The patron does not have to answer every time either.

**What has been granted does not require a roll.** A warlock invocation, the paladin aura, every feature earned once is out of scope. The distinction in a single sentence: *what is asked for anew with every use requires a roll.*

# Paladin — 34 spells

| Level | Spell |
|---|---|
| **1st level** | Bless · Command° · Cure Wounds° · Detect Evil and Good · Detect Magic° · Detect Poison and Disease° · Divine Favor · Divine Smite · Heroism° · Protection from Evil and Good° · Purify Food and Drink° · Searing Smite° · Shield of Faith |
| **2nd level** | Aid° · Find Steed · Lesser Restoration° · Magic Weapon° · Protection from Poison° · Shining Smite · Zone of Truth° |
| **3rd level** | Create Food and Water · Daylight° · Dispel Magic° · Magic Circle° · Remove Curse° · Revivify |
| **4th level** | Aura of Life · Banishment° · Death Ward · Locate Creature° |
| **5th level** | Dispel Evil and Good · Geas° · Hallow · Raise Dead° |

## The @[Oath of Will](entity:subclass/Oath of Will) exemption

The oath's **always prepared** spells require no roll at any level — no one is asked, they come from the oath itself:

*Comprehend Languages · Locate Object · See Invisibility · Nondetection · Clairvoyance · Locate Creature · Arcane Eye · Legend Lore · Scrying*

Every spell the paladin **additionally prepares** from the Paladin list is subject to the table above. *Shield of Faith* appears twice and it is not a contradiction: the one from the oath is free, the one prepared from the list needs the roll.

**Divine Smite does not exist on this continent.** In SRD 5.2.1 it stands as a 1st-level spell; the Oath of Will replaces it with @[Oath Strike](entity:trait/Oath Strike) — that is not a spell but a trait, and it requires no roll.

# Cleric — 105 spells

**All of them require the roll.** This card does not shorten the list; seeing that it is not shortened is itself what conveys the weight of the rule.

| Level | Spell |
|---|---|
| **Cantrip** | Guidance° · Light° · Mending° · Resistance° · Sacred Flame · Spare the Dying° · Thaumaturgy |
| **1st level** | Bane° · Bless · Command° · Create or Destroy Water° · Cure Wounds° · Detect Evil and Good · Detect Magic° · Detect Poison and Disease° · Guiding Bolt · Healing Word° · Inflict Wounds · Protection from Evil and Good° · Purify Food and Drink° · Sanctuary · Shield of Faith |
| **2nd level** | Aid° · Augury · Blindness/Deafness° · Calm Emotions° · Continual Flame° · Enhance Ability° · Find Traps° · Gentle Repose° · Hold Person° · Lesser Restoration° · Locate Object° · Prayer of Healing · Protection from Poison° · Silence° · Spiritual Weapon · Warding Bond · Zone of Truth° |
| **3rd level** | Animate Dead° · Beacon of Hope · Bestow Curse° · Clairvoyance° · Create Food and Water · Daylight° · Dispel Magic° · Glyph of Warding° · Magic Circle° · Mass Healing Word° · Meld into Stone° · Protection from Energy° · Remove Curse° · Revivify · Sending° · Speak with Dead° · Spirit Guardians · Tongues° · Water Walk° |
| **4th level** | Banishment° · Control Water° · Death Ward · Divination° · Freedom of Movement° · Guardian of Faith · Locate Creature° · Stone Shape° |
| **5th level** | Blade Barrier° · Commune · Contagion° · Dispel Evil and Good · Flame Strike · Geas° · Greater Restoration° · Hallow · Insect Plague° · Legend Lore° · Mass Cure Wounds° · Planar Binding° · Raise Dead° · Scrying° |
| **6th level** | Create Undead° · Find the Path° · Forbiddance · Harm · Heal° · Heroes' Feast° · Planar Ally · True Seeing° · Word of Recall |
| **7th level** | Conjure Celestial · Divine Word · Etherealness° · Fire Storm° · Plane Shift° · Regenerate° · Resurrection° · Symbol° |
| **8th level** | Antimagic Field° · Control Weather° · Earthquake° · Holy Aura |
| **9th level** | Astral Projection° · Gate° · Mass Heal · True Resurrection° |

# Warlock — 68 spells

**All of them require the roll.** The reason is not divinity but being granted — the patron does not answer every call.

| Level | Spell |
|---|---|
| **Cantrip** | Chill Touch° · Eldritch Blast · Mage Hand° · Minor Illusion° · Poison Spray° · Prestidigitation° · True Strike° |
| **1st level** | Charm Person° · Comprehend Languages° · Disguise Self° · Expeditious Retreat° · Hellish Rebuke · Hex · Illusory Script° · Protection from Evil and Good° · Unseen Servant° |
| **2nd level** | Darkness° · Enthrall° · Hold Person° · Invisibility° · Mind Spike° · Mirror Image° · Misty Step° · Ray of Enfeeblement° · Shatter° · Spider Climb° · Suggestion° |
| **3rd level** | Counterspell° · Dispel Magic° · Fear° · Fly° · Gaseous Form° · Hypnotic Pattern° · Magic Circle° · Major Image° · Remove Curse° · Tongues° · Vampiric Touch° |
