| **4th level** | Banishment° · Blight° · Charm Monster° · Dimension Door° · Hallucinatory Terrain° |
| **5th level** | Contact Other Plane° · Dream° · Hold Monster° · Scrying° |
| **6th level** | Circle of Death° · Conjure Fey° · Create Undead° · Eyebite° · Flesh to Stone° · Mass Suggestion° · True Seeing° |
| **7th level** | Etherealness° · Finger of Death° · Forcecage° · Plane Shift° |
| **8th level** | Befuddlement° · Demiplane° · Dominate Monster° · Glibness° · Power Word Stun° |
| **9th level** | Astral Projection° · Foresight° · Imprisonment° · Power Word Kill° · True Polymorph° |

# 38 spells almost never seen on this continent

The following are **only** on the Cleric, Paladin and Warlock lists: no other class can cast them, which means on this continent these spells can **never** be cast without the roll.

| Level | Spell |
|---|---|
| **Cantrip** | Eldritch Blast · Sacred Flame · Thaumaturgy |
| **1st level** | Bless · Detect Evil and Good · Divine Favor · Divine Smite · Guiding Bolt · Hellish Rebuke · Hex · Inflict Wounds · Sanctuary · Shield of Faith |
| **2nd level** | Augury · Find Steed · Prayer of Healing · Shining Smite · Spiritual Weapon · Warding Bond |
| **3rd level** | Beacon of Hope · Create Food and Water · Revivify · Spirit Guardians |
| **4th level** | Aura of Life · Death Ward · Guardian of Faith |
| **5th level** | Commune · Dispel Evil and Good · Flame Strike · Hallow |
| **6th level** | Forbiddance · Harm · Planar Ally · Word of Recall |
| **7th level** | Conjure Celestial · Divine Word |
| **8th level** | Holy Aura |
| **9th level** | Mass Heal |

**For the DM:** this table is not a list of prohibitions but a list of **rarity**. When a player attempts a 3rd-level *Revivify*, this is what happens at the table: the threshold, the hourly counter, and the spent slot. When an NPC visibly casts one of these, it becomes the only thing talked about in the city (@[The Gods and the Whisper](entity:lore/The Gods and the Whisper)).

lore.source_name: Hıkka — The Record in the Books

mapping.name: Hıkka — The Record in the Books
mapping.description:
A small, shell-shedding species living in the shallow waters of the Beyond. There is no witness living on the coasts of Meridia; the knowledge exists only **in books** — the continent's isolation is not geographic but archival.

**Appearance.** The largest of them reaches a human's waist. Stocky and round: short arms, short legs, a broad body, a low center of gravity. The skin is turquoise — glossy when wet, matte when dry. The shell is a single piece and splits along the back; it starts between blue and green and shades into orange toward the edges. The eyes are large and completely dark, with no whites.

**On land and in water.** In water they are fast, with a motion that rolls the body; on land they do not run, they scuttle in short lunges over wet rock. They do not see in firelight — their fleeing from a torch is not fear, it is blindness.

**Sound.** The gill slits on the sides of the neck do not close fully on land. That is why the sound they make when speaking mostly resembles **hiccuping**: their own language, but said with the wrong breath on land. In water they do not speak like this. To a human ear the sound resembles weeping.

**Shedding.** They shed their shells at regular intervals. What is left behind is a shell split along the back, hollow but **complete in shape**; washed up on the shore, from a distance it looks like a crouching body. A fresh shell is colorful; an old one is faded by sun and salt.

**The few days after shedding.** One that has just shed is **soft**: defenseless, slow, unable to hunt. The colony's entire order is built around these few days — who will protect whom, who will bring food to whom. There is no rank; there is a rota.

**The aging.** One who stops shedding no longer grows; over the years its shell thickens layer upon layer and loses its color. Its size stays the same, its hardness multiplies. It does not leave the water.
mapping.dmNotes:
## Behavior

They do not seek a fight: they withdraw when they see light, return to the water when they hear a sound, chase no one on land. **But the threshold is very low.** A sudden lunge, a cut-off escape route, someone walking straight at them — they turn aggressive instantly and **all together**. When the nest is approached, this threshold is almost zero: there is no warning, no distance, no expectation of withdrawal there.

This is the balance to give the table: an encounter on the shore is manageable; **pressing up against the nest's mouth means thirty of them coming at you at once.**

## Spice

The gill membrane, left open on land, cannot bear a sharp smell. **They flee from spice.** In Meridia spice comes in through @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr) and is expensive — but what is needed is not the good kind: the bottom of the stall, sifted dust, an old batch gone bitter, broken roots no one buys. A blend is made from the cheap stuff and scattered along the shoreline.

**What it does:** it makes the scattered strip unusable for a few nights; the racks are saved.
**What it does not do:** it does not break up the colony, does not find the nest, does not end the hunger. They move on to another cove, and the coast is long.

So it is not a resolution but a **breather**.

## History — what is known

| DC | What it gives |
|---|---|
| **8** | It is not an animal of this continent. There is nothing like it on the coasts of Meridia |
| **12** | A species of the Beyond's shallow waters; they shed their shells, this is their sound, and there is not a single record of them harming people **unless provoked** |
| **15** | Their name in the books — **Hıkka** — and that the old coastal peoples kept them away with **sharp smells** |

The name in the books is a natural historian's attempt to put that hiccuping sound into writing; that is, a garbled form of their own name. Their real name is not learned in Act 1.

## DM — why they are here (not given to the players)

They fled from Vorstrand. The @[Blight — Infection](entity:curse/Blight — Infection) touched their shedding there: the young could no longer set their new shells, the change stopped halfway. **Those who could flee were the ones who could still shed** — which means none of those who arrived here is a carrier, and the sickness did not touch Votumar.

There is no one to tell the table this: there is no common language, and what they carry is not testimony but **evidence**. The table can reach the conclusion *'these fled from something'*; it cannot get the *why* in Act 1.

With the trio's arrival from @[Vorstrand](entity:location/Vorstrand) (`act1 §3.1`), these are two separate stories of the same sea. The card makes this connection nowhere; the table makes it.

lore.source_name: The Black Fleet — What Is Known

mapping.name: The Black Fleet — What Is Known
mapping.description: The name sailors give to the black-sailed ships. As much as the table can hear at sea.
pages:
# The Black Fleet — what is known

In the water between the two continents, ships with pitch-black hulls and sails. Sailors call them **the Black Fleet**; no one says whose fleet it is.

## What is told on the wharves

- When a black sail is sighted, the course is changed. No one goes close to look.
- In the water near the Beyond, drums are heard at night. A ship that hears the drums puts out its lantern.
- No one has ever come back to tell of boarding a black-sailed ship. Everything that is told was seen from a distance.
- Many tie the ships that never arrive to them; no one has seen it.

## The unknown

How many ships there are, whom they serve, what they want. They fly no banner, and they have never been seen docking at any harbor.
mapping.dmNotes:
The table fills this card in with what it hears at sea: @[Maren's Course](entity:scene/Maren's Course) (four regions, as much as Maren knows) · @[The Smugglers' Deck](entity:scene/The Smugglers' Deck) (the drum rumor) · @[Black Sail](entity:location/Black Sail) (what they saw).

There is little on this card on purpose. Whose the Black Fleet is, the other three ships, and its tie to the ships that never arrive are not written — all of it is the DM's.

mapping.name: Aegis
mapping.description: A world of two continents: Meridia and Vorstrand. Ships run between the two continents without ever stopping.
mapping.description_long:
A world with two continents: @[Meridia](entity:location/Meridia) and @[Vorstrand](entity:location/Vorstrand). Between the two continents there is a sea, and on the sea ships run every season. Words from other languages are heard in the harbors, the other continent's cloth and spice are sold in the markets. Seeing a foreigner surprises no one.

## Travel in this world

The roads are open. A villager can walk to the city, a merchant can send goods to the other continent. Between the continents you go by ship; within a continent news goes on horseback.

## The unknown

The people of Aegis do not know what happened three hundred years ago. There is a founding story told in the squares; documents that would show what lies behind that story either do not exist or are kept somewhere no one can reach. See @[Age of Will](entity:lore/Age of Will).
mapping.secrets: Ship traffic between the continents has never stopped. The Blight too was carried by this traffic, in the bodies of travelers coming from Vorstrand to Meridia.

mapping.name: Meridia
mapping.description: The continent of white stone cities, the guild assembly and open roads.
mapping.description_long:
The continent the characters stand on. It is bordered by mountains to the west, a white limestone coast to the east, a forested bowl ringed by coastal mountains to the north, and forest to the south.

## Terrain

- **The western mountains.** Steep mountains that hold snow. A river runs through them, comes out of a cleft in the mountain and pours into the sea at @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr).
- **The eastern coast.** Cliffs of white limestone dropping sheer to the sea. There are few places for a ship to put in; in the one deep bay stands the castle of @[Votumar](entity:location/Votumar). Along the coast runs the @[Watchtower Line](entity:location/Watchtower Line).
- **The northern tip.** The continent narrows toward the north and at the very tip opens into a forested bowl ringed by coastal mountains. This tip is close to the equator; snow does not reach it. @[Radenhall Courtyard](entity:location/Radenhall Courtyard) is in this bowl; a single narrow path leads down into it.
- **The southern forest.** The forest of the timber villages. @[Silverwater](entity:location/Silverwater) lies inside this forest.

## Settlements

| Place | What | Where |
|---|---|---|
| @[Lucid Triton](entity:location/Lucid Triton) | The capital of white marble; the Guild Assembly meets here | The middle of the continent |
| @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr) | The official seaport, also called Claport | The west, at the river mouth |
| @[Votumar](entity:location/Votumar) | The paladin castle and military governorate | The eastern bay |
| @[Argenfon](entity:location/Argenfon) | A fishing village | The eastern coast, near Votumar |
| @[Cinervik](entity:location/Cinervik) | A road village full of inns and farriers | The northern road |
| @[Silverwater](entity:location/Silverwater) | A forest village | The southern forest |
| @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor) | The harbor of ships that skip customs | On the coast; where is not told |
| @[Radenhall Courtyard](entity:location/Radenhall Courtyard) | The druids' runed stone rings | The northern tip |

## Travel

The roads on the continent are free: leaving a village, going to the city, going down to a harbor needs no one's permission. The only thing that costs money is boarding a ship.

News travels on horseback. **A mounted courier gets from Lucid Triton to Votumar in 2 days.**

## White stone

Meridia's great buildings are of white stone. Lucid Triton's facades are white marble, Votumar's walls white limestone. At sunset both cities look pink from afar.
mapping.secrets: The continent's tie to the outside never broke; what broke is the knowledge of the past. The continent's archives keep almost nothing about three hundred years ago, and this is not an accident.

mapping.name: Vorstrand
mapping.description: The continent on the far side of the sea. No one in Meridia uses its name; everyone says "the Beyond".
mapping.description_long:
The continent across from @[Meridia](entity:location/Meridia). You go by ship, you come by ship (@[The Open Sea](entity:location/The Open Sea)).

Almost no one in Meridia says this name. People say **the Beyond**: *came from the Beyond, going to the Beyond, that's how it is in the Beyond.* In the harbors the Beyond's cloth, dye and news are sold; no one on this continent can say whether the news is true.

What the people know about this continent: @[Vorstrand — What Is Known](entity:lore/Vorstrand — What Is Known).
mapping.secrets: The Blight came to Meridia from here. @[Alton Leagallow](entity:npc/Alton Leagallow), @[Merla Tealeaf](entity:npc/Merla Tealeaf) and @[Kromanna](entity:npc/Kromanna) set out from Vorstrand and entered Meridia without passing through customs.

mapping.name: The Open Sea
mapping.environment: The open sea between the two continents
mapping.description: The sea between @[Meridia](entity:location/Meridia) and @[Vorstrand](entity:location/Vorstrand). Every ship coming to the continent and leaving it passes through here; the ships that should have come and did not would have passed through here too.
mapping.description_long:
> Once the coast is behind you, the world comes down to two things: the sky above, the water below. For a while the land still shows as a line, then that goes too. The wind sticks salt to your lips. The ship's hull groans with every wave, the ropes creak, and when night comes the lantern's light shows nothing past a few fathoms.

The open sea between the continents. From Meridia to @[Vorstrand](entity:location/Vorstrand) — the Beyond, as the people say — you go by ship and come by ship. Whichever harbor you sail from — @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr) or @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor) — this water is crossed.

## Three ships

The ships the table can board:

- ***Honest Scales*** (@[Honest Scales](entity:location/Honest Scales)) — @[Captain — Maren](entity:npc/Captain — Maren)'s trading ship; sails from @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr). The legal way: whoever carries a countersigned paper is signed on as crew, and stands watches.
- **Caelynn's ship** — the well-kept ship moored at @[The Wharf](entity:location/The Wharf): its ropes are new, its deck washed every morning (@[Captain Caelynn](entity:npc/Captain Caelynn)).
- **Holg's ship** — the patched ship at the same pier: its gunwale patched in two places, its crew playing dice (@[Captain Holg](entity:npc/Captain Holg)).

## At sea

There is a trade route from coast to coast that everyone knows, and most ships follow it. How long the voyage takes is not written. The sea is not a road but an interval: there is no land, there is no record, and no one gets off the ship.

The voyage: @[The Continent on the Horizon](entity:quest/The Continent on the Horizon). The *Honest Scales*'s course: @[Maren's Course](entity:scene/Maren's Course). On smuggling ships: @[The Smugglers' Deck](entity:scene/The Smugglers' Deck). When land appears on the horizon: @[Land Ho](entity:scene/Land Ho).
mapping.secrets:
**Ships are going missing, and why they go missing is not written.** The ledger of the @[Border and Trade Guild](entity:lore/Border and Trade Guild) knows which ships did not arrive (@[Border and Trade Guild Council Chamber](entity:location/Border and Trade Guild Council Chamber)); no card knows where or why they went missing. The answer is the DM's (@[Where They Came From](entity:quest/Where They Came From)). Whether the table will run into that question while crossing this water is the DM's too.

**The *Fate*, which brought the three strangers, came over this water**, and after that night it never put in again. Its captain is still at sea.

**In the four regions of the route there are four ships of the Black Fleet,** a different ship in each region. In the region closest to Vorstrand is the smallest of the four: a pitch-black-hulled, black-sailed orc warship with drums, and below its deck are @[the Turned](entity:monster/The Turned). The *Honest Scales* leaves the trade route and passes outside the first three regions; in the last water, near the Beyond, there is no room to go around (@[Maren's Course](entity:scene/Maren's Course)).

That ship: @[Black Sail](entity:location/Black Sail). The meeting begins with @[The Sound of Drums](entity:scene/The Sound of Drums) and continues with @[Hull to Hull](entity:encounter/Hull to Hull); if someone bitten stays on the ship, @[Quarantine Night](entity:scene/Quarantine Night).

As much as sailors know: @[The Black Fleet — What Is Known](entity:lore/The Black Fleet — What Is Known).

mapping.name: Silverwater
mapping.description: A small village in the southern forest that lives on timber and healing herbs. Three strangers lie in the cabin outside the village; the fourth is upstairs at the inn, and he is not sick.
mapping.description_long:
> The forest road comes out between the last trees, drops into a clearing and ends among wooden houses. Most of the roofs have gathered moss; a thin wood smoke rises from the chimneys. In a yard a copper cauldron is boiling, and the sharp smell of lye mixes with the smoke. Freshly washed linens sway on the lines. Several doors carry fresh chalk lines, and beside each line a charm the size of a palm, carved from wood, has been nailed.
>
> Two women at the well are talking about the sickness. They do not lower their voices; they talk about it the way they would talk about the price of bread. At the entrance to the village a youth with a spear, sitting on a stump, stands up on seeing you, without raising the spear. *"Who are you looking for?"*

A small village deep in the southern forest that lives on timber, healing herbs and game. The sickness is on everyone's lips in the village, but the village has not stopped working: bread is baked, laundry is washed, the watch is kept. So far no one has died.

## The village's order

Silverwater is bound to no one; once a year it sends the kingdom a token tax. The village's problems are looked after by the **Council of Elders**, made up of the oldest. The head of the council is @[Duran](entity:npc/Duran), but he does not decide alone.

There are no soldiers in the village. Volunteer villagers take turns keeping watch with spears in hand; the watch post is the stump at the village entrance.

Little money circulates. The villagers mostly barter: a back-load of timber goes for a sack of flour, a bundle of dried herbs for a bowl of oil.

Whatever comes from outside — salt, thread, nails, a good knife, a bottle of medicine — enters the village on @[Corvin](entity:npc/Corvin)'s back. The village does not know about @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor) and does not ask where the goods come from; the only thing it knows is that Corvin goes and comes back. Corvin was not born in the village and is not counted a villager — but he is loved.

## The village's places

- **The well.** In the middle of the village, a well with a stone rim. Mornings and evenings there is a queue for buckets. Everything talked about in the village is talked about here first.
- **@[Goodbarrel's Hearth](entity:location/Goodbarrel's Hearth).** The village's only inn; in the evenings half the village sits by the hearth.
- **The houses.** Houses of thick planks with mossy roofs. Most doors carry chalk marks and carved charms; signs of plenty are carved into the window frames.
- **@[The Cabin](entity:location/The Cabin).** Past the village's last house, in the scrub. The three strangers thought to be sick lie there.

## Faith

The villagers believe in the voice of the **Great Forest** and in the spirits of nature. The city's teaching is hardly spoken of here. The charms on the doors are carved by the village elders.

## What the villagers tell

If the characters talk with villagers at the well, at the inn or in the bread queue, they hear the following:

- Three strangers lie in the cabin outside the village: two halflings and a tiefling. The village took them there by its own decision; no one ordered it.
- Food is left at the cabin door. No one goes inside.
- When the strangers came to the village, they first stayed at Milo's inn.
- There is a **fourth** stranger in the village and he is not sick: @[Halim](entity:npc/Halim), staying upstairs at @[Goodbarrel's Hearth](entity:location/Goodbarrel's Hearth). The villagers call him *"the man from the city"* and do not know what he does.
- *"No one has died."* The villager who says this looks relieved.

## Who is there

- @[Duran](entity:npc/Duran) — head of the Council of Elders. An old man with calloused hands who talks while looking at the village road.
- @[Umay](entity:npc/Umay) — the half-elf woman who has tended the village's sick for forty years. She never lacks the smell of vinegar.
- @[Corvin](entity:npc/Corvin) — a man who lives in the village, goes down to the shore carrying loads on his back, and knows the roads. He wants his fee in advance. He is not always in the village; he stops by from time to time.
- @[Milo Goodbarrel](entity:npc/Milo Goodbarrel) — the innkeeper. Repeats out loud every sentence heard in the common room.
- @[Halim](entity:npc/Halim) — the stranger staying upstairs at the inn, **not a villager.** The @[Border and Trade Guild](entity:lore/Border and Trade Guild) sent him to look into the situation: he will look, go back, and report. He does not give his name or who sent him the first time he is asked.
mapping.secrets:
**The three strangers brought the sickness.** All three came from @[the Beyond](entity:location/Vorstrand), entered the continent through @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor) without passing through customs, and the last place they could reach was Silverwater. The village is not the source of this sickness.

@[Duran](entity:npc/Duran) knows where the three came from and does not want to say. @[Umay](entity:npc/Umay) touched them and is hiding it.

**The Cabin.** Those in the cabin are about to pass into the last stage; the threshold is written, the moment is the DM's. When they turn, their direction is the village (@[The Dawn Turning](entity:scene/The Dawn Turning)), and whether the village stays standing depends on who stands between the cabin and the village at that moment.

mapping.name: The Cabin
mapping.environment: A one-room cabin outside the village
mapping.description: The cabin outside Silverwater where the three strangers thought to be sick lie. Food is left at the door; no one goes inside.
mapping.description_long:
> Past the village's last house the path enters waist-high scrub and ends in front of a crooked cabin. The walls are thick planks nailed one over another; the gaps are stuffed with moss. On the flat stone in front of the door stands a pot, its lid tied down with a cloth. Fat has congealed on the rim of the pot. No one has touched it.
>
> A cough comes from inside, then a hoarse voice: half a sentence, to whom it is not clear. Then silence. The door's latch is open.

The three strangers Silverwater believes to be sick lie here. The village's rule is simple: food is brought, left in front of the door, and no one goes inside.

## General features

- **Light.** No windows. Light comes in only through the door and the gaps between the planks; with the door closed, it is dim inside.
- **Air.** It is hot and stuffy inside. It smells of sweat, wet straw and iron.
- **Sound.** The planks creak in the wind. The village's sounds cannot be heard from the cabin; nor the cabin's from the village.

## Inside

A single room, and three beds. The beds are not evenly arranged: two side by side against the back wall, the third right beside the door.

- **The two beds by the back wall.** @[Alton Leagallow](entity:npc/Alton Leagallow) and @[Merla Tealeaf](entity:npc/Merla Tealeaf). Both wear a wedding band forged in the same style.
- **The bed beside the door.** @[Kromanna](entity:npc/Kromanna). When someone approaches the door, she tries to sit up.
- **Belongings.** The strangers' clothes lie folded at the foot of the beds. There are no other belongings: no trunk, no letter, no bundle.

## What the three strangers carry

| What | Where | How it is found |
|---|---|---|
| Clothes | On them and at the foot of the beds | Whoever looks sees. A tightly woven cloth not woven on this continent, dyed with a dye unknown on this continent |
| A purse of gold | At Alton's waist | Whoever looks sees. The purse is full |
| A few scrolls | In the inner pocket of Merla's clothes | Whoever looks sees. The scrolls are all blank |
| A ring | In the hidden pocket of Kromanna's clothes | Searching her and **Investigation DC 15**. See @[The Sealless Ring](entity:trinket/The Sealless Ring) |

There is nothing else. If the characters look for other belongings, they will not find any.

## Entering the cabin

Every character who enters the cabin makes an **exposure** roll: **CON DC 12**, +1 Sickness Score on a failure. Touching a sick person or their fluids and spending a night in the cabin are separate exposures. The rule: @[Blight — Infection](entity:curse/Blight — Infection).

The conversation in the cabin and the traces that can be found: @[Questioning at the Cabin](entity:scene/Questioning at the Cabin).
mapping.secrets:
**All three are about to pass into the last stage.** They have reached the end of their sickness; no one knows when they will turn. When they turn: @[The Dawn Turning](entity:scene/The Dawn Turning).

The bed closest to the door is Kromanna's, because she is the two halflings' servant and protector.

mapping.name: Goodbarrel's Hearth
mapping.description: Silverwater's only inn. In the evenings half the village sits by the hearth.
mapping.description_long:
> When you open the door the heat hits your face. In the common room on the ground floor a stone hearth is burning, and a pot bubbles on the hook above it. Villagers sit at half of the six tables; muddy boots have been left to dry in front of the hearth. The room smells of fried onions and wet wool. Behind the counter, on a high stool, a halfling wipes mugs and repeats once more, out loud, in their own words, every sentence they hear from the tables.
>
> Seeing you, they toss the cloth over a shoulder. *"A bed, or a meal?"*

It is not really an inn but a two-story house that became an inn over time. Its owner is @[Milo Goodbarrel](entity:npc/Milo Goodbarrel). Because few travelers come, the rooms are empty most nights; the common room, though, fills up every evening.

## The common room

A low-ceilinged room with thick beams. The stone hearth is on the north wall; there are six tables and two long benches. Bundles of dried herbs and two sets of antlers hang on the walls. The counter faces the door; on the shelf behind it stand mugs, a barrel of beer and a barrel of cider.

In the evenings the table by the hearth belongs to the elders. If a stranger sits there no one says anything, but after a while those at the table move to another one.

## Upstairs

Two rooms reached by a narrow staircase. Each room has two beds, a chest and a basin. The windows look out on the village road.

**One of the two rooms is taken.** @[Halim](entity:npc/Halim) is staying there — he came before the characters, paid in advance, and he is the village's only **healthy** stranger.

## The stable

Behind the house, a stable for three horses. The straw is fresh.

## Prices

| | |
|---|---|
| Bed and two meals | **4 sp** / night |
| Meal only | **3 cp** |
| Stable | **1 sp** / night |

Milo does not haggle and does not lower prices, but writes up debts. Since little money circulates in the village, this is ordinary business.

## What is learned here

- **What the village is talking about.** Sitting in the common room and listening requires no roll; Milo repeats what is heard out loud anyway.
- **Comings and goings.** Milo remembers who came, how many nights they stayed and who paid. If asked, Milo tells.
- **The fourth stranger.** Most evenings @[Halim](entity:npc/Halim) sits in the common room, **at the table closest to the door**, and listens. He takes no notes; he asks about what was told again and again, then memorizes it. It is clear he is not a villager; whose man he is, is not.
mapping.secrets:
**The three strangers spent their first two nights in the village here**; they were moved to the cabin afterward. Milo was the first to see the foreign cloth of their clothes. Milo saw the money too: the three paid for their rooms **in advance, without haggling and more than enough**.

Milo has nothing to hide, and the common room is a door that always stands open: sitting by the hearth requires no roll.

mapping.name: Hidden Harbor
mapping.description: The way out of Meridia without passing through customs: a three-pier harbor hidden behind the cliffs.
mapping.description_long:
> The road winds down between two cliffs and suddenly opens out. Below, in a narrow cove sheltered from the wind, three crooked piers reach into the sea. Boats of every size are moored at the piers, and none of them flies a flag from its mast. Smoke rises from the chimneys of wooden shacks leaning against the shore. The wind carries up the smell of salt, tar and incense. On the face of the cliff, a man's height up, old half-worn symbols have been carved.
>
> No gate, no guard, no sign. Someone sitting on a barrel at the bottom of the road starts watching you while you are still halfway down.

A cove on the coast whose location is not told. Everyone who wants to leave or enter Meridia without passing through the @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr) customs comes through here. Where the ships put in and the business turns is @[The Wharf](entity:location/The Wharf).

## People and names

Everyone here has come from somewhere else: debtors, fugitives, sailors who lost their ships, people who want to leave their names behind. No one says the name they were born with. Everyone is called by a nickname, a trade name or the name of their ship: Twine, Mouse, Velvet. The only person without a nickname is @[Captain Caelynn](entity:npc/Captain Caelynn).

**Not everything here is recorded, only goods.** The harbor is not like the city: the ledger writes down which ship brought what, unloaded what and paid what. Who came, who stood guarantor for whom, is not written.

## Getting in

**No one is let in without a guarantor.** A newcomer is accepted in one of three ways:

1. Someone inside stands guarantor for them.
2. They do a job for someone inside.
3. They come with a real load to sell.

Money is not discussed at this stage. See @[Admitted to the Harbor](entity:scene/Admitted to the Harbor).

## Getting out

There are two ways to board a ship: a **good writ** or **good money**.

- **Good money** is far more than a traveler carries in their purse. It is earned by working at the harbor, selling goods or taking over someone's debt.
- **A good writ** is a passage paper carrying the countersignature of a seat in the Assembly. It is not found at the harbor; it is brought from @[Lucid Triton](entity:location/Lucid Triton).

Bargaining and the captains: @[Bargaining for Passage](entity:scene/Bargaining for Passage).

## Order

No chief, no flag. Business is run by a few people; their word counts, because breaking their word costs everyone dearly. The only law is spoken: @[The Harbor Compact](entity:lore/The Harbor Compact).

## Magic and faith

No one here asks about a magic license. Rare spell components enter the continent through here. In the nooks of the shacks incense is burned and old symbols are carved into the rocks: for the sailors' forgotten god, **blind luck**.

## Who is there

- @[Twine](entity:npc/Twine) — the gnome who keeps the harbor's goods ledger. The ledger in their lap is wider than they are.
- @[Mouse](entity:npc/Mouse) — the barefoot halfling apprentice. She sees everything that happens on the wharf.
- @[Captain Caelynn](entity:npc/Captain Caelynn) — the captain of the clean and expensive voyage.
- @[Captain Holg](entity:npc/Captain Holg) — the captain of the cheap and bad voyage.
- @[Velvet](entity:npc/Velvet) — the best-dressed man on the wharf. His hands have never held a load. The visible proof that a guild has a hand in the harbor.
- @[Enamel](entity:npc/Enamel) — the dwarf jeweler with a workbench in a back room.
mapping.secrets:
**The Council knows about this harbor and partly uses it.** Some guild members move contraband through here. That is why no one is afraid if the characters threaten the harbor with the Council.

**The three strangers came through here.** Had they come through Elymsyr, their names would be in the customs ledger. They were brought by a ship called the **Fate**. Their names are not at the harbor either, because people are not written here.

**No one knows the captain's name.** At the harbor no one says the name they were born with; that captain was known by the name of the ship. **After that night the Fate never put in again.** The only person who knew where the three strangers came from has gone out to sea, and the trail goes cold here.

**Who knows.** The harbor's location is not common knowledge, but it is not a secret either: some Council officials, some members of @[The Council and the Guild Assembly](entity:lore/The Council and the Guild Assembly), and very rarely the paladin officers of the @[Order of the Silver Shield](entity:lore/Order of the Silver Shield) know the way. @[Silverwater](entity:location/Silverwater) does not know — the village's trade with the outside runs through @[Corvin](entity:npc/Corvin), and the villagers do not ask where the goods come from.

Corvin knows the way to the harbor, because he carried goods from here and still does. **When he dies, no one in the village will be left who knows that way**; the harbor can still be found, but the way to it then goes through Lucid Triton.

@[Enamel](entity:npc/Enamel) filed off the seal face of @[The Sealless Ring](entity:trinket/The Sealless Ring) in her own back room, and struck no stamp on it — no one here signs anything.

The real name of @[Velvet](entity:npc/Velvet) is **Halet Custar**. This is not revealed in Act 1.

mapping.name: The Wharf
mapping.description: The piers of Hidden Harbor: boats without flags, loads marked in chalk, day wages paid in the evening.
mapping.description_long:
> Three wooden piers reach out into the sea, and none of them is straight; the planks flex under your feet and green water shows between them. There is no crane: loads come down by rope, by hook and by shoulder. Boats of every size are moored, from a fishing skiff to a two-masted cargo ship. There are no stamps on the barrels and crates; there are arrows, crosses and numbers drawn in chalk. The ropes creak. Someone shouts a price, someone else a lower one.
>
> A few workers on the pier look at you without stopping their work. A barefoot halfling child sitting on a barrel stops swinging her legs.

The working face of @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor). The ships put in here, the loads change hands here, most of the day is spent here.

## General features

- **The piers.** Three piers; the longest is forty paces. Some of the planks are rotten and patched. No lanterns are lit at night.
- **Loads.** Barrels, bales, crates. None of them stamped; their owners mark them in chalk and the chalk washes off with every rain.
- **Smell.** Salt, tar, fish guts and wet hemp.
- **Shacks.** At the foot of the piers, wooden shacks leaning against the cliff: a tavern, a storehouse, a net mender.

## What is done here

- **Day labor.** No one asks the name of whoever carries loads; they are paid in cash in the evening. A day's work earns a traveler one night's meal. Earning ship's fare takes weeks of work.
- **Watching the ships.** Which ship put in when, which night it was loaded, can be seen from here. @[Mouse](entity:npc/Mouse) remembers all of it.
- **Rumors.** Rumors are plentiful on the wharf and generally true.

## The rule

Word of whoever starts a fight on the wharf spreads through the whole harbor (@[The Harbor Compact](entity:lore/The Harbor Compact)). That is why voices rise here, but knives are not drawn.

## Who is there

The ships of @[Captain Caelynn](entity:npc/Captain Caelynn) and @[Captain Holg](entity:npc/Captain Holg) are moored at the piers. Most days @[Velvet](entity:npc/Velvet) stands at the head of a crate reading his papers. @[Mouse](entity:npc/Mouse) watches the whole wharf from the top of a barrel.
mapping.secrets: Someone who carries a cargo hook and knows how to use it is hired without questions (@[Dockworker](entity:background/Dockworker)). The workers do not talk to a newcomer on the first day; they talk on the second.

mapping.name: Lucid Triton
mapping.description: The capital of Meridia: white marble facades, avenues lined with trees of colored leaves, the Guild Assembly.
mapping.description_long:
> From afar the city looks white, and the closer you get, the whiter it is. The marble facades throw back the noon sun and you squint. Trees with red, orange and purple leaves have been planted on both sides of the broad avenues; the fallen leaves lie on the white stone like colored stains. In the square rises a stone statue of an architect, and on its pedestal only a name and a trade are written.
>
> The crowd is large, but the noise is little. People walk with papers in their hands and wait in line in front of doors. Somewhere a seal comes down on wood with a dull thud. The official at the city gate opens a ledger and asks you not what you want, but on whose behalf you have come.

The capital of Meridia, and the continent's largest city. Most of the people are human. Its official name is **Lucidum Triton**, but no one uses that name.

## What the city lives on

Lucid Triton produces very little. The continent's business is approved here: passage papers, licenses, assay stamps, guild permits. The city's wealth comes from the fees for these papers. The goods go through @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr); the goods' paper comes here. The share the city consumes itself is carried upstream by the barges of the Golden River and delivered at the foot of the wall (@[River Loading Yard](entity:location/River Loading Yard)); this is a delivery, not transit — no goods pass through the city and move on.

## The people

In the city there are people with two names and people with one. The second name shows belonging to a house or a guild; those with one name serve. No one openly looks down on anyone. Rising is possible and really happens. See @[The Steps of Service](entity:lore/The Steps of Service).

## The look of the city

- **Marble and trees.** The buildings do not climb to the sky; they are two or three stories, but the stonework is flawless. Every avenue has trees with colored leaves.
- **Statues.** There are no statues of gods in the squares. There are architects, engineers and soldiers whose names are unknown.
- **Lanterns.** At night all the avenues are lit with lanterns. The lamplighters make the same round every evening; a lantern gone out is counted a bad sign and is relit before morning.
- **Ceremony.** There is no temple in the city, but there is plenty of ceremony: naming, enrollment as an apprentice, the transfer of a seal.

## Magic

Casting magic within city limits requires a **Guild License** (@[Wizards' Guild](entity:lore/Wizards' Guild)). Someone who casts divine magic is seen not as working a miracle but as committing an irregularity — but no one in this city has ever seen such a thing. Many have heard of it, no one has seen it (@[The Gods and the Whisper](entity:lore/The Gods and the Whisper)).

## The city's important places

- @[Assembly House](entity:location/Assembly House) — the Guild Assembly's building; inside it the @[Assembly Hall](entity:location/Assembly Hall) and the @[Hall of Seals](entity:location/Hall of Seals).
- @[The Chancery](entity:location/The Chancery) — behind the Assembly; inside it the @[Hall of Records](entity:location/Hall of Records) and the @[Countersign Desk](entity:location/Countersign Desk).
- @[Border and Trade Guild Council Chamber](entity:location/Border and Trade Guild Council Chamber) — in the trade quarter; tonnage, customs copies, a signatory room. The guild of @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar).
- @[Wizards' Guild Academy](entity:location/Wizards' Guild Academy) — the license desk, the teleportation register, the testing room.
- @[Healers' Barracks](entity:location/Healers' Barracks) — licenses, potions and declarations of cause of death. The apprentice @[Sindri](entity:npc/Sindri) is here.
- @[Upper Market](entity:location/Upper Market) — the licensed market and the assay table. The assay master @[Kildrak Ferrun](entity:npc/Kildrak Ferrun) is here.
- @[Lower Market](entity:location/Lower Market) — the foot of the wall: repairs, secondhand goods, debts passed on. @[Lamp](entity:npc/Lamp)'s stall is here.
- @[Architects' Square](entity:location/Architects' Square) — the main square; the statue, the lanterns, the ceremonies.
- @[City Gates](entity:location/City Gates) — where entry is written down. @[Sergeant Krusk](entity:npc/Sergeant Krusk) is the sergeant of the night patrol.
- @[Silent Street](entity:location/Silent Street) — the street of those who honor the old gods; in no district ledger.
- @[River Loading Yard](entity:location/River Loading Yard) — the barges of the Golden River, the weighbridge, and the wall.
- @[Bargemen's Inn](entity:location/Bargemen's Inn) — the bargemen's inn, at the edge of the loading yard.

## Politics

The city is governed in the Council's name by the **Guild Assembly**: six seats, five houses, one appointment. Decisions are made before the session, behind closed doors; in session they are only announced. A seat holder who wants to object does not come to the session. See @[The Council and the Guild Assembly](entity:lore/The Council and the Guild Assembly).
mapping.secrets:
**The sickness has not reached the city yet; the news of it has.** The Assembly's six seats are silencing the news in six different ways. Few in the streets talk about the sickness.

There is a document that shows the city knows: a copy of the sickness's first declaration is with @[Sindri](entity:npc/Sindri). The declarations were changed on the orders of @[Chief Physician — Caramip Kalender](entity:npc/Chief Physician — Caramip Kalender).

**The three strangers' trail never reached this city.** Since they did not pass through customs, they have no line in any city ledger. If the characters search here they will find nothing, and finding nothing is information: these three people entered the continent off the record.

mapping.name: Hall of Seals
mapping.environment: A long hall with high windows
mapping.description: The room in Lucid Triton where decisions are sealed. The only sounds are paper and seals.
mapping.description_long:
> A long room; the windows are so high that only the sky can be seen through them. The desks are set in two rows, and on each desk is an open ledger, a wax burner and a seal box with its lid raised. No one speaks. Paper is turned; now and then a seal comes down on hot wax and a dull thud carries to the end of the room. The air smells of melted red wax and lamp oil.
>
> The clerk at the desk beside the door holds out a hand without looking up. Waiting for your paper.

Decisions announced in the @[Assembly Hall](entity:location/Assembly Hall) come here and are sealed. A decision that has not received its seal has not yet come into force.

## The hall

- **The desks.** Two rows of desks; at each a clerk and a seal box.
- **Wax burners.** On each desk, a copper cup that melts wax over a small lamp. That is why the room is always warm.
- **The back wall.** A cabinet of pigeonholes where sealed papers wait. The cabinet's key is on the head clerk's belt.

The clerk who seals a decision writes in the ledger in which guild's name they sealed it. If a seal has come down on the desk, that decision counts as given by that guild.
mapping.secrets: A decision announced in the Assembly may never arrive here. If a seat holder does not want a decision sealed, the paper is held up on the way. In the Assembly no one openly says *no*; the paper just never reaches this room.

mapping.name: Assembly Hall
mapping.description: The cool stone hall where the Guild Assembly's six seats sit in a half circle.
mapping.description_long:
> A cool hall with a high ceiling. Six heavy wooden seats are arranged in a half circle. On the wall behind five of them hangs a house's sign: a hammer, a scale, a compass, a sword, a key. The back of the sixth seat is bare stone. Facing the seats is a low wooden railing where petitioners stand; the railing is polished where hands hold it. It smells of stone and wax. Every sound hangs under the ceiling for a while.
>
> At the lectern beside the railing a clerk asks your name, writes it down, lifts the pen and waits.

The hall where @[The Council and the Guild Assembly](entity:lore/The Council and the Guild Assembly) meets. Petitioners stand behind the railing and the clerk reads out their names in turn.

## The seats

From left to right:

| Seat | Guild | Sign on the wall |
|---|---|---|
| @[Rector — Quarion](entity:npc/Rector — Quarion) | Wizards' Guild | None; bare stone |
| @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar) | Border and Trade Guild | A key |
| @[Head Journeyman — Adrik Ferrun](entity:npc/Head Journeyman — Adrik Ferrun) | Smithing and Labor Guild | A hammer |
| @[Chief Physician — Caramip Kalender](entity:npc/Chief Physician — Caramip Kalender) | Alchemy and Healers' Guild | A scale |
| @[Registrar — Valen Custar](entity:npc/Registrar — Valen Custar) | Military Law Guild | A sword |
| @[Master of the Board — Perhun Mizan](entity:npc/Master of the Board — Perhun Mizan) | Architecture and Planning Guild | A compass |

## How a session works

The clerk reads the petitioner's name, the petitioner speaks, the seat holders answer. No vote is held. Decisions were made before the session; in session they are only said. If a seat holder is against a decision, they do not come to the session that day.

The characters' session here: @[The Assembly Session](entity:scene/The Assembly Session).
mapping.secrets:
Five of the seats see the sickness through their own guild's interest; even if the characters come here with proof, these attitudes do not change easily. What can really be heard here is why each of them says no.

@[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar) has an offer in hand: @[The Offer at the Door](entity:scene/The Offer at the Door).

mapping.name: Countersign Desk
mapping.environment: A desk at the end of a long corridor
mapping.description: The place the people call the Passage Court. The passage paper is collected here: name and details written, preliminary approval given. Its countersignature is given in the guild's signatory rooms.
mapping.description_long:
> A long, windowless corridor; the light of the wall lamps drops yellow rings on the stone floor. At the end of the corridor, a single desk, and in front of the desk a line moving slowly forward. Everyone waiting in line has a paper in hand, and no one folds their paper. On the corner of the desk sits a pile waiting for signatures; the edges of the papers at the bottom have yellowed. The clerk signs one paper, slides the next to the bottom of the pile without reading it. The scratch of the pen carries to the head of the corridor.
>
> The man in front of you coughs, looks about to say something, but stays silent. It is your turn.

The place the people call the **Passage Court**. The passage paper of the @[Border and Trade Guild](entity:lore/Border and Trade Guild) sets out on its road from this desk. In the harbors, a countersigned passage paper is called a **good writ**. Someone carrying a good writ can board a ship both in @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr) and at @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor).

## How it works

The passage paper is collected from this desk, and it is collected under a name: the clerk writes the name and all the details on the paper, enters the paper in the countersignature ledger and signs it. This is called **preliminary approval**. A paper that has not come out of this desk never comes before any signatory.

What makes the paper official is the **countersignature**, and it is given by one of the guild's **signatories** (@[The Council and the Guild Assembly](entity:lore/The Council and the Guild Assembly)). For this, the paper is taken to a **signatory room**. If the paper has any places left blank, the signatory fills them in, and signs.

## The signatory rooms

The rooms that countersign the passage paper of the @[Border and Trade Guild](entity:lore/Border and Trade Guild) are in three places; it makes no difference which one you go to:

- @[Assembly House](entity:location/Assembly House) — the most crowded.
- @[Border and Trade Guild Council Chamber](entity:location/Border and Trade Guild Council Chamber) — in the city's trade quarter, in the guild's own house; its signatory is @[Signatory — Selvi](entity:npc/Signatory — Selvi).
- @[Customs House](entity:location/Customs House) — in @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr), right by the ships.

The clerk says *no* to no one. A paper the clerk does not want to sign waits in the pile, and the pile never gets smaller.

## The desk

An oak desk, and on it an inkwell, three pens, a sand shaker and the countersignature ledger. Behind the clerk's chair, in a locked cabinet, stand the old ledgers.

The clerk at the desk: @[Corin Sancar](entity:npc/Corin Sancar).
mapping.secrets:
**The wait for preliminary approval is shortened with bribes.** This is the place on the continent where the most bribes are paid. The clerk says *no* to no one; a paper the clerk does not want to sign waits in the pile, and the pile never gets smaller.

**The man who favored the clerk with this desk is @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar).** @[Corin Sancar](entity:npc/Corin Sancar) sits here not because he earned it but because of his name — and he knows it. For characters who use Orvan's name, this is both a key and something that breaks Corin.

See @[In Line at the Passage Court](entity:scene/In Line at the Passage Court).

mapping.name: Assembly House
mapping.description: The Guild Assembly's building: the petition courtyard, the clerks' rooms, the six guilds' own offices and two halls.
mapping.description_long:
> The moment you enter the courtyard the sound changes: the noise of the avenue outside stays behind the gate, and in its place come the scratch of pens, the shuffle of shoes, and now and then the name a clerk calls out. The courtyard is arcaded on three sides; under the arches people sit in rows, all with papers in their laps. The marble floor is worn hollow where the petition line stands. A clerk steps into the middle of the courtyard and reads out a name, no one stands, and the clerk reads the name once more.
>
> Of the two doors at the far end of the courtyard, one is open, one closed. The clerk beside the open one looks up from a list at you.

The city's government building. Inside, each of the six guilds has its own office: its own clerk, its own ledger, its own waiting line. Everyone who comes to the building first says which guild's business they are doing; only then do they join the line.

## The building

- **The petition courtyard.** Arcaded on three sides, open to the sky. Business is waited for here.
- **The guild offices.** The rooms around the courtyard. On each door the guild's sign: hammer, scale, compass, sword, key — and on one door no sign.
- **The signatory room.** Behind the door marked with the key, the room where the passage papers of the @[Border and Trade Guild](entity:lore/Border and Trade Guild) are countersigned. The most crowded of the guild's three signatory rooms (@[Countersign Desk](entity:location/Countersign Desk)).
- **@[Assembly Hall](entity:location/Assembly Hall)** — the hall where the six seats meet.
- **@[Hall of Seals](entity:location/Hall of Seals)** — the long room where decisions are sealed.

The building is the *front* of the Assembly; the place where people and passage are written down is @[The Chancery](entity:location/The Chancery) behind it.
mapping.secrets:
Decisions are not made in this building. They are made before the session, in rooms that do not look out on this courtyard; in the hall they are only said (@[The Council and the Guild Assembly](entity:lore/The Council and the Guild Assembly)).

Someone who stands in the courtyard for a long time may notice something: some of the names the clerks read out never get an answer and are not read again. Those names are not in the line; they are being held outside it — this building's counterpart to the pile at the @[Countersign Desk](entity:location/Countersign Desk).

mapping.name: The Chancery
mapping.environment: A two-story stone building behind the Assembly
mapping.description: The small building assigned to the back of the Assembly House: people are written into the ledger here, the paper to leave the continent is written here.
mapping.description_long:
> In the narrow street behind the Assembly, a two-story building left in shadow. Its facade is plain, its door a single leaf, and the threshold worn down in the middle. Inside it smells of ink and wet paper; from the hall on the first floor comes a child's voice and, behind it, the low murmur of a crowd. The only sound from the other end of the corridor is the scratch of a pen.
>
> The official at the door does not stop you, only asks: *"To be written, or for a signature?"*

The people give this building no name; they say the name of the desk they went to. Saying *"I was written at the Chancery"* means entering the ledger; saying *"I went up to the Court"* means waiting for a passage paper.

## The building

- **@[Hall of Records](entity:location/Hall of Records)** — the first floor. A person's name and line are opened here.
- **@[Countersign Desk](entity:location/Countersign Desk)** — at the end of the long corridor on the ground floor. The people call it the **Passage Court**.
- **The old ledgers.** In the locked room on the upper floor, arranged by year. The key is with the head clerk.

Both of the city's procedures of @[The Banner Register](entity:lore/The Banner Register) are carried out in this building: opening a line and countersigning a line.
mapping.secrets:
In this city a person begins in the same building and leaves from the same building. Do not say this when you put the card on the table; the player will see it for themselves when they leave the @[Hall of Records](entity:location/Hall of Records) and enter the corridor.

The old ledgers upstairs also hold the provincial copies. The copy of a line being kept in two places (@[The Banner Register](entity:lore/The Banner Register)) makes this room a target later on; in Act 1 no one tries to get in here.

mapping.name: Hall of Records
mapping.environment: A ceremonial hall with high windows
mapping.description: The hall where a child is named and at the same moment written into the ledger. In this city the two are a single act.
mapping.description_long:
> The hall is crowded and hot. The light falling from the high windows lands on the long table in the middle and on the open ledger on top of it. A family stands in front of the table; the child in the woman's arms is crying and no one tries to quiet it. The clerk reads the four boxes out loud: name, house, guild and rank, guarantor. The clerk stops at the third box, looks at the family, and leaves that box empty.
>
> Lifts the pen. *"Guarantor?"*

On this continent, registration does not come with birth; it comes with **surety** (@[The Banner Register](entity:lore/The Banner Register)). Naming and entering the ledger happen on the same day, in the same hall, and the people do not count them as separate things. To say a person *"has a name"* is to say *"is in the ledger"*.

## The hall

- **The long table and the open ledger.** A line is four boxes: name · house · guild and rank · guarantor.
- **The waiting benches.** Wooden benches where families sit. Polished along the wall, at shoulder height.
- **The guarantor's lectern.** The low lectern where the guarantor says their name. Whoever stands guarantor also carries the debts of the one they vouch for.

If the house box is empty, the person is sealless. If the guarantor box is empty, **the line is never opened.**
mapping.secrets:
Halfling and dwarf surnames do not count as houses; the ledger writes them as *"single name + empty house"*. The trio's false identity fits exactly into this gap (@[Alton Leagallow](entity:npc/Alton Leagallow) · @[Merla Tealeaf](entity:npc/Merla Tealeaf)) — there is no record to check.

In this hall a character can ask for their own line. Someone with the @[Archivist](entity:background/Archivist) or @[Guild Member](entity:background/Guild Member) background sees their own guarantor's name there; a @[Guild Scion of Rank](entity:background/Guild Scion of Rank) sees their family's seal in the house box. An unregistered character finds nothing here, and finding nothing is this hall's real lesson.

location.source_name: Border and Trade Guild Council Chamber

mapping.name: Border and Trade Guild Council Chamber
mapping.description: The main building of the Border and Trade Guild. The oldest seal, the most neglected building.
mapping.description_long:
> The stone key relief above the door is worn, but because it was carved deep it can still be read. Inside it is cold; there is no fire in the hearth and the spines of the volumes on the shelves have swollen with damp. A clerk at the foot of the stairs fills in a register on one knee — there is no desk. A creak of wood comes from upstairs and a door closes.
>
> The clerk speaks without looking up from the register: *"Tonnage, or passage?"*

The headquarters of the @[Border and Trade Guild](entity:lore/Border and Trade Guild), in the city's trade quarter. Customs registers, tonnage ledgers, grain prices and copies of the cargo lists coming from @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr) are gathered here.

## The building

- **The register room.** The copies of the lists from Elymsyr, arranged by year and ship.
- **The grain office.** The room where the price is written; here the price of the city's bread is an import line.
- **The signatory room.** Passage papers are countersigned here too; this is the business the clerk means by *"passage?"* (@[Countersign Desk](entity:location/Countersign Desk)). Its signatory is @[Signatory — Selvi](entity:npc/Signatory — Selvi); the room is the quietest of the city's three signatory rooms.
- **Upstairs.** The seat holder's room. If @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar) is not in the Assembly, he is here.

This guild's income comes from flow, not property. As the ships grow rarer, the building ages along with them: the Assembly's oldest seal sits in its least cared-for building.
mapping.secrets:
**Elymsyr's governor copies are in this building.** The @[Customs Governor](entity:npc/Customs Governor) writes loads that were unloaded short as complete in the ledger; that ledger's second copy is in the register room. Someone who knows how to read it (@[Archivist](entity:background/Archivist)) can compare what each ship brought and what it unloaded.

The signature that sat @[Corin Sancar](entity:npc/Corin Sancar) at the @[Countersign Desk](entity:location/Countersign Desk) came out of this building. The characters can learn this here too; Corin himself will also tell it, but in a different voice.

mapping.name: Wizards' Guild Academy
mapping.description: The Wizards' Guild's academy: the license desk, the teleportation register and the testing room.
mapping.description_long:
> As soon as you pass through the garden gate the air changes — a few degrees cooler, and smelling of chalk dust and burnt herbs. In the courtyard a group of students kneels around a ring drawn in chalk; the stone inside the ring is not wet but gives off steam. A master raises a hand, the students draw back, and the ring goes out.
>
> The clerk at the desk beside the entrance turns the ledger toward you. The page is blank. *"Your name, and what you will do."*

The academy of the @[Wizards' Guild](entity:lore/Wizards' Guild). The Assembly's sixth seat comes from here, and that seat is **without a house** — the Assembly appoints it. The guild's power is not in property but in the record it keeps: who is permitted to cast magic, and who goes where.

## The building

- **The license desk.** Casting magic within the city requires a **Guild License**. Unlicensed magic is the crime of "threatening public safety", and the crime is written up by the @[Military Law Guild](entity:lore/Military Law Guild) — so an unlicensed caster ends up in debt to two guilds at once.
- **The teleportation register.** Long-distance teleportation goes only through this guild. Keeping the register is not a formality but the service itself: who goes where is kept in this ledger.
- **The testing room.** A windowless stone room marked with chalk lines. What a thing is, is tested here.
- **The library.** A character with the @[Magic Guild Student](entity:background/Magic Guild Student) background can enter here; every opening is recorded.

Necromancy and Enchantment involving mind control are not opened even with a license.
mapping.secrets:
**The test was done.** Behind the sentence @[Rector — Quarion](entity:npc/Rector — Quarion) says in the Assembly, *"no detection spell showed anything"*, there is a record in this room, and the record does not say "nothing" — it says **"could not be read"**. The paper is there; the result column has been left blank.

A character can learn this through library rights or by pressing Quarion. What they get when they learn it is not the sickness's name, but the fact that the Assembly's strongest denial is **ignorance**.

mapping.name: Healers' Barracks
mapping.description: The building where the apprentices of the Alchemy and Healers' Guild live. Licenses, potions and declarations of cause of death pass through here.
mapping.description_long:
> A long stone building; even with the door open it is dim inside. The corridor is full of the smell of vinegar, boiled cloth and a sweetish herb, and the smell settles on you. An apprentice edges past sideways carrying bottles stacked one on another, stops on seeing you and leans an elbow against the wall so as not to drop the bottles. From the back yard comes the sound of a copper vessel striking stone.
>
> The apprentice looks at you from behind the bottles. *"Are you sick, or do you need a paper?"*

The apprentice dormitory and apothecary of the @[Alchemy and Healers' Guild](entity:lore/Alchemy and Healers' Guild). The physician's license is granted here, potions are made here, and a death's cause is declared here.

## The building

- **The dormitory.** The apprentices' ward. @[Sindri](entity:npc/Sindri) works here and sleeps here.
- **The apothecary.** The room where licensed potions are made. The reason healing potions are scarce is not money but the **license**.
- **The declaration office.** The desk where declarations of cause of death are written. Each declaration is made out in two copies.

The licensed physicians who could make the @[Sherbet of Resistance](entity:adventuring-gear/Sherbet of Resistance) on this continent belong to this guild.
mapping.secrets:
**A copy of the sickness's first declaration is in this building.** The declarations were changed on the orders of @[Chief Physician — Caramip Kalender](entity:npc/Chief Physician — Caramip Kalender); but a declaration is made out in two copies and the second copy stays in the declaration office.

So the document of what the city knows is here, and the person who could hand it over is an apprentice. @[Sindri](entity:npc/Sindri) does not hand it over easily — the day she does, her license and her bed are gone.

mapping.name: Upper Market
mapping.description: The city's licensed market: marble arches, the assay table, visible police. Expensive, and every sale written in a ledger.
mapping.description_long:
> It is cool under the arches, and as soon as sound enters here it rises: haggling, the clink of a copper scale pan, somewhere three hammer blows in a row. The stalls are set out jumbled — a draper next to a cutler, next to him a woman selling silk purses — but those who do the same work have gathered under the same arch, as if someone had put them there. A license plaque hangs on the corner of every stall.
>
> At the assay table at the foot of the arch a master holds a piece up to the light, then turns it toward you. *"Is it your turn?"*

The city's great market. Selling here requires a license, and a licensed stall is a stall the police protect. The goods are mixed: food, cloth, tools and jewelry are all found together on the same street — but a buyer knows where to look for something, because over time the stalls have clustered on their own.

## The market

- **The assay table.** The table where a metal's fineness is measured and the stamp struck. @[Kildrak Ferrun](entity:npc/Kildrak Ferrun)'s workbench is here.
- **License plaques.** Hanging on every stall. A stall without a plaque is removed within a day.
- **Police.** The @[Smithing and Labor Guild](entity:lore/Smithing and Labor Guild)'s own police stand inside the market; they come quickly, and decide who is in the right by looking at the plaque.

Prices are markedly higher than in the @[Lower Market](entity:location/Lower Market), and buyers come here knowing it: what is bought here has a record.
mapping.secrets:
**Unstamped work cannot be sold here.** A character who takes @[The Sealless Ring](entity:trinket/The Sealless Ring) to a stall in this market cannot make a sale; what they do opens a **question**. @[Kildrak Ferrun](entity:npc/Kildrak Ferrun) reads the piece and says what the lack of a stamp means — but what was read was read at a workbench, and a workbench is a ledger.

If the characters are not careful here, the record of what they are looking for will spread through the city ahead of them.

mapping.name: Lower Market
mapping.environment: A cloth-covered market at the foot of the wall
mapping.description: The market at the foot of the wall: repairs, secondhand goods, debts passed on. Cheap, and most sales have no record.
mapping.description_long:
> In the narrow street at the foot of the wall, the stalls are covered with cloths stretched on ropes, and the light under the cloths turns yellowish. It smells of frying fat, wet wool and soot. A repairer is taking apart the soles of a pair of boots and tossing the pieces into a box beside them; the box is full. Two stalls away a man speaks in a low voice, the one across from him nods, and no money changes hands.
>
> A voice calls to you from under the cloth covers, but you cannot tell which one: *"Whatever you're looking for, we have it. Just don't ask."*

The city's cheap market. Most of what is sold here belonged to someone before. Repairs, secondhand, pawn and debt transfer — all four kinds of business are done at the same stall.

## The market

- **Cloth covers.** There are few fixed shops; most stalls are packed up in the evening.
- **The repairers' row.** The line closest to the foot of the wall. Where something came from is not asked here.
- **Debt transfer.** Taking over someone's debt is done here without writing, and because it is unwritten there is no going back. @[Lamp](entity:npc/Lamp)'s half-empty stall is here.
- **Police.** They come, but they come late. If a crime has no owner, there is no crime (@[Courts of Honor](entity:lore/Courts of Honor)).
mapping.secrets:
**"Good money" is found here.** The money needed for the smuggler's way of @[The Continent on the Horizon](entity:quest/The Continent on the Horizon) is in this market: goods to sell, a day's work, or taking over someone's debt.

@[The Sealless Ring](entity:trinket/The Sealless Ring) can be sold here — no one asks about a stamp. But the ring is the chain's only object (@[Where They Came From](entity:quest/Where They Came From)); the day it is sold, it does not come back. This is not a punishment but a choice: when you put the card on the table, do not remind them what the ring is.

mapping.name: Architects' Square
mapping.description: The city's main square. There are shops around its edge but the square does not belong to them: this is a place of ceremony.
mapping.description_long:
> The square is broad, and quiet for its crowd. The stone statue in the middle shows a man: a compass in his hand, an open drafting board at his feet. There are two lines on the pedestal — a name, and a trade. The lantern posts around the square are set at even intervals; a lamplighter has climbed a post, is wiping the glass with a cloth and saying something to those below, and those below laugh. There are red and orange leaves on the stone, and they have not been swept.
>
> The crowd at the foot of the statue parts: a family stands in the middle, and the child beside them is holding a new apprentice's caftan.

The city's main square and place of ceremony. Naming, enrollment as an apprentice and the transfer of a seal are celebrated here — @[The Chancery](entity:location/The Chancery) does the procedure, the square makes it visible.

## The square

- **The architect's statue.** There are no statues of gods in the squares: there are architects, engineers and soldiers whose names are unknown. On the pedestal only a name and a trade are written.
- **Lantern posts.** The city's lantern discipline starts here. A lantern gone out counts not as neglect but as a bad sign.
- **The edge shops.** The shops facing the square are expensive and most sell ceremonial goods: caftans, candles, sealing wax, gifts.
- **The notice stone.** The flat surface where the Council's proclamations are posted. Every paper posted has a seal in its corner.
mapping.secrets:
**In this city divine magic has been heard of, not seen** (@[The Gods and the Whisper](entity:lore/The Gods and the Whisper)). If a character casts a divine spell here, in this crowd, it is read not as a miracle but as an **irregularity** — and since the square is the most crowded place in the city, the number of witnesses needs no roll.

The punishment for this is not written on the card because its institutional answer is unclear: the @[Wizards' Guild](entity:lore/Wizards' Guild) writes up a license violation, the @[Military Law Guild](entity:lore/Military Law Guild) a crime, and neither knows which of the two this is.

mapping.name: City Gates
mapping.environment: A gate in the wall and guardrooms
mapping.description: The place where entry into the city is written down. By day an official, by night a patrol; each with its own ledger.
mapping.description_long:
> Under the gate arch it is cool even by day, and it smells of horses, stone dust and cold iron. Carts coming in stop for a moment under the arch, the wheels clunk as they drop into the stone channel, then roll on. On the stone bench beside the arch an official sits, shielding the ledger on their knee from the wind with an arm. From above, someone calls something down from the battlements; the official raises a hand in answer without looking up.
>
> The official turns a page of the ledger and asks you not what you want, but **on whose behalf you have come**.

The city's gates. Whoever enters is written down, and what is written is not the person themselves but **on whose behalf they have come**: a guild, a house, a business.

## The gate

- **The day officials.** The bench under the arch. The ledger is kept here, and the carts stop here once.
- **The night patrol.** The round of the streets after the gates are shut. @[Sergeant Krusk](entity:npc/Sergeant Krusk) is the sergeant of this patrol.
- **The guardroom.** The narrow room inside the arch: a hearth, a bench, and a record plaque hanging on the wall.

The paper of a load passing through the gate goes to the @[Border and Trade Guild](entity:lore/Border and Trade Guild), the person's line goes to @[The Chancery](entity:location/The Chancery).
mapping.secrets:
**The night ledger is shorter than the day ledger**, and the reason is not that few people enter at night. Some loads that come in at night are written into the day column — no one writes a lie, the hour just isn't written.

@[Sergeant Krusk](entity:npc/Sergeant Krusk) knows this and does not count it a problem: Krusk's job is who entered, not when. If the characters ask *"who came in on such-and-such night"*, the answer they get will be incomplete, and the incompleteness itself is information.

mapping.name: Silent Street
mapping.environment: A narrow street in an outlying quarter
mapping.description: The street of those who honor the old gods. Not forbidden — unseen: this street is not in the Architecture Guild's district ledger.
mapping.description_long:
> The street is so narrow two people can pass shoulder to shoulder, and there is no sign at its entrance. Inside it smells of candles, dried flowers and damp stone. Small things have been left in the niches in the walls: a slice of dry bread, a ribbon, a handful of salt, a bird's bone. A woman stands before a niche, her lips moving but no sound coming out; she hears you pass and does not turn until she has finished speaking.
>
> The door at the end of the street stands ajar. Inside is not dark — somewhere a candle is burning.

The city address of @[The Silent Shrines](entity:lore/The Silent Shrines). Scraps of ancient gods, the cult of ancestors, nature spirits, blind luck and the Spirit of the Current — they all take the same form here: a niche in a wall, and something left in front of it.

There is no temple here because a temple is a building and a building requires a **permit** (@[Architecture and Planning Guild](entity:lore/Architecture and Planning Guild)). Asking for a permit means being seen. That is why faith has settled not into a building but into the walls of a street.

## The street

- **Wall niches.** Not altars, niches. What is left is taken, and who takes it is not asked.
- **Doors ajar.** The front rooms of some of the houses on the street stay open in the evenings. No invitation, no barrier either.
- **No sign.** The street has no name. When it is described, it is always described as the back of something else.

No one raids this place. @[The Way of Will](entity:lore/The Way of Will) does not count it a threat — it counts it a shortcoming.
mapping.secrets:
**This street is not in the Architecture Guild's ledger of district boundaries.** The records of those who live here are written to the neighboring street. In the world of records this has a single consequence: **someone looked for here cannot be found by address.**

In Act 1 this has no use, and do not force one. If the characters come in here, what they get is not information but a picture of how the city forgets — and for someone who has seen this street, the sentence of @[Master of the Board — Perhun Mizan](entity:npc/Master of the Board — Perhun Mizan), *"this city was planned so that it would not fall sick"*, sounds different.

mapping.name: River Loading Yard
mapping.environment: A pier outside the wall and a weighbridge yard inside it
mapping.description: The area where the Golden River's barges are unloaded. The load waits outside the wall; its paper is written inside.
mapping.description_long:
> At the pier outside the wall the barges are moored side by side, and the wood groans as the ropes tighten. It smells of wet sacks, river mud and hemp. A laborer drops the sack from their back onto the weighbridge pan, the pan shakes, and the clerk at the head of the weighbridge calls out the number and writes it in the ledger. The carts entering through the narrow gate at the foot of the wall stop one by one.
>
> On the part of the wall to the left of the gate, the mortar between the stones has been freshly plastered and the color has not taken. The weighbridge clerk catches your glance and closes the ledger.

@[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr) brings the load into the continent; the barges of the **Golden River** carry the share that falls to the capital upstream. The city still produces nothing — what happens here is **delivery**, not transit.

## The area

- **The pier outside the wall.** The wooden wharf where the barges tie up, and the waiting area. The load stays here through the night.
- **The weighbridge.** At the foot of the wall. Every sack weighed is entered in the ledger, and the number is called out loud.
- **The narrow gate.** The gate through which the load is taken inside the wall; kept separate from the great gates.
- **The yard inside the wall.** The office and the storehouses. The paper goes from here to the @[Border and Trade Guild Council Chamber](entity:location/Border and Trade Guild Council Chamber).
mapping.secrets:
**The wall repairs stayed on paper.** The stretch of wall to the left of the weighbridge looks repaired, but only its face has been plastered; the mortar did not go deep. This wall is the physical counterpart of the sentence @[Master of the Board — Perhun Mizan](entity:npc/Master of the Board — Perhun Mizan) says in the Assembly, *"this city was planned so that it would not fall sick"*.

A character needs no roll to see this, stopping to look is enough; to understand what it is, they need to know the @[Architecture and Planning Guild](entity:lore/Architecture and Planning Guild) or stonework.

**The load spends the night outside the wall.** This is the only place in the city that stays outside the record: inside is written, outside is waiting.

mapping.name: Elymsyr
mapping.environment: A terraced harbor city built at a canyon mouth
mapping.description: Meridia's official seaport, also called Claport. Built over the water and up the slopes at the canyon mouth of the Golden River; the continent's door and face.
mapping.description_long:
> The **Golden River** comes down from the mountains of the east and south, passes below @[Lucid Triton](entity:location/Lucid Triton), and here pours into the sea between two long canyons. The city is built at the river's wide mouth, **on both banks at once**: stone terraces set into the rock, one above another, step by step — and spilling out of the mouth, along the coast. Gnome-made cranes turn on the warehouse roofs, chains rattle, a cargo lift lets off steam with a hiss. The air smells of salt, tar and cloves; half a dozen separate languages are spoken on the wharf and none of them in a whisper.
>
> Looking inland, in the canyon's first kilometers you can see wooden structures nailed to the wall and lifts swaying on ropes. On the towers on both sides of the narrows the guards' spear points glint. A customs official with a writing board walks through the crowd straight toward you.

Meridia's official seaport; its other name is **Claport**. Every spice, cloth, rare ore and fine tool that enters the continent enters here. The noisiest place on the continent.

## How the city is built
