The city is not a coastal city but a **mouth** city: it is built on both banks at once where the river pours into the sea between two long canyons, has spilled out beyond the mouth, and has climbed the canyon wall inland. There is no bridge between the banks; barges come and go.

And the city is **two parts:**

- **The entry structures over the water.** At the river's mouth, piers built on pilings, waiting structures and the customs. A ship puts in here first; no one is written down before going ashore.
- **The terraces on the slope.** Stone buildings built step by step up the mountain's steep face: houses, warehouses, taverns, interpreters' shops, at the very top the governor's palace.

*The part built on the water works, the part built on the rock lives.*

## The gate and the chain

The city's gate is wide and **always open**: closing it would mean cutting off the flow, and in this city when the flow is cut, the first thing cut is the purse of the @[Border and Trade Guild](entity:lore/Border and Trade Guild). On both sides of the narrows, in towers set into the rock, the **River Guard** (*River Wardens*) keep watch — attached to the river and sea arm of the **Iron Legion**; their sergeant is the @[River Guard Sergeant](entity:npc/River Guard Sergeant). The ballistae in the slope emplacements can sink any ship entering the narrows, but they have not been used in a long time and stand under covers: the reason is not maintenance but appearance — a ballista standing in the open frightens the trade network.

The real defense is the heavy iron **chain** lying under the water, tied to giant winches in rooms carved into the rock on both shores. When it is drawn taut, entering the river becomes physically impossible — but the chain **has not been raised in a long time.** It used to be tested a few times a year with an air of ceremony; now the children growing up have never seen it rise. No one forbade the test, and no one asked for it either: on a test day the narrows close, no ship can enter that day, and no one wants to write the accounts for that day.

## The city's parts

- @[Customs House](entity:location/Customs House) — the hall where every load is opened, weighed and written down; the guild's coastal signatory room is here too. See @[The Customs Wharf](entity:scene/The Customs Wharf).
- @[Lower Wharf](entity:location/Lower Wharf) — the warehouses, hangars and gnome cranes on both banks.
- @[Canyon Lifts](entity:location/Canyon Lifts) — the river's first kilometers; the wooden line where goods go up to the inland settlements.
- **The terraces.** Houses, taverns, interpreters' shops built step by step up the slope. On the highest terrace, the governor's palace. On one of the terraces, the @[Military Law Chamber](entity:location/Military Law Chamber) that the @[Military Law Guild](entity:lore/Military Law Guild) is setting up.

## Government

The city is run by the @[Customs Governor](entity:npc/Customs Governor) appointed by the Council and the officials under him. The customs answers to the @[Border and Trade Guild](entity:lore/Border and Trade Guild). A list is drawn up for every load; a copy is sent to @[Lucid Triton](entity:location/Lucid Triton).

**This is the continent's face.** An envoy or merchant from the outside world sees Meridia first in this city; a foreigner who reaches the capital has already been recorded once, weighed once and received once.

**Smuggling is the city's gravest crime.** Its punishment is lifelong hard labor on the river works.

## The people

In the city almost everyone is a dockworker, a rope-maker, an interpreter, a warehouse guard or a customs official. Life turns on the arrival times of the ships. Foreigners are ordinary here. A local saying: *"A guest is welcomed at the door, not in the heart."*

The division of labor has settled along the races, and no one takes it for a rule: **humans** in administration and the army, **gnomes and dwarves** in the upkeep of the cranes, the cargo lifts and the chain, **half-elves** in interpreting and mediation. In the harbor district there are always foreigners staying temporarily — tabaxi, dragonborn, and races whose names are not known here. What is an event in the rest of Meridia is a Tuesday here.

The official teaching is the Way of Will, but sailors show the river a respect older than that: before setting out they throw a piece of **silver** into the water, for the Spirit of the Current. Everyone does it, no one speaks of it.

## Who is there

- @[Customs Governor](entity:npc/Customs Governor) — the man who lives among numbers on the highest terrace, in a room that looks out on the river.
- @[The Governor's Deputy](entity:npc/The Governor's Deputy) — the governor's red-scaled dragonborn deputy; the one who receives a stranger in the courtyard.
- @[River Guard Sergeant](entity:npc/River Guard Sergeant) — the sergeant of the unit that keeps watch in the towers of the narrows.
- @[Crane Master](entity:npc/Crane Master) — the gnome who looks after the wharf's cranes and the canyon lifts.
- @[The Interpreter](entity:npc/The Interpreter) — the half-elf waiting for work at the head of the piers.
- @[Captain — Maren](entity:npc/Captain — Maren) — the captain of the *Honest Scales*; signs on whoever carries a countersigned paper as crew (@[The Continent on the Horizon](entity:quest/The Continent on the Horizon)).
mapping.secrets:
**In Elymsyr the rumor's trace is in the ledger.** Which ship did not arrive, which load was unloaded short, which crew did not go ashore: the customs ledgers tell this to whoever knows how to read them (@[Archivist](entity:background/Archivist)).

The city's three cracks are on three separate cards: the governor's ledger (@[Customs House](entity:location/Customs House)), the neglected chain (this card), and the night unloadings (@[Lower Wharf](entity:location/Lower Wharf)).

**The city does not close.** The gate is always open, the chain always under the water. It looks like negligence; in fact it is a decision — if the flow stops, the @[Border and Trade Guild](entity:lore/Border and Trade Guild) starves.

mapping.name: Customs House
mapping.environment: A broad stone building in the middle of the wharf
mapping.description: The building where every load is opened, counted and written down. The goods stop here; their paper goes to Lucid Triton.
mapping.description_long:
> A guard stands on each side of the door and neither looks at anyone; what they look at is the crates coming through the door. Inside is a single long hall: squares drawn in chalk on the stone floor, a load in each square, an official at the head of each load. The lid of a crate is lifted, the straw inside is raked through by hand, then the lid is nailed back in place. As the pan of the weighbridge at the end of the hall rises and falls its chain jingles, and every number is called out loud and written in the ledger.
>
> An official with a writing board stops in front of you and sets the tip of the pen to the paper: *"Load? Ship? On whose behalf?"*

The heart of @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr). Every load that enters the continent is opened, counted, weighed and written down in this building. The building keeps the ledger of the @[Border and Trade Guild](entity:lore/Border and Trade Guild); the load goes in, the paper goes to @[Lucid Triton](entity:location/Lucid Triton).

## The building

- **The hall.** A floor divided with chalk. A load cannot leave its square until it is cleared, and no one touches another's square.
- **The weighbridge.** At the far end of the hall, a copper pan hanging on a chain. Tonnage comes out here; the fee is calculated from the tonnage.
- **The ledger room.** The hall's side room: cargo lists, crew lists, passage papers. A copy of every list is made and sent upriver by barge.
- **The signatory room.** The coastal signatory room of the @[Border and Trade Guild](entity:lore/Border and Trade Guild). A passage paper collected from the @[Countersign Desk](entity:location/Countersign Desk) can be countersigned here too, just before boarding the ship.
- **The governor's room.** The room upstairs with a single window looking out on the river. The @[Customs Governor](entity:npc/Customs Governor) spends most of the day here, among numbers.

The characters' scene here: @[The Customs Wharf](entity:scene/The Customs Wharf). A countersigned passage paper — in the language of the harbors, a **good writ** — ends arguments in this hall; the place the paper comes from is the @[Countersign Desk](entity:location/Countersign Desk).
mapping.secrets:
**Loads unloaded short are written in the ledger as complete.** The @[Customs Governor](entity:npc/Customs Governor) does this not for himself but for the numbers: a load that comes in short means a fee that comes in short and a bad column going to the Assembly.

This lie shows in only one place: **the weighbridge ledger and the cargo list do not match.** The two are kept in separate rooms and no one puts them side by side. For a character with the @[Archivist](entity:background/Archivist) background this is something readable; for anyone else it is two separate numbers. A bundle of weighbridge slips that does put the two side by side is in the cellar of the @[Military Law Chamber](entity:location/Military Law Chamber) (@[The Masked Job](entity:quest/The Masked Job)).

Smuggling is the city's gravest crime, and its punishment is lifelong hard labor on the river works. No one beats a character caught in this hall — they write it down. What is written is not taken back.

mapping.name: Lower Wharf
mapping.environment: Warehouses and cranes on both banks of the river
mapping.description: The city's working face: warehouses, hangars and gnome cranes on both banks. Work begins before sunrise.
mapping.description_long:
> Warehouses line both banks of the river, and on their roofs gnome-made cranes turn. A cargo lift lets off steam with a hiss, chains rattle, a stack of crates lifts into the air and heads for the upper terrace. Below are the sacks on the laborers' backs, the shouts of the rope-men, and the crews trading jibes on the barges that link the two banks. It smells of salt, tar and cloves.
>
> The half-elf standing at the head of the pier sees you, folds the paper in his hand, tucks it into a pocket and walks toward you — having chosen which language to speak before even hearing what you say.

The working face of @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr), on **both banks** of the river at once. There is no bridge between the banks; barges come and go, and crossing from one bank to the other is not a journey but a fee.

## The wharf

- **Warehouses and hangars.** Kilometers of storehouses along the river. Where a load waits after leaving customs.
- **Cranes and cargo lifts.** Gnome-made, all working, all well kept. The @[Crane Master](entity:npc/Crane Master) looks after them.
- **The head of the pier.** Where the ships tie up, and where those waiting for work stand. @[The Interpreter](entity:npc/The Interpreter) stands here; half a dozen foreign dialects are spoken here and none of them in a whisper. Ships looking for crew are moored here too: like the *Honest Scales* of @[Captain — Maren](entity:npc/Captain — Maren) (@[The Continent on the Horizon](entity:quest/The Continent on the Horizon)).
- **Barges.** Where the load goes up the **Golden River** to the inland settlements and the capital: @[Canyon Lifts](entity:location/Canyon Lifts).

## Who works

The upkeep of the cranes, the cargo lifts and the chain in the narrows is the work of **gnomes and dwarves**; the city's engineering marvels came from their hands. Most of those waiting for work at the head of the pier are **half-elves** — the most sought-after side in interpreting and mediation. On the wharf there are always temporary foreigners who are never written permanently into any ledger: a tabaxi deckhand, a dragonborn foreman, a traveler whose continent no one knows.

Work begins before sunrise and turns on the arrival times of the ships. A foreigner here is not an event — the local saying sums it up: *"A guest is welcomed at the door, not in the heart."*
mapping.secrets:
**Some night unloadings are given a crane.** A load that does not pass through customs can come ashore with the official harbor's own crane, on its own wharf. The @[Crane Master](entity:npc/Crane Master) knows this, because the Crane Master is the one who provides the crane — so that the workshop does not close.

This is the **second carrier** for the question *how do you buy unregistered passage*: the first is @[Twine](entity:npc/Twine) at @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor). Whichever harbor the table goes to, the line does not close. The difference is not the price but the audience: here the job is done at night, on a wharf where a hundred people work.

**The three strangers' trail never came here.** The trio in the cabin did not enter through customs, so they were not written down on this wharf either. There is no line to look for here, and the absence of a line is information.

mapping.name: Canyon Lifts
mapping.environment: Wooden platforms hanging on the canyon wall
mapping.description: The river's first kilometers: wooden structures and lifts built on the canyon wall. Goods go up from here.
mapping.description_long:
> Behind the city the canyon narrows and two walls rise at once. Wooden platforms and narrow walkways have been nailed to the face of the rock, thirty or forty cubits above the water; between them swing ropes, pulleys and lifts working with counterweights. A lift cage, loaded full, creaks as it rises, and the rope-men keep time from below. Down below the river is narrow and green; seen from above, the barges look the size of plates.
>
> A rope-man reaches out and pulls you in from the edge, laughing: *"Look down, go on. Then never look again."*

The river's first kilometers after it opens to the sea. The city is built at the canyon's mouth but **has spilled out beyond the mouth too**, and climbs inland as well: wooden structures hanging on the wall, walkways and lifts.

## What it is for

- **Hauling up.** The goods of the nearby settlements to the north and south do not come by ship; they are hauled up from here. The loads of the barges going upriver are also lightened here.
- **Lifts.** Cages and pulley lines working with counterweights. Their upkeep belongs to the @[Crane Master](entity:npc/Crane Master)'s people, their operation to the **rope-men**.
- **Walkways.** Narrow wooden paths between the platforms. Slippery in the rain, shifting in the wind, and no one runs here with a load.
- **Upriver.** The barges go from here as far as the @[River Loading Yard](entity:location/River Loading Yard) of @[Lucid Triton](entity:location/Lucid Triton).

This is neither the hall of the @[Customs House](entity:location/Customs House) nor a guild market; it is a place left between two records.
mapping.secrets:
**The rope-men have their own ledger.** What rode in which cage is kept not by a guild but on a tally the head rope-man keeps — the only count on the continent with no seal behind it. No one counts this a crime; no one asks for a copy of it either.

The practical consequence: **a load that goes up by lift can reach the inland settlements without ever entering the customs hall.** This is not smuggling but custom — the fee is paid to the rope-man and no one hides anything. If a character notices this, their impression of how tightly the city is controlled changes.

**Last winter a cage fell.** The two rope-men in it died and the event entered no ledger; both of them were unregistered (@[The Banner Register](entity:lore/The Banner Register)). Up above, the pulley of the line that fell still swings empty.

mapping.name: Votumar
mapping.description: The paladin castle of the eastern bay. White limestone walls, a military governorate; the region calls itself the "Unshakable Armor".
mapping.description_long:
> Across the grey water of the bay a white wall rises: walls of limestone, on top of cliffs that drop sheer to the sea. The waves strike the foot of the cliff and their foam leaps halfway up the walls. No other sound comes from atop the walls. The villagers you meet on the road up to the gate greet you with a nod, but do not speak. On either side of the gate, behind tower shields taller than they are, two paladins stand motionless; salt crystals glint on their armor.
>
> The officer at the gate takes the watch ledger from under an arm and raises a hand. Asks your name and on whose behalf you have come.

The paladin castle built in the one deep cove of the eastern bay. The region calls itself the **"Unshakable Armor"**. A mounted courier from @[Lucid Triton](entity:location/Lucid Triton) gets here in 2 days.

## The castle

- **The walls.** Walls of white limestone; on the side facing the sea they rise out of the cliff itself. Catapult emplacements are ranged along the walls.
- **The gate.** There is a single gate from the land; its watch is kept by @[Gate Commander — Nevra](entity:npc/Gate Commander — Nevra). Everyone who passes through the gate has their name written in the watch ledger.
- **The courtyard.** A broad courtyard strewn with sand; in the mornings the paladins drill the shield wall here. During drill a single voice of command is heard, no other sound.
- **The lower levels.** Iron forges carved into the rock. Dwarf masters maintain the catapults, the wall mechanisms and the armor here; the hum of the forges can be felt through the soles of your feet in the courtyard.

## Government

Votumar is a military governorate. All administrative, judicial and military authority rests with the **High Command**. The Council appoints the Lord Commander.

Civil law does not apply in the castle; in its place apply the **Laws of Honor and Oath**. Even a minor crime can be counted *Treason against the Will*.

The castle's paladin company is the @[Order of the Silver Shield](entity:lore/Order of the Silver Shield). Along the bay runs the @[Watchtower Line](entity:location/Watchtower Line).

## The people

The people who serve the castle count themselves **the continent's first guardians**. The most respected are the craftsmen and farmers who help the castle most. Trade is done not for profit but for supply: armor, lasting food, horse fodder. Fishing is done along the shore; there is no open-sea trade.

Humans are the knights and administrators. Dwarves are at the head of the catapults and the iron forges. Dragonborn are the elite of the Coast Watchers.

Here it is shameful to speak loudly. *"Patient as the bay, upright as the castle"* is praise. The fishers quietly leave flowers on the shore and carve runes into the stones to calm the sea's anger; they do it at hours when the knights are not looking.

## Who is there

The office of the High Command is here, but **the Lord Commander has not been in the castle for two months.** He was known as a man who never left the camp; he went to the capital and took only one of his two deputies with him. The remaining deputy is running the castle, the orders come by word of mouth, and the soldiers openly complain about it — that is what is talked about in the courtyard, at the gate and beside the forges.

- @[Deputy Lord Commander — Aren](entity:npc/Deputy Lord Commander — Aren) — has in practice been running the castle for two months. She has the authority, not the orders.
- @[Gate Commander — Nevra](entity:npc/Gate Commander — Nevra) — the officer who never lets go of the watch ledger.
- @[Forgemaster — Torvun](entity:npc/Forgemaster — Torvun) — the dwarf master at the head of the iron forges on the lower levels.
- @[Castle Clerk — Nerion](entity:npc/Castle Clerk — Nerion) — all the castle's ledgers come together on her desk at the end of the day.
- @[The Shore Siblings — Kessa, Bram and Tomas](entity:npc/The Shore Siblings — Kessa, Bram and Tomas) — three siblings of the fishing family on the shore; they bring fish and news to the castle.
- @[Lord Commander — Varhan](entity:npc/Lord Commander — Varhan) — the holder of the office. A man the people love, in flawless armor; at the moment in @[Lucid Triton](entity:location/Lucid Triton).
mapping.secrets:
**@[Lord Commander — Varhan](entity:npc/Lord Commander — Varhan) is the Faceless.** The people and the soldiers alike truly trust him, and that trust has never been shaken.

**Some high-ranking officers sense something wrong.** There are logical errors in the Lord Commander's orders, and his manner is not what it used to be: cold, unfeeling. No one says this out loud. Whoever says it is counted as having slandered a man the people love, and the price of that is honor before rank.

**For the last two months the orders have come verbally.** There is not a single written order from the Lord Commander's hand. @[Gate Commander — Nevra](entity:npc/Gate Commander — Nevra) knows this.

A few people in the castle each separately sense that something is wrong with the Lord Commander, and none of them knows that the others know: @[Deputy Lord Commander — Aren](entity:npc/Deputy Lord Commander — Aren)'s intuition · @[Gate Commander — Nevra](entity:npc/Gate Commander — Nevra)'s empty *order* column · @[Forgemaster — Torvun](entity:npc/Forgemaster — Torvun)'s supply orders that come by word of mouth · the gap @[Castle Clerk — Nerion](entity:npc/Castle Clerk — Nerion) closed with her own hand · @[Tower Sentry — Vrask](entity:npc/Tower Sentry — Vrask), whose report never reaches the castle. They are all looking at the same two months.

Votumar is not an enemy fortress. Everyone in the castle does their work well and trusts their commander.

**When he left, he gave @[Deputy Lord Commander — Aren](entity:npc/Deputy Lord Commander — Aren) a written and sealed two-point order; no one else in the castle knows of it.** The order forbids the soldiers from going far and ties the news of the sickness directly to him (@[The Last Written Order](entity:quest/The Last Written Order)).

mapping.name: Watchtower Line
mapping.description: Signal towers ranged along the bay: fire by night, giant mirrors by day. At the very tip, a lighthouse.
mapping.description_long:
> Along the coast, stone towers are ranged at intervals where each can see the next. The giant mirror atop the nearest tower turns slowly, catches the sun and sends a brief flash to the next tower; a breath later the tower beyond passes the same light to the one after. On the flats between the towers catapults are lined up, their arms raised to the sky. The wind carries salt and the smell of old soot. At the very tip, on the rocks, stands a lighthouse.
>
> The dragonborn sentry standing at the door of the nearest tower lets go of the mirror's chain and turns to you.

The coastal defense line of @[Votumar](entity:location/Votumar). A continent with weak sea power protects its coast with towers and catapults.

## The towers

Each tower has three floors: at the bottom provisions and water, in the middle the room where the sentries sleep, at the top the mirror and the fire bowl. The top is reached by a narrow stone spiral stair. The walls of the stair are blackened by the soot of fires that have burned for years.

A watch ledger is kept in every tower: what was seen, at what hour, which signal was sent.

## The signal system

News is sent by **fire** at night, by **mirror** by day. A shadow seen at the mouth of the bay is reported to the castle within a few breaths. Every signal is also written in a ledger at the castle.

## The Coast Watchers

The Coast Watchers keep watch in the towers; their elite are dragonborn. One sentry: @[Tower Sentry — Vrask](entity:npc/Tower Sentry — Vrask).

At the castle end of the line stands @[Watch Captain — Drahan](entity:npc/Watch Captain — Drahan): every signal from the towers is entered first in Drahan's ledger, then passed on to the castle.
mapping.secrets: **A signal a tower sent one night did not enter the castle's ledger.** The sentry saw something and sent the signal; the castle's ledger has no record of that night. Where the signal stopped can be read in two places: the line ledger of @[Watch Captain — Drahan](entity:npc/Watch Captain — Drahan) and the record desk of @[Castle Clerk — Nerion](entity:npc/Castle Clerk — Nerion) at the castle.

mapping.name: Radenhall Courtyard
mapping.environment: A forested bowl ringed by coastal mountains
mapping.description: At the continent's far north, in the middle of the forest ringed by coastal mountains, the druids' runed stone rings. A single narrow path leads down inside.
mapping.description_long:
> The path crosses the last ridge and the forest suddenly opens. Below, on a broad flat ringed by trees, stands a circle of giant stones; inside and outside it are rings of smaller stones, each stone a different size from its neighbor. There are runes on the faces of the giant stones, but they can be made out only when the sun strikes from the side. The air is warm and dry; it smells of grass, pine resin and sun-warmed stone. From under the trees comes the sound of an adze, somewhere someone is singing, and a child runs across a vine bridge strung between two trees.
>
> Someone sitting among the stones straightens up and walks toward you without hurrying.

Meridia's northernmost tip. The cold of the north is not here: this end of the continent is close to the equator, snow does not reach it, and the weather is mostly clear and fine.

## The path

Radenhall is ringed by the coastal mountains, and a single narrow path leads down through the mountains into the bowl. The path is watched constantly; @[Path Scout — Addluin](entity:npc/Path Scout — Addluin) meets everyone who wants to come in halfway down. Both sides of the path are sheer rock, and two people cannot walk side by side. From @[Lucid Triton](entity:location/Lucid Triton) it is a 4–5 day journey.

## The Courtyard

The middle of the bowl is a broad, open flat. In its center, giant stones with barely legible runes carved on their faces form a circle; inside and outside the circle are inner and outer rings of smaller stones of different sizes. The ceremonies of harvest, birth and death are held among these stones.

## The forest and the houses

Just outside the Courtyard the forest begins and climbs to the peaks of the coastal mountains ringing the bowl. The houses are under the trees: wooden houses large and small, each of a different shape. Some stand on the ground, some are up in a tree, some are wrapped in vines strung tight between two trees. The tribe's history is written not in books but in songs, and in the evenings songs are sung among the stones.

## The people

People of every race and every gender live here together. They have grown up with respect for nature. Their clothes are mostly made from plants; some look like cloth, but that cloth too is woven from bamboo and similar plants.

## Barter

Gold is hardly worth anything here. Healing herbs, runed stones and the @[Sherbet of Resistance](entity:adventuring-gear/Sherbet of Resistance) change hands by barter. The sherbet's recipe is here too.

## Government

On paper Radenhall is bound to Meridia, but it lives by its own rules. The region is governed by the @[Wardens of the North](entity:lore/Wardens of the North), and the tribe is led by the village elder. The Council counts this place harmless but uncontrollable and does not meddle in its affairs. None of its people are written in any guild ledger.

## Who is there

- @[Eldest Druid — Halder](entity:npc/Eldest Druid — Halder) — the village elder; the woman who makes the tribe's decisions and carries a runed stone in her hand.
- @[Path Scout — Addluin](entity:npc/Path Scout — Addluin) — the elf who guards the path with a dire wolf at his side.
- @[Healer — Iven](entity:npc/Healer — Iven) — the young healer who gathers healing herbs and brews the sherbet.
- @[Bard — Tamsin](entity:npc/Bard — Tamsin) — the halfling bard who starts the songs among the stones in the evenings.
mapping.secrets:
**The druids have known about the rot for months.** They read it not from a rumor but directly from the soil and the trees. No one came to ask, because asking meant crossing the path.

The answers are here, and beside them, how late it already is. What this place really gives is the second. See @[Welcome in the Courtyard](entity:scene/Welcome in the Courtyard).

**The sherbet's price.** The Wardens give both the @[Sherbet of Resistance](entity:adventuring-gear/Sherbet of Resistance) and its recipe not for gold but in trade. What they ask in return is the DM's.

Quest: @[What the Stones Know](entity:quest/What the Stones Know).

mapping.name: Cinervik
mapping.description: A village on the northern road full of inns, horse-hirers and farriers. Lately the roads are quiet.
mapping.description_long:
> The northern road runs right through the middle of the village and brings its dust with it: the walls of the houses, the signs of the inns, the flanks of the horses tied in front of the farrier, all the same grey. The ringing from the farrier's anvil never stops. In front of the inns three different songs are sung in three different languages; most of the tables listening to the songs are empty. A horse drinks at the trough by the roadside, and the child beside it gives the same answer to everyone who asks whose horse it is: *"Gone."*
>
> An innkeeper stands in front of the door, looking to both ends of the road. Then looks at you, and the innkeeper's face lights up.

A large village on the northern road where travelers change horses, eat and spend the night. A stop where people from different parts of the continent meet.

## The village's places

- **The road.** The village's one big street; inns, stables and shops on both sides.
- **The inns.** Half a dozen inns on either side of the road. Their signs are big enough to read from both ends of the road.
- **The farrier and the horse-hirers.** At the village entrance, a broad fenced area.
- **The guard hut.** The hut of the village's small army unit. The soldiers check the road by day; in the evenings they drink with travelers in the inns and tell stories.
- **The monument and the altar.** In the village square, a small monument to Will, and right beside it a modest altar to the old gods. No one is bothered by the two standing side by side.

## Government

The village is run by guild representatives and an old headman. The real decisions are talked over at the tables of the innkeepers and merchants.

## The people

Innkeeping, horse hire, farriery, selling provisions to travelers. The people are hurried and curious: every new traveler means a new story, and as the travelers grow fewer the stories change too.
mapping.secrets:
**In Cinervik rumors are plentiful and mostly false.** As the roads went quiet the inns emptied, and invention took the place of the news that did not come. The characters are told a great deal here; half of what they are told is made up.

Do not tell the characters the rumor is false. Rumors are plentiful at @[The Wharf](entity:location/The Wharf) too, and there they are true. If the characters gather information from both places, they will see the contradiction for themselves.

mapping.name: Argenfon
mapping.description: A fishing village near Votumar: stone houses, drying nets, paladins who come down to the village and chat with the tradespeople.
mapping.description_long:
> Plain stone houses are ranged facing the sea. On the side the wind comes from, the walls are built an arm's length thick, and the windows on that side are very narrow. Fishing nets dry in front of the doors; the whole village smells of salt, seaweed and dried fish. In the square on the shore, a paladin with a wool cloak thrown over the armor laughs out loud at something a boatman is telling. The waves slap the boats' keels and draw back.
>
> A woman holds out a piece of warm bread to you from the door of her house. Before asking what you are looking for, she asks where you came from.

A fishing village on the eastern coast, near @[Votumar](entity:location/Votumar).

## The village's places

- **The shore square.** The pebbly shore where the boats are pulled up, and the square in front of it. In the mornings fish is sold here.
- **The houses.** Sturdy, plain stone houses shaped by the wind. The roofs are covered with flat stones.
- **The workshops.** The small craft work the castle needs: rope, sailcloth, straps.

## Government

The village is run jointly by a village council and a liaison officer appointed by Votumar; decisions are generally made with the people's consent. There is no barracks in the village. The castle's paladins often come down to the village, chat with the tradespeople and join the festivals. Protecting the village is the job of its own young people.

## The Sea Festival

The biggest event of the year. The whole village comes down to the shore; paladins come from the castle too.

## The people

Helpful and calm people; they open their doors to strangers. Their friendship with the knights is the village's pride. They respect the Way of Will, but their fear of the sea binds them to old habits: on stormy nights they leave flowers on the shore.
mapping.secrets:
**Here the sickness is spoken of with worry, but every conversation ends in the same place:** *"The Lord Commander will handle it."*

The villagers say this sincerely. When you consider who @[Lord Commander — Varhan](entity:npc/Lord Commander — Varhan) is, this sentence grows heavy; let the characters notice it themselves.

mapping.name: Tide Mouth
mapping.environment: A nest mouth in the tidal rocks
mapping.description: The rocks an hour beyond @[Argenfon](entity:location/Argenfon). The mouth beneath the rock is visible only when the water recedes; when the water rises, there is no door at all.
mapping.description_long:
> About an hour beyond the village the shore leaves the soft sand and turns to rock. Black stones descending like steps, pools of salt water left between them, and over everything a layer of dry mussel shells — they crackle when you step on them.
>
> When the water is high there is nothing here: the waves come right up to the foot of the rock and end there.
>
> When the water recedes, beneath the rock, a hand's breadth above the ground, **a mouth as wide as a pair of shoulders** opens. The inside cannot be seen. The edges of the mouth are smooth; something has been going in and out of there for a long time.

An hour on, the village's shore leaves the soft sand and turns to rock. The fishers do not come this far: there is nowhere to pull up a boat, no shallows to cast a net, and the shell layer cuts the feet. For someone looking from @[Argenfon](entity:location/Argenfon), this is where the shore ends.

## General features

- **The tide.** The mouth is exposed only at the hours when the water is lowest. At high water the waves come right up to the foot of the rock and the underside of the rocks is completely closed.
- **The shell layer.** The tops of the black stones are covered with dried mussel shells; everyone who steps on them makes noise. Someone who wants to approach quietly moves from pool to pool, stepping on wet stone.
- **The edge of the mouth.** As wide as a pair of shoulders, a hand's breadth above the ground, and its edges worn smooth — something has been going in and out of there for a long time.
- **Pools.** Between the stones descending like steps, troughs of salt water remain. In them, small shellfish, and here and there fragments of broken shell.
- **The way.** You walk along the shore; there is no need to climb the rocks. Finding the way in the dark is another matter.
mapping.secrets:
The colony is here. **About thirty** @[Hıkka — The Record in the Books](entity:lore/Hıkka — The Record in the Books), about ten of them **softs** that have just shed their shells.

The mouth can be passed only at **the lowest tide**, and it is narrow; an armored human cannot get in, an unarmored one gets in by crawling. Inside, after a few meters, the water drops away and opens into an **air pocket**: that is where the colony lives.

The mouth is held by the @[Holdfast](entity:monster/Holdfast). It does not chase, does not come out, does not budge — and a 2nd-level table is not expected to get past it.

**This is the only place the patrol cannot see:** for someone walking on the beach, there is not even a door.

mapping.name: Bargemen's Inn
mapping.environment: An inn on the riverbank; a cellar beneath it
mapping.description: The bargemen's inn at the edge of the River Loading Yard. In the cellar beneath it, names and clothes are made ready.
mapping.description_long:
> The smell of wet rope and fried onions carries in through the door. Bargemen sit at long tables, river mud dried on their arms; one counts weighbridge slips one by one, lips moving with each slip. The woman behind the counter pulls the bung from a barrel, and the beer splashes two drops onto the stone floor.
>
> At the end of the counter, beside the curtain that opens onto the kitchen, there is a narrow stair leading down. No one stands at the head of the stair, but a lamp is burning below.

At the edge of the @[River Loading Yard](entity:location/River Loading Yard), the inn of those who come on the Golden River's barges. Upstairs it is an ordinary inn: long tables, cheap beer, bargemen counting weighbridge slips.

## The cellar

In the cellar beneath the inn, **names and clothes** are made ready. Someone who does not want to be written onto a passage paper under their own name comes down here, and leaves with a name to be written on the paper and clothes to match that name: a merchant's clerk's jacket, a deckhand's salt-stained boots, an apprentice's plain caftan.

Two jobs are done in the cellar, and the same hand does both: writes the name, and sews the clothes.

A passage paper is collected under a name. Whoever leaves the cellar goes to the @[Countersign Desk](entity:location/Countersign Desk) under the name they got in the cellar.

## Who is there

- @[Innkeeper — Aysel](entity:npc/Innkeeper — Aysel) — behind the counter; the counter faces the stair.
- @[Bargeman — Rüstem](entity:npc/Bargeman — Rüstem) — the bargeman counting weighbridge slips; his barge goes down to Elymsyr.
- @[Needle](entity:npc/Needle) — in the cellar; the hand that writes the name and sews the clothes.

## Who knows the way

- @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar) — when a passage paper needs a name.
- @[Lamp](entity:npc/Lamp) — as someone who lost his name to debt, he knows where in the city a new name is to be had.
mapping.secrets:
**The name written in the cellar is not invented.** The name rests on a line written in the ledger of the @[Border and Trade Guild](entity:lore/Border and Trade Guild) by Orvan's hand; the cellar makes that line wearable. It has worked this way for thirty years.

**The work done in the cellar is written in no ledger.** The only thing written is the name itself, and that name becomes official the day it receives the countersignature on a passage paper.

**The price.** What the cellar asks in return is the DM's.

See @[Good Writ](entity:quest/Good Writ).

mapping.name: Military Law Chamber
mapping.environment: A two-story stone house under repair, on one of the upper terraces
mapping.description: The room the @[Military Law Guild](entity:lore/Military Law Guild) is setting up in @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr): an old two-story stone house with a cellar on one of the upper terraces. The ground floor is being made ready for clerks; building work continues upstairs.
mapping.description_long:
> The terrace widens here, and the houses thin out. A large, old stone house stands almost alone, and looks unfinished: the stone of the front facade ends at the first floor, above it rises a story of new wood, and the front of that story is still open, closed only by a railing. A scaffold like a cage has been put up in the narrow alley to the left of the house. Half the roof is nothing but rafters; the sky shows between them. The smell of freshly planed wood mixes with the sharpness of tar. A newly nailed signboard hangs over the door, with nothing written on it yet.
>
> The light of a lantern leaks through the gap in the front window's shutters.

On one of the upper terraces of @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr), an old two-story stone house with a cellar. The @[Military Law Guild](entity:lore/Military Law Guild) bought the house a short while ago and is setting up a room for itself in the harbor: for the first time in the city, another guild's clerks will sit beside the customs. By day craftsmen work upstairs; at night hired watchmen hold the house.

## The map

One map, three floors: the ground floor on the left, the upper floor on the right, the cellar below. One square is 5 ft. The same letter is the same passage:

- **A**: the inner stair in the stair hall, from the ground floor to the upper floor.
- **B**: the cellar hatch in the hearth hall, from the ground floor to the cellar.
- **C**: the ladder in the alley, from the street to the scaffold and from the scaffold to the upper floor.

## Ground floor

Old stone walls, new wooden partitions inside; four rooms.

- **The front door.** A single-leaf oak door opening onto the terrace street; two stone steps in front of it, beside it a few barrels and fresh timber leaning against the wall. A small window on each side of the door.
- **The clerks' room.** The front room the door opens into. In front of each of the two windows a new writing desk and chair, crates full of paper in the corners, an empty shelf on the left wall. The hearth hall is reached through a wide frame whose door has not yet been hung.
- **The ledger room.** To the right of the clerks' room, through a door. Empty shelves the length of the wall and a pile of shelf boards on the floor; the guild's ledgers will come here.
- **The hearth hall.** The back half of the house. A stone hearth on the back wall, firewood beside it; in the middle a long table with two benches. At night the watchmen sit here. In front of the right end of the table, a square wooden hatch in the floor (**B**).
- **The stair hall.** To the right of the hearth hall, through a door. A wooden stair along the right wall going up to the upper floor (**A**).
- **The alley.** To the left of the house, a narrow passage between the scaffold's poles. Two windows of the ground floor open onto the alley; it has no door.

## Upper floor

Almost entirely new wood. The back and right walls are the house's old stone; the left wall is a new timber frame. It has no door to the street.

- **The landing.** The stair (**A**) comes up in the back right corner; a rough railing around the stairwell.
- **The timber room.** The back half. Fresh timber stacked in piles at the foot of the back wall; beside it buckets full of caulking tar and coils of rope. A bed in one corner.
- **The unfloored part.** In the middle of the timber room the floorboards have not yet been nailed down: there are only joists, and through them the light of the hearth hall shows below. Whoever slips between the joists falls into the hearth hall.
- **The partitions.** Only the studs of the walls that will divide the rooms have been put up. You can see between them, but a person can pass only through the gaps left.
- **The front room.** A plank laid across trestles, a ladder lying on the floor, stacked roof tiles, a barrel of nails.
- **The open front.** The front wall does not exist yet; in its place there is a temporary wooden railing. From here the harbor and the river mouth can be seen; the street is one floor below.
- **The scaffold.** A planked scaffold along the left outer wall; reached from the street by ladder (**C**). The two window openings in the left wall have no shutters yet: the upper floor can be entered from the scaffold.

## Cellar

Only under the back half of the house, beneath the hearth hall and the stair hall. A stone vault, stone floor; three sections.

- **The stair.** A narrow wooden stair coming down from the cellar hatch (**B**), landing in the middle of the big cellar.
- **The big cellar.** Oak barrels along the left wall, sacks of grain on the back wall, a shelf of jugs on the front wall; left over from the house's former owner. The vault is carried by two square stone pillars.
- **The back room.** Through an arched passage. Full of barrels. In the corner, behind the barrels, a small iron-banded chest; locked.
- **The woodshed.** Through the other arched passage: firewood, a heap of coal, a broken crate.

## General features

- **Stone and wood.** The walls of the ground floor and the cellar, and the back and right walls of the upper floor, are stone and do not burn. The rest is wood and burns: the floors, the partitions, the stairs, the upper floor's framed wall, the scaffold and the timber.
- **Light.** At night a hearth and a lantern burn on the ground floor; the upper floor and the cellar are dark.
- **Sound.** The terrace street is narrow: shouting and breaking wood can be heard from the neighboring houses. A fire burning on the upper floor can be seen from the harbor.
mapping.secrets:
**What is in the chest.** A bundle of weighbridge slips. Each came from the weighbridge of the @[Customs House](entity:location/Customs House) and records a ship's weighed load; beside each is pinned the same ship's figure from the ledger. The two do not match: in the ledger the load is complete every time. This is the heaviest paper that could be got against the ledger of the @[Customs Governor](entity:npc/Customs Governor), and the guild knows it. How the slips came into the guild's hands is not written on this card.

**The lock.** **DC 15** with thieves' tools. The key is on the belt of the @[Head Watchman](entity:monster/Head Watchman). Breaking it requires **Strength DC 15** and is noisy: everyone in the house hears.

**Who is guarding.** At night the house is held not by guild men but by hired hands: a few @[Site Watchman](entity:monster/Site Watchman), two @[Hired Cutlass](entity:monster/Hired Cutlass) passing the time with dice, and the @[Head Watchman](entity:monster/Head Watchman) who carries the key. The guild plans to bring its own police when the room opens. The encounter: @[The Night Worksite](entity:encounter/The Night Worksite).

**After the fire.** The arson is written up by the @[Military Law Guild](entity:lore/Military Law Guild), because it is the guild that writes up crimes. A burned room is rebuilt; the bundle taken from the cellar does not come back. The quest: @[The Masked Job](entity:quest/The Masked Job).

mapping.name: Black Sail
mapping.description: *Black Sail*: the Black Fleet's ship in the water closest to @[Vorstrand](entity:location/Vorstrand), and the smallest of the four: a sailing orc warship with a pitch-black hull and sails and war drums on its deck.
mapping.description_long:
> As the smudge on the horizon grows it turns into a ship, and the ship shows no color. Its hull is pitch-black and tarred; so are its sails, matte as if swallowing the light. When the wind blows from its side, its sound arrives before the ship: a deep, heavy drum. Three beats, a silence, three beats. Along its gunwale, row on row of shields, and between them the points of javelins glint. Someone stands at its bow, looking at you.
>
> The drum quickens.

A sailing orc warship; a little smaller than the @[Honest Scales](entity:location/Honest Scales), but not by much. One of the Black Fleet's four ships on @[The Open Sea](entity:location/The Open Sea). Someone looking from outside sees nothing but an orc warship.

## The deck

- **The bow.** The hook chains lie coiled here; the @[Hookman](entity:monster/Hookman)s set up the boarding from here and from the waist gunwale.
- **The waist deck.** Where the @[Orc Warrior](entity:monster/Orc Warrior)s hold the line. In its middle, at the foot of the mainmast, a heavy iron-banded **hatch**: the only mouth of the lower hold.
- **The quarterdeck.** The great war drum is here, in front of the helm. The @[Drummer](entity:monster/Drummer) is at its head, @[Orc Captain — Mordha](entity:npc/Orc Captain — Mordha) beside it.
- **The captain's cabin.** Below the quarterdeck; narrow, low, and the smell of the hatch has settled here too.

## The lower hold

The front half of the hold, closed off with thick planks. With the hatch shut only its smell gets out: sour and metallic. While the drum is playing no sound comes from inside. When the drum stops, nails scrape on wood.

## The crew

@[Orc Captain — Mordha](entity:npc/Orc Captain — Mordha) · one @[Drummer](entity:monster/Drummer) · two @[Hookman](entity:monster/Hookman)s · eight @[Orc Warrior](entity:monster/Orc Warrior)s. In the lower hold, eight to ten @[the Turned](entity:monster/The Turned), among them one or two @[Turned Orc](entity:monster/Turned Orc)s. The orcs on deck are women and men together, and their heights, builds and skin colors are nothing alike; the captain is a woman too.

The encounter: @[Hull to Hull](entity:encounter/Hull to Hull).
mapping.secrets:
**Some of those in the lower hold were the ship's own crew.** Who the rest are is the DM's. The rhythm of the drum controls them (@[Rhythm](entity:creature-action/Rhythm)); why the rhythm passed to them is the DM's too.

**The key to the hatch** is on the belt of @[Orc Captain — Mordha](entity:npc/Orc Captain — Mordha).

**Tangible proof of the sickness is on this ship:** the lower hold, and, if she stays alive, the captain (@[Where They Came From](entity:quest/Where They Came From)).

Why the ship is waiting in this water, and for whom it carries the Turned, is the DM's.

**A paper in the cabin.** On the table, on a greasy paper, **the characters** are written down. If they came the legal way, by the names written on their passage papers: few people know those names — @[Needle](entity:npc/Needle), who writes the name in the cellar, the room that signed the paper, and @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar). If they came the smuggler's way, by a nameless description: how many they are, what they carry, which night they boarded — as much as someone like @[Velvet](entity:npc/Velvet), who saw them at @[The Wharf](entity:location/The Wharf), would see. Who wrote the paper and how it came to the ship is the DM's.

**A magical trace.** If a character who can cast spells or has magical knowledge looks at those who come out of the lower hold, **Arcana DC 13**: on them is a trace that does not fade, does not scatter, and stays tied to somewhere — the same as the trace of the three strangers in @[Questioning at the Cabin](entity:scene/Questioning at the Cabin). It has no direction, no distance, no name.

mapping.name: Honest Scales
mapping.description: The trading ship of @[Captain — Maren](entity:npc/Captain — Maren): medium-sized, sturdy, comes with a legal cargo and leaves with a legal cargo. Since ships began to go missing it has carried guards on its deck.
mapping.description_long:
> The deck under your feet does not keep still for a moment. The hold hatches are closed and lashed crosswise with ropes; on top of them two deckhands sit cross-legged, sewing a sail patch. At the stern, a ballista with its tarpaulin half drawn back faces the sea, and the guard beside it is oiling its string with a cloth. The smell of wet sacks and cloves rises from the hold. Someone at the bow shouts the name of a watch.
>
> The deckhand beside you turns to you without letting go of the rope: *"You're new. Report to the sergeant."*

A trading ship sailing from @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr), belonging to @[Captain — Maren](entity:npc/Captain — Maren). Whoever boards with a countersigned paper is signed on as crew and stands watches; there is no pay.

## Who is there

About twenty-two people: the captain, @[Scales Sergeant — Hulda](entity:npc/Scales Sergeant — Hulda) and four guards, and about sixteen deckhands divided into four watch teams. The crew is women and men together; most are human, among them two dwarves, a half-orc and a gnome.

## The deck

- **The bow.** The lookout mast and the anchor.
- **The waist.** The hold hatches; the cargo below, as it was counted at customs.
- **The stern.** The helm, the ballista and the captain's cabin. In the cabin a map lies open on the table (@[Maren's Course](entity:scene/Maren's Course)).

## The ballista

An old ballista scrapped from the Elymsyr towers; @[Scales Sergeant — Hulda](entity:npc/Scales Sergeant — Hulda) brought it, and she looks after it. **Ranged Weapon Attack: +6** to hit, range 120/480 ft, one target. **Hit:** 16 (3d10) piercing damage. Loading takes an action, aiming and firing takes an action.

## The guards

All four are former River Guards; their sergeant chose them herself: two humans (one a woman), a half-elf woman and a halfling. AC 16 (chain shirt, shield), 11 hit points, spear **+3** to hit, 4 (1d6+1) piercing damage.

The voyage: @[The Continent on the Horizon](entity:quest/The Continent on the Horizon).
mapping.secrets:
**Maren pays the guards' wages out of her own purse,** and this voyage half her earnings go to them. After the losses half her crew were going to leave the ship; the guards were their condition for staying.

**The ballista has never been fired at a real ship.** In the towers there were only drills.

mapping.name: Duran
mapping.description:
Head of Silverwater's Council of Elders. He spent his youth cutting timber, and he is the most listened-to of the village elders. He spends most of the day sitting in the village square or on the bench in front of his own door; every stranger who comes to the village passes in front of him sooner or later.

He does not like outsiders meddling in the village's affairs, but he is not rude.
mapping.appearance:
A man past sixty, tall and still standing straight. Broad-shouldered, his arms thick from timber work. He keeps his white hair cut short; he has no beard. His face is darkened by wind and sun, and three deep lines cross his forehead.

He wears a jacket of thick wool, patched at the elbows. His hands are calloused, and the tip of the little finger of his left hand is missing. He smells of pine resin and pipe tobacco.

His voice is low and slow.
mapping.mannerisms:
Before answering a question he repeats the question slowly, word by word. Not because he is thinking; he is weighing how much of it to say.

When he talks, he looks not at the other person's face but at the village road. When he does not want to say something, he begins to fill his pipe.

*"You'll go to the cabin? Go. But go in the morning."*
mapping.goals: That the village does not fall apart, and that no outsider lays a hand on the village's affairs. Taking the strangers into @[The Cabin](entity:location/The Cabin) was the village's own decision; Duran wants that decision to stay in the village's hands.
mapping.secrets:
**He knows where the three strangers came from**, and does not want to say. He fears that if he says it, someone from outside, perhaps someone from the city, will come to the village.

What he knows is this: the strangers came from a hidden harbor on the coast, @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor).
mapping.dmNotes:
**If the characters ask.** The first time he is asked, Duran says *"they came by the road, like everyone"*. If the characters convince him that they are asking for the village's good, he says one short sentence: *"They came from the harbor."* He does not say which harbor; he adds that @[Corvin](entity:npc/Corvin) knows the way.

He does not talk under threat or force. If pressed, he gets up and leaves and does not talk again that day.

He is the head of the council, but he does not decide alone. If he makes the characters a promise in the village's name, he may not be able to make the council keep it.

mapping.name: Umay
mapping.description:
The half-elf woman who has tended Silverwater's sick for forty years. Half the village was born into her hands. Her house is beside the well; in front of her door there are always bundles of herbs hung up to dry.

She is one of those who bring food to the three strangers in the cabin, and she is also the only one who does not stop at the door.
mapping.appearance:
Half-elf. Her face looks younger than those of her age in the village; her hands do not: the knuckles swollen, the skin reddened by hot water. She has tied her grey hair in a tight bun at the back of her head and pinned it with a wooden skewer. Her ears are thin and long; the tip of one carries an old cut scar.

Her sleeves are rolled to the elbow, her apron clean and starched. Hanging from her belt are a pair of scissors, a roll of bandage and a small knife. She smells of vinegar and dried sage.

Under her eyes lie the purple shadows of someone who has not slept these last few days.
mapping.mannerisms:
She does not speak of the sick as *"them"*; she says their names. Before answering a question she wipes her hands on her apron.

She speaks in short, clear sentences, and when describing a symptom she shows its place on her own body with her hand: *"Here. On the inside of the joint. Thin, black — turns purple when you hold it to the light — like a hair."*

When someone says *"no one has died"*, she falls silent and turns her head away.
mapping.goals: That the three people in the cabin live.
mapping.secrets:
**She touched the strangers, and she is hiding it.** She went into the cabin, checked their fevers, dressed their wounds. She told no one.

**She noticed that the three arrived sick.** The sickness is older than the village thinks; the symptoms have been there since the day the three strangers came to the village. Umay saw this, but cannot put a name to it.
mapping.dmNotes:
**If the characters ask.** Umay describes the symptoms as she saw them, without requiring a roll: tiredness, the purplish-black veins in the joints, the dried purplish-black trace at the corners of the eyes, the hardening skin. She also says that the sickness came to the village along with the three strangers. This is the same conclusion a character examining the bodies reaches with **Medicine DC 12**.

She can see nothing about magic and can say nothing about it.

If the characters ask directly whether Umay herself went into the cabin, she does not lie; she falls silent and straightens her apron. Whoever is watching sees that she is hiding something.

Tell the players, from Umay's mouth, **that the Sickness Score never goes down** before they go into the cabin: *"This doesn't pass. I've never seen it pass."*

mapping.name: Corvin
mapping.description:
A man who lives in Silverwater but is seldom found in the village. He goes down to the shore carrying loads on his back, and brings goods from the shore to the village. The villagers do not ask what he brings from where; he does not tell either.

He knows the way to @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor), and for guiding he wants his fee in advance.

The village's trade with the outside runs on his back: salt, thread, nails, a good knife, a bottle of medicine. The village does not know about the harbor and does not ask where the goods come from; the only thing it knows is that Corvin goes and comes back.

He was not born in Silverwater and is not counted a villager — to the village he is a stranger. Still he is loved: no one is wary of him, the children tag along after him, the innkeeper writes up his debts.
mapping.appearance:
A short, strong man of about forty. On his shoulders is the shiny, hardened mark that years of load ropes have left; his palms are calloused. His face has seen harsh wind, and an old scar sits above his eyebrow. His black hair is dried out by salt.

He wears a long brown coat that has eaten road dust; from the coat's inner pocket a ball of twine and the handle of a knife show. His boots are good, and newly resoled. He smells of sweat, salt and tar.
mapping.mannerisms:
He does not talk about the road before talking about the price. When he takes money in hand, he counts it, twice. His only exception is @[Mouse](entity:npc/Mouse): he does not call her *Mouse*, he calls her **Squirrel**, and he asks her for not a penny.

When he sees good cloth his eyes light up and he cannot help rubbing it between his fingers. He talks about the cloth of the strangers in the cabin without anyone asking: *"That cloth isn't from around here. Nor that dye. If I carried something like that it'd be worth a purse of gold a month."*
mapping.goals: Money.
mapping.secrets: He knows @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor), because he carried goods from there and still does.
mapping.dmNotes:
**Guiding.** He agrees to take the characters to the harbor; he wants the fee in advance. He is open to bargaining but does not go below half the fee.

**At the harbor.** At the harbor Corvin is a guest; he is not counted one of its people. If he stands guarantor for the characters his word is listened to, but on its own it is not enough. See @[Admitted to the Harbor](entity:scene/Admitted to the Harbor).

**The cloth.** Without anyone asking, he says that the clothes of those in the cabin are of an expensive cloth from another continent.

**When he is in the village.** Corvin is not in the village all the time; he goes back and forth between the shore and the village and stops by from time to time. Whether he is in the village when the characters arrive is your decision.

**If Corvin dies**, the road to the shore closes to the characters and there is no one in the village to open it. There is no making up for this; do not produce a replacement guide. But the world does not close: there are those on the continent who know where @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor) is — some Council officials, some members of @[The Council and the Guild Assembly](entity:lore/The Council and the Guild Assembly), and very rarely the paladin officers of the @[Order of the Silver Shield](entity:lore/Order of the Silver Shield). The door that closes with Corvin can be opened again from Lucid Triton: by a longer, more expensive road that leaves more traces.

**His relationship with the village.** To the village he is a stranger, but a loved stranger. The village's trade with the outside runs through him and the village does not know about the harbor — if the characters ask the villagers about the shore no one knows anything; they point to Corvin.

**Squirrel.** He knows the wharf's apprentice (@[Mouse](entity:npc/Mouse)) and is very fond of her; he calls her **Squirrel**. He is the only one on the wharf who does this. Corvin is a haggling, money-minded man, but at heart he is not a bad person — you see this most clearly in how he treats Mouse. If the characters treat Mouse badly, Corvin's attitude turns.

**Enamel.** He also knows @[Enamel](entity:npc/Enamel)'s back room; someone who has been bringing goods to the same wharf for years knows the jeweler's door. If asked, he describes the way; he does not describe her work.

mapping.name: Milo Goodbarrel
mapping.description:
The owner and innkeeper of @[Goodbarrel's Hearth](entity:location/Goodbarrel's Hearth). Hears everything heard in the village and says what was heard once more, in Milo's own words. Does not lower prices, but writes up debts.

The three strangers spent their first two nights in the village at Milo's inn.
mapping.appearance:
A halfling nearing fifty with plump cheeks. Curly, light-brown hair thinned above the ears; thick eyebrows that go up with every sentence. Nose and cheeks always red from the heat of the hearth.

Wears a grease-stained apron, and under the apron a linen shirt with the sleeves rolled up. A cloth always hangs over one shoulder. Stands behind the counter on a stool high enough to see the whole common room. Smells of onions, bread yeast and beer.
mapping.mannerisms:
Repeats out loud every sentence spoken at the tables, as if saying it for the first time: *"A woman at the well says no one's gone into the cabin again. No one's gone in!"*

Remembers and counts, without being asked, who came, how many nights they stayed and who paid. While telling a customer something, wipes the counter with the cloth, and if what is being told is important, wipes faster.
mapping.goals: That the inn is full and the customers' bellies are full.
mapping.dmNotes:
**If the characters ask**, Milo tells everything Milo knows, hiding nothing:

- When the three strangers came to the village they stayed here two nights, in the room upstairs.
- All three were dressed in the same foreign cloth. *"I've never seen the like in my life."*
- They paid **in advance, without haggling and more than enough**. Milo wanted to give them change; they would not take it.
- The tiefling woman never left the two halflings' side, and ate her meals after them.
- When they were moved to the cabin everyone in the village was relieved. Milo too.

Milo has nothing to hide. The common room is a door that always stands open: sitting by the hearth and listening requires no roll.

mapping.name: Alton Leagallow
mapping.description:
One of the three strangers in the cabin. The village knows him by this name. He lies in one of the beds by the back wall and spends most of the day asleep.

The sickness has struck him hardest with tiredness.
mapping.appearance:
A halfling in his thirties, grown thin. His cheeks are sunken, his lips cracked. His light-brown hair is stuck to his forehead with sweat. At his joints, under the skin, purplish-black veins as thin as a hair show; on his wrists and neck the skin has hardened and flaked in places.

His clothes are worn but expensive: a tightly woven cloth not woven on this continent, dyed a dark green with a dye unknown on this continent. The buttons at his collar are carved bone. On the ring finger of his left hand is a thin gold wedding band; on the inner face of the ring a line has been engraved in fine letters. His breath is sour, and with each breath a faint rattle comes from his chest.
mapping.mannerisms:
Tiredness presses him into the bed. He closes his eyes in the middle of a sentence and falls asleep before finishing it; a few minutes later he wakes and begins another sentence.

When speaking he is polite and careful. When asked how he met Merla he suddenly wakes up and answers at once, too readily: *"We met on the road."*
mapping.goals: To live.
mapping.secrets:
**His name is false.** His real name is **Cortia Greenbottle**. He is the husband of @[Merla Tealeaf](entity:npc/Merla Tealeaf). They use separate surnames so as to look like two travelers who met on the road.

He came from @[the Beyond](entity:location/Vorstrand), through @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor), without passing through customs. Whether he paid for the voyage himself, or someone paid for him, nothing he says in the cabin reveals.

**He is about to pass into the last stage.**
mapping.dmNotes:
**If the characters ask.** Alton brushes off where he came from with *"from far away"*. He does not know how he fell sick and says he does not know. He does not give his real name.

**The wedding bands.** Alton and Merla lie in the same row of beds and wear two wedding bands forged in the same style, but they give two separate surnames. A character who looks at the rings notices this without rolling.

**Inside the band — the key to the real names.** On the inner face of both rings is the same line: *C. & P. Greenbottle.* Reading it requires taking the ring off and looking inside; Alton does not give up his ring, and whoever tries to take it off meets resistance. After @[The Dawn Turning](entity:scene/The Dawn Turning) this line is there for free on the corpse.

**His real name.** No one in Silverwater recognizes the name *Cortia Greenbottle*. In Lucid Triton, @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar) recognizes it — whether he hears the name, or listens to someone describing two halfling spouses.

When he turns: @[Turned Alton](entity:monster/Turned Alton).

mapping.name: Merla Tealeaf
mapping.description:
One of the three strangers in the cabin. The village knows her by this name. She lies by the back wall, in the bed next to Alton's.

The sickness strikes her fitfully: lucid one moment, lost the next.
mapping.appearance:
A halfling woman in her thirties. Her dark chestnut hair was braided; the braid has begun to come undone. Her skin is grey, her lips purplish. At the corners of her eyes and under her earlobes is the trace of a dried, purplish-black fluid; someone tried to wipe it away, and it did not come off completely.

Her clothes are of the same foreign cloth as Alton's; small leaves are embroidered on the collar with a fine silver thread. On her finger is a wedding band, the twin of Alton's; on its inner face the same engraving. Her hands are cold, and she never lets go of the edge of the blanket.
mapping.mannerisms:
One moment her eyes clear; she sits up, politely tries to show her visitors where to sit, asks their names. The next moment she is looking at the wall, her lips moving, and she does not know who is beside her.

If she is asked, in one of her lucid moments, how she met Alton, she gives the same answer, just as fast: *"We met on the road."*
mapping.goals: To live.
mapping.secrets:
**Her name is false.** Her real name is **Portia Greenbottle**. She is the wife of @[Alton Leagallow](entity:npc/Alton Leagallow).

She came from @[the Beyond](entity:location/Vorstrand), through @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor), without passing through customs. They did not choose Silverwater; it was the last place they could reach.

**She is about to pass into the last stage.**
mapping.dmNotes:
**If the characters ask.** In her lucid moments she talks, but what she describes does not reveal their past: a beautiful house, a garden, the sea. She does not say where it was or how they fell sick. In her lost moments she does not answer questions; sometimes she says a name into the empty air and falls silent.

**Inside the band.** The same line as Alton's: *C. & P. Greenbottle.* See @[Questioning at the Cabin](entity:scene/Questioning at the Cabin).

When she turns: @[Turned Merla](entity:monster/Turned Merla).

mapping.name: Kromanna
mapping.description:
The third stranger in the cabin: the two halflings' servant and protector. She lies in the bed right beside the door.

The sickness has not weakened her body; on the contrary, it is making it strong earlier than it should.
mapping.appearance:
A tall tiefling woman in her late twenties. Her skin is deep red; the tips of the two horns that curl back from her forehead were filed down long ago. She keeps her black hair cut short at the nape. Her eyes are yellow, and glow faintly in the dark.

Her clothes are of the same foreign cloth as her employers', but the cut is plain; the sleeves have been unpicked at the seams for ease of movement. Despite the sickness her arms are full, her shoulders broad, and under her skin the muscles now and then tense and relax on their own. On her neck, under the collar, a patch of grey skin hardened into scales shows.
mapping.mannerisms:
When someone approaches the door, she tries to sit up so as to come between the two halflings and the door. If she cannot sit up, she props one arm on the edge of the bed and makes a shield of her body.

Her voice is hoarse but clear. When asked her name she gives it without hesitation. When speaking of her employers she does not say their names but *"them"*: *"Don't touch them. If you need something, tell me."*
mapping.goals: To protect the two halflings.
mapping.secrets:
**Her name is real.** A tiefling woman changing her name does not hide her, so she did not change it.

She is not a slave but a servant hired for wages; she has served the same house for years. The house found her valuable enough to dress her like her employers and take her along on the voyage.

**In a hidden pocket of her clothes she carries a ring:** @[The Sealless Ring](entity:trinket/The Sealless Ring). Finding the ring requires the characters to say they are searching her and **Investigation DC 15**. Kromanna does not show the ring of her own accord and does not mention it exists.

**She is about to pass into the last stage.**
mapping.dmNotes:
**If the characters ask.** Kromanna says nothing about her employers: *"Their business is theirs."* She answers briefly what is asked about herself. She says she does not know how they fell sick.

**A search.** If someone tries to search Kromanna, she has no strength to resist, but she does not take her eyes off whoever is searching.

When she turns: @[Turned Kromanna](entity:monster/Turned Kromanna), the strongest of the three Turned.

mapping.name: Twine
mapping.description:
The gnome who keeps the goods ledger of @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor). Which ship brought what, unloaded what, paid what — it is all in Twine's ledger. Twine does not write people: here who came does not enter the ledger, only their goods. The harbor's business passes through Twine's hands.

Twine usually greets newcomers sitting on the barrel at the bottom of the road.
mapping.appearance:
A gnome whose age is hard to guess: the face wrinkled, the eyes young. Skinny, long-fingered. Grey hair tied on top of the head with a piece of twine; the nickname is said to come from that. Wears a small pair of thick-lensed spectacles on the tip of the nose and looks over them when reading something.

The ledger in Twine's lap is wider than Twine; its leather cover is whitened by salt. Fingertips purple with ink. The jacket pockets are full of pens, lead and bits of twine. Smells of ink and beeswax.
mapping.mannerisms:
Licks a finger before turning a page of the ledger. Says a price once; if asked a second time, turns the page and starts writing something else.

Before looking at a person, asks about their guarantor: *"Whose guests are you?"* If the answer is not to Twine's liking, the ledger closes.
mapping.goals: That the harbor runs without a hitch.
mapping.secrets:
**The *Fate* brought the three strangers.** Twine does not know the captain's name; no one at the harbor knows it; that captain was known by the name of the ship.

**After that night the Fate never put in again.**

**Twine's real name is Burgell.** Almost no one at the harbor knows this.
mapping.dmNotes:
**If the characters ask.** Twine talks openly about admission to the harbor, surety and ship fares; these are Twine's business.

Twine does not talk easily about the three strangers. If the characters have been accepted at the harbor and have done Twine a favor, or give Twine a good reason, Twine names the ship that brought the three strangers — because saying it does no one any harm:

*"The Fate. I didn't ask the captain's name, no one here does. There was a ship; that was the name."*

*"The Fate never put in again after that night. I'm waiting. You can wait too."*

If the characters look for the three strangers in the ledger they will not find them, because people are not written at this harbor: *"People aren't written here. Goods are."*

**It ends here.** Twine sends no one to the city, because there is no address to send them to. No one at the harbor knows where the three strangers came from; the only man who knew has gone out to sea. This sentence is the last link of the @[Where They Came From](entity:quest/Where They Came From) chain: what comes after does not exist in Act 1.

**The real name** is something the characters can learn through their own efforts. Twine tells it only to someone seen as a friend, and only after long trust has been built.

mapping.name: Mouse
mapping.description: The apprentice of @[The Wharf](entity:location/The Wharf): carries rope, runs messages, counts barrels. Because no one asks her anything, she sees and remembers everything that happens on the wharf. No one calls her pretty; still, the whole wharf loves her, and everyone who passes throws her a word. On the wharf everyone calls her *Mouse* — and she does not like it.
mapping.appearance:
A barefoot halfling girl of fourteen or fifteen. A face darkened by the sun, smudged with soot and harbor grime; jet-black hair cut by her own hand, with a knife, standing in tufts. Her nose is crooked, one of her front teeth broken. The soles of her feet are hardened from the planks of the pier.

She wears a sailor's shirt three sizes too big for her, the sleeves rolled up many times. At her waist, tied on with a piece of twine, a purse and a wooden whistle. The smell of salt and fish never leaves her.
mapping.mannerisms:
She sits on a barrel, swings her legs, and counts the ships at the pier with her finger.

She answers without being asked. When she says a ship's name, she adds which night it put in, how many crates it unloaded and what its captain drinks: *"The blue one, the Swallow. Came three nights ago, at midnight. Unloaded eight crates, two of them heavy. The captain drinks cider."*

When someone listens to her, her face lights up.

When she is called *Mouse* she pauses for a moment, then answers; the same pause for years. The only exception is @[Corvin](entity:npc/Corvin): he calls her **Squirrel**, and when Mouse hears that name she looks up and laughs.
mapping.goals: To be taken on a ship as crew one day.
mapping.secrets:
Her real name is **Trym**.

She does not like the name *Mouse*. She has told no one; she learned early that telling does no good.
mapping.dmNotes:
**If the characters ask.** Mouse does not ask for money; the only thing she wants is for someone to listen to her. The wharf loves her but does not listen — everyone throws her a word and moves on, no one stops to ask a question. If the characters chat with her, buy her a meal or take her questions seriously, she tells everything she knows about the wharf: which ship came when, which captain takes whom, who owes whom.

**The Compact's truths.** On the first day the characters come to the harbor, Mouse, without being asked, tells them the three fixed truths of @[The Harbor Compact](entity:lore/The Harbor Compact). She stresses the third in particular: *"If you kill someone here you can never get into this harbor again. No one will do business with you."*

Mouse is the door that always stands open on the wharf: she sits on a barrel, and tells everything to someone who listens.

**The Fate.** If the characters have heard this name, Mouse remembers that ship, because she remembers all the ships: which night it put in, who got off, who got on. She describes the night the three passengers got off, and says the ship never came again. She does not know the captain's name either.

**Enamel's workbench.** Mouse knows @[Enamel](entity:npc/Enamel) and knows what she does; she tells it without being asked: *"She works with jewelry. Takes in rings, mends chains."* If the characters are asking about unstamped work or a jeweler, she points out the shack: *"The back room. Don't knock, she doesn't like it."*

**Her name.** She does not like being called *Mouse*, but she does not correct anyone. If a character notices this, asks her real name, or calls her by another name, it opens her up faster than money or food. The name **Squirrel** belongs to @[Corvin](entity:npc/Corvin); if anyone else uses it, Mouse's face closes and does not open again that day.

**Corvin.** She knows and loves the man who brings goods down from Silverwater to the wharf; he loves her too and treats her well. When Corvin comes to the harbor, Mouse drops her work and goes to him. If the characters came with Corvin, Mouse talks to them from the first day.

mapping.name: Captain Caelynn
mapping.description: The expensive one of the two captains at @[The Wharf](entity:location/The Wharf): her ship sturdy, her crew sober, her voyage clean. The only person at the harbor without a nickname.
mapping.appearance:
