A tall half-elf woman in her forties. A few white strands in her short-cut black hair. Her face is hardened by wind; on her left cheek a thin, old scar runs to her ear.

She wears a dark blue captain's jacket with brass buttons; the collar clean, the sleeves carefully patched. Her boots are salt-stained. At her belt a short sword and a compass pouch. She smells of tar and clean sailcloth.
mapping.mannerisms:
She does not leave her ship's ropes to her crew; every morning she checks them one by one herself.

She gives no price without seeing what the cargo is. She stands at the head of a crate with its lid shut, crosses her arms and waits for it to be opened: *"Open it. I don't carry what I haven't looked at."*

She speaks little and plainly; she does not repeat a word.
mapping.goals: To carry cargo she knows the nature of.
mapping.secrets: **She turned the three strangers away.** Later she heard that they left on another ship.
mapping.dmNotes:
**The voyage.** Caelynn takes the characters aboard her ship, but she wants either a **good writ** or **a high fee**. See @[Bargaining for Passage](entity:scene/Bargaining for Passage) · @[The Continent on the Horizon](entity:quest/The Continent on the Horizon).

**If the characters ask.** She remembers the three strangers: two halflings and a tiefling, expensive clothes. If asked why she refused them, she says a single sentence: *"I don't carry cargo I can't see."* She does not know which ship they left on.

On board: @[The Smugglers' Deck](entity:scene/The Smugglers' Deck).

mapping.name: Captain Holg
mapping.description: The cheap one of the two captains at @[The Wharf](entity:location/The Wharf). Sails fast, asks no questions, and makes no promise about what will be met at the end of the voyage.
mapping.appearance:
A broad-shouldered, paunchy half-orc in their fifties. The lower teeth jut up over the lips; the tip of one is broken. The head is shaved, with an anchor tattoo at the nape. The arms are thick and hairy.

An oily leather vest, with nothing underneath. Two different brass rings in one ear. At the belt a cutlass and a bottle. Smells of rum and old sweat. The ship's gunwale is patched in two places, and one of the patches has not been painted yet.
mapping.mannerisms:
Holg is the first to ask the price, and shouts a price before the other has answered. In bargaining Holg always comes down, and in the end holds out a hand, laughing.

*"I don't ask where you're going, you don't ask about my ship. Deal?"*
mapping.goals: Money, and putting to sea as soon as possible.
mapping.secrets: Neither the ship nor the crew can be trusted. The crew eyes the passengers' belongings; the ship is in no condition to weather a storm.
mapping.dmNotes:
**The voyage.** Holg offers a cheap and bad voyage. This is a real option; if the characters accept, Holg keeps the word given and takes them. The voyage itself goes hard. See @[Bargaining for Passage](entity:scene/Bargaining for Passage) · @[The Continent on the Horizon](entity:quest/The Continent on the Horizon).

On board: @[The Smugglers' Deck](entity:scene/The Smugglers' Deck).

mapping.name: Velvet
mapping.description:
A go-between doing business for the Council at @[The Wharf](entity:location/The Wharf). He does not hide; most days he stands at the head of a crate reading his papers. Everyone at the harbor knows he is some great one's man; no one knows whose.

Everyone who speaks in the Council's name is really speaking in the name of a guild (@[The Council and the Guild Assembly](entity:lore/The Council and the Guild Assembly)) — Velvet is that sentence's counterpart on the wharf: the visible proof that a guild has a hand in the harbor. No information is to be had from him.
mapping.appearance:
A man in his thirties, of medium height and slender build. His light-brown hair is carefully combed, his beard short and neat. His face is pale; he is not someone who goes out in the sun on the wharf.

He is better dressed than anyone on the wharf: a clean, starched collar, spotless black boots, a dark green velvet coat without a single salt stain on it. His nickname comes from his coat. His hands are white and soft; they have never held a load. He smells faintly of lavender oil.
mapping.mannerisms:
He carries his papers close to his chest, inside a leather folder. Before speaking he waits, for the other person to speak first.

His voice is soft, his sentences short: *"Tell me what you want. Then what you can give."*
mapping.goals: That the harbor stays useful to the Council.
mapping.secrets:
He knows which seats in the Council take a share from the harbor.

**His real name is Halet Custar.** The Custars are the house of the @[Military Law Guild](entity:lore/Military Law Guild). At the harbor Velvet manages that seat's money. No one at the harbor knows this name; in the city it is written in a guild ledger.
mapping.dmNotes:
**What he is for.** Velvet is not a source of information but a **sign:** he shows that a **guild's hand** is in the harbor. He opens no door in the chain and sends no one anywhere.

**If the characters ask.** He does not engage. Polite, brief, and gives nothing: *"You've come to the wrong man."* If they insist, he puts his papers in the leather folder and ends the conversation.

**What he gives, what he does not.** He gives no names, no papers, no money, and stands guarantor for no one. If asked on whose behalf he stands, he does not answer.

**Being recognized.** A character who comes from a guild or from the Order's officers (@[Guild Member](entity:background/Guild Member), @[Guild Scion of Rank](entity:background/Guild Scion of Rank), @[Guild Agent](entity:background/Guild Agent), @[Paladin Officer](entity:background/Paladin Officer)) recognizes Velvet without rolling. Not his face but his kind: his bearing, the way he carries papers, his waiting before speaking. *This man is the man of a great institution, and he stands here on its behalf.*

Other characters understand with **Insight DC 13** that he is not one of the wharf's people; they cannot tell whose man he is.

**The Custar identity is not revealed in Act 1.** Everything in the secrets field is kept for later: Velvet does not say which seat's man he is, and in this act there is no other card that could say it. The only thing this card gives is that **a** seat has a hand in the harbor.

mapping.name: Enamel
mapping.description: The jeweler of @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor). She has a workbench in the back room of one of the shacks; she takes in rings, mends chains, and does work no one asks about too. She tells no one her clan name.
mapping.appearance:
A short, stocky dwarf woman over a hundred years old. She wears her red hair in a single thick braid over her shoulder; at the end of the braid is a small iron ring. She has no beard. Her eyebrows are bushy, her eyes small and attentive. On the bridge of her nose are two red dents left by spectacles.

She wears a leather apron; its pockets are full of files, tweezers and wire. Her fingertips are grey with metal dust, her nails cut very short. On her workbench are laid out fine files, a small anvil, a loupe and a jar full of small stamping hammers. Her room smells of hot coal and brass dust.
mapping.mannerisms:
Asked her name, she says *"Enamel"* and falls silent. If anyone asks her clan, she moves on to the next job and does not look up again.

When she takes a piece of metal in hand she first weighs it, then holds it to the light. She does not talk while she works: *"Wait. Or go."*
mapping.goals: That her workbench stays open, and that no one asks about her clan.
mapping.secrets:
**She is the one who filed the ring.** She flattened the seal face of @[The Sealless Ring](entity:trinket/The Sealless Ring) at her own workbench.

**She strikes no stamp.** For a jeweler a stamp is a signature, and Enamel left her name behind. That is why none of her work can be traced.

**She saw the old face before filing it.** A mark with no counterpart on this continent: it resembled no house, no guild, nothing in any index. She does not know what it is, but she can describe it.

**She does not say her clan name.** For a dwarf this is heavier than a human saying *"I have no name"*. Enamel left her old name and her ties behind of her own will.
mapping.dmNotes:
**If the characters ask.** Enamel does not talk about her customers' work. If the characters put the ring in front of her, she looks at it a long time and says *"good work"*, nothing more.

**Finding her.** No one can point her out by name; they can point out her workbench. @[Mouse](entity:npc/Mouse) knows both the shack and what she does — jewelry, rings, chains; @[Twine](entity:npc/Twine) knows too. @[Corvin](entity:npc/Corvin), who has been bringing goods to the wharf for years, also knows the door.

If the characters give her a good reason, she does not deny filing it. She cannot say for whom she did it, because she does not know: a captain left the money and gave no name.

**Getting her to describe the old face.** If the characters insist, Enamel draws the mark she remembers on paper. The drawing opens no door in Act 1 — no one recognizes it. Give it to the player, and keep it.

mapping.name: Rector — Quarion
mapping.description:
The Wizards' Guild's seat in the Assembly. Quarion has no house; the seat came by the Assembly's appointment, and Quarion is known by a single name. In sessions Quarion is usually the first to speak.

*"We tested. No detection spell showed anything. What is not seen does not exist."*
mapping.appearance:
An elf; their age cannot be read from the face. Thin, long-faced, thin-lipped. Silver hair falls dead straight to the shoulders and not a single strand strays. The eyes are pale grey.

Quarion wears a navy academy robe, its collar embroidered with silver thread. There are no rings on the fingers. The wall behind the seat is the only bare wall in the hall. When seated, Quarion joins their fingers on the table and does not move them for the whole session. Smells faintly of ink and sulfur.
mapping.mannerisms:
Quarion speaks in definite sentences and likes to end them with *"does not exist"*, *"cannot be"*, *"was not shown"*. When answering a question, Quarion never raises their voice.

When someone objects, Quarion tilts their head slightly to one side, as if having spotted an interesting mistake.
mapping.goals: That the guild's dependence on the Assembly does not show.
mapping.secrets: **The test was done, but its result could not be read.** The detection spells showed that something **is** on the sick; they could not show what. Quarion says this as *"nothing was seen"*.
mapping.dmNotes:
**If the characters press.** If the characters insistently ask which test was done, who did it and how the result was written, Quarion's certainty cracks. Quarion stops saying *"what is not seen does not exist"* and, once, with a brief pause, says *"we could not see"*. Nothing more than that.

Because Quarion owes the seat to the Assembly, Quarion does not openly say something the Assembly does not want to hear.

mapping.name: Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar
mapping.description:
The Border and Trade Guild's seat in the Assembly, and head of House Sancar. He carries the Assembly's oldest seal, and is the Assembly's poorest member.

The only seat holder who does not deny the sickness — and the man no one in the hall trusts.
mapping.appearance:
A tall, bony man in his sixties. His face is long, his cheeks sunken; his grey beard short and neat. There are bags under his eyes. The crown of his head is bald; he combs what hair remains back.

He wears the oldest coat in the hall: dark brown, of good wool, but shiny at the elbows. Its collar has been carefully resewn and the seam shows. On the index finger of his right hand is a heavy seal ring with a worn stone. When he speaks his voice is tired but calm.
mapping.mannerisms:
He speaks, and while he speaks no one in the hall turns to look at him. He knows this, and still carries his sentence through to the end.

When listening to someone he leans forward and rests his elbows on his knees. When making a promise he turns his ring: *"I have no money. What I can give is a signature."*
mapping.goals: That the border gates and trade open again, and that his house stays standing.
mapping.secrets:
**His record is dirty; this matter of his is clean.** For thirty years Orvan played favorites, ran schemes, took signature for signature. There is no one in the city who does not know it. What he says about the sickness is true, and that is exactly why no one listens.

**He favored his own clerk himself.** @[Corin Sancar](entity:npc/Corin Sancar) at the @[Countersign Desk](entity:location/Countersign Desk) sits at that desk thanks to Orvan. If the characters use Orvan's name, that door opens.

**He recognizes the real names — in two ways.** Saying the names *Cortia* and *Portia Greenbottle* is enough; but a description is enough too: two halfling spouses from the Beyond, wearing expensive cloth, giving separate surnames. If either comes to the table, Orvan says three sentences, and does not say the fourth:

1. *"These two names are not strange to me. Free traders; their names are written on the other continent."*
2. *"Someone whose name is written comes through customs: enters by the gate, gives their name, pays their tax."*
3. *"If they didn't come that way, and especially if they came by a hidden road, there's a problem. And the problem isn't them. It's whoever brought them across."*

He does not know how the three strangers fell sick.
mapping.dmNotes:
**Why he believes.** The sickness came in over the border, and the border's ledger is in his guild. He was the first to see the sickness. In the Assembly he is right, but in the hall his word carries no weight at all.

**Why no one trusts him.** Not because he lies; because he wants something in return for everything. He worked this way for thirty years, and now he has nothing left to give. His record gives reason enough not to trust him; this matter stands outside that record.

**Playing him.** He does not beg. He bargains like a merchant, because he has nothing in hand but bargaining. If the characters throw his record in his face he does not deny it: *"All true. What I'm saying today is true too."*

**His offer.** Orvan has an offer in hand (@[The Offer at the Door](entity:scene/The Offer at the Door)). When and where he makes it is not written: he makes it if the characters reach him, or if he finds them useful. It does not have to be at the door of the hall.

**What he wants.** Ships are going missing: to find out why they go missing, to stop it if need be, and proof of the sickness that cannot be denied in the Assembly (@[Where They Came From](entity:quest/Where They Came From)). He does not know himself why the ships go missing.

**He does not sign himself, and he pays in advance.** He has his guild's signatory, @[Signatory — Selvi](entity:npc/Signatory — Selvi), sign, before the job; the share of his house's inheritance comes when the job is done (@[Good Writ](entity:quest/Good Writ)). If a name is needed to write on the passage paper, he knows the way too: the cellar of the @[Bargemen's Inn](entity:location/Bargemen's Inn).

**He knows the north.** To someone who wants more about the sickness, he can say that a tribe that reads nature lives at the continent's far north (@[Radenhall Courtyard](entity:location/Radenhall Courtyard)).

mapping.name: Head Journeyman — Adrik Ferrun
mapping.description:
The Smithing and Labor Guild's seat in the Assembly, and head of House Ferrun. He speaks for the continent's most crowded guild.

*"The workbenches are turning, production hasn't dropped. A sick man can't swing a hammer."*
mapping.appearance:
A broad, heavy dwarf of about two hundred. His arms are thick as if he had just come away from the anvil; an old burn scar shines on his right forearm. His black beard falls to his chest and is gathered in three places with iron rings.

He wears a dark red vest and a thick linen shirt with the sleeves rolled up. In front of him lies a pile of papers of figures, and he goes through the figures one by one with his thick finger. The smell of coal and iron has never left him.
mapping.mannerisms:
He says figures, not names: *"Last month four hundred and twelve workbenches worked. This month, four hundred and twelve."*

When he does not like a question he sets his fist on the table, without striking it.
mapping.goals: That the day wages are not cut, and that the workbenches keep turning.
mapping.secrets: **The figures did not drop, because the same men are working two shifts.** New names were written in place of the workers who fell sick or did not come; nothing looks missing in the ledger.
mapping.dmNotes: **If the characters press.** If the characters ask not how many workbenches are working but who is working (names, shifts, those who did not come), Adrik is forced to turn from figures to people. He admits that some masters and journeymen are sick and that others have been written in their places.

mapping.name: Chief Physician — Caramip Kalender
mapping.description:
The Alchemy and Healers' Guild's seat in the Assembly, and head of House Kalender. Their guild decides who may practice medicine in the city, and how it is written down why someone died.

*"This is not something unknown, it is an advanced fever. It has a name, it has a treatment."*
mapping.appearance:
An old, short gnome who moves quickly. White, fluffy hair sticks out on either side of the ears. The nose is long, its tip red. The eyes are small, black, and constantly roaming the room.

Wears a green physician's robe whose pockets are full of small bottles stoppered with cork. With every movement the bottles clink against each other. The fingers are yellowed by plant juice. Smells of mint, camphor and alcohol.
mapping.mannerisms:
When speaking of the sickness Caramip always uses the same word: *fever.* On hearing another word, Caramip cuts in and corrects it.

Speaks quickly and starts the next sentence before finishing one. When cornered, takes a bottle from a pocket, uncorks it, sniffs it and closes it.
mapping.goals: That the guild does not look helpless.
mapping.secrets:
**Caramip had the sickness's declarations changed.** The first declarations spoke of an unknown sickness; Caramip had them rewritten as *fever*. Admitting not to know would bring down the claim on which the guild's right to grant licenses rests.

A copy of the first declaration is with the apprentice @[Sindri](entity:npc/Sindri).
mapping.dmNotes: **If the characters press.** If the characters ask the treatment's name, which patient it worked on, and the name of someone who recovered, Caramip cannot answer. Caramip tries to change the subject; if cornered, says *"the investigation is ongoing"* and falls silent.

mapping.name: Registrar — Valen Custar
mapping.description:
The Military Law Guild's seat in the Assembly, and head of House Custar. He holds the city's criminal record, policing authority and the right to declare quarantine.

*"Sickness is not a legal category. Quarantine requires martial law; there is no declared war."*
mapping.appearance:
A man in his fifties, of medium height, who sits rigidly. His face is clean-shaven, his jaw square. His dark hair is short, his temples gone white. His unmoving eyes see the whole hall.

He wears a black legal robe with a dark collar; on his chest his house's silver sword sign. He keeps his hands on his knees. Not once during the session does he lean back. He smells of soap and leather.
mapping.mannerisms:
He speaks in short, orderly sentences. When relying on a law he gives its article by number: *"Ninth book, fourteenth article."*

When asked a question, before answering he translates the question into legal language.
mapping.goals: Not to be forced to use his authority.
mapping.secrets:
**He has the authority to declare quarantine.** He has not used it for two seasons, because the day he uses it, all the responsibility becomes his too.

His house takes a share from the harbor: @[Velvet](entity:npc/Velvet) on the wharf is a Custar.
mapping.dmNotes: **If the characters press.** If the characters show that not declaring quarantine is also a decision, and that this decision too will be tied to his name, Valen's silence breaks. He begins listing the legal conditions for quarantine; this is admitting the authority is in his hands.

npc.source_name: Master of the Board — Perhun Mizan

mapping.name: Master of the Board — Perhun Mizan
mapping.description:
The Architecture and Planning Guild's seat in the Assembly, and head of House Mizan. His guild plans the city's waterways, district boundaries and walls.

*"This city was planned so that it would not fall sick: the water flows separately, the wind cleans."*
mapping.appearance:
A thin, tall man in his forties. His face is narrow, his nose aquiline. His light-brown hair reaches his shoulders and is tied with a ribbon. His fingers are long, with pencil dust under the nails.

He wears a grey jacket, plain but very well tailored; a compass and a ruler show from his pocket. In front of him lies a rolled city plan, and as he talks he keeps smoothing the roll's curling edge. He smells of parchment and wax.
mapping.mannerisms:
When he speaks of the city he says *the plan*: *"In the plan, the eastern district's water is separate."* He does not realize he is speaking not of the city itself but of paper.

If someone describes something they saw in the street, he opens the plan and finds the place with his finger.
mapping.goals: That the city's plan is not questioned.
mapping.secrets: **The wall repairs stayed on paper.** The plan shows a repaired wall; the wall was not repaired. For some time the plan has not described the city correctly.
mapping.dmNotes: **If the characters press.** If the characters describe the present state of the wall or a waterway as they saw it with their own eyes, Perhun cannot deny the difference between the plan and the street. He first opens the plan, then closes it, and admits the repairs were postponed.

mapping.name: Corin Sancar
mapping.description: The clerk at the @[Countersign Desk](entity:location/Countersign Desk). Passage papers come from his hands: he writes the name and details, he gives the preliminary approval. A member of House Sancar, but not at the head of the house — behind a desk.
mapping.appearance:
A thin, pale man in his late twenties. His black hair has begun thinning early and is carefully combed to one side. His face is shaven, his lips thin. His eyes are tired but quick.

He wears a dark blue clerk's robe; its cuffs are shiny from rubbing against the desk. On the side of his right hand is a blue ink stain that never comes off. The pile of signatures on his desk never gets smaller. He smells of ink and sand.
mapping.mannerisms:
Before reading a paper he looks at the signatures below it. If he does not like the signatures, he slides the paper to the bottom of the pile without reading it.

He says *no* to no one: *"Pending. Its signature will come."*
mapping.goals: That it be known he sits at that desk because of his work, not because of his name.
mapping.secrets:
**He sits at that desk through the favor of @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar).** A member of the house, but not its head. He got the desk not because he earned it but because of his name. He knows this, and does not like it.

**Orvan's name is both a debt and a burden on him.** When he hears that name he signs, and while signing he is angry.
mapping.dmNotes:
**He says no to no one.** A paper he does not want to sign he slides unread to the bottom of the pile and says *"pending"*. The obstacle the characters face is not a refusal but a stretch of time. The pile never gets smaller.

**Two levers:**

- **A bribe.** The easiest, and this is the desk on the continent where the most bribes are paid. It leaves no trace, no one is surprised.
- **Orvan's name.** It works, but it diminishes Corin: he signs, and he does not let the characters forget it.

Scene: @[In Line at the Passage Court](entity:scene/In Line at the Passage Court).

mapping.name: Signatory — Selvi

location_ref.value: Border and Trade Guild Council Chamber

mapping.description: The signatory who sits in the signatory room of the @[Border and Trade Guild Council Chamber](entity:location/Border and Trade Guild Council Chamber): one of the hands that countersign passage papers. When @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar) has a paper to be signed, he puts it in front of her.
mapping.appearance:
A thin, upright human woman in her forties. Her dark hair is cut short; a reading glass on her nose, its cord around her neck. Her fingertips are permanently blue with ink.

The Council Chamber's hearth is never lit: a shawl over her dark wool robe, fingerless gloves on her hands. On her desk three different inks, a stick of sealing wax and a stone to weigh down the papers. She smells of beeswax and cold stone.
mapping.mannerisms:
Before signing a paper she reads it from beginning to end, moving her lips. When she sees a place left blank she reaches for the pen: *"No blank space stays blank. If it does, I fill it in, and it goes out under my name."*

Her room is quiet, and she likes it staying quiet. When the line at the room in the Assembly House is mentioned, she smiles.
mapping.goals: That her signature means something: that her name never stands under a paper she has not read.
mapping.secrets: **She knows that some of the names on the papers Orvan brings come from the cellar** (@[Bargemen's Inn](entity:location/Bargemen's Inn)). She does not ask. Every line she reads is written correctly; whether it is true is not her business.
mapping.dmNotes:
**Orvan's advance signature.** If the offer was accepted (@[The Offer at the Door](entity:scene/The Offer at the Door)), Orvan himself puts the paper that came from the desk with its preliminary approval in front of Selvi, and Selvi countersigns it, before the job. The paper's preliminary approval comes from the desk (@[Countersign Desk](entity:location/Countersign Desk)); Selvi fills in the places left blank and signs.

**If the characters ask.** She knows all three signatory rooms: the most crowded one in the @[Assembly House](entity:location/Assembly House), the quietest one her own, the one in Elymsyr right by the ships (@[Customs House](entity:location/Customs House)).

Quests: @[Good Writ](entity:quest/Good Writ) · @[Where They Came From](entity:quest/Where They Came From).

mapping.name: Kildrak Ferrun
mapping.description: The assay master in Lucid Triton's smiths' market. Measures the purity of metals and reads the index that shows which workbench each assay stamp belongs to.
mapping.appearance:
A dwarf nearing three hundred, back slightly bent. The white beard reaches the knees and is folded once at the waist and tucked into the belt. The eyebrows droop over the eyes. A thick loupe-glass sits on the nose.

In the pocket of the leather apron, a magnifying glass; on the workbench, stamping hammers lined up by size. The hands are surprisingly steady for that age. The noise of the smiths' market reaches the workbench, but Kildrak does not look up. Smells of oil and brass.
mapping.mannerisms:
Before taking a piece of metal in hand, Kildrak holds it to the light and turns it. On seeing a stamp, Kildrak names not its owner but its workbench: *"Harbor work. Fresh. Struck left-handed."*

Kildrak leaves impatient customers waiting, and does it on purpose.
mapping.goals: That the profession stays clean.
mapping.secrets: **Kildrak has seen a filed seal ring before**, and not just once. None of them had a stamp.
mapping.dmNotes:
**If the characters bring the ring.** Kildrak holds the ring to the light, turns it, lowers the loupe. Then does not open the index — there is nothing to open it for:

*"There's no assay stamp on this. Never struck. The workmanship is good, but not labored over: whoever did it knew the work, but hurried and didn't sign it."*

*"On this continent a jeweler who does unstamped work doesn't sit at a guild workbench. Go south. Look for a harbor. If you can find one, your smith is there."*

Kildrak cannot give a name, because Kildrak does not know one. What Kildrak gives is a direction, and that direction leads to @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor).

**Kildrak also sees the filed face** and says what it means: *"Someone wanted to erase whose ring this is."*

mapping.name: Sindri
mapping.description: A young alchemist's apprentice working in the healers' barracks. One of the hands that write out the guild's declarations fair.
mapping.appearance:
A young gnome woman; in her early twenties, small but fully grown. She has short, messy, blond hair that someone has not found the time to cut. Her nose is freckled, her eyes large and blue.

She wears the guild's green apprentice apron; its pockets are full of rolls of paper. Her fingers are two different colors: her right hand blue from ink, her left green from plant juice. She is always hurrying somewhere down the barracks corridor with a roll of papers in hand. She smells of camphor and ink.
mapping.mannerisms:
She can read a declaration from memory, and while reading it she does not change a single word. She cannot help correcting someone who repeats a sentence wrong.

When she gets excited she talks fast and touches her nose as if pushing up her spectacles, though she is not wearing any.
mapping.goals: That what she writes stays true.
mapping.secrets: **She has the copy of the first declaration.** @[Chief Physician — Caramip Kalender](entity:npc/Chief Physician — Caramip Kalender) had the declarations changed. While writing out the first declaration fair, Sindri set aside a copy for herself and hid it. This copy is the document proving that the sickness was known in the city and was rewritten under another name.
mapping.dmNotes:
**If the characters ask.** Sindri is afraid to talk about the declarations; she would be going against her master and her guild. If the characters give her confidence and convince her they will not use the copy for a bad purpose (for example by telling what they saw in the cabin), she admits the copy exists and shows it. She does not want to let the copy out of her hands.

**She knows where the sherbet comes from.** The @[Sherbet of Resistance](entity:adventuring-gear/Sherbet of Resistance) is made in the barracks, but that the recipe came from the north, from the druids of @[Radenhall Courtyard](entity:location/Radenhall Courtyard), is known in the guild and not said.

mapping.name: Lamp
mapping.description: An indebted tradesman in the Lucid Triton market. The only person in the city known by a nickname: once he had a name and a tie to a house; when he fell into debt he lost both.
mapping.appearance:
A tall man in his forties, but with drooping shoulders. His face is lined, the skin under his eyes purple. His thin light-brown hair is combed behind his ears. His nose was once broken and knit crooked.

He wears a jacket that was once good and is now patched at the elbows. His stall is half empty: a few lamps, a box of wicks, two bottles of oil. On the wall above the shelves, two nails where a sign once hung. His stall smells of lamp oil.
mapping.mannerisms:
When he talks about the guild police he does not lower his voice, but before starting the sentence he looks to both ends of the market.

He has a bitter humor: *"What was my name? I forgot. They didn't forget my debt, though."*
mapping.goals: That his debt is deferred, and that one day he can hang his sign again.
mapping.secrets:
He knows whom the guild police beat in the market, and who ordered it.

Once he had a name. He lost it to debt; only his nickname remained.
mapping.dmNotes:
**If the characters ask.** Lamp explains how the market and the street work: which guild's police do what on which street, whose word counts where, the price of a bribe in the city. In return he wants a contribution to his debt or a favor.

**He knows where a name is written.** As someone who lost his name to debt, he also knows where in the city a new name is to be had: the cellar of the @[Bargemen's Inn](entity:location/Bargemen's Inn). He does not say this for nothing either.

mapping.name: Innkeeper — Aysel
mapping.description: The owners of the @[Bargemen's Inn](entity:location/Bargemen's Inn): Aysel and her husband Kerem. Aysel stands behind the counter and chalks the bargemen's debts on the wall; Kerem opens the barrels. No one stands at the head of the stair down to the cellar; there is no need, because the counter faces the stair.
mapping.appearance:
Two tieflings in their fifties, husband and wife. Aysel is broad-shouldered, thick-wristed; her skin is ash-red, and she has short horns curling back from her forehead. She has tied her greying black hair behind her horns with a cloth; her sleeves are rolled to the elbow, her apron stained with beer and onion.

Kerem is a head taller than her, thin and slightly stooped; he has a tired, ordinary face; his skin is ash-grey, faintly purplish, the tip of his left horn broken, his thin tail curling at the foot of his boots. He carries a barrel cloth on his shoulder. The wall behind them is full of chalk lines: each bargeman's debt is a column. They smell of yeast and frying fat.
mapping.mannerisms:
Before looking at a customer, Aysel looks at their shoes: if they are muddy, it is a bargeman; if they are clean, they have come for some other business. When asked a question she starts wiping the counter with a cloth, and answers while wiping.

*"Downstairs is the cellar. What's in the cellar? Barrels."*

Kerem talks little. While his wife answers he pulls the bung from a barrel, and he says the end of the sentence.
mapping.goals: That the inn is full, and the bargemen's debts are paid.
mapping.secrets: Both of them see who goes down the stair, and they are paid for pretending not to have seen. They know what is done below; neither of them has ever gone down.
mapping.dmNotes:
**The cellar door.** The way to the cellar is pointed out by @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar) or @[Lamp](entity:npc/Lamp); the one who lets you down the stair is Aysel. To someone who says who sent them, she nods toward the stair. To someone who does not, she talks about barrels.

**If the characters ask.** She knows which barge came when, and when which bargeman will go down the river (@[Bargeman — Rüstem](entity:npc/Bargeman — Rüstem)).

Quest: @[Good Writ](entity:quest/Good Writ).

mapping.name: Bargeman — Rüstem
mapping.description: A bargeman hauling a barge on the Golden River. He carries loads from @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr) to the @[River Loading Yard](entity:location/River Loading Yard), takes the weighbridge slip, and before taking his money counts his slips one by one at the inn's table.
mapping.appearance:
A big, sun-darkened human man in his late thirties. His hands are calloused from rope; on his right palm is the mark of an old rope burn. White strands in his thick black beard.

He wears a sleeveless vest and trousers rolled to the knee; river mud has dried on his bare feet. At his belt a roll of weighbridge slips tied with string. He smells of wet hemp and the river.
mapping.mannerisms:
When he counts the slips his lips move, and until the count is done he answers no one. He calls Elymsyr *"downriver"* and Lucid Triton *"upriver"*.

*"Upriver comes heavy, downriver light. These last months upriver's light too."*
mapping.goals: That the weighbridge slip matches the list, and that he is paid in full.
mapping.secrets: **The weighbridge does not match the list.** The load written on the cargo list that comes by barge from @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr) weighs lighter on the weighbridge of the @[River Loading Yard](entity:location/River Loading Yard); these last months, always. That is why he counts his slips. He has told no one, and no one has asked.
mapping.dmNotes:
**The river road.** His barge goes down to @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr) empty or half empty, and takes passengers. What he asks in return is the DM's.

**His slips.** Put side by side with the list copies in the register room of the @[Border and Trade Guild Council Chamber](entity:location/Border and Trade Guild Council Chamber), the slips show the load unloaded short: the trace in Lucid Triton of the governor's ledger in the @[Customs House](entity:location/Customs House).

Quests: @[Where They Came From](entity:quest/Where They Came From) · @[Good Writ](entity:quest/Good Writ) · @[The Continent on the Horizon](entity:quest/The Continent on the Horizon).

mapping.name: Needle
mapping.description: The gnome who makes ready names and clothes in the cellar of the @[Bargemen's Inn](entity:location/Bargemen's Inn). She is the one who writes the name and the one who sews the clothes. No one knows her own name; her nickname comes from her work.
mapping.appearance:
A small, wiry gnome woman in her sixties. Her white hair is in a tight bun, and three or four needles are stuck through the bun. She has no spectacles; she threads a needle on the first try.

She wears a dark, plain dress; a pincushion is pinned to her chest. On her table, an inkwell, a pair of scissors, and piles of folded cloth: a clerk's jacket, a deckhand's shirt, an apprentice's caftan. The cellar's air smells of lamp oil and new cloth.
mapping.mannerisms:
With someone who comes in, she looks first not at their face but at the width of their shoulders and at their hands; the name comes after that. Before writing a name she says it out loud once, then has the other person say it.

*"Again. Until it sits in your mouth."*
mapping.goals: That her work stays clean: that none of the names she gives is ever unpicked on a wharf.
mapping.secrets: **She remembers every name she has given.** No ledger is kept in the cellar; there is no need for one. She is the only person who knows which name was given to whom.
mapping.dmNotes:
**Where the name comes from.** The name she writes is not invented: it is a line written in the ledger of the @[Border and Trade Guild](entity:lore/Border and Trade Guild) by the hand of @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar). Needle makes that line wearable: a name, and clothes to match that name.

**The order.** A passage paper is collected under a name. Whoever leaves the cellar goes to the @[Countersign Desk](entity:location/Countersign Desk) under that name.

**The price.** What she asks in return is the DM's.

Quest: @[Good Writ](entity:quest/Good Writ).

mapping.name: Sergeant Krusk
mapping.description: A guild police sergeant in Lucid Triton. Serves at the city gates by day and on patrol by night.
mapping.appearance:
A heavily built half-orc in their thirties. Thick, greenish-grey skin, two short tusks jutting up from the lower lip. Black hair in a tight topknot ponytail. One ear torn.

The police badge on the chest is polished; the chain mail beneath it is not, and is rust-stained. A club and a short sword hang at the belt. Garlic on the breath.
mapping.mannerisms:
Krusk says that an order was received, not who gave it: *"Those are the orders. You can't pass."*

While talking, Krusk looks past the other person, at who is coming through the gate. Krusk does not get angry at an offered bribe; Krusk listens to the figure.
mapping.goals: That no trouble comes up on watch.
mapping.secrets: Krusk knows that the orders received come not from the Military Law Guild itself but from **a single house**.
mapping.dmNotes: **If the characters ask.** Krusk knows who goes in and out of the city gates, who walks about at night and where the patrol is at which hours. Krusk does not tell this easily; wants a good reason or a good fee.

mapping.name: Customs Governor
mapping.description: The governor who runs Elymsyr in the Council's name. Head of the customs and the city's richest official. His office is on the highest terrace, in a palace that looks out on the river.
mapping.appearance:
A short, plump man in his fifties. His face is round and clean-shaven, his cheeks red. His hair is thin and carefully oiled. Three different rings on his fingers, one with a dark ruby.

He wears a dark green velvet jacket with gold embroidery; its buttons strain at his belly. On his desk, open ledgers, and on top of the ledgers a chart showing the ships' arrival times. His room smells of cloves and beeswax; through the window comes the sound of the cranes' chains.
mapping.mannerisms:
He answers a question with a figure: *"A hundred and thirteen ships last month. Every one written down."* A question that has no figure he pretends not to have heard.

While talking he turns one of his rings on his finger.

He addresses his deputy not by name but only as *sir*.
mapping.goals: That the figures look tidy, and that his seat stays safe.
mapping.secrets: **He knows that loads unloaded short are written as complete in the ledger.** Some ships unload less than they declare; the governor shows them as complete in the ledger.
mapping.dmNotes:
**If the characters ask.** The governor helps with official passage: customs permission to board a ship, fees, waiting times. A passage paper that came from the @[Countersign Desk](entity:location/Countersign Desk), that is, a good writ, gets you onto a ship in Elymsyr as well.

If asked about short loads, he shows the figures, and the figures are flawless. Unless the characters compare the ledgers with what they saw on the wharf, they find nothing.

**He has an offer.** He does not want the @[Military Law Guild](entity:lore/Military Law Guild) setting up a room in the harbor, and he has a job to give to faces no one knows: @[The Masked Job](entity:quest/The Masked Job). The offer is carried by @[The Governor's Deputy](entity:npc/The Governor's Deputy).

Scene: @[The Customs Wharf](entity:scene/The Customs Wharf).

mapping.name: River Guard Sergeant
mapping.description: The sergeant of the River Guard who keep watch in the towers of the narrows. The towers, the ballistae and the chain are her responsibility.
mapping.appearance:
A bony, tall woman in her forties. Her face is reddened and flaking from the river wind; her lips cracked. She keeps her red hair cropped very short. Two fingers of her right hand were crushed in a ballista string and knit crooked.

She wears the Guard's blue-grey cloak and leather armor. A tower's key ring jingles at her belt. How many times a day she goes up and down the tower stairs shows in the slight bend of her knees as she walks. She smells of river water and oiled leather.
mapping.mannerisms:
When the chain is mentioned she turns the subject to the ballistae: *"Forget the chain. Look at my ballistae."*

She does not shout when giving orders; the guards listen to her anyway.
mapping.goals: That the chain never has to be tried in real danger.
mapping.secrets: **She knows the chain mechanism is neglected.** The chain tried at the ceremonies rises with difficulty every time; in a real attack it might not rise in time.
mapping.dmNotes: **If the characters ask.** The sergeant knows which ship passed through the narrows when, the towers' watch schedule and the ballistae's range. If the characters win her trust (by helping a guard, or by showing they come from the Order or the army), she also tells the state of the chain.

mapping.name: Crane Master
mapping.description: The master of the gnome cranes on the Elymsyr wharf. Knows every crane, every gear, every chain by name.
mapping.appearance:
A short, muscular gnome in their fifties. The coal-black beard is shortened by burns in places. Around the eyes is a clean ring left by protective goggles; the rest of the face is blackened with grease.

Wears a grease-stained apron with torn pockets. Three wrenches of different sizes and a hammer swing at the belt. Is usually found with an ear pressed to a crane's gears, eyes closed, listening. Smells of machine oil and hot metal.
mapping.mannerisms:
Speaks of a crane like a person: *"This old girl's being fussy today. She's tired. She works better at night."*

When answering a question, wipes their hands on the apron and spreads the grease even further.
mapping.goals: That the workshop and the cranes keep working.
mapping.secrets: **Provides a crane for some night unloadings.** These loads are not written in the customs ledger. Goods that do not pass through customs thus enter the continent through the official harbor too.
mapping.dmNotes:
**If the characters ask.** The Crane Master at first denies the night work. If the characters see with their own eyes that the cranes work at night, or show they are someone to be trusted, the Crane Master explains how a load that skips customs gets through Elymsyr and how much it costs.

Even if the characters never go to Hidden Harbor, they can learn from the Crane Master how passage without customs is bought.

mapping.name: The Interpreter
mapping.description: A half-elf interpreter waiting for work on the Elymsyr wharf. He sells language to the foreigners who come with the ships, to customs officials and to merchants.
mapping.appearance:
A slender half-elf man in his thirties. He has braided his long black hair on one side and let the other side fall loose. Three earrings in one pointed ear, one in the other.

He wears pieces from the fashions of three different harbors: a narrow-cut vest from the Beyond, a linen shirt of Meridian make, a striped, wide sash from somewhere no one knows the name of. On the wharf he waits at the spot closest to the ships' gangplanks. He smells of cinnamon and tobacco.
mapping.mannerisms:
Before translating a sentence he asks for whom he is translating: *"For you, or for him? The price changes."*

While talking he switches from language to language; when he cannot find a word in the Meridian tongue he says it in the tongue of the Beyond and shrugs.
mapping.goals: The next job.
mapping.secrets: He keeps everything he hears and holds it in mind.
mapping.dmNotes: **If the characters ask.** The Interpreter tells the fresh news carried by ships from @[the Beyond](entity:location/Vorstrand): what is being talked about there, which harbors have closed, which goods have grown dearer. None of this news can be verified in Meridia. He wants a fee in return.

mapping.name: Captain — Maren
mapping.description: The captain of a trading ship sailing from @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr), the *Honest Scales*. Her ship comes with a legal cargo and leaves with a legal cargo; part of her crew are passengers signed on with a countersigned paper.
mapping.appearance:
A short, stocky human woman in her fifties. Her grey hair is in a tight bun at the nape; her face is darkened by sun and salt, with deep lines at the corners of her eyes. Two fingers of her right hand are cut off at the second joint.

She wears a captain's jacket of grey wool, worn but clean; the corner of a crew list sticks out of her breast pocket. At her belt, a pen case and a rope knife. She smells of tar, ink and wet wool.
mapping.mannerisms:
When she takes a passage paper in hand, she looks first at the signature, then at the face: *"The paper doesn't concern me. The signature does."*

She calls her crew not by name but by job: *"Bow! Rope!"* She does not ask the name of someone newly signed on until they have finished their first watch.
mapping.goals: That her ship sails full every time, and comes back whole.
mapping.secrets: **She knew one of the missing ships.** One of the ships that should have come to Elymsyr was the ship of one of her former crew. She told no one at customs; even if she had, the ledger would not have changed.
mapping.dmNotes:
**The voyage.** She signs on characters who carry a countersigned passage paper as crew: she takes no fare, she wants watches. She cannot sign on someone without a paper, because the crew list is counted at customs along with the cargo. Scene: @[The Customs Wharf](entity:scene/The Customs Wharf). Ships boarded for money are at @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor) (@[Bargaining for Passage](entity:scene/Bargaining for Passage)).

**If the characters ask.** She gives the name of one of the ships that should have come to Elymsyr and did not (@[Where They Came From](entity:quest/Where They Came From)). She does not know why it did not come.

**The ship.** @[Honest Scales](entity:location/Honest Scales); its guards are led by @[Scales Sergeant — Hulda](entity:npc/Scales Sergeant — Hulda).

**The course.** She does not take the trade route; she draws a wide arc far from the route the missing ships followed. Scene: @[Maren's Course](entity:scene/Maren's Course).

Quests: @[The Continent on the Horizon](entity:quest/The Continent on the Horizon) · @[Where They Came From](entity:quest/Where They Came From). The end of the voyage: @[Land Ho](entity:scene/Land Ho).

mapping.name: Lord Commander — Varhan
mapping.description:
Votumar's Lord Commander. The sole holder of the administrative, judicial and military authority in the castle and the region. A commander the people and the soldiers truly love and trust.

**He has not been at the castle for two months.** He was known as a man who never left the camp; now he is in @[Lucid Triton](entity:location/Lucid Triton), with only one of his two deputies beside him. His orders reach the castle by word of mouth.
mapping.appearance:
Apparently in his late forties, a tall, broad-shouldered human. His face is regular, square-jawed; his short grey hair flawlessly combed. His eyes are light brown.

He wears the white cloak and polished plate armor of the Order of the Silver Shield. There is not a single scratch on his armor. His bearing is flawless, his steps measured. When he speaks nothing in his face changes: not a smile, not a raised eyebrow. Someone looking closely may notice that he never blinks.
mapping.mannerisms:
He gives his orders verbally and does not repeat them. When handed a paper he does not read it; he asks whoever brought it to tell him.

His voice is calm, his sentences short: *"The bay is safe. The people are safe. Return to your duty."*
mapping.goals: Obedience, and gaining time.
mapping.secrets:
**The Lord Commander is a Faceless.** King Lucian's hand; the will behind him is not his own.

The people and the soldiers obey him not because they fear him but **because they truly trust him**. A Faceless sitting in this seat does not need to persuade anyone; sitting there is enough.

**The real Lord Commander is being held somewhere.**

**For the last two months he has not given a single written order.** The two-point order he left when he departed, at the start of those two months, is the last written thing from his hand, and it is only with @[Deputy Lord Commander — Aren](entity:npc/Deputy Lord Commander — Aren) (@[The Last Written Order](entity:quest/The Last Written Order)).

The Council appointed him to this seat; that is, a guild, without realizing it, seated him here with its own hand.

**He has not been to the castle for two months, and this suits him.** The absence of a beloved commander raises fewer questions than the presence of an unloved one: the soldiers complain, no one opens an inquiry. Distance protects him — the castle is two days away, and no one there speaks in his name.

The deputy he left at the castle is @[Deputy Lord Commander — Aren](entity:npc/Deputy Lord Commander — Aren); the deputy he took with him is **Belen**.
mapping.dmNotes:
**Where.** The characters cannot find him at the castle. For two months he has been in Lucid Triton; the orders that come and go to the castle on business are carried by his deputy Belen, and all of them by word of mouth. If there is to be an encounter, it will be in the capital.

**Playing him.** Do not play the Lord Commander as a villain. He is a polite, calm and effective commander. He might even help the characters, but he gives nothing in writing.

A few people in the castle each separately sense that something is wrong with the Lord Commander, and none of them knows that the others know: @[Deputy Lord Commander — Aren](entity:npc/Deputy Lord Commander — Aren) · @[Gate Commander — Nevra](entity:npc/Gate Commander — Nevra) · @[Forgemaster — Torvun](entity:npc/Forgemaster — Torvun) · @[Castle Clerk — Nerion](entity:npc/Castle Clerk — Nerion) · @[Tower Sentry — Vrask](entity:npc/Tower Sentry — Vrask).

**If the sickness comes up.** The following are ordered to follow the flow of a conversation. Go down them in order; do not use them all. His face changes in none of them.

*First he refuses:*

- *"I have listened to what you told me. This is not a sickness, it is a fear. The two spread at the same speed, but only one of them kills people."*
- *"I have been commander on this bay for eleven years. In eleven years I have heard of plague four times. None of the four came."*

*Then he explains:*

- *"On this continent a rumor of sickness rises every autumn. The cause is not sickness; it is the harvest. A man whose belly isn't full looks for a reason, and the easiest reason is something unseen."*
- *"In the provinces a fever is always a curse. In the city it is always a conspiracy. Both are the same fever."*
- *"If you answer a rumor with quarantine, you confirm it. Then the harbor closes, then the bread runs out, then people really die. I have seen that chain from beginning to end."*

*If they ask for proof — the bar cannot be reached, but it looks reasonable:*

- *"How many dead? ... Three. And all three arrived there already sick, you said so yourselves. You have not described an epidemic to me. You have described three dead."*
- *"I do not question what you saw. I question the name you give what you saw."*
- *"Bring me a sealed physician's report. Then we will talk."* — The man who would give that seal is @[Chief Physician — Caramip Kalender](entity:npc/Chief Physician — Caramip Kalender), that is, the person who changed the first declarations.

*If a paper is handed over:*

- *"I will not read it. You tell me. A man's voice says more than his paper."*

*If they insist:*

- *"Raising your voice does not confirm what you are saying."*
- *"The authority to quarantine is not in this castle. It is in @[Lucid Triton](entity:location/Lucid Triton). Two days away. Do you have a horse?"*

*He closes — the part of the conversation that looks like help:*

- *"Thank you for bringing this to me. I will do what is necessary."* And it is written down nowhere.
- *"Your road has been long. My deputy will find you a place to stay."*

*If they ask for a written order or document:*

- *"Do not ask for it in writing. What is written multiplies."*
- *"I have given my word. What need is there for paper?"* — A character from the Order knows this is irregular: an order is always written.

**Scene note.** As he says these things nothing in his face changes, and he does not blink. Do not tell the players; describe it two or three times over the course of the conversation. Whoever notices, notices; whoever does not hears it from @[Deputy Lord Commander — Aren](entity:npc/Deputy Lord Commander — Aren).

**Who knows.** A character with the @[Paladin Soldier](entity:background/Paladin Soldier) or @[Paladin Officer](entity:background/Paladin Officer) background knows that the Lord Commander has not been at the castle for months and that the order complains about it — this is something talked about inside the Order. If there is no such character at the table, the chance of this news being heard before reaching Votumar is very low.

mapping.name: Gate Commander — Nevra
mapping.description: The officer who holds the gate of the castle of Votumar. Everyone who comes and goes at the castle passes in front of her.
mapping.appearance:
A woman in her late thirties, of medium height and compact build. She has tied her black hair in a tight bun at the nape. Her face is serious; there is a red line on her forehead left by the helmet.

She wears the Order's white cloak and the silver-striped pauldrons of the gate watch. The straps of her armor are buckled at the same hole every morning; the leather around the holes is worn. She always carries the watch ledger under her arm. She smells of oiled leather and sea salt.
mapping.mannerisms:
She writes everything in the ledger: who came, at what hour, on whose behalf. When she cannot write something down, she holds her pen above the paper for a while.

Her sentences are formal and complete: *"Your name. On whose behalf you have come. How long you will stay."*
mapping.goals: That her watch closes clean.
mapping.secrets:
**She knows that for the last two months the orders have come verbally.** Not a single written order has come from the Lord Commander. The watch ledger's *order* column has been empty for two months.

**The ledger has the Lord Commander's departure line, but no return line.** Two months ago he left with one of his deputies; he never came in through the gate again. Nevra sees this every morning when she opens the ledger.
mapping.dmNotes:
**If the characters ask.** The Gate Commander openly explains the rules for entering the castle and the watch schedule.

She does not talk easily about the orders; that would be questioning the Lord Commander. If the characters ask to see the watch ledger, or ask her directly how the orders come (especially if a character from the Order asks), she says only a single sentence: *"For the last two months the orders have come verbally."* She says no more than that.

She does not hide that the Lord Commander is not at the castle — everyone at the castle knows it and the soldiers openly complain. What she does not hide but also does not volunteer is the ledger itself: if asked, she shows the departure line; she does not mention the missing return line, because nothing is written there.

mapping.name: Deputy Lord Commander — Aren
mapping.description: One of the Lord Commander's two deputies at Votumar, and the one who stayed at the castle. When the Lord Commander went to the capital he took the other with him; for two months the castle's daily business has rested on Aren. She has the authority, not the orders: the orders of the castle she runs do not come from her.
mapping.appearance:
A tall, upright tiefling woman in her mid-thirties. Her skin is deep red, she has two horns curling backward, and her black hair is drawn tight at the nape. An old sword scar on her chin is a faint line — it does not harden her face, it only says where she has come from. She has a face that turns heads in the castle, and she does not use it as a card to play; it is doubtful she even notices. Her insignia are complete, her cloak flawless. Her voice is low.

Her armor is the Order's fine work: plate with carved edges, more elegant than it needs to be — not ceremonial, a master's work. On her back she carries a sword close to her own height; its hilt rises above her left shoulder.

Before speaking of the Lord Commander she looks around and makes sure the door is closed. While she talks her hand goes to the leather wrapping above her shoulder and fidgets there; meanwhile the tip of her tail never stops.
mapping.mannerisms:
She always voices her suspicion as a question, never as a claim: *"Did you see the Lord Commander blink while he was talking to you?"*

Before answering a question she is silent for a long while.
mapping.goals: To be proven wrong.
mapping.secrets:
She noticed the logical errors in the Lord Commander's orders and a coldness that was never there before. She told no one. If she did, she would have slandered a man the people love, and the price of that is honor before rank.

**She fears part of her suspicion is pride.** For years she was the one at his side; when he went to the capital, the Lord Commander took the other. Aren asks herself this question every day: *did I see something wrong, or was I left behind?* That is why she will not be the first to say it — but she will be the first to believe whoever does.

**She holds the written, sealed order the Lord Commander left when he departed, and she has shown it to no one.** Two points: *no soldiers will be sent to distant places without permission* · *rumors of sickness will be reported directly to me.* Aren reads this like a border order and obeys it to the letter — it is the last written thing to come out of the castle (@[The Last Written Order](entity:quest/The Last Written Order)).
mapping.dmNotes:
**If the characters ask.** Aren refuses to talk about the Lord Commander, and does it without rudeness: she turns the subject to the castle's business, helps the characters, behaves as if she did not hear the question.

**How she opens up.** If the characters bring her not an intuition but a gap, she listens: two months without a written order, a night that never entered the castle's ledger, a supply list that came by word of mouth. **Two** of these together are enough for her; one is not, because one can always be explained as a slip.

**The authority in her hands.** For two months the castle has in practice run on her signature. If she wishes, she can issue a written order, request an inspection of the records, draw up a sealed report, or send a letter to the capital in her own name. Which of these she will do — or whether she will do none — becomes clear at the table; the card does not write it in advance.

**She is the first voice from inside the institution to believe.** In Votumar the answer to a claim is writing, and the characters have no writing in hand; Aren does.

mapping.name: Tower Sentry — Vrask
mapping.description: A dragonborn Coast Watcher who keeps watch in one of the watchtowers. Has kept watch in the same tower for years.
mapping.appearance:
A young, large dragonborn; bronze scales dulled by salt and wind. One of the short spines running from the back of the head down the neck is broken. Bright yellow eyes.

Wears the Coast Watchers' grey cloak and light armor. The hand that holds the mirror's chain is calloused, and one finger carries a deep mark left by the chain. When Vrask speaks the voice is deep and hoarse; a faint smell of soot comes on the breath.
mapping.mannerisms:
Vrask tells what was seen completely the first time; asked a second time, tells it in the same words.

Vrask does not leave the watch ledger's side. If someone approaches the ledger, Vrask puts a hand on it.
mapping.goals: To be able to report what was seen.
mapping.secrets: **A signal Vrask sent one night did not enter the castle's ledger.** The sentry saw something at the mouth of the bay and sent the signal. The castle has no record of that night. The sentry is hiding this, because saying it would mean doubting either their own eyes or the castle.
mapping.dmNotes:
**If the characters ask.** The sentry explains how the signal system works. Says nothing of the silent night. If the characters notice the turned-down page in the ledger, or do something to win the sentry's trust (a character from the Order, or a promise to protect the sentry's honor), Vrask tells of that night and of the report that vanished.

Vrask does not know how far the report went. At the castle end of the line stands @[Watch Captain — Drahan](entity:npc/Watch Captain — Drahan), at the record end @[Castle Clerk — Nerion](entity:npc/Castle Clerk — Nerion); where the signal stopped can be read with those two.

mapping.name: Eldest Druid — Halder
mapping.description: The eldest druid of the Wardens of the North, and Radenhall's village elder. She makes the tribe's decisions; her authority rests not on a vote but on the cycle of nature and the sign of the runes.
mapping.appearance:
A very old woman, but with a straight back. Her face has seen the sun, full of deep lines; her white hair reaches her waist and raven feathers are braided into it. Her eyes are light green and clear.

She wears a light-colored robe woven from bamboo fiber that at first glance passes for linen; around her neck, a string of dried seeds. In her hand she carries a flat stone with runes carved on it. She smells of resin, dry grass and sun-warmed earth.

Her race is human or elf, depending on the characters.
mapping.mannerisms:
She is not surprised, does not scold, does not grieve. She tells what is asked, not what is not.

While talking she turns the stone in her hand with her fingers. Silence does not bother her; while waiting for an answer she can stay silent a long time.

*"You'll be asking about the rot."*
mapping.goals: That Radenhall and its tribe go on living by their own rules.
mapping.secrets: **She is hiding how long she has known about the rot.**
mapping.dmNotes:
**If the characters ask.** The druid describes how she reads the rot in nature: where it began and which way it is walking. She is not surprised the characters have come; she receives them as if she had been waiting for them.

If asked how long she has known, she sidesteps the question. If pressed, she says *"a long time"*.

**Saying "the druid called them".** The tribe has been reading the rot for months and waiting for no one to come. If word comes from below that someone is asking about the rot, @[Path Scout — Addluin](entity:npc/Path Scout — Addluin) brings them in himself; this is not an invitation but the tribe's own curiosity.

**She can sense the sickness.** If one of the characters has been infected, the druid may sense it. Whether she senses it, and if she does whether she says so, is the DM's. If she senses it, she is not surprised.

**The sherbet.** The recipe for the @[Sherbet of Resistance](entity:adventuring-gear/Sherbet of Resistance) is known in the tribe, and the sherbet is given here in trade. What is asked in return is the DM's.

Quest: @[What the Stones Know](entity:quest/What the Stones Know). Scene: @[Welcome in the Courtyard](entity:scene/Welcome in the Courtyard).

mapping.name: Path Scout — Addluin
mapping.description: An elf who guards the single narrow path down to Radenhall. Everyone who wants to come in meets him first.
mapping.appearance:
A tall, broad-shouldered elf man. His long hair is tied at the nape.

He wears earth-colored clothes woven from plant fiber and soft undyed leather; his pauldrons are large dried leaves layered one over another. In his hand a short bow. Beside him stands a grey dire wolf the size of a pony; its head low, its eyes on the stranger.
mapping.mannerisms:
He tells someone he has stopped to turn back once: *"Back down from here. Now."* He does not say it a second time.

While talking he lays his hand on the wolf's head.
mapping.goals: That no one crosses the path uninvited.
mapping.secrets: He knows who has tried to cross the path in recent months.
mapping.dmNotes:
**If the characters ask.** The scout knows who is looking for Radenhall and why, but does not tell strangers.

**The path has two keys; one is enough.** Convincing the scout that their purpose is good; or **speaking of the rot** — someone asking about the rot in nature, a character carrying the Arcana DC 13 trace of @[Blight — Infection](entity:curse/Blight — Infection), or someone telling what they saw in Silverwater makes the scout take a second look. Either way the scout takes them in himself; the tribe has been waiting for this for months (@[Wardens of the North](entity:lore/Wardens of the North)).

Scene: @[Welcome in the Courtyard](entity:scene/Welcome in the Courtyard).

mapping.name: Healer — Iven
mapping.description: One of Radenhall's healers. He gathers and dries healing herbs, and brews the @[Sherbet of Resistance](entity:adventuring-gear/Sherbet of Resistance). In the tribe, healers are, together with bards, the most respected.
mapping.appearance:
A slender human man in his late twenties. His short-cut brown hair is stuck to his forehead with sweat; his fingertips and the beds of his nails are stained green from herbs.

He wears a sleeveless vest woven from bamboo fiber and cloth leggings wrapped to the knee; small pouches nested one inside another swing at his belt. He smells of crushed mint, pine resin and smoke.
mapping.mannerisms:
While talking his hands never stop working: he snaps a stem, sniffs a root, ties the mouth of a pouch. Before answering a question he looks not at the asker's face but at their hands.

*"Bitter? It's going to be bitter. The sweet kind doesn't work."*
mapping.goals: That the herbs are gathered on time, and that no one in the tribe is left without sherbet.
mapping.secrets: He knows that the recipe for the sherbet the licensed physicians in the city sell so dearly came from here. He does not keep it as a secret; no one asked.
mapping.dmNotes:
**The hand that brews the sherbet.** The @[Sherbet of Resistance](entity:adventuring-gear/Sherbet of Resistance) is given here in trade, and the one who brews it is Iven; he knows the recipe too. He is the sherbet's second carrier in the tribe. What is asked in return for the trade is the DM's.

**If the characters ask.** He does not hide what the sherbet does or how long it lasts. He does not give the recipe without a trade.

Quest: @[What the Stones Know](entity:quest/What the Stones Know).

mapping.name: Bard — Tamsin
mapping.description: The bard of the Wardens of the North. Radenhall's history is kept not in books but in songs, and most of those songs pass from her mouth to the next.
mapping.appearance:
A stocky, round-faced halfling woman in her forties. Her curly hair, beginning to grey, is short; a raven feather is tucked behind her ear.

She wears a long shirt woven from bamboo fiber that at first glance passes for linen. On her back she carries a small stringed instrument made of tree bark. Her voice is bigger than her body.
mapping.mannerisms:
She hears a stranger's name once and does not forget it. Before answering a question she falls silent, as if thinking about which song the question belongs to, then speaks.

*"We don't write. What is written gives permission to be forgotten."*
mapping.goals: That the songs pass whole to the next generation.
mapping.dmNotes:
**If the characters ask.** She tells Radenhall's past in the language of song: that people came here fleeing the turmoil of the kingdom, which ceremonies are held among the stones. She leads the songs sung among the stones in the evenings.

Quest: @[What the Stones Know](entity:quest/What the Stones Know).

mapping.name: Halim
mapping.description:
The fourth stranger in Silverwater, and the only one on his feet. He came before the characters and is staying in one of the two rooms upstairs at @[Goodbarrel's Hearth](entity:location/Goodbarrel's Hearth).

The @[Border and Trade Guild](entity:lore/Border and Trade Guild) sent him here **to look into the situation**. He was not asked to solve anything, fix anything, or find anyone; he will look, go back, report, and get paid. He himself describes the job exactly like that.

He is not an agent. A job accepted once, and a man who has long since realized it is not worth the money he took.
mapping.appearance:
A thin man past forty with a long neck. His hair is thinning, his beard unevenly trimmed. His hands are clean but his nails broken.

His clothes say his trade: a patched wool cloak with brush wear at the knees, an old pair of boots that has shaped itself to his feet, a knife and a small rope reel at his belt. No bow, no shield, no armor. Someone who knows how to walk in a forest; not someone who knows how to fight.

He smells of wet wool and cold ash. His voice is low and quick.
mapping.mannerisms:
When he enters a room he sits at the spot closest to the door and stays there.

He takes no notes. He asks about what was told again and again, then memorizes it — a man who carries papers is easy to find.

When a voice rises outside, he breaks off the conversation and listens. He pays no mind to the sound of an argument; at the sound of a fight he stands up.

*"They told me to look. I'm looking."*
mapping.goals:
To finish the job and get back safe and sound, collect his money, and never take a job like this again.

He has no aim of saving the village, solving the sickness or helping anyone — and he does not hide it.
mapping.secrets:
**He does not say who sent him the first time he is asked.** *"I'm passing through,"* he says, and says it badly.

The only name he knows is @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar); he has not met him face to face, he got the job from the seat's apprentice. He knows the Sancars are a fallen house and that this job's money will be paid late.
mapping.dmNotes:
**How he is recognized — no roll.** A character who comes from the guild line (@[Guild Member](entity:background/Guild Member) · @[Guild Scion of Rank](entity:background/Guild Scion of Rank) · @[Guild Agent](entity:background/Guild Agent)) recognizes him **on sight** as an institution's man: from his bearing, the way he listens, his waiting before speaking. For other characters, **Insight DC 12** — they see he is not a villager, they cannot see whose man he is.

**Getting him to talk is easy.** No threats needed; two questions and a little patience are enough. The moment he says who sent him, the road to @[Lucid Triton](entity:location/Lucid Triton) and the name of Orvan Sancar fall onto the table.

**He does not fight.** If the turning happens while he is in the village (@[The Dawn Turning](entity:scene/The Dawn Turning)), he runs and does not stop. Do not give him a turn, do not look for a stat block: he has no move, he has a direction. He cannot be persuaded to stay and fight — his fear is not an attitude, it is the man himself.

**If he gets back alive.** Halim's job is to look and go back and report. If he gets back alive, what he saw in Silverwater reaches the seat; if the characters were there, their names are in that report too.

**He locks no one in.** The road to the Assembly opens from him, but also from the trio's trail, and from going straight to the guild. Halim is not a door but a shortcut.

mapping.name: Forgemaster — Torvun
mapping.description: The dwarf master at the head of the iron forges on Votumar's lower levels. The wheels of the catapults, the chains of the wall gates and the Order's armor pass through Torvun's hands. Torvun is the source of the hum felt through the soles of your feet in the courtyard.
mapping.appearance:
A short, thick dwarf with a chest like a barrel. The lower half of the face is soot-stained; the red beard is split into two braids gathered with leather rings, the braids' ends singed short by fire. No eyebrows — they burned and never grew back.

The leather apron has dozens of small burn holes. The arms carry a permanent redness left by forge light. Whoever comes near first feels the heat, then smells coal and quenched iron.

The voice is louder than it needs to be; like someone who has talked beside forges for years.
mapping.mannerisms:
While talking Torvun does not put down the work in hand; even while answering, the hammer falls. When Torvun does not understand a question there is no answer, only a look and a wait.

Torvun talks in numbers: *"This month three catapult arms, two gate chains, forty-one armor straps. All of it came by word of mouth. None of it's on paper."*
mapping.goals: That the forges do not stop and the supplies arrive on time.
mapping.secrets:
**For two months the supply orders have come by word of mouth too.** Torvun keeps a ledger: what was made, for whom, and what was received in return. That ledger's *ordered by* column has carried the same word for two months — *verbal*.

Torvun takes this for a personal failing. Torvun thinks it was Torvun who forgot to ask for paper, who did not insist, and a master working like that is shameful.
mapping.dmNotes:
**If the characters ask.** Torvun gladly talks about the forges, the catapults and the castle's upkeep; strangers meddling does not bother Torvun, who likes to talk about the work. Torvun is the first person at the castle who will talk to strangers.

To whoever asks how the orders come, Torvun answers directly — counting it not a secret but an irregularity: *"By word of mouth. For two months. I don't write it down anymore either; in whose name would I write it?"*

**The second witness to the same thing.** The empty *order* column in @[Gate Commander — Nevra](entity:npc/Gate Commander — Nevra)'s watch ledger and Torvun's supply ledger show the same two months, and Torvun opens up more easily: Nevra is an officer, Torvun a craftsman.

**The proof in hand.** Torvun's own ledger. Torvun shows it to whoever asks, and hands it over if it needs to be handed over.

**The job in hand.** The supply storehouse's count does not add up, and Torvun cannot look into it personally; whoever looks reports it, and whatever is reported enters the ledger. It is the only job Torvun can give a stranger: @[The Missing Count](entity:quest/The Missing Count).

mapping.name: Castle Clerk — Nerion
mapping.description: The dragonborn clerk who sits in the castle's records room. The watch ledgers, the supply lists and the signal reports from the towers all come together on her desk at the end of the day. Votumar's memory is in this room.
mapping.appearance:
A slender, long-fingered dragonborn woman; her scales a pale bronze. The side of her right hand is permanently darkened by ink — a stain that has worked in under the scales and does not come off with scrubbing. When she bends over the desk, the row of scales at her nape catches the light differently.

The records room is cold: the clerk lights a small brazier so the ink will not freeze, but also keeps the window open — she says the smell of ink in a closed room gives her a headache. She carries a constant smell of ink, soot and wet paper.

When she speaks she does not raise her voice; in the room there is never a sound louder than the rustle of paper.
mapping.mannerisms:
When asked a question, she first opens the relevant ledger, then answers — not because she does not trust her memory, but because she wants the ledger to be trusted.

Her sentences are measured: *"This is what I have. If you ask about something I don't have, I'll tell you I don't have it."*
mapping.goals: That the ledger closes complete.
mapping.secrets:
**One night's signal record never reached the castle, and she closed that gap with her own hand.** If the line stays empty, at inspection it is the clerk's fault; Nerion wrote *calm* for that night. What she wrote is not true, and she knows it every time she opens the ledger.

There is a second thing too: for two months nothing has come to write under the *orders* heading. For a clerk an empty column is more unsettling than a wrong line.
mapping.dmNotes:
**If the characters ask.** Nerion explains the castle's record-keeping completely: which ledger comes from where, when it closes, who signs it. She shows strangers no ledger; she has no authority to.

**She does not lie.** If asked directly *"what was written that night"*, she reads the page, and does not hide that what she is reading is her own writing. If the tower's own account is in hand too (@[Tower Sentry — Vrask](entity:npc/Tower Sentry — Vrask)), the two records do not match, and she is the first to notice.

**Not a culprit, a clerk.** Do not play Nerion as a collaborator; what she did is an official's fear of an empty line. Pressed, she closes up; if she feels understood, she talks.

npc.source_name: The Shore Siblings — Kessa, Bram and Tomas

mapping.name: The Shore Siblings — Kessa, Bram and Tomas
mapping.description:
Three siblings of a fishing family who cast nets at the mouth of the bay; the boat is in practice theirs now. They bring fish to the castle, and along with the fish, sometimes news.

- **Kessa** — seventeen, human. In charge of the boat, and the tight-lipped one of the three.
