- **Bram** — fifteen, human. His mouth never stops; when he sees something he is the first to say it, and no one believes him the first time.
- **Tomas** — fourteen, tiefling. The youngest. He loves showing that he can tie a net knot with his tail, and he shows it.
mapping.appearance:
All three are youngsters with wind-reddened cheeks and salt-stiffened hair; all their hands are scratched from net rope.

Kessa is tall and thin, her hair gathered in a single thick braid, wearing a big oilskin coat left from her father — the sleeves rolled up twice. Bram is a head shorter than her, his knees patched, always standing on top of something: a rock, the edge of a boat, a barrel. Tomas's scaleless red skin looks like copper in the sea light; his horns are still short and curve back, his sister has tied a piece of string to the tip of his tail, and he does not untie it.

All three smell of fish, salt and tar. When they talk on the shore they laugh — no one else does that at the foot of the castle wall.
mapping.mannerisms:
They finish each other's sentences, and the one whose sentence was finished objects every time.

Bram tells it, Tomas exaggerates it, Kessa pulls both of them back down: *"It was a light." "It was huge!" "It was a light."*

When they talk about the knights all three lower their voices at once — they say *"the ones up there"*, and they do not mean it as disrespect.
mapping.goals: That the boat and each other stay safe; and one day to see beyond the bay.
mapping.secrets:
**That night they saw a light at the mouth of the bay.** It was not the towers' fire, and it was on the water. It was Bram who saw it, but all three were there.

They did not tell the knights, because they were not supposed to be there at that hour: they had gone to leave flowers on the shore and carve runes in the stone. The fishers do this at hours when the ones up there are not watching, and telling what you saw means telling where you were.

Kessa's real fear is not the light: the youngest was out with her that night, and she is the one who answers for it.
mapping.dmNotes:
**They can be reached without entering the castle.** The three are found on the shore, on the stony stretch where the boats are pulled up. They are the only witnesses who do not need to pass through the gate and whose names are not written in the ledger.

**How they open up.** They will not say a word to an officer; Tomas, seeing the Order's white cloak, goes quiet, Kessa steps forward and the conversation is over. If the characters do not look like men of the ones up there, it is easy: **Bram already wants to tell**, and all he needs is to be believed. Seeing the flowers on the shore and not asking, or showing that you understand, takes the place of Kessa's permission.

**Play the three separately.** Bram tells and inflates; Tomas can draw what he saw — beside the runes he carved in the stone, with the same pocketknife; Kessa cuts in and trims what is told. The trimmed version is true.

**Tone.** These are the three most cheerful people in the act, and in Votumar that means something: in a place where people say *"patient as the bay, upright as the castle"*, they are the only group that laughs out loud. That is also what puts them in danger.

**What it confirms.** The siblings' night is the same night as @[Tower Sentry — Vrask](entity:npc/Tower Sentry — Vrask)'s night. If the two accounts come together, no sentry's mistake remains: there really was something in the bay.

**What they do not know.** They do not know what the light was. Bram guesses — a ship, a signal, a monster — and his guesses are not evidence; the only truth this card carries is that the light was seen.

mapping.name: Watch Captain — Drahan
mapping.description: The captain at the castle end of the Watchtower Line. Every signal from the towers goes first into Drahan's ledger, then on to the castle. The line's reputation rests on Drahan's shoulders.
mapping.appearance:
An old, large dragonborn; the grey-green scales have worn open at the tip of the snout and on the hands. Above the left eye is a thin, straight scar — the mark left by a breaking mirror glass.

Drahan fastens the Coast Watchers' grey cloak at the shoulder with a single clasp. Drahan sets the line ledger not on the desk but on a knee, and leans forward to write. The breath is heavy and hot; someone standing nearby hears Drahan's breathing before Drahan speaks.

Drahan stands with hands clasped behind the back, and talks that way.
mapping.mannerisms:
Drahan talks as if reporting: first what, then when, then who. On reaching a place Drahan does not want to talk about, Drahan forms a military sentence and falls silent: *"The line's record is in order."*

To someone who asks a question a second time, Drahan repeats the same sentence word for word.
mapping.goals: The line's reputation: that every signal sent finds its answer.
mapping.secrets:
**Drahan did not enter that night in the ledger, and was told so by word of mouth.** Drahan did not know the man who brought the order; there was no written paper, and Drahan wrote nothing either. That night's page has stood empty for two months, and at every change of watch Drahan looks at that gap.

For a captain this is heavier than a lost report: a lost report is an accident, an unwritten report is a decision, and Drahan made the decision.
mapping.dmNotes:
**The carrier who is hard to open.** Drahan says not a word about this to civilians. Opening Drahan up requires a character with the @[Paladin Soldier](entity:background/Paladin Soldier) or @[Paladin Officer](entity:background/Paladin Officer) background, the presence of @[Deputy Lord Commander — Aren](entity:npc/Deputy Lord Commander — Aren), or the tower's own account in hand (@[Tower Sentry — Vrask](entity:npc/Tower Sentry — Vrask)).

**Who gave the order is not written, and Drahan does not know.** Drahan can describe the man who brought it — he said he came from the castle, he had no cloak — but does not know his name. This is not a gap: what this card carries is the absence of the name. **Do not invent one.**

**If missed, no lock.** The same night was seen by @[Tower Sentry — Vrask](entity:npc/Tower Sentry — Vrask), not recorded by @[Castle Clerk — Nerion](entity:npc/Castle Clerk — Nerion), and seen from the shore by @[The Shore Siblings — Kessa, Bram and Tomas](entity:npc/The Shore Siblings — Kessa, Bram and Tomas).

mapping.name: Sevran
mapping.description: Half the drying racks in Argenfon belong to Sevran's household. In the last few weeks Sevran has lost the most, and what was lost is not money but **winter**: dried fish, what the village will eat in February.
mapping.appearance: A fisher in their forties with sun-cracked hands and eyes permanently narrowed. The face is cut into vertical lines, the eyebrows and lashes bleached colorless by the sun, the beard stiff with salt; on the head a knitted wool cap that never comes off, on the wrist a piece of tarred string, on one hand a missing fingertip — a fishing line cut it years ago. While talking Sevran does not let go of the rope or net in hand; without looking, keeps tying knots with a bone netting needle.
mapping.mannerisms:
When telling something, Sevran gives the number first: *"Fourteen racks. Nine empty. Fourth night."*

When speaking of the castle, Sevran's voice never changes, and the sentence always ends in the same place: *"They came. They looked. They said it was quiet."* No reproach; being angry at the knights would occur to no one in Argenfon.
mapping.goals: To save what is left of the winter fish.
mapping.secrets:
None. Sevran tells everything known without being asked.

The one thing missing is a connection: Sevran **knows** that neighbor @[Iraz](entity:npc/Iraz)'s rack has never been touched, but has not counted it as a clue — *"hers is out of the way"*, Sevran thought.
mapping.dmNotes:
**Sevran gives the quest, but not a job.** Sevran tells the trouble; asks nothing of the table. If asked, Sevran shows the way, gives a boat, gives food. Sevran cannot give money — the village has no cash.

**Why they do not go to the castle:** they went. A patrol came, stayed two nights, saw nothing, said *"we've got our eye on it"*. That is Argenfon's reflex anyway (`bolge §5.2`): the worry is spoken, and the sentence always ends with *"it'll be handled"*. No one feels like bothering the knights a second time over fish.

Chain: @[Night of the Tide](entity:quest/Night of the Tide).

mapping.name: Iraz
mapping.description:
The only household that spices its fish while salting it. In the village this is not a sign of wealth but a habit: her mother-in-law did it that way, so she does it that way.

**Her rack has never been touched.**
mapping.appearance: A fast-talking halfling woman in her fifties. For years she has climbed onto the same worn stool to reach the salting table made for taller folk. Greying curly hair escaping from a dark red headscarf, small gold hoops in both ears; her fingers, and her hands right down to the nail beds, permanently brick-colored from spice. She carries a constant smell of salt and cumin; she says she cannot smell it herself.
mapping.mannerisms: She gives recipes without being asked. Whatever the subject, at some point it comes round to what her mother-in-law did.
mapping.goals: That no one starts on her rack too.
mapping.secrets: None — and nothing she is aware of either. **She does not know why her rack was skipped**; she puts it down to luck.
mapping.dmNotes:
**A clue with no roll.** When asked who in the village lost something, Iraz's name comes up on the side of *those who did not lose*. Whoever looks at her rack sees the difference: fourteen racks emptied, this one full.

**This is the first carrier of the spice door** (@[Hıkka — The Record in the Books](entity:lore/Hıkka — The Record in the Books)); the second is the books (History DC 15). One is enough.

If asked, Iraz says she spices it, because it does not occur to her that this is a secret.

mapping.name: The Governor's Deputy
mapping.description: The deputy of the @[Customs Governor](entity:npc/Customs Governor); a red-scaled dragonborn. The deputy carries the jobs the governor cannot have put on paper. No one knows the deputy's name; the governor calls them only *sir*.
mapping.appearance:
A tall, narrow-waisted dragonborn in their early forties. The scales are a deep red, the color of an old brick; under the chin and at the throat they lighten to copper. The short horns curving back from both sides of the head are carefully filed, with fine gold rings slipped over their tips. The eyes are yellow and seldom blink.

The deputy wears a midnight-blue velvet jacket: mother-of-pearl buttons, a starched and snow-white collar, not a single crease in the sleeves. Thin leather gloves on the hands. A faint smell of cedar and ink. In the middle of the wharf's noise, never in a hurry.
mapping.mannerisms:
Says *sir* to everyone, opens the door for everyone. Thanks a question first, then answers it: *"A fine question, sir. The governor would like to tell you about that himself."*

Asked for a name, the deputy smiles: *"The governor calls me sir. You may do the same."*
mapping.goals: That the governor sleeps easy; and that the deputy's own name never appears in any ledger beside the governor's.
mapping.secrets:
**The deputy does not know what is in the chest.** What the deputy knows is that there are papers inside and that the governor wants nothing else from that house. The deputy did not ask; not asking is part of the job.

**The deputy knows the house.** Before the guild bought it, the deputy learned on the governor's behalf that the house was for sale and walked through it once: knows the cellar hatch, the stairs, the scaffold on the upper floor. For a few nights now the deputy has been watching the watchmen from the corner of the street; knows how many they are and where the lantern burns.

**There is a limit.** The deputy does not enter the house and raises a hand to no one. If the characters are caught, the deputy does not know them.
mapping.dmNotes:
**The deputy is the one who finds the characters.** A stranger who comes to Elymsyr first passes through customs, and the deputy is the first to see whoever passes through customs. The deputy is the one who carries the governor's offer to the characters, politely, in the courtyard of the @[Customs House](entity:location/Customs House): *"The governor would like to entertain you over a glass of wine, sir. There's no hurry."*

**During the job.** The deputy is the one who guides a table that accepts @[The Masked Job](entity:quest/The Masked Job): hands out the masks, describes the layout of the @[Military Law Chamber](entity:location/Military Law Chamber), escorts them as far as the terrace street and waits at the corner. The deputy wants the chest handed over; the deputy takes it to the governor. If the chest has been opened, the deputy notices. Whether the deputy tells the governor is the DM's.

**If the characters ask.** The deputy does not talk about the governor's ledger, ships or guild business: *"Those are not things I could know, sir."* The streets of Elymsyr, its inns and which captain is honest, though, the deputy gladly describes.

mapping.name: Orc Captain — Mordha
mapping.description: The captain of @[Black Sail](entity:location/Black Sail). Not turned, of sound mind; she is the one who says what the drum will play and when the hatch will open.
mapping.appearance:
A tall, bony orc woman in her forties; long-armed, her back slightly hunched from years of leaning on the helm. Her ash-grey skin is hardened by wind and salt; there are deep lines on her forehead and at the corners of her eyes. Her brow ridge is thick and jutting, her eyes small in its shadow; her nose broad, broken once and knit crooked. Her lower teeth are yellow, one longer than the other. Black soot has been smeared with a finger on both sides of her face, from under the eyes to the jaw; thicker than her crew's. The sides of her head are shaved; the black hair down the middle is a single thick braid at the nape.

Black-dyed studded leather, on her shoulders two rusty plates pried from other armor; over it a wool cloak whitened by salt. On her shoulder a two-handed axe, on her belt a single iron key. She smells of tar, soot, and something sour — the smell of the lower hold, settled into every part of the ship.
mapping.mannerisms:
She counts the drum's rhythm by tapping a finger on the rail. While talking she looks not at the person in front of her but at the hatch on her own deck.

Her Common is broken but understandable: *"Keep the hatch shut. They are mine."*
mapping.goals: To reach the cure that was promised for those in the lower hold.
mapping.secrets: **Some of those in the lower hold were her own crew.** Someone promised her a cure; in return asked her to wait in this water. Who made the promise, and whether there is a cure, is the DM's. The captain believes in the cure; if she did not, she would not keep her ship in this water.
mapping.dmNotes:
**In combat** her stats are the @[Orc Captain](entity:monster/Orc Captain). She stands on the quarterdeck, beside the drum. The encounter: @[Hull to Hull](entity:encounter/Hull to Hull).

**If she surrenders.** If the drum has fallen silent and she is below half her hit points, she offers to surrender; in return she asks that those in the lower hold not be touched. If her own crew sees her surrender, they stop fighting.

**If she stays alive**, she is the standing proof of the sickness, and she says little: she knows her own water, her own drum, her own promise (@[Where They Came From](entity:quest/Where They Came From)). Whether she will say the promiser's name is the DM's.

**In her cabin** there is a paper waiting for the characters (@[Black Sail](entity:location/Black Sail), `secrets`). If the captain is asked, she does not say whom she got the paper from; why she does not say is the DM's too.

mapping.name: Scales Sergeant — Hulda
mapping.description: The retired River Guard who leads the guards of the @[Honest Scales](entity:location/Honest Scales). She brought the ship's ballista from the tower.
mapping.appearance:
A low, broad dwarf woman in her sixties. Her grey hair is in two thick braids, their ends tucked into her belt; her face is reddened by salt and wind. Half of her left ear is missing.

A faded old version of the Guard's blue-grey cloak, a chain shirt beneath it. At her belt a short sword and the ballista's string key. She smells of fish oil and wet leather.
mapping.mannerisms:
At every change of watch she walks the deck from end to end and counts, moving her lips. When the count matches she says a single word to the captain: *"Twenty-two."*

She knows newcomers not by name but by what they carry: *"Sword. Books. And this one, shield."*
mapping.goals: To get everyone who boards the ship ashore. That the count matches.
mapping.secrets: **She has never fired the ballista at a real ship.** In the tower there were only drills.
mapping.dmNotes:
**In combat** she leads the guards and stands at the ballista. If the characters propose a plan she listens; if the plan makes sense, she places her guards accordingly. The encounter: @[Hull to Hull](entity:encounter/Hull to Hull).

**Afterward** she counts. She wants the bitten put somewhere separate, and she tells @[Captain — Maren](entity:npc/Captain — Maren) so too (@[Quarantine Night](entity:scene/Quarantine Night)).

mapping.name: Knows No Pain
mapping.description: When it drops to zero hit points it does not make death saves; **it dies.**
mapping.benefits: The person inside the Turned died when consciousness shut down. A Turned that falls cannot be saved.

mapping.name: Relentless Stride
mapping.description: When its hit points drop below half its maximum, its speed becomes **40 ft** and it does not provoke opportunity attacks.
mapping.benefits: The body that could not get out of bed yesterday has forgotten tiredness today. As it is wounded it does not slow down; it speeds up.

mapping.name: Fitful
mapping.description:
At the start of its turn, roll 1d6.

- **1–2:** it stares off at something and loses its action.
- **5–6:** it makes an extra Claw attack.

The die is rolled **in the open**.
mapping.benefits: One moment it stares into empty air, the next it attacks twice.

mapping.name: Early Empowerment
mapping.description: On its first turn it makes an extra Claw attack.
mapping.benefits: The body the sickness has strengthened the most.

mapping.name: Manifestations of Order
mapping.description:
The order of Mechanus has left its mark on you. Each time you cast a spell, the same thing appears. Choose one:

1. Spectral gears appear and turn behind you.
2. Clock hands turn in your eyes.
3. Your skin briefly shines like brass.
4. Equations and geometric shapes float in the air.
5. Your spellcasting focus briefly turns into a small clockwork mechanism.
6. An audible ticking or chiming follows you.
mapping.benefits: No mechanical effect. The manifestation you choose repeats with every spell you cast.

mapping.name: Restore Balance
mapping.description: When a creature you can see within 60 ft is about to roll a d20 with advantage or disadvantage, you cancel the advantage or disadvantage **with your reaction**.
mapping.benefits: Uses equal to **your proficiency bonus**; all return on a long rest.

mapping.name: Trance of Order
mapping.description: **Bonus action**, 1 minute: attack rolls against you cannot have advantage, and on your d20 rolls a 9 or lower counts as a 10.
mapping.benefits: 1 free use per long rest; after that, 5 sorcery points.
mapping.mechanical_notes: Once the free use is spent it can be opened again by paying 5 sorcery points — the sorcery point pool is the class's own counter; this line does not track it.

mapping.name: Clockwork Cavalcade
mapping.description: **Action:** within a 30 ft cube you distribute a total of 100 hit points, repair damaged objects, and end spells of 6th level and lower.
mapping.benefits: 1 free use per long rest; after that, 7 sorcery points.

mapping.name: Draconic Gift
mapping.description: The bond formed with the Drake leaves its mark on you too: when you move your hand through the air, you notice the air answering.
mapping.benefits:
You learn the **Thaumaturgy** cantrip; for you it is a Ranger cantrip and does not count against the number of spells you know.

You learn the **Primordial** language.

You choose your drake's **essence type**: acid, poison, cold or lightning.

player_choices.label: Essence Type
player_choices.prompt: Each time you summon the Drake you can choose its essence type again.

mapping.mechanical_notes:
The essence type you choose determines three things at once: the drake's damage immunity, the type of all extra damage tied to the drake, and the resistance you gain at 7th level.

**Deviation:** **fire** was removed from the original list, and in place of the **Draconic** language the original text grants, **Primordial** is given — there are no dragons in this world.

mapping.name: Drake Companion
mapping.description: You summon the drake you have bonded with to your side.
mapping.benefits:
As an **action** you summon the drake to an unoccupied space you can see within 30 ft.

**Once free** per long rest; after that each summoning spends **a spell slot of 1st level or higher**.

The drake shares your initiative but acts **after** you. If you do not command it with a bonus action, it takes the **Dodge** action on its turn. If you become incapacitated, the drake acts on its own and attacks.

A newly summoned drake arrives at full hit points; you can choose its essence type again with each summoning.
mapping.mechanical_notes: The drake's stat block is on the `animal/Drake` card; its AC and hit points scale with your Ranger level.

mapping.name: Draconic Essence
mapping.description: The essence the drake carries also shuts it off from its own damage.
mapping.benefits: The drake is **immune** to the essence type chosen when it is summoned (**acid, poison, cold or lightning**). All extra damage tied to the drake is also of that type.

mapping.name: Bond of Fang and Scale
mapping.description: As the bond tightens the drake grows: its shoulders broaden, its scales thicken. **It does not grow wings** — there is no flying drake in this world.
mapping.benefits:
The drake becomes **Medium** size.

It can carry a Medium or smaller rider **on land**; it becomes your mount.

The drake's bite deals **+1d6** essence damage.

**You** become **resistant** to the essence type you chose.
mapping.mechanical_notes:
The resistance is tied to the chosen essence type (`Draconic Gift`), so no fixed damage type is written here: add the resistance to the character sheet by hand.

**Deviation:** the **wings + flying speed** the original text grants at this level were removed; nothing was put in their place.

mapping.name: Drake's Breath
mapping.description: The bond fills two pairs of lungs at once: you or the drake cover the cone in front of you with essence.
mapping.benefits:
**Action.** You or the drake exhale essence in a 30 ft cone.

**Once free** per long rest; after that each use spends **a spell slot of 3rd level or higher**.
mapping.mechanical_notes: Once the free use is spent it can be opened again by paying a slot of 3rd level or higher — the class's own counter tracks the slots; this line does not track them.

mapping.name: Reflexive Resistance
mapping.description: The bond works both ways: when one of you is struck, the other flinches.
mapping.benefits:
While you and the drake are within **30 ft** of each other, when one of you takes damage, you use your **reaction** to grant **resistance** to that damage.

Uses equal to **your proficiency bonus**; all return on a long rest.

mapping.name: Perfected Bond
mapping.description: The bond now covers both bodies. The drake reaches its final size — **still wingless**, still a creature that walks the ground.
mapping.benefits:
The drake becomes **Large** and continues to carry you **on land**.

The drake's bite adds **another 1d6** (+2d6 essence damage in total).

**Drake's Breath** now deals **10d6** damage.
mapping.mechanical_notes:
**Deviation:** the **"can fly while ridden"** clause the original text grants at this level was removed; nothing was put in its place.

If your table finds the loss too heavy, there is one dial: add the line **"the drake cannot be knocked down (immune to Prone)"**.

mapping.name: Weight of the Oath
mapping.description:
Your **Strength** score **increases by 1** (to a maximum of 20).

You gain proficiency in the **History** and **Investigation** skills.
mapping.benefits: The order taught you not to pray but to read a ledger and to stay standing in a shield wall. The single point of strength is not a bonus but a **trade**: it is the counterpart of the lost divine line, and the only reason the oath-sworn can hold the field.

mapping.name: Oath Strike
mapping.description:
When your melee weapon attack hits a creature, you can spend a **spell slot** to deal an extra **2d8 force** damage. **+1d8** for each slot level above 1st, to a maximum of **5d8**.

If the target is a **Blighted** creature, an extra **+1d8**.

Usable once per turn.
mapping.benefits: Replaces *Divine Smite*; a paladin who keeps this oath does not prepare Divine Smite. Not light but weight: there is no holiness that burns what you strike, there is the body of a word kept.

mapping.name: Oath Vow: Hold the Line
mapping.description: **Channel Divinity.** As an action you repeat your oath out loud. Until the end of your next turn, you and your allies within **10 ft** roll their @[Blight — Infection](entity:curse/Blight — Infection) exposure saves **with advantage**.
mapping.benefits: The one thing the order has done for three centuries: not to give up a line until someone comes.

mapping.name: Unbroken Word
mapping.description:
Your allies within **10 ft** of you (you included) roll **with advantage** every saving throw that would give a **Sickness Score** (@[Blight — Infection](entity:curse/Blight — Infection)).

At 18th level the range becomes **30 ft**.
mapping.benefits: That the one standing beside you does not fall sick is, in this order, not a matter for prayer but a job description.

mapping.name: Untiring Oath
mapping.description:
**You cannot be frightened.**

In addition, when you take damage that would drop you to 0 hit points, you **stay at 1 hit point**.
mapping.benefits: Staying at 1 hit point is used **once per long rest**.

mapping.name: Vowbound
mapping.description: **Bonus action**, lasts 10 minutes. For the duration, the range of your auras increases to **30 ft** and your attack rolls against **Blighted** creatures have **advantage**.
mapping.benefits: **Once per long rest.**

mapping.name: Bulwark
mapping.description:
**Once per long rest.** When you cast an **abjuration** spell of 1st level or higher by spending a slot, you can set aside part of that spell's power and raise a **Bulwark** around you.

**Raising it is your decision.** Not every abjuration spell forces the bulwark up — while casting you say *this time I raise it*. The bulwark is always raised on the back of that spell; it cannot be raised any other way.

**The bulwark's hit point capacity: `2 × wizard level + Intelligence modifier`.**

The bulwark lasts from the moment it is raised **until it breaks**, and takes damage aimed at you in your place.
mapping.benefits:
**It is fed automatically.** While the bulwark stands, every abjuration spell of 1st level or higher you cast gives the bulwark back **spell level × 2** hit points. It does not exceed its capacity. You spend no separate action or extra slot for this — casting the spell is enough.

**Breaking.** **The moment the bulwark's hit points drop to 0, the bulwark breaks**; you take the damage left over from that hit and the bulwark **is gone**. A broken bulwark does not come back by being fed.

**One until the long rest.** Whether it breaks or stays standing, you cannot raise a second bulwark until your next long rest. Deciding when to raise it is therefore the real game of this card.

**Example (5th level, Intelligence 16):** capacity `2×5 + 3 = 13`. On the first turn you raised the bulwark while casting *Shield*. A 2nd-level abjuration spell you cast in the same fight writes **+4** hit points to the bulwark. When a hit exceeding 13 hit points comes, the bulwark breaks and you are without a bulwark for the rest of that fight.

mapping.name: Extend the Bulwark
mapping.description: The bulwark now holds not only you but **everyone you can see**.
mapping.benefits:
As a **reaction**, you redirect damage coming at a creature you can see within **30 ft** to your Bulwark. If the damage exceeds the bulwark's hit points, **the bulwark breaks** and the creature takes the leftover damage.

There is no limit on the number of uses; the limit is the bulwark's hit points and your having a single reaction per turn. This is what this school puts in place of divine healing: **damage not taken.**

mapping.name: Countermage
mapping.description: **Counterspell** and **Dispel Magic** are always prepared for you and **do not count** against the number of spells you prepare.
mapping.benefits:
**Not wasted.** When you spend a slot on *Counterspell* and the target passes its saving throw and the spell cannot be stopped, **the slot counts as not spent.**

**You are a master at unpicking.** When *Dispel Magic* requires an ability check against an effect of 4th level or higher, you add your **proficiency bonus** to the check.

mapping.name: Resistance to Magic
mapping.description:
You are **resistant to all damage** from spells.

You make **every saving throw** against a spell's effects **with advantage**.
mapping.benefits: For the bulwark to stand somewhere, you must first stand there. At this tier the school begins to protect its bearer.

mapping.name: Hiccup
mapping.description:
On land, the gill slits on the sides of the neck do not close fully; as it breathes out it makes a sound like a hiccup. As long as this creature breathes on land it **cannot stay silent.**

**At the table:** on land it has disadvantage on Stealth checks, and a character who **hears** it knows its direction even without seeing it. In water this trait does not apply.

mapping.name: Water-Bound
mapping.description:
It cannot stay away from water for long. If it stays on land for more than **10 minutes** without a break, it makes a **Constitution DC 10** saving throw for every additional 10 minutes; on a failure it takes 1 level of Exhaustion. Entering the water clears Exhaustion gained this way within an hour.

**The consequence:** raids are short and do not stray from the waterline. A Hıkka that comes ashore cannot be chased inland — the chaser wins, and what they win is a tired animal.

mapping.name: Soft Shell
mapping.description:
It has just shed its shell; the new one has not hardened yet. **It is vulnerable to all physical damage** (vulnerable: bludgeoning, piercing, slashing), and has disadvantage on Constitution saving throws.

Within a few days this passes and the creature becomes a @[Shellback](entity:monster/Shellback). The card describes not a kind but a **state**.

mapping.name: No Threshold
mapping.description:
When it, or a Hıkka within its line of sight, is threatened — a sudden lunge, a cut-off escape route, someone walking straight at it — it **attacks at once** and does not withdraw for that round.

**Within 30 ft of its nest** this condition is not required: there, everyone who enters is a threat.

In addition, if another Hıkka is within 5 ft of the creature it attacks, it has **advantage** on the attack roll. This is the mechanical form of thirty of them coming at you at once.

mapping.name: Layered Shell
mapping.description:
It has not shed its shell for years; the layer on it has thickened layer upon layer and lost its color. It is **resistant** to **nonmagical** bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage.

**At the table:** you hit it, nothing happens. Its threat is not the damage it deals but that it **cannot be gotten past** — and since it does not chase, escaping it is always possible.

mapping.name: Never Comes Ashore
mapping.description:
Because of its weight and thickened shell it becomes useless on land. **It does not leave the waterline** — does not chase, does not follow, does not come two steps past the water.

**The consequence:** escaping it is always possible. What it holds is not an area but a **mouth**.

mapping.name: Unfalling
mapping.description: The first time it drops to 0 hit points it does not fall; it stays standing with **1 hit point**. This works once. The second time it drops to 0 hit points, @[Knows No Pain](entity:trait/Knows No Pain) applies.
mapping.benefits: The orc body is the one the sickness lets go of last. You do not turn your back on a Turned Orc that has fallen.

mapping.name: Claw Attack
mapping.description:
*Melee Attack:* **+2** to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. **Hit:** 1d4 piercing damage (avg. 2).

No weapon: hardened nails, teeth, shoulder. It does not aim; it comes walking and strikes. This is the claw of small bodies — low down, at the knees and hips.

**It does not spread the sickness.** A Turned's claw opens a wound but does not carry the Blight — no saving throw is made because of the claw (@[Blight — Infection](entity:curse/Blight — Infection)).

mapping.name: Mighty Claw Attack
mapping.description:
*Melee Attack:* **+2** to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. **Hit:** 1d8 piercing damage (avg. 4).

The same claw, a heavier body. A blow with its whole weight behind it; it pushes a shield aside, crushes armor. Medium and stronger bodies use this.

**It does not spread the sickness.** A Turned's claw opens a wound but does not carry the Blight — no saving throw is made because of the claw (@[Blight — Infection](entity:curse/Blight — Infection)).

mapping.name: Leaping Bite
mapping.description:
*Recharge 5–6.* The Turned bends its knees and leaps up to **15 ft** — three or four long strides — landing on a creature it can see. **No attack roll is made:** the leap lands.

**Hit:** 1d8 piercing damage (avg. 4). The target then makes a **Constitution DC 8** saving throw; on a failure, **+1 Sickness Score** (@[Blight — Infection](entity:curse/Blight — Infection)). The saving throw answers not the damage but **the sickness**.

The claw comes from a distance; this does not. It rides you down with its weight, its teeth go into the skin of the throat or shoulder, and teeth are not the only thing that goes in. This is the **only** attack through which a Turned can pass on the Blight.

mapping.name: Restore Balance
mapping.description:
*Trigger:* a creature you can see within 60 ft is about to make a d20 roll with **advantage** or **disadvantage**.

With your reaction you cancel the advantage **or** disadvantage on that roll; the die is rolled straight.

mapping.name: Bastion of Law
mapping.description:
Spend **1–5 sorcery points**. Give yourself or a creature you can see within 30 ft a ward made of **d8 ward dice** equal to the points you spent.

When the warded creature takes damage, it can spend and roll as many ward dice as it likes; the total is subtracted from the damage it takes.

It lasts until your long rest or until the dice run out. You can have only one ward at a time.

mapping.name: Trance of Order
mapping.description:
For 1 minute:

- Attack rolls against you **cannot have advantage**.
- On every d20 you roll, **a result of 9 or lower counts as 10**.

**Once free** per long rest; after that, **5 sorcery points**.

mapping.name: Clockwork Cavalcade
mapping.description:
Spirits of order appear in a **30 ft cube** centered on you. You heal each creature of your choice in the cube, you included, sharing out a total of **100 hit points** however you like.

Damaged but not destroyed objects in the cube are mended and fully repaired.

Every spell of **6th level or lower** in the cube ends.

**Once free** per long rest; after that, **7 sorcery points**.

mapping.name: Drake's Breath
mapping.description:
You or the drake exhale essence in a **30 ft cone** in front of you.

Each creature in the cone makes a **Dexterity** saving throw — DC **your spell save DC**. On a failure it takes **8d6** essence damage; on a success, half.

**10d6 at 15th level.**

**Once free** per long rest; after that each use spends **a spell slot of 3rd level or higher**.

mapping.name: Reflexive Resistance
mapping.description:
*Trigger:* you or the drake take damage while within 30 ft of each other.

With your reaction you give the one taking the damage **resistance** against that damage.

mapping.name: Bite
mapping.description:
*Melee Attack:* **+3 + the bonded ranger's proficiency bonus** to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. **Hit:** **1d6 + proficiency bonus** piercing damage.

*(The +5 and 1d6+2 in the table are the 3rd-level form — proficiency bonus 2.)*

**From 7th level** it also adds **+1d6**, **from 15th level** a total of **+2d6** essence damage.

mapping.name: Infusing Strike
mapping.description:
*Trigger:* a creature within 30 ft of the drake hits with a weapon attack.

With its reaction the drake infuses that hit with its essence: the attack deals **+1d6** essence damage.

mapping.name: Extend the Bulwark
mapping.description:
*Trigger:* a creature you can see within **30 ft** takes damage and you have a **Bulwark** standing.

With your reaction you redirect that damage to the bulwark; the bulwark takes the damage, not the creature.

If the damage exceeds the bulwark's current hit points, **the bulwark breaks** and the creature takes the excess.

If the creature has **resistance or vulnerability** to that damage type, this is applied when calculating the amount written to the bulwark.

There is no limit on uses; the limit is the bulwark's hit points.

mapping.name: Raise the Bulwark
mapping.description:
*Trigger:* you cast an **abjuration spell of 1st level or higher** by spending a slot.

From that spell's power you raise your **Bulwark**. Capacity `2 × wizard level + Intelligence modifier`.

It costs no action, bonus action or reaction — you decide while casting the spell. **Once per long rest.**

The bulwark **breaks** when its hit points drop to 0 and does not come back until a long rest; so which spell you raise it with is this school's real decision.

mapping.name: Grab
mapping.description:
Melee Weapon Attack: **+4** to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. **Hit:** 1d4 slashing damage (avg. 2).

Less an attack than a **snatch**: the webbed hand reaches out, the claw tears the skin, and the creature pulls back in the same motion. Against a target with something portable in hand it prefers to take this — what it really wants is not a fight but **the thing in hand.**

mapping.name: Shell Slam
mapping.description:
Melee Weapon Attack: **+4** to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. **Hit:** 1d6 bludgeoning damage (avg. 3).

It rolls its body and strikes with the thick edge of the hard shell at shoulder height. The whole weight of something stocky and low lands on a single point; the sound is like a blow on wood.

mapping.name: Bear Down
mapping.description:
Melee Weapon Attack: **+5** to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. **Hit:** 2d6+3 bludgeoning damage (avg. 10), and the target makes a **Strength DC 13** saving throw; on a failure it falls **prone**.

No lunge, no speed. It topples forward and lets the whole weight of its layered shell come down on you. Someone who falls in a narrow mouth cannot get up.

mapping.name: Hook
mapping.description:
Melee Weapon Attack: **+3** to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. **Hit:** 3 (1d4+1) slashing damage, plus 3 (1d6) piercing damage.

The wharf's cargo hook: its point catches in the flesh, and opens the wound as it is pulled.

mapping.name: Cutlass
mapping.description: Melee Weapon Attack: **+4** to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. **Hit:** 5 (1d6+2) slashing damage.

mapping.name: Three Attacks
mapping.description: The Head Watchman makes three attacks: each with the **Rapier** or the **Pistol**, in any mix.

mapping.name: Rapier
mapping.description: Melee Weapon Attack: **+6** to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. **Hit:** 8 (1d8+4) piercing damage.

mapping.name: Pistol
mapping.description:
Ranged Weapon Attack: **+5** to hit, range 30/90 ft, one target. **Hit:** 8 (1d10+3) piercing damage.

A flintlock, single-shot pistol. The Head Watchman keeps it loaded in his lap.

mapping.name: Javelin
mapping.description:
Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: **+4** to hit, reach 5 ft or range 20/60 ft, one target. **Hit:** 5 (1d6+2) piercing damage.

A short-shafted spear with a heavy head. The orc crew first throws it from the gunwale, then holds it in hand once the boarding is made.

mapping.name: Chain Hook
mapping.description:
Melee Weapon Attack: **+4** to hit, reach **15 ft**, one target. **Hit:** 5 (1d6+2) piercing damage. If the target is Large or smaller, it makes a **Strength DC 12** saving throw; on a failure it is pulled **10 ft** straight toward the hookman.

- If the path it is pulled along crosses a gunwale, the target falls **Prone** on the other side of the gunwale.
- If the path drops into the gap between the two ships, the target **falls into the water.** Climbing the hull takes a full round and **Athletics DC 12**.

A three-pronged iron at the end of a chain. The hookman swings it from the gunwale; the same hook makes the boarding and pulls the man in.

mapping.name: Mallet
mapping.description:
Melee Weapon Attack: **+4** to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. **Hit:** 5 (1d6+2) bludgeoning damage.

The drum's mallet: its head wrapped in hide, its shaft ringed with iron. The drummer uses it as a weapon only while defending the drum.

mapping.name: Rhythm
mapping.description:
The drummer changes the rhythm and plays one of three rhythms. The rhythm lasts until the drummer's next turn, and every @[Turned](entity:monster/The Turned) that hears the drum follows it.

- **Come** — a single, heavy, long beat. If the lower hold's hatch is open, **two more Turned** come out of the hatch.
- **Strike** — fast and dense. Every Turned within **60 ft** of the drum uses its reaction to make a @[Mighty Claw Attack](entity:creature-action/Mighty Claw Attack).
- **Hold** — three beats, a silence. The Turned do not attack orcs; if an orc is beside them, they move away from it.

**If the drum falls silent** — the drummer falls, the drum splits, or the drummer plays no rhythm on their turn — the Turned are left without direction: they attack **the nearest creature**, orc or not. If the drum is intact, another orc can take up the mallet on their next turn and keep the rhythm going.

**The drum.** On the quarterdeck, a barrel body with hide stretched over it: AC 12, 10 hit points. Once split, it never plays again.

mapping.name: Two Attacks
mapping.description: The Orc Captain attacks twice with the @[Battleaxe](entity:creature-action/Battleaxe).

mapping.name: Battleaxe
mapping.description:
Melee Weapon Attack: **+6** to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. **Hit:** 11 (2d6+4) slashing damage.

A broad-bladed axe held in two hands. Its haft has a leather wrapping whitened by salt.

mapping.name: The Turned
mapping.ac_note: no armor; hardened skin does not make it easier to dodge
mapping.language_note: Understands the languages it knew, but cannot speak.
mapping.description: > A familiar face, familiar clothes. But the skin has faded: neither the color of the living nor of the dead; somewhere between pale green and purplish grey. At the neck and wrists the skin has hardened and cracked like a crust; one shoulder has dropped, one hand has clenched and stayed that way. A purplish-black fluid has seeped from the corners of the eyes and from inside the cracks, and dried on the chin. Its breath is rasping and smells sour, like metal. When you call its name it does not stop; it turns its head toward the voice and begins walking toward you.
mapping.traits_md:
The body of a person who has reached the Blight's last stage. Under the rule of @[Blight — Infection](entity:curse/Blight — Infection), every villager, soldier or traveler whose Sickness Score reaches 9 comes to this. Consciousness shuts down; the body grows strong.

**Appearance.** No symptom is the same in every Turned; what is marked in one may be wholly absent in another.

- **The skin** usually fades: across a range from a pale skin to pale green, and from there to purplish grey. In some from head to toe, in some in patches; in some the old color still remains in spots.
- **The body** can be deformed: a shoulder drops, a face slides to one side, a hand clenches and stays, the skin hardens and cracks. One carries most of these, another almost none.
- **The fluid** is purplish black — close to black, turning purple in the light. In some it flows fresh from the cracks, the eyes or the mouth; in some a dried trace remains; in some it does not show at all.

A Turned carries the body of whoever it was before the sickness, in a corrupted form. A detailed appearance pool for an orc: @[Turned Orc](entity:monster/Turned Orc).

It feels no pain, does not withdraw, does not surrender. It does not answer when spoken to, but it turns toward sound.

Its claw **does not spread** the sickness — the claw only opens wounds. **Its mouth does:** when it leaps onto you and bites with @[Leaping Bite](entity:creature-action/Leaping Bite), the Blight passes.

When it is killed, the corpse of someone familiar remains; everything on it is still in place.
mapping.dmNotes:
**Tactics.** The Turned use no tactics. They walk toward the nearest sound and movement and attack. If the leap is ready they leap — without choosing, they jump at the nearest target.

A player character who turns no longer belongs to that player: the DM runs the character and uses these stats. There is no coming back.

**With the drum.** On @[Black Sail](entity:location/Black Sail) the Turned follow the rhythm of a drum: @[Rhythm](entity:creature-action/Rhythm).

mapping.name: Turned Alton
mapping.ac_note: clumsy body; stiffening joints spoil its dodging
mapping.language_note: Understands the languages it knew, but cannot speak.
mapping.description: > The halfling who fell asleep in the middle of a sentence stands in the cabin doorway. His eyes are open, and do not blink. His expensive green clothes are torn; the skin showing through the tears has faded to a color verging on pale green, and in places has crusted over. His left arm has twisted at the elbow to an angle it should not have. A purplish-black fluid has run from below his ear down to his collar and dried. His breathing is rasping but steady. His bare feet make no sound at all as they crush the wet grass. The gold wedding band on his finger is still in place.
mapping.traits_md:
The turned form of @[Alton Leagallow](entity:npc/Alton Leagallow). Derived from the stats of @[The Turned](entity:monster/The Turned). In him the sickness began with tiredness.

The body that could not get out of bed no longer tires. As it is wounded it does not slow down; it speeds up.
mapping.dmNotes: He is the first out of the cabin. If a staggered exit is used in @[Dawn Clash](entity:encounter/Dawn Clash), the other two come a round later.

mapping.name: Turned Merla
mapping.ac_note: clumsy body; stiffening joints spoil its dodging
mapping.language_note: Understands the languages it knew, but cannot speak.
mapping.description: > The halfling woman stands on the threshold and stares into empty air. Her undone braid is scattered over her face. Her face has faded to a purplish grey, and one corner of her mouth has pulled down and stayed that way. A fresh, purplish-black fluid trickles from her eyes down her cheeks. Her lips move, but the only sound from her throat is a dry clicking, like the sound of an insect's wings. Then, without any warning, she throws herself at you.
mapping.traits_md:
The turned form of @[Merla Tealeaf](entity:npc/Merla Tealeaf). Derived from the stats of @[The Turned](entity:monster/The Turned). In her the sickness began with fitful coming and going.

One moment she stares into empty air, the next she attacks twice.
mapping.dmNotes: Roll the *Fitful* die **in the open**. Let the players see that the three Turned are nothing alike.

mapping.name: Turned Kromanna
mapping.ac_note: no armor; hardened skin does not make it easier to dodge
mapping.language_note: Understands the languages it knew, but cannot speak.
mapping.description: > The tiefling woman stoops out through the cabin's low door. As she straightens, the door frame scrapes her shoulder and breaks with a crack. Her shoulders are broader than they should be; under her unpicked sleeves the muscles strain her skin. The red of her skin has faded and turned a purplish grey; in places the skin has cracked into crusts, and a purplish-black fluid seeps from several of the cracks. Her yellow eyes glow in the dim light. The woman who tried to put herself in front of the two halflings is not looking at them now.
mapping.traits_md:
The turned form of @[Kromanna](entity:npc/Kromanna). Derived from the stats of @[The Turned](entity:monster/The Turned). In her the sickness began with the body growing strong early. Her resistance to fire is left over from her tiefling blood.

This is the body the sickness has strengthened the most.
mapping.dmNotes:
The most dangerous of the three Turned, and she shows it on the first round: she attacks twice.

@[The Sealless Ring](entity:trinket/The Sealless Ring) is still in the hidden pocket of her corpse.
mapping.resistance_note: left over from her tiefling blood

mapping.name: Softling
mapping.alignment_note: It has its own order; it does not fit this continent's alignment table.
mapping.language_note: They speak their own language. The sound they make on land resembles hiccuping; they know none of the coastal languages.
mapping.description:
> Something stocky and round that comes a little above a human's knee. Its skin is a glossy turquoise; the shell on top is paler and translucent in places — as if not yet properly set. Its large, completely dark eyes shy away from the light.
>
> With every breath a broken, stuttering sound comes from its neck. It sounds like a crying child, and the resemblance is a coincidence.
mapping.traits_md:
A Hıkka that has just shed its shell. The colony's most defenseless state: it cannot hunt, cannot protect itself, depends on others to be fed.

**These are not the ones that come ashore.** The adults that empty the racks carry the food for these. The table meeting a Softling means the table has gone inside the nest.

Within a few days the shell hardens and this creature becomes a @[Shellback](entity:monster/Shellback).
mapping.dmNotes:
**It does not fight.** At the first chance it flees toward the water; if cornered, it strikes once with @[Grab](entity:creature-action/Grab) and tries to flee again.

**Tempo note.** Do not use this card like a combat card. There are **ten** of these in the nest, and none of them is a threat. What the table does there may be the hardest moral question in this act — the card says so nowhere.

mapping.name: Shellback
mapping.alignment_note: It has its own order; it does not fit this continent's alignment table.
mapping.language_note: They speak their own language. The sound they make on land resembles hiccuping; they know none of the coastal languages.
mapping.description:
> A stocky, low body that comes up to the waist. The turquoise skin gleams when wet; the single-piece shell on its back is between blue and green, shading into orange toward the edges. The hands at the end of the short arms are too big for the body, and webbed.
>
> It does not run on the wet rock — it scuttles in short lunges, stopping at the end of each lunge and looking. With its breath comes that broken, stuttering sound.
mapping.traits_md:
An adult Hıkka. The colony's walking, carrying, protecting state.

These are the ones that come ashore and empty the racks — and the food they carry goes not to themselves but to the @[Softling](entity:monster/Softling)s in the nest.

Unless provoked, it does not attack. When provoked, or when its nest is approached, @[No Threshold](entity:trait/No Threshold) kicks in and there is no such thing as a step back.
mapping.dmNotes:
**Meeting on the shore.** Its first reaction is to turn back to the water. As long as its way is not cut off, no fight starts; if it is cut off, one does, and not alone — there are always two or three more nearby.

**Meeting in the nest.** Something else entirely. There are about thirty of them, all with @[No Threshold](entity:trait/No Threshold), and in a narrow mouth the advantage is theirs.

**Tempo note.** On the shore, **two or three** is the right measure for a 1st–2nd level table. In the nest, do not try to give a number; that is not an encounter but a **decision**.

mapping.name: Holdfast
mapping.alignment_note: It has its own order; it does not fit this continent's alignment table.
mapping.language_note: They speak their own language. The sound they make on land resembles hiccuping; they know none of the coastal languages.
mapping.description:
> Just behind the mouth, in the water, something stands motionless. It is no bigger than the others — but it has no shape: the color is gone, the shell has thickened layer upon layer, its edges grown over with mussels and weed. It looks less like a creature than a piece of rock that does not belong there.
>
> Then that sound comes, and you realize the rock is breathing.
mapping.traits_md:
A Hıkka that has stopped shedding. It did not grow — **it hardened.**

It is not a king or a leader. In this species, to stop shedding is to give up growing and choose **to stay hard forever**, and that hardness has a job: holding the mouth.

It does not leave the water, does not chase, does not budge.
mapping.dmNotes:
**It was not written to be overcome.** A 2nd-level table is not expected to deal with AC 18 and resistances; its threat is not damage but **insurmountability** — you hit it, nothing happens.

**And it does not chase.** Escaping it is always possible, always free. Fleeing something huge is ordinary; turning back from in front of something that stands like a stump, does not chase you and that you cannot hurt is more unsettling.

**This card is the quest's price.** The *going inside* ending is knowingly the most expensive one; the other endings of @[Night of the Tide](entity:quest/Night of the Tide) exist for this.

mapping.name: Site Watchman
mapping.description: > A man who has set his lantern on the ground and leans his back against the stone wall. He wears a patched leather vest, and at his belt a sharp-pointed cargo hook. He blows into his palms; his breath fogs in the lantern's light. Then he hears a footstep and pulls the hook from his belt.
mapping.traits_md: A dockworker who carries loads on the wharf by day and watches a house at night for a few coppers. Not a guild man; he does not even quite know whom he is watching the house for.
mapping.dmNotes:
**He was not hired to die.** When he drops below half his hit points he flees or surrenders. A watchman who flees goes out into the street and shouts.

**What he knows:** who holds the house (@[Head Watchman](entity:monster/Head Watchman)), how many they are at night, and that the craftsmen work upstairs by day. He knows nothing of the chest.

mapping.name: Hired Cutlass
mapping.description: > Two people at the head of the long table, a handful of coppers and two bone dice between them. One wears a ring earring, the other has a half-faded ship tattoo on one arm. Their cutlasses lie on the table, right next to their hands. While the dice are in the air, both look at the door.
mapping.traits_md: A sword hired from the wharf. A sailor whose ship never came, or who was thrown off their ship; in Elymsyr there is one like this in every tavern. They do not ask whom they fight against; they ask how much they are paid.
mapping.dmNotes:
**They fight as much as they are paid.** They fight while the @[Head Watchman](entity:monster/Head Watchman) is standing; if the Head Watchman falls, they flee. A better offer can end the fight: **Persuasion DC 13**, and the offer has to be real.

They know nothing of the chest.

mapping.name: Head Watchman
mapping.ac_note: studded leather and a light shield
mapping.description:
> A man sits at one of the writing desks; he has tipped his chair back on its rear legs, his boots on the desk. His grey hair is tied at the nape, his face tanned to leather by the sun. A loaded pistol in his lap, a thin sword at his side, a single iron key on his belt. He does not get up.
>
> *"Shut the door,"* he says. *"It doesn't warm up in here as it is."*
mapping.traits_md: The man who holds the house for the night. Once he gave orders on a ship's deck; now in Elymsyr he gathers men for whoever pays and leads them. He chose all the watchmen, he pays all of them.
mapping.dmNotes:
**He has the key.** The chest's key is on his belt. He does not know what is in the chest and does not care; the only thing he was told is that the chest does not leave the house.

**He bargains.** He fights for his own life and purse, not for the guild's house. When he drops below half his hit points he offers to surrender or to give up the key; in return he asks to be let go. If he has seen a face, he does not forget it.

**The table's toughest opponent.** Difficulty notes are in @[The Night Worksite](entity:encounter/The Night Worksite).

mapping.name: Orc Warrior
mapping.description: > Row on row of shields along the gunwale, and faces between the shields. None of them looks like another: one tall and skinny, one short and paunchy, one with shoulders slumped forward, standing hunched. Their skins range from ash grey to earth brown, from greenish grey to pale yellow. Their brow ridges are thick and jutting, their noses broad, their lower teeth jutting over their lips. Each has black soot smeared on their face with a finger, from under the eyes to the jaw. Women and men, young and old, in the same row. Their armor did not come from a single hand: rusty iron scraps riveted onto leather vests, one with a plate on the shoulder pried from some other armor. Each has a javelin in hand and two more on the back. As the drum beats, the shields come down on the gunwale all at once, and the sound of the wood mixes with the sound of the drum.
mapping.traits_md: The crew of @[Black Sail](entity:location/Black Sail). Not turned, of sound mind, and they do not go against their captain's word. They hold the line at the gunwale, throw javelins, and do not cross over until the boarding is made and the defense on the opposite deck has broken.
mapping.dmNotes:
**They do not go first.** The Orc Warriors stay at their own gunwale and wait for the Turned to cross first. When the defense on the opposite deck breaks, they cross over the hook ropes. Layout: @[Hull to Hull](entity:encounter/Hull to Hull).

**If the captain falls or surrenders**, they stop fighting. Those who came out of the lower hold do not.

**If the drum falls silent**, they flee from the Turned on their own deck; that round an Orc Warrior either flees or fights its own Turned.

mapping.name: Hookman
mapping.description: > Two orcs at the bow, without shields: one a young, thin, long-armed woman; the other an old, short man with a hunched back. They have wound chains around their arms; at the end of each chain swings a three-pronged iron hook. One slowly whirls the hook above their head and the chain whistles in the air with every turn. The other is not looking at you: they are looking at which plank of your gunwale is rotten.
mapping.traits_md: The hand that makes the boarding. There are two hookmen on @[Black Sail](entity:location/Black Sail); both throw the hook at a rope or at a man with the same ease.
mapping.dmNotes: **First the rope, then the man.** In the first rounds they throw the hooks at the opposite gunwale and pull the two ships together. Once the boarding is made, they pick someone left alone on the opposite deck and drag them to their own side — dropping them into the gap suits them too. Layout: @[Hull to Hull](entity:encounter/Hull to Hull).

mapping.name: Drummer
mapping.description: > On the quarterdeck, in front of the helm, a drum as big as a barrel. Its hide is darkened and taut; iron rings around its rim. At its head stands a skinny, long-armed orc; you can count the ribs on their bare back. A mallet in each hand. Eyes closed. Between beats the lips move, as if counting.
mapping.traits_md: The orc who plays the great drum of @[Black Sail](entity:location/Black Sail). There are no oars, the ship is under sail; this drum makes no one row.
mapping.dmNotes:
**The lock of the battle.** The drummer plays the rhythm (@[Rhythm](entity:creature-action/Rhythm)), and the rhythm controls those who came out of the lower hold. The drummer does not leave the drum; uses the mallet as a weapon only against whoever comes at the drum.

**How the table notices.** Seeing that the Turned change when the rhythm changes: **Arcana or Insight DC 12**, in the middle of the battle, by watching for a round. Why the rhythm passed to them is the DM's.

Layout: @[Hull to Hull](entity:encounter/Hull to Hull).

mapping.name: Orc Captain
mapping.description: > Beside the drum, leaning on the quarterdeck rail, a tall, bony orc woman. She has no shield; she rests a two-handed axe on her shoulder. The black soot on her face is thicker than the others'. She is looking not at you but at the iron-banded hatch in the middle of her own deck, and tapping the drum's rhythm on the rail with one finger.
mapping.traits_md: The combat stats of @[Orc Captain — Mordha](entity:npc/Orc Captain — Mordha).
mapping.dmNotes:
**The drum is her weapon.** She stands on the quarterdeck, beside the drum, and tells the drummer the rhythm. She does not join the fight unless her own deck is reached; she turns her axe on whoever walks toward the drum.

**Surrender.** If the drum has fallen silent and she is below half her hit points, she offers to surrender. In return she asks one thing: that those in the lower hold not be touched. Personality: @[Orc Captain — Mordha](entity:npc/Orc Captain — Mordha).

**To make it easier:** a single attack and 26 hit points. Layout: @[Hull to Hull](entity:encounter/Hull to Hull).

mapping.name: Turned Orc
mapping.ac_note: no armor; hardened skin does not make it easier to dodge
mapping.description: > First two hands come out of the mouth of the hatch and grip the wood with their nails. Then an orc body, but not shaped the way an orc should be: its spine crooked, one shoulder a hand's span higher than the other, its face as if slid to one side. Its skin has faded, a color between pale green and purplish grey, and has cracked into crusts; a purplish-black fluid seeps from the cracks, from the corners of the eyes and from the lips. One of its lower teeth is broken. A black-dyed crew cloth is still tied around its neck. The drum beats. It turns its head toward the sound, then toward you.
mapping.traits_md:
The turned form of an orc. Derived from the stats of @[The Turned](entity:monster/The Turned), but it falls later. Some still have around their necks the black-dyed cloth the orcs on deck wear. None looks like another: the sickness corrupts each orc body in a different place — one swells and hunches, one thins and lengthens, one's face splits. The pallor of their skins does not match either.

## Appearance

Build each Turned Orc from this pool. **No feature is required:** what is marked in one may be wholly absent in another. Pick one or two things from each heading, leave the rest empty. Do not let two Turned Orcs look like two colors of the same face.

### First, an orc

Before the sickness it was an ordinary orc — of every height and every build, like the other races. The sickness corrupts that body; it does not make a new one. There are big, muscular ones too, but they are few.

- **Height and build:** short · medium height · tall · stocky · thin and bony · paunchy · puny · broad- or narrow-shouldered · long-armed · short, thick-necked · muscular.
- **Face:** long · broad · narrow · bony · hollow-cheeked · high cheekbones · jutting jaw.
- **Brow and forehead:** thick, jutting brow ridge · low forehead · deep forehead lines.
- **Eyes:** small · deep-set · close together · narrow · in the shadow of the brow.
- **Nose:** broad · flat · short · long · crooked · broken once · wide-nostriled.
- **Mouth and teeth:** wide mouth · thin or thick lips · lower teeth jutting over the lip · yellow, crooked, pointed, broken or missing teeth.
- **Ears:** pointed · long · short · torn · one different from the other.
- **Hair:** bald · thin · short and black · long and matted · sides shaved, a braid down the middle · sparse, coarse or patchy beard.
- **Old marks:** a cut · a burn · a bone knit crooked · a missing piece of ear · deep wrinkles.

### Then the sickness

These too in a different measure in each.

- **Skin:** a range from pale skin to pale green, and from there to purplish grey. Some faded from head to toe, some in patches; in some the orc's old color — ash grey, earth brown, greenish grey — still remains in spots.
- **Hide:** dry · cracked into crusts · hardened and flaking · swollen in places · thin and taut. One is cracked everywhere, another only at the neck.
- **Deformity:** crooked spine · one shoulder higher than the other · a face slid to one side · a swollen or lengthened limb · a hand clenched and stuck · a split lip or cheek. In one all three at once, in another none.
- **Fluid:** purplish black — close to black, turning purple in the light. It seeps from the cracks, the corners of the eyes, the ears, the mouth. In some it flows fresh, in some a dried trace, in some it does not show at all.
- **Eyes:** clouded · bloodshot · darkened at the rims · never blinking.

### What remains on it

They were the crew of *Black Sail*: a black-dyed crew cloth at the neck · a torn leather vest · a rusty armor piece with its rivets pulled · bare feet · an empty scabbard at the belt. Not all of them on every one.
mapping.dmNotes:
There are one or two in the lower hold of @[Black Sail](entity:location/Black Sail). It comes out of the hatch together with the others, and like the others follows the drum (@[Rhythm](entity:creature-action/Rhythm)).

One of the orcs who sees one wearing a cloth at the neck may call out a name to it when the drum falls silent. No answer comes.

mapping.name: Blight — Infection
mapping.description: The rule form of what the people call the sickness: a single counter, the Sickness Score, five stages, an end with no way back.
mapping.trigger:
*A rule added on top of 5e.*

**Contact.** There are four routes:

- touching the fluids of a sick person or a corpse,
- spending a night in the same closed space with a sick person,
- the **bite** of a @[Turned](entity:monster/The Turned),
- every day spent on Blight ground beyond the front, in the **Sickness Mist**.

> Each exposure: **CON saving throw, DC 12.** Failure: **+1 Sickness Score.**

**The claw does not infect, the bite does.** A @[Turned](entity:monster/The Turned)'s claw opens a wound but does not carry the Blight; the hit has no saving throw of its own. The mouth is different: a creature hit by @[Leaping Bite](entity:creature-action/Leaping Bite) rolls **CON DC 8** — not the normal DC 12 of an exposure, an easier roll. On a failure, +1 Sickness Score.

It spreads outside combat too: a character who touches the fluids of a fallen Turned or searches its corpse rolls by the first route above.

**No roll without exposure.** If a character is falling sick, they have done something: touched a corpse, carried a sick person, gone into a cabin.
mapping.effect:
## Sickness Score

The Blight is not something caught all at once but **a poison that builds up slowly in the body.** Its single counter is the **Sickness Score**. *(Not to be confused with hit points.)*

**Everyone with 1 point is a carrier and infects others.**

**How the score rises.** +1 for every failed exposure. In addition, someone carrying the sickness (1+ points) makes a **CON DC 13** saving throw, +1 on a failure:

- **every day** on which no long rest is taken in a safe zone;
- **every 3 days** even if a long rest is taken in a safe zone every day.

**The score does not go down.** A safe zone (a sheltered settlement with no source of exposure: a city, a guild building) makes the roll rarer; it does not erase the score. In the wild, a successful **Medicine DC 15** intervention skips that day's roll.

## General course

The scores count at the table; inside a person, the sickness roughly follows this road:

- **Incubation — about a week.** The symptoms are mild and easily brushed off.
- **Progression — usually about a month.** The stages follow one another. The duration varies from person to person; it lengthens in a safe zone, shortens in the wild.
- **The end — one of two roads.** The body collapses and the patient **dies**, or consciousness shuts down and the patient **fully turns.**

## Five stages

| Stage | Score | Symptoms | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1 — Incubation** | 1–2 | Slight cough, thin purplish-black veins at the joints, a metal taste in the mouth that does not go away | Disadvantage on **ability checks** that rely on CON. Visual distortions begin in spells; no mechanical hindrance |
| **2 — Systemic Spread** | 3–4 | High fever, wounds slow to close, skin turning grey | Speed **−10 ft** · the hit points healed by Hit Dice spent on a long rest drop **by half** · a **Corruption Check** is required for spells of 3rd level and higher |
| **3 — Severe Degeneration** | 5–6 | Purplish-black fluid from the eyes and ears, shortness of breath, hearing the whispers of the gods | Disadvantage on **all** ability checks |
| **4 — Morphological Dissolution** | 7–8 | Skin hardening and flaking, involuntary spasms, speech falling apart | Disadvantage on **all** saving throws · every spell, whatever its level, triggers a **corruption surge** (like Wild Magic) · as if constantly under the effect of level 3 Exhaustion |
| **5 — Total Collapse** | 9+ | Consciousness shuts down | The character dies or becomes a @[Turned](entity:monster/The Turned) |

**Stage 5.** Consciousness goes, the body grows strong. The character is no longer a character: the sheet passes to the DM and takes the Turned stat block. **There is no coming back.**

## No two patients walk the same road

This rule affects not the dice but the narration. At each new stage the DM changes how the symptoms look: in one patient tiredness comes to the fore, another comes and goes fitfully, another's body grows strong early. The scores are the same; the picture is not.

## Not only biological

The Blight spreads like a disease and progresses like a disease, but it is **magical** and **tied to a source.**

> **Arcana DC 13** — when a character who casts or knows magic stands beside a patient, they **sense** that this is not something that happened on its own. A trace that does not fade, does not scatter, and stays **tied to** somewhere. No direction, no distance, no name.

*Detect Magic* and similar detection spells arrive at the same place: something **is there**, what it is **cannot be read.** Being magical does not mean it is not biological.

## Corruption Check

> **Trigger:** casting a spell of **3rd level or higher** on ground under heavy Blight. For a carrier at Stage 2 or above the ground does not matter: the check is required for every 3rd+ level spell.
>
> **Roll:** a Constitution **or** spellcasting ability saving throw, the caster's choice. **DC 13.**
>
> **Failure:** the spell **takes effect**, but corrupted: the caster takes **+1 Sickness Score**. A carrier at Stage 2 or above also loses hit points equal to the spell's level.

- A **Druid** gets **+2** on this roll.
- A **Paladin** more easily shrugs off the physical effects of the corruption: the symptoms of Stage 1 do not show in them. Their score and mechanics do not change.
mapping.mechanical_notes:
Exposure: CON saving throw DC 12; failure +1 Sickness Score.
Routes of exposure: touching the fluids of a sick person or corpse, a night in the same closed space, a Turned's bite, every day spent in the Sickness Mist.
A Turned's claw does not spread the sickness; no saving throw is made for the hit.
A Turned's bite (Leaping Bite): no attack roll, 1d8 piercing, then CON DC 8; on a failure +1 Sickness Score. Recharge 5-6, range 15 ft.
Anyone with 1 or more points is a carrier and infects others.
Daily roll: CON DC 13, failure +1; every day on which no long rest is taken in a safe zone.
Even if a long rest is taken in a safe zone every day, the daily roll is made every 3 days.
The score is never erased.
General course: about a week of incubation; progression usually about a month; the end is death or full turning.
In the wild, Medicine DC 15 skips that day's roll.
Stage 1 (1-2 points): disadvantage on CON ability checks.
Stage 2 (3-4 points): speed -10 ft; Hit Die healing on a long rest is halved; Corruption Check on 3rd+ level spells.
Stage 3 (5-6 points): disadvantage on all ability checks.
Stage 4 (7-8 points): disadvantage on all saving throws; every spell triggers a corruption surge; as if under the effect of level 3 Exhaustion.
Stage 5 (9+ points): death or Turned; no coming back.
Arcana DC 13: the magical trace on the patient, tied to somewhere, is sensed.
Corruption Check: a 3rd+ level spell on heavy Blight ground; CON or spellcasting ability saving throw DC 13.
Corruption Check failed: the spell takes effect, +1 Sickness Score; a Stage 2+ carrier also loses hit points equal to the spell level.
Stage 2+ carrier: Corruption Check on every 3rd+ level spell regardless of ground.
Druid: +2 to the Corruption Check.
Paladin: Stage 1 symptoms do not show; score and mechanics do not change.
Lesser Restoration: +2 to the next sickness roll; does not erase the score; the caster takes 1 level of Exhaustion.
Greater Restoration: +4 to the next sickness roll; does not erase the score; the caster permanently loses one Hit Die.
Sherbet of Resistance: +8 to exposure and daily sickness rolls for 24 hours.
mapping.removed_by:
**There is no known treatment.** The score is not erased; its rise can only be slowed.

- *Lesser Restoration* — **+2** to the next sickness roll. **The caster takes 1 level of Exhaustion.**
- *Greater Restoration* — **+4** to the next sickness roll. **The caster permanently loses one Hit Die.**
- The @[Sherbet of Resistance](entity:adventuring-gear/Sherbet of Resistance) does not push the sickness back; it makes it harder **to get in**: **+8** to exposure and daily sickness rolls for 24 hours.
- **At Stage 5 nothing works.** A Turned is killed, not healed.

Few can cast these spells, and whoever casts them loses something of their body each time. In the city the guilds decide who may cast these spells.
mapping.dmNotes:
What the people know is on a separate card: @[Blight — What Is Known](entity:lore/Blight — What Is Known). No one in the world has a diagnosis; this card works **like** a disease.

**The source.** The Blight is not nature's work but someone's. Do not name, show or point to the source. The only way the characters can sense this is the Arcana DC 13 above; and that shows no direction either, it only makes them feel that this has an owner.

**The three people in the cabin** are about to pass into the last stage; you choose when they turn. Think of the sick in the world not by score but by the *General course*: in incubation, in progression, near the end. The score is the player characters' counter.

Every character who enters the cabin makes an exposure roll and carries the points they get even after leaving the village. Tell the players in advance that the score **never goes down**.

mapping.name: Arrival at the Village
mapping.description:
> There is a queue for buckets at the well. An old man filling his bucket raises his voice over the creak of the chain and asks the woman beside him who took food to the cabin last night. The woman shrugs: *"They left it at the door again. No one went in."* The door of the inn across the road is open; from inside drift hearth smoke, the smell of fried onions and a halfling's voice. The halfling repeats the same sentence once more, louder.
>
> The old man sets his bucket on the rim, turns to you and looks you up and down. *"Did you come for that too?"*
mapping.beats:
## The door

**When this scene stands.** When the characters arrive in @[Silverwater](entity:location/Silverwater). They do not all need to come on the same day; those who come later can find the earlier ones at @[Goodbarrel's Hearth](entity:location/Goodbarrel's Hearth).

**Which doors can open from here.** None is required, none has an order.

| Door | Its keys |
|---|---|
| Going into the cabin (@[Questioning at the Cabin](entity:scene/Questioning at the Cabin)) | The village's rule *food is left at the door* — this is not a prohibition but a habit. No one stops the characters |
| *"These three came to the village sick"* | **Medicine DC 12**, or asking @[Umay](entity:npc/Umay) (no roll) |
| *"They came from the harbor"* | @[Duran](entity:npc/Duran), if he believes he is being asked for the village's good · or @[Corvin](entity:npc/Corvin), because he knows the coast roads |
| The name of @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar) | Seeing that @[Halim](entity:npc/Halim) is not a villager (**Insight DC 12**; a character from the guild line, no roll) → @[The Table Nearest the Door](entity:scene/The Table Nearest the Door) |

## The village — what state it is in

- **The village is working.** The cauldron boils, the doors are marked with chalk, linens on the lines, someone is baking bread. The first thing seen is not rot but a village doing its work.
- **The sickness is talked about openly.** At the well, at the inn, in the bread queue. No one whispers.
- **The cabin.** In @[The Cabin](entity:location/The Cabin) outside the village three strangers lie. Food is left at the door, no one goes in. The village decided this itself.
- **"No one has died."** The villager who says this looks relieved. If @[Umay](entity:npc/Umay) hears the same sentence she turns her head away and says nothing; if asked, she says that in forty years someone in this village has died every year.

## Who is in the village, what they know

| Who | What they give unasked | If asked |
|---|---|---|
| @[Milo Goodbarrel](entity:npc/Milo Goodbarrel) | Everything talked about in the common room | The strangers' first two nights, their clothes, how they paid — in advance, without argument, too much |
| @[Corvin](entity:npc/Corvin) *(not always in the village)* | That the strangers' cloth is expensive and foreign | That he knows the roads to the shore; more if the fee is discussed |
| @[Duran](entity:npc/Duran) | Says little; it shows he knows something | *"They came by the road, like everyone."* If he believes he is being asked for the village's good: *"They came from the harbor."* |
| @[Umay](entity:npc/Umay) | The state of the sick | What the body says — the sickness is older than the village thinks |
| @[Halim](entity:npc/Halim) | That he is not a villager (Insight DC 12; a character from the guild line, no roll) | Who sent him, and the name of @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar) |

## Situation

The three sick are **about to pass into the last stage.** Neither the villagers nor Umay know it. The threshold is written, the moment is yours: @[The Dawn Turning](entity:scene/The Dawn Turning).

The villagers' offer to spend the night in the village is not a steer but the village's habit — *"Go in the morning. The road is dark at night."* Staying and going are both the table's business.
