**Corvin.** @[Corvin](entity:npc/Corvin) is not always in the village; he goes back and forth between the shore and the village and stops by from time to time.
mapping.dmNotes:
**Bringing the characters into play.** If a character's background fits one of these four roles, use it in this scene:

- **The Warner** — the character who says the rot is not natural.
- **The Suspicious** — the character who senses the sickness is older than it looks.
- **The Fugitive** — the character who asks who was taken where.
- **The Marked** — the character whose body reacts to the sickness.

If no character fits a role, @[Umay](entity:npc/Umay) says what that role would say.

**This scene has no right way to go.** Going straight to the cabin, waiting for morning, setting off without stopping in the village at all — all three play. The village, the NPCs and the state of the sick are written above; the table builds the order.

mapping.name: Questioning at the Cabin
mapping.description:
> The door creaks open inward. Inside it is dim and hot; the smell of sweat, wet straw and iron hits your face. There are three beds, and they are not evenly arranged: two side by side against the back wall, the third right beside the door. In the two beds at the back lie two halflings, and on their fingers gleam two gold wedding bands forged in the same style. One is asleep; a faint rattle comes from his chest. The other looks at the wall, her lips moving silently.
>
> The tiefling woman lying in the bed by the door tries to raise herself on an elbow and puts her body between you and the halflings. Her voice is hoarse, but clear: *"Who are you?"*
mapping.beats:
## The door

**When this scene stands.** When someone enters the cabin. The village's rule is *no one goes in*, but it is not a prohibition: the door's latch is open and the village stops no one.

**Which doors can open from here.** None is required; the story makes up for what is missed.

| Door | Its key |
|---|---|
| *"These three came to the village sick"* | **Medicine DC 12**, or @[Umay](entity:npc/Umay) (no roll) |
| @[The Sealless Ring](entity:trinket/The Sealless Ring) | Searching her + **Investigation DC 15** |
| *"There's more here than a sickness"* | **Arcana DC 13**; only a character who can cast spells or has magical knowledge |
| The real names | Looking inside one of the two wedding bands — below |
| Foreign cloth, full purse, blank scrolls | No roll; whoever looks sees |

## Entering the cabin

Every character who enters the cabin makes an exposure roll: **CON DC 12**, +1 Sickness Score on a failure. Touching a sick person or their fluids and spending a night in the cabin are separate exposures (@[Blight — Infection](entity:curse/Blight — Infection)).

## The three sick

- **@[Alton Leagallow](entity:npc/Alton Leagallow)** falls asleep in the middle of his sentences. Polite, tired.
- **@[Merla Tealeaf](entity:npc/Merla Tealeaf)** is lucid and hospitable one moment, does not know where she is the next.
- **@[Kromanna](entity:npc/Kromanna)** tries to protect the two halflings. She answers briefly.

All three can talk. Whatever they are asked, they do not say where they came from, how they fell sick, or who paid for the voyage. They do not give their real names either.

**The wedding bands.** If the two halflings are asked how they met, both give, separately and just as fast, the same answer: *"We met on the road."* Yet the bands on their fingers are a pair. Noticing this needs no roll.

**Inside the band.** On the inner face of both rings the same line has been engraved in fine letters: *C. & P. Greenbottle.* Reading it requires taking the ring off and looking inside. The sick do not give up their rings and whoever tries to take them off meets resistance; after @[The Dawn Turning](entity:scene/The Dawn Turning) this line is there for free on the corpses. The name *Greenbottle* means nothing in Silverwater; in the @[Assembly Hall](entity:location/Assembly Hall) it does.

## Traces

| Trace | How it is found | What it shows |
|---|---|---|
| **The cloth** | No roll; whoever looks sees. @[Milo Goodbarrel](entity:npc/Milo Goodbarrel) or @[Corvin](entity:npc/Corvin) also say it | The clothes are of an expensive cloth not woven on this continent. Foreigners, and rich ones |
| **Purse and scrolls** | No roll; they are on them | The purse is full: their money has not run out, their road has. The scrolls are blank: they carry not a single document |
| **The ring** | Searching her and **Investigation DC 15** | The only object hidden in Kromanna's hidden pocket. See @[The Sealless Ring](entity:trinket/The Sealless Ring) |
| **The body** | **Medicine DC 12**, or asking @[Umay](entity:npc/Umay) (no roll) | The sickness is older than the village thinks. These three came to the village sick |
| **Magical trace** | **Arcana DC 13**; only a character who can cast spells or has magical knowledge | This is not only a sickness. On the three is a trace that does not fade, does not scatter, and stays tied to somewhere. No direction, no distance, no name |
| **Inside the band** | Taking the ring off and looking inside | *C. & P. Greenbottle.* Not the names they gave |

There is nothing else on them.

## The state of the three

All three are about to pass into the last stage. The threshold is written, the moment is yours: @[The Dawn Turning](entity:scene/The Dawn Turning).
mapping.dmNotes:
The most important information in this scene is *these three came to the village sick*. The characters can learn it in two ways: by examining the bodies (Medicine DC 12) or by asking Umay (no roll). If both are missed, the villagers go on thinking the sickness started in the village.

The ring and the magical trace are hard to find and can be missed. If they are missed, the story still moves on.

mapping.name: The Dawn Turning
mapping.description:
> From the direction of the cabin comes a crack: the sound of a plank straining, then splitting. A dog starts barking, and suddenly falls silent. Another smell mixes with the wood smoke in the cool air, sour and metallic.
>
> At the village entrance the young sentry grips the spear with both hands. Looking not at the cabin road, but at you.
mapping.beats:
## The door

**When this scene stands.** When the three's sickness has reached its end. The threshold is written, **the moment is yours.** The turning is not the punishment for a choice but the sickness's own road: no decision of the characters triggers it, none delays it.

**Which doors can open from here.**

| Door | What it takes |
|---|---|
| @[Dawn Clash](entity:encounter/Dawn Clash) | The characters being between the cabin and the village at that moment. If they are not, there is no fight either |
| What the trio carry becomes searchable | The corpses are there: the cloth, the full purse, the blank scrolls, @[The Sealless Ring](entity:trinket/The Sealless Ring) in @[Kromanna](entity:npc/Kromanna)'s hidden pocket, and the line inside the wedding bands |
| @[Duran](entity:npc/Duran) talking | If the village stays standing, he knows his debt |
| A report to the city | If @[Halim](entity:npc/Halim) gets back alive, what he saw can reach the @[Border and Trade Guild](entity:lore/Border and Trade Guild) |

## In the village

The village's reflex is clear: doors shut, children are pulled inside. Two of the volunteer militia are left with their spears between the cabin and the village and do not know what to do.

@[Halim](entity:npc/Halim) has no reason to stay here. His job was to look and go back and report; he cannot be persuaded to stay and fight, and he has no move.

If @[Corvin](entity:npc/Corvin) is in the village, he neither flees nor rushes forward; he stands in front of his own door, knife in hand. If he is not protected, he may die.

## The village after the turning — two states

The only thing that separates them is who stands between the cabin and the village at that moment.

**Standing.** There are dead, but the village lives. Within a few hours the doors open again, the hearth is lit, someone takes out bread. Provisions and beds cost the characters nothing, and this offer is not taken back. @[Duran](entity:npc/Duran) is in their debt and knows it: he talks about the things he would not talk about. The three corpses are there; everything on them is in place.

**Broken.** Most of the village is dead. There are some who survived by luck and most of them set off that day; those who stay are busy burying their dead and talk to no one. The three Turned are **loose** — the DM decides where they go; they do not come back to the village. The hearth is out, the cauldron overturned, the doors left open.

## True in both states

- Whoever gets out of the village alive carries two sentences: *"they were sick"* and *"they weren't from around here."*
- The sickness has a name: the villagers say *the sickness* or *the Blight*.
- The three strangers came from a harbor (@[Duran](entity:npc/Duran)).
- @[Corvin](entity:npc/Corvin) knows the way to @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor) on the coast. **If he dies, this line drops:** no one else in the village knows the coast road and no guide appears in his place. The harbor can still be found — some Council officials, some members of @[The Council and the Guild Assembly](entity:lore/The Council and the Guild Assembly), and very rarely the paladin officers of the @[Order of the Silver Shield](entity:lore/Order of the Silver Shield) know the way — but that door now goes through Lucid Triton.
- The three strangers came to the village **sick** (Medicine DC 12, or from @[Umay](entity:npc/Umay), no roll).
- If there is a character who knows magic: there is more than a sickness on them (Arcana DC 13).
mapping.dmNotes:
Each of the three strangers who lay sick now also has a @[Turned](entity:monster/The Turned) card. When narrating the fight, call them by name; let the characters know whom they are fighting.

**Do not set the Turned after the characters.** If the characters are not in the village, there is no fight — the village has paid. Putting them in the characters' way on the road is forcing back a skipped scene.

**Do not give Halim a turn.** No need to look for a stat block: he has no move, he has a direction.

**In the broken state the three Turned are loose**, and this is not a debt but material: a trail in the forest, a rumor in the next village, or nothing. Your call.

mapping.name: Admitted to the Harbor
mapping.description:
> The road ends behind the cliff. No gate, no guard, no sign; below stand three crooked piers and boats without flags. The wind brings up the smell of salt and incense, and from one of the shacks comes the tap of a hammer. At the bottom of the road a skinny gnome sitting on a barrel closes the thick ledger in their lap and pushes their spectacles down to the tip of their nose with a finger.
>
> The gnome looks at you, then at those beside you, then at you again. *"Whose guests are you?"*
mapping.beats:
## The door

**When this scene stands.** When the characters find the way to the harbor and come down to the cove. The way is found with one of three separate keys:

- @[Corvin](entity:npc/Corvin) — fee in advance, knows the way;
- @[The Sealless Ring](entity:trinket/The Sealless Ring) → @[Kildrak Ferrun](entity:npc/Kildrak Ferrun) reads the unstamped work and points south, to a harbor (@[The Assay Table](entity:scene/The Assay Table));
- an official in @[Lucid Triton](entity:location/Lucid Triton) who knows the way — the longer, more expensive road that leaves more traces.

**Which doors can open from here.** @[The Wharf](entity:location/The Wharf) · @[Twine](entity:npc/Twine)'s ledger · @[Mouse](entity:npc/Mouse)'s memory · @[Enamel](entity:npc/Enamel)'s workbench · @[Bargaining for Passage](entity:scene/Bargaining for Passage) (a ship: @[The Continent on the Horizon](entity:quest/The Continent on the Horizon)).

## The rule

@[Twine](entity:npc/Twine) lets no one in without a guarantor. Admission comes one of three ways:

1. **A guarantor.** Someone inside stands guarantor for them.
2. **A job.** They do a job for someone inside.
3. **A load.** They come with a real load to sell.

## Playing the scene

- **Coming with Corvin.** If @[Corvin](entity:npc/Corvin) stands guarantor, Twine listens to him, but Corvin is a guest here too. His word is enough to get down to the wharf; boarding a ship or doing business takes a stronger guarantor or a job.
- **Offering money.** Twine does not discuss money at this stage: *"Money later. First, who are you."* Money is discussed in the second stage, in the bargaining for a ship: @[Bargaining for Passage](entity:scene/Bargaining for Passage).
- **Threatening.** Threatening with the Council does not work; the Council knows about this place already. Any other threat does not start a fight, but word of it spreads at once: prices go up, no one stands guarantor (@[The Harbor Compact](entity:lore/The Harbor Compact)).
- **If they are let in**, @[Mouse](entity:npc/Mouse), on the first day, without being asked, tells them the Compact's three truths. She stresses the third in particular: whoever kills someone here can never enter this harbor again.

## What is on the wharf

A deckhand having their load written into Twine's ledger; the best-dressed man on the wharf, @[Velvet](entity:npc/Velvet), reading his papers at the head of a crate; the sound of a hammer from the back room of a shack (@[Enamel](entity:npc/Enamel)'s workbench); at the pier, two ships, one well kept, one patched.
mapping.dmNotes: A character who comes from a guild or from the Order's officers understands without rolling that Velvet is an institution's man. Others see with Insight DC 13 that he is not one of the wharf's people.

mapping.name: Bargaining for Passage
mapping.description:
> Two ships are moored side by side. One has new ropes, its deck washed this morning and still wet; at the head of the pier a half-elf captain reads the cargo list line by line and at every line looks up at the crates. The other's gunwale is patched in two places; on deck the crew plays dice, and a bottle goes from hand to hand. Its half-orc captain, before you even reach the pier, shouts a price with rum-scented breath.
>
> Both captains are going the same way. Both first ask you the same thing: what you will pay with.
mapping.beats:
## The door

**When this scene stands.** If the characters have been accepted at the harbor (@[Admitted to the Harbor](entity:scene/Admitted to the Harbor)) and want to board a ship.

**Which doors can open from here.** A ship: @[The Continent on the Horizon](entity:quest/The Continent on the Horizon).

**There are two keys; one is enough:** a **good writ** or **good money.**

## Boarding a ship

Neither is ready in a traveler's purse.

- **Good money.** Far beyond the money a traveler carries. It has to be earned: day labor at @[The Wharf](entity:location/The Wharf), goods to sell, or taking over someone's debt.
- **A good writ.** A passage paper carrying the countersignature of a seat in the Assembly. It is not found at the harbor; it is brought from @[Lucid Triton](entity:location/Lucid Triton). See @[Good Writ](entity:quest/Good Writ) · @[The Offer at the Door](entity:scene/The Offer at the Door).

## The captains

- **@[Captain Caelynn](entity:npc/Captain Caelynn)** offers a clean voyage: a good writ or a high fee. She takes no one aboard without seeing the cargo.
- **@[Captain Holg](entity:npc/Captain Holg)** offers a cheap and bad voyage. If accepted, Holg keeps the word given, but the voyage goes hard.

## Who can help

- @[Twine](entity:npc/Twine) knows the fees and the surety.
- @[Mouse](entity:npc/Mouse) knows which captain sails when.
mapping.dmNotes: In Meridia the roads are free; the only thing that costs money is boarding a ship. Ship's fare is not earned in a day at this harbor — this is not an obstacle but a price.

mapping.name: The Assembly Session
mapping.description:
> The clerk reads your name, and the voice hangs under the ceiling for a while. All six of the six seats turn to you. The elf rector has joined their fingers on the table. The bottles in the gnome physician's pocket clink once and fall silent. The dwarf head journeyman turns the paper in front of him. The registrar does not move. The master of the board smooths the curling edge of the plan in front of him. Only the man wearing the oldest coat in the hall leans forward, elbows on his knees, ready to listen to you.
>
> *"Speak,"* says the rector. *"Keep it short."*
mapping.beats:
## The door

**When this scene stands.** When the characters step up to the railing of the @[Assembly Hall](entity:location/Assembly Hall). The hall is reached with four separate keys; one is enough:

- **The petition line.** Open to all, but the line does not move on its own (@[The Petition Courtyard](entity:scene/The Petition Courtyard));
- **A guild line.** A character with the @[Guild Member](entity:background/Guild Member) · @[Guild Scion of Rank](entity:background/Guild Scion of Rank) · @[Guild Agent](entity:background/Guild Agent) background can join the line from their own guild's office;
- **The report @[Halim](entity:npc/Halim) carries.** If he got back alive, what he saw in Silverwater reaches the @[Border and Trade Guild](entity:lore/Border and Trade Guild) and the characters' names are in that report;
- **A name from the harbor.** A name @[Velvet](entity:npc/Velvet) saw can pass in the city (@[The Council and the Guild Assembly](entity:lore/The Council and the Guild Assembly)).

**Which doors can open from here.**

| Door | What it takes |
|---|---|
| The **reason** for the six refusals | The sickness being mentioned. This is what the hall really gives |
| @[The Offer at the Door](entity:scene/The Offer at the Door) | @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar) having heard of the characters |
| @[Where They Came From](entity:quest/Where They Came From) | The name *Greenbottle*, or the description of two halfling spouses, reaching Orvan |
| A small admission | Pressing a seat holder at their own weak point (*If the characters press* on the NPC cards) |

## What is in the hall

The clerk is at the lectern beside the railing; the clerk reads the names. No vote is held — the decisions were made before the session, in rooms that do not look out on this hall. If a seat holder is against a decision, they do not come to the session that day.

## Six answers

If the sickness is mentioned, every seat has an answer ready. None of them is lying; each sees the sickness only through the window of their own profession.

- @[Rector — Quarion](entity:npc/Rector — Quarion): *"We tested. No detection spell showed anything. What is not seen does not exist."*
- @[Head Journeyman — Adrik Ferrun](entity:npc/Head Journeyman — Adrik Ferrun): *"The workbenches are turning, production hasn't dropped. A sick man can't swing a hammer."*
- @[Chief Physician — Caramip Kalender](entity:npc/Chief Physician — Caramip Kalender): *"This is not something unknown, it is an advanced fever. It has a name, it has a treatment."*
- @[Registrar — Valen Custar](entity:npc/Registrar — Valen Custar): *"Sickness is not a legal category. Quarantine requires martial law; there is no declared war."*
- @[Master of the Board — Perhun Mizan](entity:npc/Master of the Board — Perhun Mizan): *"This city was planned so that it would not fall sick: the water flows separately, the wind cleans."*
- @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar) does not deny the sickness. He speaks, and no one in the hall turns to look at him.

**Every answer has a weak point.** Which sentence cracks where is written on the NPC cards under the heading *If the characters press*. Pressing a seat holder can silence them or force a small admission; their guild's interest stays where it is.

## Greenbottle

@[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar) recognizes this name. It can reach him in two ways: the names *Cortia* and *Portia Greenbottle* being said, or the description — two halfling spouses from the Beyond, wearing expensive cloth. Either one is enough; his three sentences are on the NPC card.

## The hall's decision

The attitudes of the five seats are above, and each comes from its own guild's interest — proof does not easily change that. What the hall decides comes out at the table.

npc_refs.value: Master of the Board — Perhun Mizan

mapping.dmNotes:
The weight of this scene is not in the decision: what can really be heard here is why each of the seats says no.

None of the seat holders means harm. Each one's silence comes from their own guild's interest.

The only one who speaks is @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar), and the reason the hall does not turn to look at him is not indifference: **Orvan's word is cheap.** For thirty years he asked everyone for something, worked a deal for everyone. The one day he tells the truth is the day no one believes him.

**The hall may never be reached.** This scene is not a stop but an open door: Orvan can be reached without ever going to the Assembly, and the sickness is not pursued only from here.

mapping.name: The Offer at the Door
mapping.description:
> The hall's heavy door closes behind you. The cool stone of the corridor sends back the sound of your steps, and somewhere a lamplighter is carrying a ladder. Someone is waiting at the head of the stairs: the man wearing the oldest coat in the hall. He does not look around. He walks straight to you, turns the seal ring on his finger once, and speaks without lowering his voice.
>
> *"What you said is true."*
mapping.beats:
## The door

**When this scene stands.** When @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar) has heard of the characters. The news can reach him four ways; one is enough:

- The characters bring up what they learned in Silverwater at @[The Assembly Session](entity:scene/The Assembly Session);
- @[Halim](entity:npc/Halim) reaches the city alive and his report reaches the seat — the characters' names are in that report;
- The characters hear his name from @[Halim](entity:npc/Halim) or elsewhere and look for him directly (@[The Table Nearest the Door](entity:scene/The Table Nearest the Door) · @[Border and Trade Guild Council Chamber](entity:location/Border and Trade Guild Council Chamber));
- The trio's real name or description reaches him.

The offer is in Orvan's hands. **Where, when, and whether he carries it himself or his apprentice does — yours.** It does not have to be at the door of the hall.

**Which doors can open from here.** The offer opens three jobs at once: @[Where They Came From](entity:quest/Where They Came From) (Orvan's job) · @[Good Writ](entity:quest/Good Writ) (a signature in advance: the countersignature on the passage paper) · @[The Continent on the Horizon](entity:quest/The Continent on the Horizon) (the ship the signature puts you on). A share in House Sancar's inheritance when the job is done.

## The offer

Orvan says three sentences:

1. *"What you said is true. No one in that hall will look at it, me included. My word carries no weight there."*
2. *"Ships are going missing. Not late, missing. And this sickness came into the continent on a ship. Find out why they go missing, stop it if need be. And bring me proof of this sickness that no one in that hall can deny."*
3. *"I have no money. What I can give is a signature, and I'll give the signature now. My house's share comes at the end of the job."*

## The reward

- **A signature — in advance.** Orvan gives the signature before the job, and does not sign himself: he puts the paper in front of his guild's signatory, @[Signatory — Selvi](entity:npc/Signatory — Selvi) (@[Border and Trade Guild Council Chamber](entity:location/Border and Trade Guild Council Chamber)). This is the countersignature on the passage paper, the signature that completes what the harbors call a *good writ*. The paper itself is collected from the @[Countersign Desk](entity:location/Countersign Desk); if another name is to be written on the paper, Orvan knows the way to that too (@[Bargemen's Inn](entity:location/Bargemen's Inn)). See @[Good Writ](entity:quest/Good Writ).
- **A share in his house's inheritance — when the job is done.** Orvan has no money to give, but he has a house: the Sancars, the Assembly's oldest seal. It is paid when the answer is brought to him.

## The untrustworthy man

If anyone asks about Orvan, what is heard in the city is not good: a man who plays favorites, runs schemes, wants something back for every favor. All of it is true, and Orvan does not deny it:

*"All true. What I'm saying today is true too. You have to carry both at once."*

No one works with him for the sake of a rumor. The weight of this offer is not in Orvan, but in Silverwater.

## The melting inheritance

Orvan's guild earns its income from trading ships, and the ships are both growing fewer and going missing. The share he offers shrinks every day because of the very problem he wants solved. If asked, he does not deny it: *"True. I can't wait. That's why I'm here."*

## The job's three ends

The three things Orvan wants are a single job: why the ships go missing, stopping it if need be, and hard proof of the sickness. Who brought the three strangers across sits where these three cross: the sickness came on a ship, and that ship never put in again. The trail leads to @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor); the sickness itself to the cabin and to @[Radenhall Courtyard](entity:location/Radenhall Courtyard).
mapping.dmNotes:
**Do not reveal the melting inheritance like a twist.** If the characters see it, they see it. Orvan not denying it earns him trust.

**Orvan does not know why the ships go missing**, and no card carries the answer. The answer is the DM's.

**The passage paper leaves a trace.** Both the preliminary approval and the countersignature are written in the ledger; where the characters go is known.

**There are other roads too.** Money gives the same voyage (@[Bargaining for Passage](entity:scene/Bargaining for Passage)); the harbor too is entered through two doors (@[Duran](entity:npc/Duran)/@[Corvin](entity:npc/Corvin), or through the ring via @[Kildrak Ferrun](entity:npc/Kildrak Ferrun)).

**Signature in advance, inheritance after.** A table that takes the signature can leave the continent without doing the job. Orvan knows this and gives it anyway: he has nothing in hand but bargaining, and a table that boards a ship passes along the road of the ships that never arrive.

**If not taken.** Even without the offer, @[Where They Came From](entity:quest/Where They Came From) stays open; the other way off the continent is money and the harbor (@[The Continent on the Horizon](entity:quest/The Continent on the Horizon)).

scene.source_name: In Line at the Passage Court

mapping.name: In Line at the Passage Court
mapping.description:
> The line does not move. The woman in front of you holds out the same paper to the desk for the third time, and for the third time the clerk, without looking up, says the same sentence: *"Its signature hasn't come."* The woman does not ask which signature. She takes her paper back, presses it unfolded to her chest and walks to the end of the line; the sound of her shoes on the stone carries down the corridor. One of the wall lamps sputters.
>
> The clerk looks up and lays an inky hand on the desk. It is your turn.
mapping.beats:
## The door

**When this scene stands.** If the characters want to leave the continent with a passage paper. The paper's first stop is this desk.

**The lock has two keys; one is enough:** a bribe · Orvan's name.

**If missed, no lock.** You can leave the continent without a countersignature too: money and @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor) (@[Bargaining for Passage](entity:scene/Bargaining for Passage)).

## Why here

The passage paper is collected from this desk, and it is collected under a name: the clerk writes the name and all the details on the paper, enters the paper in the ledger and signs it. This is called **preliminary approval**. The countersignature that makes the paper official is given by one of the guild's signatories, in a **signatory room** (@[Countersign Desk](entity:location/Countersign Desk)). A paper that has not come out of this desk never comes before any signatory.

## The obstacle

The clerk at the desk is @[Corin Sancar](entity:npc/Corin Sancar). He takes the paper, looks first at the signatures below it, then slides it to the bottom of the pile:

*"Pending. Its signature will come."*

If asked when, he gives no date. The woman waiting in line got the same answer for the third time. **This is not a refusal but a stretch of time.**

## Two roads

- **A bribe.** The wait shortens, no one is surprised, no one is angry; this is the desk on the continent where the most bribes are paid. @[Twine](entity:npc/Twine) knows the price; if not known, someone in line will tell.
- **Orvan's name.** Corin sits at that desk through Orvan's favor. On hearing the name he signs — and as he signs his face changes. This door is cheap, and Corin's resentment is included in the price.

## Forcing it

Threats or attempts to jump the line do not make Corin raise his voice. He puts the paper at the very bottom of the pile and calls the next name. There is police at the end of the corridor; @[Sergeant Krusk](entity:npc/Sergeant Krusk)'s men are inside in two steps.
mapping.dmNotes:
**This is not an investigation scene but a lock.** There is a paper in hand and the door is shut. The scene's whole weight is here: on this continent no one has to say *no*. The pile is always there, and the line never moves.

**Play it quickly.** As soon as one of the two keys comes to the table, the paper is signed. Do not turn this into a puzzle.

**Preliminary approval leaves a trace.** The paper is written in the ledger under the name brought to the desk: whose it is, on which ship, where they are going, is known in the city. Someone who wants to be written under another name comes to the desk under that name (@[Bargemen's Inn](entity:location/Bargemen's Inn)).

**If missed.** If preliminary approval is never obtained, the other way off the continent remains: money and @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor) (@[Bargaining for Passage](entity:scene/Bargaining for Passage), @[The Continent on the Horizon](entity:quest/The Continent on the Horizon)). Either road closes @[Good Writ](entity:quest/Good Writ).

mapping.name: The Customs Wharf
mapping.description:
> The customs official has a crate's lid opened and enters what is inside on the writing board one item at a time: how many bolts of cloth, how many sacks of cloves, from which ship. One of the sacks is torn; the sharp smell of spice mixes with the smell of wet stone. Behind them a crane lifts the next load into the air, its chain rattling, and the gnome at the top shouts something down. The official copies the list twice and drops one of the copies into a sealed bag marked *Lucid Triton*.
>
> The official holds the other copy out to you and keeps the pen ready. *"Your name?"*
mapping.beats:
## The door

**When this scene stands.** When the characters come to @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr) — getting off a ship, after a ship, or for official passage.

**Which doors can open from here.**

| Door | Its key |
|---|---|
| Official passage — crew on a trading ship | A countersigned passage paper (**good writ**). A paper collected from the desk but missing its countersignature is signed in the building's signatory room (@[Customs House](entity:location/Customs House)). The voyage: @[The Continent on the Horizon](entity:quest/The Continent on the Horizon) |
| *How unregistered passage is bought* | The @[Crane Master](entity:npc/Crane Master)'s night work. This question's second carrier; the first is @[Twine](entity:npc/Twine) at the harbor |
| What the ledgers say | The @[Archivist](entity:background/Archivist) background, or putting the weighbridge ledger and the cargo list side by side |

## Customs

Every load entering Elymsyr by ship passes through customs. The crates are opened, the goods counted, a list drawn up; a copy is sent to Lucid Triton. Everyone who gets off a ship is asked their name and their load.

**The punishment for smuggling** is lifelong hard labor on the river works.

## Who is on the wharf

- **The @[Customs Governor](entity:npc/Customs Governor)** in his room on the highest terrace. The man to talk to for official passage. He shows loads unloaded short as complete in the ledger; no error is found in the ledgers.
- **The @[Crane Master](entity:npc/Crane Master)** at the wharf's cranes. Provides a crane for some night unloadings; these loads are not written in the customs ledger.
- **@[Captain — Maren](entity:npc/Captain — Maren)** at the head of the pier, with the *Honest Scales*'s crew list. She signs on whoever has the paper.
- **@[The Interpreter](entity:npc/The Interpreter)** waiting for work at the head of the piers. He knows the fresh news of the ships from the Beyond.
- **The @[River Guard Sergeant](entity:npc/River Guard Sergeant)** in the towers of the narrows. She knows the ships passing through the narrows, and the chain.

## What is learned here

- **The ships' records.** Which ship did not arrive, which load was unloaded short, which crew did not go ashore: there are traces in the customs ledgers. A character who knows how to read ledgers (@[Archivist](entity:background/Archivist)) can see them.
- **Passage without customs.** The Crane Master's night work shows that entering the continent without passing through customs is possible here too.

## Boarding as crew

A countersigned passage paper shows its bearer as **crew** on a trading ship: not a passenger, a worker. That is why no fare is paid, and that is why they are counted at customs along with the cargo. The official writes the names in the ledger, copies the list twice, and sends a copy to Lucid Triton.

One of the ships at the pier looking for crew is @[Captain — Maren](entity:npc/Captain — Maren)'s *Honest Scales*: comes with a legal cargo, leaves with a legal cargo, and signs on no one without papers.

**A false identity.** If there is a @[Guild Scion of Rank](entity:background/Guild Scion of Rank) among the characters, @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar) arranges another name for them as well. Someone written onto that list under their house's name is recognized on the wharf, and this is the one place one would not want to be recognized.

That false name is a line Orvan invented in his own guild's ledger — if it is noticed, what kind of man Orvan is stands out in plain sight with no need to explain.

**The price.** Someone signed on as crew is not counted a passenger: watches are expected on board.

## Customs of the sea

Before setting out, sailors throw a piece of silver into the water.
mapping.dmNotes:
How passage without customs is bought sits in two places: here with the @[Crane Master](entity:npc/Crane Master), and at @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor) with @[Twine](entity:npc/Twine). Whichever one the table goes to, the line does not close.

A countersigned passage paper, that is, a good writ, gets you onto a ship in Elymsyr too.

mapping.name: Land Ho
mapping.description:
> The lookout at the top of the mast shouts something, and the wind carries off half the words. Everyone on deck turns the same way. For so long the horizon has been a line; now, somewhere on that line, there is a grey, low, motionless shadow. Not a cloud. A gull circles the mast once, cries, and flies toward the shadow.
>
> The deckhand beside you shades their eyes with a hand and says a single word: *"The Beyond."*
mapping.beats:
## The door

**When this scene stands.** If the characters have left the continent on a ship and the sea has been crossed. It makes no difference which ship: @[Captain — Maren](entity:npc/Captain — Maren), @[Captain Caelynn](entity:npc/Captain Caelynn) or @[Captain Holg](entity:npc/Captain Holg). What happens at sea, and how long it takes, is the DM's (@[The Open Sea](entity:location/The Open Sea)). If there are bitten on board, first: @[Quarantine Night](entity:scene/Quarantine Night).

**Which doors can open from here.** None. This scene is not a door but an ending: @[The Continent on the Horizon](entity:quest/The Continent on the Horizon) closes here, and the act ends here. Setting foot on the shore belongs to the next act.

## Playing the scene

- **Keep it short.** The moment the land appears is enough. Do not stretch the scene into an arrival, a harbor or a welcome.
- **Give everyone a moment.** Ask the characters what they left behind: Silverwater, a signature, a debt, a name. They do not have to answer.
- **Remember what is left in their hands.** The name of the *Fate*, the mark @[Enamel](entity:npc/Enamel) drew, @[The Sealless Ring](entity:trinket/The Sealless Ring), the sickness itself. None of their answers is written on this deck.

## By ship

- **If they came the legal way** they are crew: when the land appears they are on watch, and the captain does not let them drop the rope. Their names are on a customs list, the list's copy in Lucid Triton.
- **On Caelynn's ship** the deck is quiet; Caelynn does not look at the land, she looks at the sail.
- **On Holg's ship** the crew shouts, the bottle goes from hand to hand, and someone takes one last look at the passengers' belongings.
mapping.dmNotes:
**This is an ending scene.** No roll, no decision. The table should feel that it has finished something, and that something is beginning.

**The land on the horizon is @[Vorstrand](entity:location/Vorstrand)** — the Beyond, as the people say. In Meridia there is not a single verified piece of information about this continent (@[Vorstrand — What Is Known](entity:lore/Vorstrand — What Is Known)); there is little on the card on purpose. The single word in the deckhand's mouth is enough.

**The open questions stay open here:** why the ships go missing, on whose behalf the captain of the *Fate* carries, what the sickness is. If the table asks, point to the horizon.

mapping.name: Welcome in the Courtyard
mapping.description:
> The elder sitting among the stones gets up, walks to the middle of the giant stones and stops there. The sun is overhead; the stones' shadows have gathered at their feet, and a dry smell rises from the warm grass. Under the trees an adze falls silent. The elder turns the flat stone in her hand with her fingers and looks at you for a while. She does not ask what you have come for.
>
> *"You'll be asking about the rot,"* she says. She sits down at the foot of a stone, in the shade, and points with her hand to the place beside her.
mapping.beats:
## The door

**When this scene stands.** When the characters get past @[Path Scout — Addluin](entity:npc/Path Scout — Addluin) on the narrow path down to @[Radenhall Courtyard](entity:location/Radenhall Courtyard). The scout tells everyone who wants to cross the path to turn back, once.

**The path has two keys; one is enough:**

- Convincing the scout that their purpose is good;
- **Speaking of the rot.** Someone who asks about the rot in nature makes the scout take a second look — a character carrying the Arcana DC 13 trace of @[Blight — Infection](entity:curse/Blight — Infection), or someone who tells what they saw in Silverwater. The scout takes them in himself.

**Which doors can open from here.** Where the rot began and which way it is walking · seeing that it has been known here for months.

## The Courtyard

@[Eldest Druid — Halder](entity:npc/Eldest Druid — Halder) receives them as if they were someone she had been waiting for. She is not surprised, does not scold, does not grieve.

- **The druid tells.** If asked, she describes how she reads the rot in nature: where it began and which way it is walking.
- **Lateness.** There are no rumors about the sickness here, because everyone already knows. No one came to ask.
- **How long.** If asked how long she has known, she sidesteps: *"A long time."*
- **She can sense the sickness.** If one of the characters has been infected, the druid may sense it. Whether she senses it, and whether she says so, is the DM's.
- **The sherbet.** The recipe for the @[Sherbet of Resistance](entity:adventuring-gear/Sherbet of Resistance), and the trade for it, are here. What is asked in return is the DM's.

## The tribe

Someone who stays for a while sees how the tribe lives: the wooden houses under the trees, up in them and strung between them on vines, the evening songs among the stones, the herbs and sherbet traded. People of every race, every gender live together. No one here is written in a ledger, and no one misses it.
mapping.dmNotes:
Do not play this scene like a reward. An answer sits here, and beside the answer, how late it already is. That is the scene's tone.

Radenhall is not a required stop; no other card gives the map of the rot, but the act runs without that map too.

mapping.name: The Table Nearest the Door
mapping.description:
> The hearth is lit in the common room and most of the tables are full. At the table closest to the door, alone, sits a thin man with a long neck. The bowl in front of him has gone cold. No paper, no pen; he only listens. A villager tells what was heard at the well; the man tilts his head slightly and asks the same thing once more — as if he had not heard it the first time. Then he falls silent and repeats it, lips moving, to himself.
>
> Outside a voice rises. The man breaks off mid-sentence and looks at the door.
mapping.beats:
## The door

**When this scene stands.** When it is seen that @[Halim](entity:npc/Halim) is not a villager. There are two keys:

- **Insight DC 12** — shows he is not a villager, does not show whose man he is;
- **The guild line** (@[Guild Member](entity:background/Guild Member) · @[Guild Scion of Rank](entity:background/Guild Scion of Rank) · @[Guild Agent](entity:background/Guild Agent)) — no roll; they recognize him from his bearing, the way he listens, his waiting before speaking.

**Which door opens from here.** The name of @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar) and the road to @[Lucid Triton](entity:location/Lucid Triton) — and from there @[The Offer at the Door](entity:scene/The Offer at the Door).

**No lock.** The same door opens from three more places: going straight to the @[Border and Trade Guild Council Chamber](entity:location/Border and Trade Guild Council Chamber), speaking at @[The Assembly Session](entity:scene/The Assembly Session), or Halim getting back alive and his own report reaching the seat. Halim is not a door but a **shortcut.**

## Who sits at the table

The @[Border and Trade Guild](entity:lore/Border and Trade Guild) sent @[Halim](entity:npc/Halim) here **to look into the situation**. He was not asked to solve anything, fix anything, or find anyone: he will look, go back, report, and get paid. He describes the job exactly like that.

He is not an agent. A job accepted once, and a man who has long since realized it is not worth the money he took.

## Getting him to talk

No threats needed; two questions and a little patience are enough. Halim is not trying to hide anything; he just does not give it the first time he is asked:

- Asked who sent him, his first answer is *"I'm passing through"*, and he says it badly.
- The only name he knows is @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar). He has not met him face to face; he got the job from the seat's apprentice.
- He knows the Sancars are a fallen house and that this job's money will be paid late, and he complains about it.

*"They told me to look. I'm looking."*

## What Halim keeps

He takes no notes. He asks about what was told again and again, then memorizes it — a man who carries papers is easy to find. Everything the characters say beside him goes into that memory.
mapping.dmNotes:
A name from Halim's mouth is this act's shortest bridge: from Silverwater to @[Lucid Triton](entity:location/Lucid Triton).

**Do not build him as a source of information.** The only thing he knows is who sent him; about the sickness he knows less than the characters, and he does not hide it.

**A two-way door.** Whatever the characters said beside him is in the report that reaches the seat when he gets back alive — their names included. This is one of the triggers of @[The Offer at the Door](entity:scene/The Offer at the Door), and the characters do not need to know it.

mapping.name: The Petition Courtyard
mapping.description:
> The moment you enter the courtyard the sound changes: the noise of the avenue stays behind the gate, and in its place come the scratch of pens and now and then the name a clerk calls out. Under the courtyard, arcaded on three sides, people sit in rows, all with papers in their laps. The marble floor is worn hollow where the line stands.
>
> A clerk steps into the middle and reads out a name. No one stands. The clerk reads the name once more, then closes the list and goes inside.
mapping.beats:
## The door

**When this scene stands.** When the characters want to go up to the @[Assembly Hall](entity:location/Assembly Hall). The courtyard is open to all; **the line does not move on its own.**

**Four keys; one is enough.**

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| **A guild line** | A character with the @[Guild Member](entity:background/Guild Member) · @[Guild Scion of Rank](entity:background/Guild Scion of Rank) · @[Guild Agent](entity:background/Guild Agent) background joins the line from their own guild's office; their own clerk recognizes them |
| **What @[Halim](entity:npc/Halim) reported** | The office of the @[Border and Trade Guild](entity:lore/Border and Trade Guild) has already heard the characters' names |
| **A seat's name** | A tie made in the city with @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar) or another seat holder; on hearing the name the clerk shortens the line |
| **A bribe or patience** | A fee paid to one of the clerks, or waiting for days at the desk. Both work, both have a price |

**Which door opens from here.** @[The Assembly Session](entity:scene/The Assembly Session).

**No lock.** The road is open without ever going up to the Assembly: @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar) can be reached from his own guild's building (@[Border and Trade Guild Council Chamber](entity:location/Border and Trade Guild Council Chamber)).

## What is in the courtyard

Everyone who comes to the building first says which guild's business they are doing; only then do they join the line. On every door the guild's sign: hammer, scale, compass, sword, key — and on one door no sign.

**Names read and never answered.** Someone who stands in the courtyard for a long time may notice something: some of the names the clerks read out never get an answer and are not read again. Those names are not in the line; they are being held outside it — this building's counterpart to the pile at the @[Countersign Desk](entity:location/Countersign Desk).

**On this continent no one says no.** This is what the courtyard really teaches: a door does not close, the line does not move.
mapping.dmNotes:
This scene is not an obstacle but a **threshold**: it writes how the characters go up to the hall, and shows in a courtyard how the city works.

**Play it quickly.** As soon as one of the four keys comes to the table, the clerk reads the name. Do not turn this into a puzzle; what will be heard in the hall matters more than waiting in the courtyard.

Do not say here that decisions are not made in this building. They are made in rooms that do not look out on the courtyard (@[The Council and the Guild Assembly](entity:lore/The Council and the Guild Assembly)); in the hall they are only said, and the characters see that in the hall.

mapping.name: The Assay Table
mapping.description:
> On the table at the foot of the arch, stamping hammers lie lined up by size. A dwarf whose beard reaches the knees holds the piece in front of them up to the light and turns it slowly. The noise of the market reaches the table; the dwarf does not look up.
>
> Lowers the loupe. Says nothing for a while. Then sets the piece down on the table, right between the two of you.
mapping.beats:
## The door

**When this scene stands.** When @[The Sealless Ring](entity:trinket/The Sealless Ring) is put in front of an assay master. @[Kildrak Ferrun](entity:npc/Kildrak Ferrun)'s workbench is in the @[Upper Market](entity:location/Upper Market); finding it requires no roll, everyone in the market points it out.

**Which door opens from here.** Not a name but a **direction:** good work without a stamp, that is, a workbench outside the guilds, that is, a harbor. This is the second door to @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor); the first is @[Corvin](entity:npc/Corvin).

## What Kildrak reads

Kildrak holds the ring to the light, turns it, lowers the loupe. Then does not open the index — there is nothing to open it for:

*"There's no assay stamp on this. Never struck. The workmanship is good, but not labored over: whoever did it knew the work, but hurried and didn't sign it."*

*"On this continent a jeweler who does unstamped work doesn't sit at a guild workbench. Go south. Look for a harbor. If you can find one, your smith is there."*

Kildrak also sees the filed face and says what it means: *"Someone wanted to erase whose ring this is."*

Kildrak cannot give a name, because Kildrak does not know one.

## The price

**A workbench is a ledger.** Kildrak reads the piece, and what was read was read at a guild workbench. Here an unstamped piece opens not a sale but a **question**: the record of what is being sought may start going around the city ahead of those seeking it.

The cheap and traceless road is below: in the @[Lower Market](entity:location/Lower Market) no one asks about a stamp. But there the ring is not read, it is sold — and the chain's only object leaves their hands (@[Where They Came From](entity:quest/Where They Came From)).
mapping.dmNotes:
What Kildrak gives is not a name but a direction, and this is on purpose. No one in the city can point to @[Enamel](entity:npc/Enamel), because there is no stamp to follow.

**This scene is not required.** The harbor can also be reached through @[Corvin](entity:npc/Corvin); the ring may never have been found. As long as one of the two doors stays open, the line does not close.

**The record spreading is not a punishment but a price.** Do not warn the characters in advance; if they notice, they notice.

mapping.name: Empty Racks
mapping.description:
> On the village's windward slope there are rows of drying racks, and most are empty. The ropes have not been cut but **torn**: their ends frayed into fibers, a few still swinging. In the sand beneath them are two rows of broad, webbed prints; both turn toward the sea and end at the waterline.
>
> Among the racks an oldish man talks while he goes on knotting the net in his hands. He does not look at you; he looks at the racks:
>
> *"Fourteen racks. Nine empty. Fourth night."*
mapping.beats:
## The door

**When this scene stands.** When the characters stop at @[Argenfon](entity:location/Argenfon). **The quest is heard nowhere else** — if asked at the castle, the answer is honest: *"We looked. Quiet."*

**Which doors can open from here.** None is required.

| Door | Its key |
|---|---|
| What the damage is | @[Sevran](entity:npc/Sevran) — no roll, tells it without being asked |
| *"They didn't come by land"* | The prints in the sand turn toward the sea; whoever looks sees |
| An empty shell | It lies somewhere on the shore. Perception, or walking the shore |
| What they are | Looking at the empty shell or the prints, **History DC 8 / 12 / 15** (@[Hıkka — The Record in the Books](entity:lore/Hıkka — The Record in the Books)) |
| Spice | @[Iraz](entity:npc/Iraz)'s untouched rack — no roll, it is there in the village |
| When they came | In the village, people count who lost what on which night. The answer is in the tide |

**If missed, no lock.** If the table never stops at the village, this chain never opens, and nothing is missing from the act.

## The racks

The dried fish is the village's winter food; what is lost is not money but **February**. Ropes torn rather than cut, broad webbed prints, and no blood anywhere — none of it requires a roll.

## The state of the village

There is worry and it is spoken of openly, but every sentence ends tied to the same place: *"it'll be handled."* They went to the castle, a patrol came, stayed two nights, saw nothing. No one feels like bothering the knights a second time over fish (`bolge §5.2`).

No one asks anything of the table. Sevran tells the trouble and leaves it there.

## The tide

Which nights the losses happened on is **countable** in the village — no one has put the two lists side by side. Whoever does sees it: the raids happen on the nights **the water recedes the most**.

It has three carriers; one is enough: asking the fisher (no roll) · waiting two nights (no roll, time is there) · **Nature or Survival DC 12**.
mapping.dmNotes:
**This is not a job-giving scene.** No one assigns anything; there is damage on the table, and the table takes it up if it wants.

**Why the paladins did not find it — all four at once, and none of them makes them look foolish:**

1. The nest is not on the shore but **under the shore** (@[Tide Mouth](entity:location/Tide Mouth)); the patrol walks the beach.
2. A different cove every night — no single path.
3. **On the nights there is a patrol, they do not come ashore.** The sound of armor and the torches show from the water; so the patrol's report always comes out *"quiet"*. The method is built in such a way that it cannot see what it is looking for.
4. **They do not know what they are looking for** — this species has no witness living in Meridia.

Chain: @[Night of the Tide](entity:quest/Night of the Tide).

mapping.name: The Receding Water
mapping.description:
> The water has been receding for hours. At the foot of the rocks a strip has opened that was never visible before: wet, black stone covered with mussel shells.
>
> And under the lowest step, a hand's breadth above the ground, there is **a mouth as wide as a pair of shoulders**. Its edges are smooth — something has been going in and out of there for a long time. The inside cannot be seen.
>
> In the water behind the mouth something stands and does not move. Then that broken, stuttering sound comes, and you realize the rock is breathing.
mapping.beats:
## The door

**When this scene stands.** When the table is at the right cove, at the hour **the water recedes the most**. For someone who comes at the wrong hour there is not even a door — the waves come right up to the foot of the rock and end there.

**The keys** (one is enough): working out the tide line (@[Empty Racks](entity:scene/Empty Racks)) · **following** a Hıkka on the shore one night · combing the coast with @[Sevran](entity:npc/Sevran)'s boat.

**Which doors can open from here.**

| Door | What happens |
|---|---|
| The nest's location found | The quest's goal is completed here. The rest is what to do |
| Going inside | The mouth is narrow; **an armored human cannot get in**, an unarmored one gets in by crawling. And the mouth is held by the @[Holdfast](entity:monster/Holdfast) |
| Turning back | Always open, always free — that thing does not chase |

## The mouth

As wide as a pair of shoulders, a hand's breadth above the ground, passable only at the lowest tide. After a few meters the water drops away and opens into an **air pocket**; the colony is there.

Going inside is a choice, not a necessity — and going in means thirty of them coming at you at once (@[No Threshold](entity:trait/No Threshold)).

## What holds the mouth

The @[Holdfast](entity:monster/Holdfast) does not leave the water, does not chase, does not budge. When struck, nothing happens. A 2nd-level table is not expected to get past it, and it does not have to.

## A fight does not have to break out here

A table that stops in front of the mouth and turns back has **completed** its quest: what was sought was the nest's location, and the location has been found.
mapping.dmNotes:
**The goal ends here, the decision begins here.** The card tells no one to go inside; three of the four endings of @[Night of the Tide](entity:quest/Night of the Tide) take place outside this mouth.

**A light warning.** A table that comes with torches is not seen — because they cannot see in firelight anyway. But it is heard. And @[Hiccup](entity:trait/Hiccup) works both ways: the table hears them too.

**They need no reason to be aggressive here.** Within 30 ft of the nest there is no threshold.

mapping.name: Maren's Course
mapping.description:
> At the end of the watch the captain calls you to the stern cabin. A sea chart lies open on the table; on its corners have been set a rope knife, an inkwell and half a ship's biscuit. The lantern swings from the ceiling, and with every wave the shadows slide from one end of the chart to the other. The cabin smells of wet wool and tar; between the planks you can hear the water striking the hull. Between the two coasts there is a thick, straight line: the trade route everyone knows. The dots showing the ship's track left that line long ago and are drawing a wide arc.
>
> The captain lays her hand, two fingers missing, on the arc. *"The crew keeps grumbling, you've heard. They say this isn't the route. True."* She does not lift her eyes from the chart. *"Go on, ask why."*
mapping.beats:
## The door

**When this scene stands.** If the characters have been signed on as crew of the *Honest Scales* and the ship is on the open sea. The crew talks among themselves about the course leaving the trade route; the characters can ask the captain, or @[Captain — Maren](entity:npc/Captain — Maren) can call them to her cabin at the end of a watch.

**Which doors can open from here.** Which road the missing ships took: @[Where They Came From](entity:quest/Where They Came From).

## What Maren tells

She opens up as she is asked, and in this order:

- **Openly.** They are not taking the trade route, and on purpose. All the ships that should have come to the continent and did not were following that route. The arc lengthens the voyage: the water and provisions are reckoned for it, and so is the crew's patience.
- **If asked.** She does not know what is on the route; no one knows, because no one has come back. *"I don't sail the road of something I don't know. I go around it."*
- **If she trusts them.** One of the missing ships was the ship of one of her former crew. She told no one at customs; even if she had, the ledger would not have changed.
- **The end of the arc.** At the end of the chart near the Beyond, the arc ends. Every course that reaches the coast has to turn toward land in the end, and the last water is everyone's shared water. *"There's no room to go around there."*

## On board

The crew grumbles but does not go against the captain's word; the watches grow longer, the water ration smaller. A character with the @[Ship Captain](entity:background/Ship Captain) background, looking at the chart, reads without asking how much the arc lengthens the voyage.
mapping.dmNotes:
## What is at sea

In **four regions of the route between the continents there are four ships of the Black Fleet**; a different ship in each region. @[Captain — Maren](entity:npc/Captain — Maren)'s arc passes outside the first three regions, and the *Honest Scales* does not meet those three ships.

The fourth region is the one closest to @[Vorstrand](entity:location/Vorstrand), and the ship there is **the smallest** of the four:

- **An orc warship:** @[Black Sail](entity:location/Black Sail). Under sail, a little smaller than the *Honest Scales*. Its hull pitch-black, its sails pitch-black; war drums on its deck.
- **Its captain is an orc,** not turned and of sound mind. So is her crew.
- **In a hold below deck, @[the Turned](entity:monster/The Turned) are kept.** Someone looking from outside does not see this: the ship looks like nothing but an orc warship.

**Maren knows none of this.** The only thing she knows is which route the missing ships followed; she does not know why they did not arrive.

The end of the arc: @[The Sound of Drums](entity:scene/The Sound of Drums) → @[Hull to Hull](entity:encounter/Hull to Hull).

What the other three ships are, why the fourth waits there and why it carries the Turned is the DM's.

The voyage: @[The Continent on the Horizon](entity:quest/The Continent on the Horizon). When land appears on the horizon: @[Land Ho](entity:scene/Land Ho).

mapping.name: The Sound of Drums
mapping.description:
> The lookout at the top of the mast does not shout a word; they whistle, two short, one long. Everyone on deck looks the same way, but there is nothing on the horizon. Then the wind turns and the sound comes: a deep, heavy drum. Three beats, a silence, three beats. Somewhere on the horizon a sail appears, and it has no color — pitch-black, like a hole in the middle of the water's glitter.
>
> The drum quickens. Someone runs to the captain.
mapping.beats:
## The door

**When this scene stands.** If the characters are at sea on a ship and the ship is in the last water near the Beyond. The *Honest Scales*'s arc ends there (@[Maren's Course](entity:scene/Maren's Course)); the course of the other two ships is the DM's.

**Which doors can open from here.** @[Hull to Hull](entity:encounter/Hull to Hull).

## The black ship

@[Black Sail](entity:location/Black Sail) knows this water and has the wind behind it; it is faster than a ship carrying cargo. Escaping it takes not a roll but an idea — throwing the cargo overboard, a fog, a spell. If the table finds such an idea, it works.

## The chase

**Three rounds.** Each character does one thing each round and makes one roll, DC 12:

- **Sail and rope** — Athletics.
- **Reading the wind and the water** — Survival; someone with the @[Ship Captain](entity:background/Ship Captain) background rolls with advantage.
- **Lookout** — Perception. Success shows how many shields are on the black ship, the chains at the bow, and the iron-banded hatch on the waist deck.
- **Listening to the drum** — Insight or Arcana. Success says this: the ship is under sail, it has no rowers; this drum is making no one row. It is telling someone something else.
- **Preparation** — Persuasion or Intimidation: dividing the crew into teams, handing out axes, getting the ballista set up.

**Each success** wins the table an advantage, the character chooses:

- **A shot.** The ballista fires once before the boarding is made (only on the *Honest Scales*).
- **Axes ready.** Attacks against the hook chains in the first round have advantage.
- **Crew in place.** One crew team takes no losses in the first two rounds.
- **Seen.** The table goes into the fight knowing about the hatch.

**Each failure** helps the black ship: the boarding is made while a character is far from their post, or in the first round four hooks come instead of two.

## By ship

- **On @[Captain Caelynn](entity:npc/Captain Caelynn)'s ship** DC 10: a sober crew, a good hull.
- **On @[Captain Holg](entity:npc/Captain Holg)'s ship** DC 14: the crew hides the bottle first, then grabs the rope.
mapping.dmNotes:
**In this scene the table sees an orc warship,** nothing else: a black sail, a drum, a line of shields. The lower hold is not visible; at most a hatch is seen.

The end of the chase: @[Hull to Hull](entity:encounter/Hull to Hull). The advantages won carry over there.

mapping.name: Quarantine Night
mapping.description:
> The deck has been washed, but the planks are still slippery. A cough comes from under the hold hatch, then another. The bitten sit side by side below, in the light of a lantern; one has unwrapped the bandage on their shoulder and is looking at the thin, purplish-black lines at the edge of the wound. Above, the crew has made a ring around the hatch: no one comes closer, no one moves away. The wind carries soot and salt.
>
> Someone brings a rope, and without looking at anyone threads it through the hatch's ring.
mapping.beats:
## The door

**When this scene stands.** If after @[Hull to Hull](entity:encounter/Hull to Hull) there is someone bitten on board — from the crew or the characters.

**Which doors can open from here.** @[Land Ho](entity:scene/Land Ho).

## What is on board

- **The bitten.** The crew counted in the fight. No one knows which of them has caught the sickness. For each bitten person the DM secretly rolls the bite's own save (@[Leaping Bite](entity:creature-action/Leaping Bite)): **Constitution saving throw, DC 8.** Those who make it stay clean. Those who fail take **1 Sickness Score** — they are now carriers, they infect others, and they are in incubation: a slight cough, thin purplish-black veins at the joints, a metallic taste in the mouth. A bitten character made this roll in the fight, at the moment of the bite; they do not roll again here.
- **What the crew wants.** To separate the bitten, and keep them shut in the hold. Some want more than that.
- **Contagion.** Whoever spends a night in the same closed space as the bitten, dresses their wounds or touches their fluids makes the exposure roll: **CON DC 12**, +1 Sickness Score on a failure (@[Blight — Infection](entity:curse/Blight — Infection)).
- **Reading it.** **Medicine DC 12**: the purplish-black veins at the edge of the wound are the same as the trace described from Silverwater. It has no name; not at the table either.
- **The corpses.** Whoever throws the Turned corpses into the sea makes the exposure roll.
- **The black ship.** Behind: if burning, a red line on the horizon; if taken, in tow; if it fled, its drum fading away.

## By ship

- **@[Honest Scales](entity:location/Honest Scales).** @[Captain — Maren](entity:npc/Captain — Maren) does not abandon her crew, but she does not open the hatch either. @[Scales Sergeant — Hulda](entity:npc/Scales Sergeant — Hulda) counts and wants the bitten kept apart; the two argue this out on deck, in front of everyone.
- **On @[Captain Caelynn](entity:npc/Captain Caelynn)'s ship** order does not break: Caelynn takes the bitten down to the hold and puts a guard on the hatch. If a passenger was bitten, them too.
- **On @[Captain Holg](entity:npc/Captain Holg)'s ship** the crew wants to throw the bitten overboard. Holg does not stop them.
mapping.dmNotes:
**This is a decision scene, not a dice scene.** The table decides who is put where. The world's only answer is silence: there is no known treatment (@[Blight — Infection](entity:curse/Blight — Infection)).

The player of a bitten character knows their score; the character knows only the metal taste in their mouth.

When land appears on the horizon: @[Land Ho](entity:scene/Land Ho).

mapping.name: The Smugglers' Deck
mapping.description:
> The harbor's lights shrink behind you and then go out. The place set aside for you on deck is at the foot of a hold hatch, between two barrels: neither wide enough to lie down nor sheltered from the wind. The crew looks at you, and pretends not to. Somewhere a lantern sputters; the hull groans with every wave, and under the salt it smells of tar and cheap rum.
>
> The captain walks the deck once from end to end, and stops beside you.
mapping.beats:
## The door

**When this scene stands.** If the characters boarded a ship from @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor) (@[Bargaining for Passage](entity:scene/Bargaining for Passage)).

**Which doors can open from here.** @[The Sound of Drums](entity:scene/The Sound of Drums) · @[Land Ho](entity:scene/Land Ho).

## On @[Captain Caelynn](entity:npc/Captain Caelynn)'s ship

About ten sober crew, and everything has its place. Caelynn wants to see the passengers' bundles once; she does not stow them without seeing them. In the hold, barrels of lamp oil in a row.

- **If asked.** She has heard of the missing ships. *"I don't carry cargo I can't see. And I don't sail water I can't see."* She does not say her course.

## On @[Captain Holg](entity:npc/Captain Holg)'s ship

About eight crew; dice, a bottle, and eyes that slide toward the passengers' belongings. One of the crew, if they find the chance, lays a hand on one of the bundles some night. In the hold, barrels of rum. The gunwale is patched; one patch still unpainted.

- **If asked.** Holg laughs. *"If a ship didn't come, its captain was bad."*

## On both ships

An old deckhand, on the night watch, tells without being asked: in the water near the Beyond, drums are heard at night. They do not know who plays them. Whoever knows does not tell.
mapping.dmNotes:
**These ships' course is the DM's.** Whichever it is, the last water near the Beyond is everyone's shared water (@[The Open Sea](entity:location/The Open Sea)).

Keep the barrels to one side: if the black ship is met, they are fire's shortest road (@[Hull to Hull](entity:encounter/Hull to Hull)).

mapping.name: Dawn Clash
mapping.description: The three strangers who talked in the cabin have turned and are walking toward the village.
mapping.setup:
> The cabin door swings outward and hangs from a single hinge. The first out is the halfling: the man who fell asleep in the middle of a sentence is now running. His bare feet make no sound as they crush the wet grass. In the darkness behind him two more bodies stir, and a sour, metallic smell spreads from the cabin. On the village road a cauldron tips over, a door slams. Two youths with spears stand between the cabin and the village, trying to understand what they are looking at.
>
> The halfling turns toward the sound of your voice.

## The area

The cabin, the scrubby path and the village's last houses. The path is wide enough for two people to walk side by side; on both sides, waist-high scrub (difficult terrain). It is sixty paces to the village's last house.

## Layout

**Staggered exit.** First @[Turned Alton](entity:monster/Turned Alton) comes out. A round later @[Turned Merla](entity:monster/Turned Merla) and @[Turned Kromanna](entity:monster/Turned Kromanna) come out.

**The militia.** The village's two volunteer militia are on the path. They have spears in hand and do not know what to do. If the characters say nothing to them, they do not move from their places in the first round.
mapping.tactics:
**The Turned use no tactics.** They do not aim, do not withdraw, do not surrender. They walk toward the nearest sound and movement — and if the leap is ready, they leap. The scrub on both sides of the path does not slow them: the 15 ft leap jumps the difficult terrain.

**Roll Turned Merla's Fitful die in the open.** Let the players see that the three Turned are nothing alike.

**Turned Kromanna is the most dangerous.** She attacks twice on her first turn.

**The claw does not infect, the bite does.** No saving throw is made for a claw hit. @[Leaping Bite](entity:creature-action/Leaping Bite) is different: the leap needs no attack roll, deals 1d8, and the character hit rolls **CON DC 8** — on a failure +1 Sickness Score (@[Blight — Infection](entity:curse/Blight — Infection)). Roll each Turned's leap recharge (5–6) at the start of every round.

After the fight, the normal exposure roll also applies to characters who search the corpses or carry the wounded.

**Lasting Wounds.** A character dropping to 0 hit points is likely, and a roll of 1–5 can leave a character permanently lame. Tell the players the rule **before** the fight. See @[Rule Deviations](entity:lore/Rule Deviations).

**The villagers.** The villagers shut their doors. If the militia fight beside the characters they can draw the Turned's attacks onto themselves; if they are not protected, they may die.

## Afterward

The corpses are the corpses of the people who talked in the cabin. Everything on them is in place: clothes of foreign cloth, a full purse, blank scrolls, and @[The Sealless Ring](entity:trinket/The Sealless Ring) in @[Kromanna](entity:npc/Kromanna)'s hidden pocket.
mapping.dmNotes:
**Difficulty.** The three Turned together are worth 100 XP; a party of four 1st-level characters can handle it. The threat is not in the numbers but in the direction: the Turned do not stop, do not withdraw, and walk toward the village. If no one gets between them, the villagers face this on their own.

- **To make it easier:** use the staggered exit above.
- **To make it harder:** all three come out at once.
- **If the characters are 2nd level**, all three come out at once.

mapping.name: The Night Worksite
mapping.description: The hired watchmen who hold the @[Military Law Chamber](entity:location/Military Law Chamber) at night.
mapping.setup:
> There is no one on the terrace street but you. An orange light leaks through the gap in the front window's shutters; from inside comes the sound of bone dice hitting wood and a low curse. The scaffold put up against the side of the house creaks in the wind, and the smell of tar is heavy here, even in the street. In front of the door a watchman leaning against the wall has set his lantern on the ground and is blowing into his palms.
>
> The insides of the masks warm with your breath.

## The area

Three floors, one map (@[Military Law Chamber](entity:location/Military Law Chamber)): the ground floor on the left, the upper floor on the right, the cellar below; the same letter is the same passage. On the ground floor a hearth and a lantern are burning; the upper floor and the cellar are dark. The cellar hatch (**B**) is in the hearth hall, beside the long table. The scaffold on the left outer wall (**C**) goes from the street straight up to the upper floor; the upper floor has no door to the street, it is entered from the scaffold through the window openings.

## Layout

- **At the door:** one @[Site Watchman](entity:monster/Site Watchman), with a lantern.
- **By the hearth:** two @[Hired Cutlass](entity:monster/Hired Cutlass) playing dice at the long table; beside them a Site Watchman.
- **Upstairs:** two Site Watchmen beside the timber stack. One is asleep.
- **In the clerks' room:** the @[Head Watchman](entity:monster/Head Watchman), at a writing desk. The chest's key is on his belt.
- **The cellar:** empty. The chest is in the cellar's back room, in the corner, behind the barrels.
mapping.tactics:
**The watchmen were not hired to die.** The Site Watchmen flee or surrender when they drop below half their hit points; one who flees goes out into the street and shouts. The Hired Cutlasses fight as long as the Head Watchman stays standing; if he falls, they flee.

**The Head Watchman knows his job.** He stands where he can see the door and the cellar hatch. On his first turn he shoots whoever comes through the door with the pistol, and turns on whoever comes close with the rapier. Below half his hit points he opens the key to bargaining.

**Noise.** A fight that starts on the ground floor brings those upstairs down. The sound of breaking open the locked chest wakes the whole house.

**Fire.** Fire can be used in the middle of the fight too. If a tar bucket on the upper floor tips over and catches, that square and the adjacent squares burn; whoever ends their turn in a burning square takes 1d10 fire damage. The fire spreads one square each round, and if it reaches the timber stack, the upper floor burns end to end within a minute. The stone walls do not burn.

**The street.** The noise draws the neighbors to their windows; no one comes outside. A growing fire is seen from the River Guard's towers.

**Lasting Wounds.** The rule applies; tell the players **before** the fight. See @[Rule Deviations](entity:lore/Rule Deviations).

## Afterward

On the Head Watchman, the chest's key and a purse of 2d10 gold. In the watchmen's pockets, a few coppers, a deck of cards and enough bread to last till morning.
mapping.dmNotes:
**Difficulty.** Four Site Watchmen, two Hired Cutlasses and the Head Watchman together are worth 1250 XP: hard for a party of four 3rd-level characters, deadly for 1st–2nd level. Almost all of the weight is in the Head Watchman.

- **To make it easier:** reduce the Head Watchman's three attacks to two, his hit points to 52; or have the Head Watchman not be in the house that night, taking the key with him.
- **To make it harder:** put two more Hired Cutlasses at the door.
- **Without fighting:** this fight is not a condition of the job. A table that climbs to the upper floor from the scaffold, lures the watchmen outside, or gets the key some other way may never draw a sword.

mapping.name: Hull to Hull
mapping.description: @[Black Sail](entity:location/Black Sail) boards the characters' ship. It is not the orcs who cross first, but those who come out of the lower hold.
mapping.setup:
> The black hull is so close now that you can pick out the faces at its gunwale one by one: ash grey, earth brown, greenish faces; all painted with black soot. Something whistles through the air and a hook bites into your gunwale, then another. The chains tighten; the two hulls creak toward each other. The drum changes rhythm: instead of three beats, a single, heavy, long one. In the middle of the black ship two orcs lift an iron-banded hatch, and from under the hatch a sour, metallic smell comes to you on the wind.
>
> Something stirs in the dark.

## The area

The two ships hull to hull. The gap between them is **15 ft**; it closes as the hook chains tighten.

- **Your own deck.** Bow, waist and stern; which ship it is, below.
- **The gap.** Water beneath. The hook chains stretch taut over the gap.
- **@[Black Sail](entity:location/Black Sail).** The hatch on the waist deck, the drum and the captain on the quarterdeck.

**The hook chains.** Each AC 11, 5 hit points; slashing damage or an attempt to pry it loose (Athletics DC 13). If no chain remains attached, the ships separate and the gap opens 5 ft each round. The orcs do not cross until the gap is down to **5 ft**; the Turned jump the 15 ft with their leap.

## Layout

- **At the bow and waist:** two @[Hookman](entity:monster/Hookman)s.
- **At the waist gunwale:** eight @[Orc Warrior](entity:monster/Orc Warrior)s, shields on the gunwale.
- **On the quarterdeck:** the @[Drummer](entity:monster/Drummer) at the head of the drum, the @[Orc Captain](entity:monster/Orc Captain) beside it.
- **In the lower hold:** eight to ten @[Turned](entity:monster/The Turned), among them one or two @[Turned Orc](entity:monster/Turned Orc)s.
- **On your own deck:** the crew, in teams of three or four.
mapping.tactics:
**The orcs do not go first.** The fight comes in waves:

1. **Hooks.** The Hookmen throw the chains, the Orc Warriors throw javelins from the gunwale.
2. **The hatch.** The drum switches to *Come* and the hatch opens. **The first wave is four Turned**: they jump the gap with @[Leaping Bite](entity:creature-action/Leaping Bite) and land on the nearest. Each time the Drummer plays *Come*, two more come out.
3. **The orcs.** When the defense on the opposite deck breaks — fewer than two crew teams left standing, or the Turned have broken a team — the Orc Warriors cross over the chains.
4. **The captain** stays on the quarterdeck.

**The drum.** The lock of the battle is the drum (@[Rhythm](entity:creature-action/Rhythm)). Seeing that the Turned change with the rhythm is **Arcana or Insight DC 12**. If the drum falls silent, the Turned attack the nearest — the orcs too, if they are on the black ship.

**Countermoves the table can find:**
