- **Going for the drum.** Crossing the gap: jumping, **Athletics DC 10** (no roll at 5 ft), over the chain, **Acrobatics DC 12**. The drum is AC 12, 10 hit points.
- **Shutting the hatch.** A heavy hatch: **Athletics DC 13**, DC 15 if it is being pushed from below. To lock it, the captain's key, or a bar of iron thrust through its ring — one action.
- **Burning the black sails.** A sail is AC 10; 5 or more fire damage sets it alight, and each round the fire takes one more sail. In the round a sail catches, half the orcs run to the fire and do not attack.
- **Going for the captain.** If the captain falls or surrenders, the orcs stop fighting. The Turned do not.

**The crew.** The crew is not played one by one. At the end of each round, every team that is fighting a Turned or an orc and has no character within 30 ft loses **1d4 people**: half fall, half are bitten. Count the bitten.

**Lasting Wounds.** The rule applies; tell the players **before** the fight. See @[Rule Deviations](entity:lore/Rule Deviations). A bite is an exposure: @[Blight — Infection](entity:curse/Blight — Infection).

## By ship

- **@[Honest Scales](entity:location/Honest Scales).** About twenty-two people: @[Captain — Maren](entity:npc/Captain — Maren), @[Scales Sergeant — Hulda](entity:npc/Scales Sergeant — Hulda) and four guards, four crew teams. The ballista at the stern. Maren does not leave the helm.
- **@[Captain Caelynn](entity:npc/Captain Caelynn)'s ship.** About ten people, two teams; a sober, orderly crew. Barrels of lamp oil in the hold: a barrel thrown and lit burns a 10 ft square (2d6 fire), and is the shortest road to the black sails. Caelynn tries to turn away before the boarding is made.
- **@[Captain Holg](entity:npc/Captain Holg)'s ship.** About eight people, two teams. The patched gunwale cannot take the chain's pull: once the hooks hold, the gap drops to 5 ft at once. Barrels of rum in the hold, burning like lamp oil. When the first Turned lands on deck, Holg tries to turn the passengers into bargaining goods; whether the orc captain listens is the DM's.

## Afterward

Whether the black ship burns, is taken or escapes is the table's. On the captain, the hatch's key and a purse of 3d10 gold. If someone bitten has stayed on board: @[Quarantine Night](entity:scene/Quarantine Night). Every character who throws the Turned corpses into the sea or carries the wounded makes the normal exposure roll.
mapping.dmNotes:
**Difficulty.** The part that falls to the table — the Drummer, the four-Turned first wave and the Orc Captain — is worth 650 XP: hard for a table of three 2nd-level characters. The Orc Warriors and Hookmen (600 XP) fight the crew; if the characters cross to the black ship they meet them too, and the fight slides into deadly. Each time *Come* is played the budget grows. This is on purpose: that is why the drum must be silenced.

- **To make it easier:** a first wave of three Turned; the Orc Captain with a single attack and 26 hit points.
- **To make it harder** (a table of four, or 3rd level): one Turned Orc in the first wave; two Orc Warriors cross with the first wave.
- **Left over from the chase:** the advantages won in @[The Sound of Drums](entity:scene/The Sound of Drums) are spent here.
- **Ending without a fight:** if the drum falls silent and the captain surrenders, the fight ends. This is not an escape; those under the hatch are still there.

**If the deck is searched:** in the cabin, the paper waiting for the characters (@[Black Sail](entity:location/Black Sail), `secrets`).

mapping.name: Chasing the Rumor
mapping.description: Rumors of the sickness set the characters on the road to Silverwater. What happened in the village, and how far that knowledge can go.
mapping.objective:
The rumor leads to @[Silverwater](entity:location/Silverwater). What happened in the village is there; what is done after that is the table's.

## Open doors

None has an order, none is required.

| Door | How it opens |
|---|---|
| **The village** | @[Arrival at the Village](entity:scene/Arrival at the Village) — the well, the inn, @[Goodbarrel's Hearth](entity:location/Goodbarrel's Hearth) |
| **The cabin** | @[Questioning at the Cabin](entity:scene/Questioning at the Cabin) — the village's rule is not a prohibition, the door is open |
| **The turning** | @[The Dawn Turning](entity:scene/The Dawn Turning) — the three's threshold is full, the moment is the DM's. If someone stands between the cabin and the village, @[Dawn Clash](entity:encounter/Dawn Clash) |
| **The city** | Who @[Halim](entity:npc/Halim) is (@[The Table Nearest the Door](entity:scene/The Table Nearest the Door)) → @[The Petition Courtyard](entity:scene/The Petition Courtyard) → @[The Assembly Session](entity:scene/The Assembly Session) |
| **The castle** | @[Votumar](entity:location/Votumar) — @[The Last Written Order](entity:quest/The Last Written Order): the one running the castle is @[Deputy Lord Commander — Aren](entity:npc/Deputy Lord Commander — Aren); @[Lord Commander — Varhan](entity:npc/Lord Commander — Varhan) has not been there for two months |
| **Radenhall** | @[What the Stones Know](entity:quest/What the Stones Know) — @[Welcome in the Courtyard](entity:scene/Welcome in the Courtyard): the map of the rot, and how late it already is |

**The two authorities are not in the same city, and neither is required.** One can go to the Assembly, or to Votumar; to both, or to neither.

## When this job leaves the table

It has no single ending. The job counts as closed when one of these happens:

- What they saw reaches an authority — the Assembly or Votumar;
- The village comes to an outcome — standing or broken, both are outcomes;
- The table leaves Silverwater behind, with an answer or without one.

---

mapping.reward:
**If Silverwater stays standing**, the village is in their debt: provisions and beds cost nothing, and @[Duran](entity:npc/Duran) talks about the things he would not talk about.

What can be taken from the village: the sickness's name; that the three strangers came from a harbor; a man who knows the way to the harbor; the ring in @[Kromanna](entity:npc/Kromanna)'s hidden pocket; the *Greenbottle* line inside the wedding bands; and, if someone knows magic, that there is more than a sickness on them.

**Two names that may be left in hand on coming back from an authority:** the only seat that believes in the sickness (@[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar)), and a commander who never blinks.
mapping.secrets:
**The three strangers in the cabin came to the village sick.** They set out from @[the Beyond](entity:location/Vorstrand) and entered the continent through @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor) without passing through customs. Silverwater is not the source of the sickness.

All three are about to pass into the last stage; the threshold is written, the moment is yours. **There is no known way to stop the Blight** — no one on this continent knows one, and no treatment sits on the cards. The table trying is not a mistake; the world's answer is silence.

This quest is not tied to any particular character; every character has set out on hearing the rumor of sickness.

**Both authorities have a refusal ready, but not for the same reason.** The Assembly's seats are sincere; each sees the sickness only through the eyes of their own profession. @[Lord Commander — Varhan](entity:npc/Lord Commander — Varhan) refuses not because he does not believe, but **to gain time**. The player may not sense the difference; you should know it.

**What Votumar gives is not the sickness but the Lord Commander himself:** a tower's vanished report, the order column of @[Gate Commander — Nevra](entity:npc/Gate Commander — Nevra) empty for two months, and @[Deputy Lord Commander — Aren](entity:npc/Deputy Lord Commander — Aren). Three carriers; one is enough.

**The real names.** The *C. & P. Greenbottle* line inside the wedding bands and the description of two halfling spouses lead to the same door: @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar) recognizes either one.

Three jobs can open from here: @[Where They Came From](entity:quest/Where They Came From), @[Good Writ](entity:quest/Good Writ) and @[The Continent on the Horizon](entity:quest/The Continent on the Horizon).
mapping.dmNotes: The card list is at the bottom of the quest's own page. The other chains and the place/character cards: @[Index](entity:lore/Index). The adventure's situation and how to run it: @[Aegis](entity:campaign/Aegis).

mapping.name: Where They Came From
mapping.description: The job of @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar). Ships are going missing, the sickness came into the continent on a ship, and the Assembly does not stir without seeing proof.
mapping.objective:
@[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar) wants three things, and all three are parts of the same job:

- **Why the ships are going missing.** The ships that should come to the continent are not late; they are going missing.
- **Stopping it, if need be.**
- **Hard proof of the sickness:** something no one in the Assembly can deny.

He can pay for it: a signature in advance, and when the job is done a share in his house's inheritance. He does not say how the job is to be done; how far it is pursued is the table's.
mapping.reward:
**In advance: a signature.** To whoever accepts his offer, Orvan gives the countersignature on the passage paper before the job; he does not sign it himself, he has his guild's signatory sign it (@[Good Writ](entity:quest/Good Writ)).

**When the job is done: a share in House Sancar's inheritance.** It is paid when the answer is brought to Orvan, even an incomplete one. Orvan is not satisfied with the answer he gets, but he pays — what he gets is more than what he had.
mapping.secrets:
**The job's road map is in this field, not on the player's card.** The fields the player sees hold only what Orvan wants and the reward.

## Open doors

None has an order, none is required.

| Door | Its keys |
|---|---|
| **The missing ships** | The register room of the @[Border and Trade Guild Council Chamber](entity:location/Border and Trade Guild Council Chamber): which ship should have come and did not · the customs copies of @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr) · @[Twine](entity:npc/Twine)'s ledger at @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor): which ship brought what · the weighbridge slips of @[Bargeman — Rüstem](entity:npc/Bargeman — Rüstem): the load written on paper is not on the weighbridge · @[Captain — Maren](entity:npc/Captain — Maren) in @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr): the name of one of the ships that should have come and did not |
| **The traces in the cabin** | @[Questioning at the Cabin](entity:scene/Questioning at the Cabin): the cloth, the full purse and blank scrolls, @[The Sealless Ring](entity:trinket/The Sealless Ring) in the hidden pocket, the bodies, the magical trace, inside the wedding band |
| **The way to the harbor** | @[Corvin](entity:npc/Corvin) (@[Duran](entity:npc/Duran) gives the direction) · the ring → @[Kildrak Ferrun](entity:npc/Kildrak Ferrun) (@[The Assay Table](entity:scene/The Assay Table)) · an official in Lucid Triton who knows the way. **If Corvin is dead** the village side closes; the remaining two doors stay open |
| **At the harbor** | @[Admitted to the Harbor](entity:scene/Admitted to the Harbor) → @[Twine](entity:npc/Twine) gives the ship's name · @[Mouse](entity:npc/Mouse) that night · @[Enamel](entity:npc/Enamel) the hand that filed the ring and the old face she remembers |
| **The real names** | The *Greenbottle* line inside the wedding band, or the description of two halfling spouses → Orvan recognizes it at @[The Assembly Session](entity:scene/The Assembly Session) |
| **Proof** | @[Halim](entity:npc/Halim)'s testimony · the copy of the first declaration with @[Sindri](entity:npc/Sindri) · what was seen in the cabin · the druid's reading of the rot at @[Radenhall Courtyard](entity:location/Radenhall Courtyard) (@[What the Stones Know](entity:quest/What the Stones Know)) |

## Where the trail ends

The **Fate** brought them. No one knows its captain's name — no one at the harbor says the name they were born with — and the ship never put in again after that night. The three strangers' trail goes cold here. Why the ships go missing lies beyond this trail.

**What is left in hand.** Not an item: a ship's name and a drawing — the *Fate*, and the mark @[Enamel](entity:npc/Enamel) drew on paper that no one recognizes. Neither opens any door in this act.

## Secrets

**Why the ships go missing is not written.** Orvan does not know, and no card carries the answer; the answer is the DM's. The card only says where the question sits: the ships are not late, they are going missing, and Border and Trade's ledger knows which ones did not arrive.

**What hard proof means.** Each of the Assembly's seats denies the sickness from its own expertise (@[The Assembly Session](entity:scene/The Assembly Session)). A witness, a copy of a declaration or a druid's word may convince one seat and not another. The druid's word is not a record either: @[Radenhall Courtyard](entity:location/Radenhall Courtyard) is Unwritten. What is enough comes out at the table.

**The crime is not spreading the sickness but hiding it.** Someone brought three sick people into the continent through a harbor that keeps no records, and sent them to a village where no one asks questions. Whoever brought them here put Silverwater in danger.

**The farthest point the chain can reach is @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor).** The *Fate* brought them, and the ship's captain is at sea. On whose behalf the captain carries, whether the three strangers paid for their own voyage, and how they fell sick cannot be proven in this act.

**The ring.** Its seal face has been flattened by filing, and there is no stamp on it at all — on this continent a jeweler strikes their stamp on their work. The lack of a stamp points to a workbench outside the guilds, that is, to the harbor. @[Enamel](entity:npc/Enamel) remembers the old face: a mark with no counterpart on this continent.

**The real names are in two carriers.** The *C. & P. Greenbottle* line inside the wedding bands, and the description of two halfling spouses. Orvan recognizes either one; if one is missed, the other is enough.

**The three strangers' trail is short.** That part is not an investigation chain but a trail going cold: what is left in hand is not an answer but where the answer ends. Do not try to stretch it.

**No lock.** The harbor is reached three ways, and Orvan can be reached without ever going to the Assembly.
mapping.dmNotes:
## When this job leaves the table

- When the answer is brought to Orvan — even an incomplete one;
- Or when the table leaves the trail and turns to something else. The job neither waits nor runs away.

**Signature in advance, inheritance after.** A table that takes the signature can leave the continent without doing the job (@[The Continent on the Horizon](entity:quest/The Continent on the Horizon)). Orvan knows this and gives it anyway: he has nothing in hand but bargaining, and a table that boards a ship passes along the road of the ships that never arrive.

mapping.name: Good Writ
mapping.description: The countersigned passage paper — in the language of the harbors, a *good writ*. The paper is collected under a name, and becomes official when one of the guild's signatories signs it.
mapping.objective:
**Goal: a countersigned passage paper.** The paper is collected under a name from the @[Countersign Desk](entity:location/Countersign Desk); what makes it official is the countersignature given by a signatory of the @[Border and Trade Guild](entity:lore/Border and Trade Guild).

The paper puts you on a ship, but the ship is not part of this job: @[The Continent on the Horizon](entity:quest/The Continent on the Horizon).
mapping.reward:
Passage as crew on a trading ship: whoever carries a countersigned paper pays no fare and stands watches (@[The Customs Wharf](entity:scene/The Customs Wharf)). The paper is good at @[Bargaining for Passage](entity:scene/Bargaining for Passage) too.

If the signature came from Orvan, a debt to @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar).
mapping.secrets:
## The paper's road

| Step | Its key |
|---|---|
| **Identity and clothes** | The cellar of the @[Bargemen's Inn](entity:location/Bargemen's Inn): the name to be written on the paper, and clothes to match that name. Because the paper is collected under a name, this step comes before the desk. Whoever wants to board under their own name skips it |
| **Paper and preliminary approval** | @[In Line at the Passage Court](entity:scene/In Line at the Passage Court): at the @[Countersign Desk](entity:location/Countersign Desk) the name and details are written. Its key: a bribe · Orvan's name |
| **Countersignature** | In a signatory room, one of the guild's signatories: the @[Assembly House](entity:location/Assembly House) (the most crowded) · the @[Border and Trade Guild Council Chamber](entity:location/Border and Trade Guild Council Chamber) (@[Signatory — Selvi](entity:npc/Signatory — Selvi)) · the @[Customs House](entity:location/Customs House) (@[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr)). The signatory fills in any places left blank and signs. If the offer was accepted, Orvan gives this signature **in advance**: he himself puts the paper in front of @[Signatory — Selvi](entity:npc/Signatory — Selvi) (@[The Offer at the Door](entity:scene/The Offer at the Door)) |

The order is the paper's road: the paper is collected under a name, a paper that has not come out of the desk does not come before a signatory, and a countersigned paper's name does not change.

## Secrets

**The paper leaves a trace.** Both the preliminary approval and the countersignature are written in the ledger, a copy of the customs list goes to @[Lucid Triton](entity:location/Lucid Triton), and under which name, on which ship, to where one went is known in the city. The traceless road is money: @[The Continent on the Horizon](entity:quest/The Continent on the Horizon).

**A false identity.** The paper's trace is the trace of the name on the paper, and that name is written on the day the paper is collected from the desk. Someone who wants to be written under another name goes to the desk under that name. In the cellar of the @[Bargemen's Inn](entity:location/Bargemen's Inn) a name and clothes to match that name are made ready; the name is a line Orvan invented in his own guild's ledger. A character with the @[Guild Scion of Rank](entity:background/Guild Scion of Rank) background who is written onto a crew list under their own name is recognized at the wharf; this step is needed by them most of all. How Orvan works is here, at work; if it is noticed, there is no need to explain.

**No lock.** If the preliminary approval or the countersignature is not obtained, you can leave the continent without a paper too: money and @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor) (@[The Continent on the Horizon](entity:quest/The Continent on the Horizon)). If money is not found, Orvan's door is open.

mapping.name: The Continent on the Horizon
mapping.description: Boarding a ship, leaving the continent, and setting out for the far side of the sea. In Meridia the roads are free; the only thing that costs money is boarding a ship.
mapping.objective:
**Goal: to board a ship, cross the sea, and reach the far shore — @[Vorstrand](entity:location/Vorstrand).**

The price of boarding a ship is one of two things: a **good writ** or **good money.** Neither is ready in a traveler's purse.
mapping.reward:
The far shore: @[Vorstrand](entity:location/Vorstrand), or as the people say, the Beyond.

What stays with you is which road you left by. Whoever left by the legal road has their name on a customs list, and written as crew on a ship. Whoever left by the smuggler's road has a guarantor, and a debt at a harbor.
mapping.secrets:
## Two roads

One is enough, and both stay open.

### A good writ — Elymsyr

| Step | Its key |
|---|---|
| **The paper** | A countersigned passage paper: @[Good Writ](entity:quest/Good Writ). The paper's countersignature can also be given in the signatory room of the @[Customs House](entity:location/Customs House), just before boarding |
| **Down to Elymsyr** | By barge on the Golden River (@[Bargeman — Rüstem](entity:npc/Bargeman — Rüstem), @[River Loading Yard](entity:location/River Loading Yard)) or overland. How long each takes is not written |
| **Boarding** | @[The Customs Wharf](entity:scene/The Customs Wharf): whoever carries the paper is signed on a trading ship as **crew** — no fare, watches instead. One of the ships at the pier looking for crew is the *Honest Scales* of @[Captain — Maren](entity:npc/Captain — Maren) (@[Lower Wharf](entity:location/Lower Wharf)) |

### Good money — Hidden Harbor

| Step | Its key |
|---|---|
| **Admission** | No one gets into @[Hidden Harbor](entity:location/Hidden Harbor) without a guarantor (@[Admitted to the Harbor](entity:scene/Admitted to the Harbor)): a guarantor, a job or a load |
| **Money** | Day labor at @[The Wharf](entity:location/The Wharf) · goods to sell in the @[Lower Market](entity:location/Lower Market) · taking over someone's debt |
| **Bargaining** | @[Bargaining for Passage](entity:scene/Bargaining for Passage): @[Captain Caelynn](entity:npc/Captain Caelynn) clean and expensive, @[Captain Holg](entity:npc/Captain Holg) cheap and bad. A good writ is good here too |

The question *how is unregistered passage bought* has two carriers: @[Twine](entity:npc/Twine) at the harbor, the @[Crane Master](entity:npc/Crane Master) in Elymsyr.

## The difference between the two roads: the trace

The legal road leaves a trace: the name, the ship and the harbor are written on a customs list, and the list's copy goes to @[Lucid Triton](entity:location/Lucid Triton) (@[The Banner Register](entity:lore/The Banner Register)). The smuggler's road is traceless, but it needs a guarantor and leaves a debt at the harbor (@[The Harbor Compact](entity:lore/The Harbor Compact)).

## At sea

In the route's four regions there are four ships of the Black Fleet (@[The Open Sea](entity:location/The Open Sea)). The *Honest Scales* leaves the trade route and passes outside the first three; in the last water near the Beyond there is no room to go around (@[Maren's Course](entity:scene/Maren's Course)). Caelynn's and Holg's courses are not written.

All three ships cross the same water (@[The Open Sea](entity:location/The Open Sea)), and that water is also the road of the ships that should have come to the continent and did not (@[Where They Came From](entity:quest/Where They Came From)). Why the ships go missing is written on no card. Nor how long the voyage takes.

Which ship one is on gives the voyage its color: watches on the *Honest Scales*, order on Caelynn's ship, on Holg's ship a crew eyeing the passengers' belongings and a hull that will not weather a storm.

**No lock.** If the paper is not obtained, the money door is open; if money is not found, Orvan's door is open. The table can also choose to stay on the continent; this job neither keeps anyone waiting nor drives anyone away.
mapping.dmNotes:
## When this job leaves the table

- **When land appears on the horizon** (@[Land Ho](entity:scene/Land Ho)). The act ends there too; setting foot on the shore is the next act's business.
- Or when the table chooses to stay on the continent.

**Who opens it.** If Orvan's offer has been made, this job is open too: the offer opens three jobs at once (@[The Offer at the Door](entity:scene/The Offer at the Door)). It opens without the offer as well — for any table that wants to board a ship.

mapping.name: Night of the Tide
mapping.description: For a few weeks now, on some nights, the drying racks of Argenfon have been emptied. The tracks turn toward the sea, and the castle's patrol looked four times and saw nothing. What is being looked for is not a thief but a **nest**.
mapping.objective:
**Goal: find the nest.** What is done once it is found is the table's.

This job opens only for a table that stops at @[Argenfon](entity:location/Argenfon) (@[Empty Racks](entity:scene/Empty Racks)). No one assigns anyone; there is damage on the table, and it is taken up or not.

## Open doors

| Door | Its keys |
|---|---|
| **Learning what they are** | The empty shell washed up on the shore · the prints in the sand → **History DC 8 / 12 / 15** (@[Hıkka — The Record in the Books](entity:lore/Hıkka — The Record in the Books)) |
| **Working out when they came** | Who in the village lost what on which night · waiting two nights · **Nature/Survival DC 12**. The answer: the nights the water recedes the most |
| **Seeing where they went** | Waiting on the shore one night — no torch, no sound of armor; or following one of them |
| **The nest** | @[The Receding Water](entity:scene/The Receding Water) → @[Tide Mouth](entity:location/Tide Mouth) |
| **Spice** | @[Iraz](entity:npc/Iraz)'s untouched rack (no roll) or the books (DC 15). The cheap spice of @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr) is scattered on the shore |

## When this job leaves the table

It has no single ending. It counts as closed when one of these happens:

- **When the nest's location is found** — whether or not anyone goes inside. That was the goal;
- **When its location is reported to the castle** — the paladins take over, no job is left for the table, the reputation remains;
- **When the raids stop** — with a strip of spice, or by leaving fish on the shore on tide nights. The softlings harden within a few weeks and the raids end on their own;
- **When the table leaves the village behind.** The village spends the winter hungrier; no one blames the table.

## What is not promised

Argenfon has no cash. What they can give is beds, food, a boat and **talk**. This job is done not for a reward but because it is there in front of you.

---

**Scenes:** @[Empty Racks](entity:scene/Empty Racks) · @[The Receding Water](entity:scene/The Receding Water)

**Places:** @[Argenfon](entity:location/Argenfon) · @[Tide Mouth](entity:location/Tide Mouth) · @[Votumar](entity:location/Votumar)

**NPCs:** @[Sevran](entity:npc/Sevran) · @[Iraz](entity:npc/Iraz)

**Creatures:** @[Softling](entity:monster/Softling) · @[Shellback](entity:monster/Shellback) · @[Holdfast](entity:monster/Holdfast)

mapping.secrets:
**Why they are here (not given to the players).** They fled from Vorstrand; the @[Blight — Infection](entity:curse/Blight — Infection) touched their shedding there. **Those who could flee were the ones who could still shed** — none of them is a carrier, and the sickness did not touch Votumar.

There is no common language; there is no one to tell the table this. The farthest layer the table can reach is *"these fled from something"*.

**Why now.** They have been here for some time and no one noticed. Then most of the young shed their shells in the same period — ten little ones suddenly unable to feed. Those that come ashore are not hunters but @[Shellback](entity:monster/Shellback)s carrying food to the @[Softling](entity:monster/Softling)s.

The weight of the nonviolent ending is here: once the softlings harden, the raids end **on their own**.

mapping.name: The Last Written Order
mapping.description: What was seen in Silverwater needs to reach an authority, and @[Votumar](entity:location/Votumar) stands two days away. The castle's gate is open; the blockage is inside: the man who would give the order has not been here for two months.
mapping.objective:
**Goal: get the castle moving.** How much it moves is the table's.

The only person who can decide is @[Deputy Lord Commander — Aren](entity:npc/Deputy Lord Commander — Aren) — she has in practice been running the castle for two months. @[Gate Commander — Nevra](entity:npc/Gate Commander — Nevra) lets them through the gate: without asking if there is a character with a Silver Shield background, otherwise for a stated reason.

**Persuasion.** If there is something in hand, no roll — in Votumar paper beats charisma: *"they came sick"* read from the bodies (**Medicine DC 12**), @[The Sealless Ring](entity:trinket/The Sealless Ring), or a signed statement from Silverwater. If there is none of these, **Persuasion DC 15**.

If she is not persuaded there is no wall: Aren listens, does not enter it in the ledger, and reports the situation to the capital.

**If persuaded she can do two things — one, the other, or both:**

| Door | What happens |
|---|---|
| **A letter** | She has @[Castle Clerk — Nerion](entity:npc/Castle Clerk — Nerion) write the report, signs it as acting authority and seals it: @[Sealed Letter](entity:adventuring-gear/Sealed Letter). She cannot send it with a soldier — the one to carry it is the table. The letter opens doors in @[Lucid Triton](entity:location/Lucid Triton) |
| **A soldier** | She sends someone she trusts to @[Silverwater](entity:location/Silverwater) in civilian clothes. No name, no tag. Whether they come back, what they bring — the DM's |

## When this job leaves the table

- When Aren does something — a letter, a soldier, or both;
- When Aren does nothing. The table leaves the castle empty-handed, and that is an outcome too;
- When the table never stops at Votumar. This chain is a prerequisite for nothing.

---

## Cards in this quest

**NPCs:** @[Deputy Lord Commander — Aren](entity:npc/Deputy Lord Commander — Aren) · @[Gate Commander — Nevra](entity:npc/Gate Commander — Nevra) · @[Castle Clerk — Nerion](entity:npc/Castle Clerk — Nerion) · @[Lord Commander — Varhan](entity:npc/Lord Commander — Varhan) *(not at the castle)*

mapping.reward: Aren. The first voice from inside the institution to believe, and the castle's pen. Votumar has no cash; what she gives is a signature and a surety.
mapping.secrets:
**When he left, Varhan gave Aren a written, sealed order, and that order is only with Aren.** He gave it on leaving, at the start of the two months — after that nothing written came out of the castle. It has two points:

1. *No soldiers will be sent to distant places without my permission.*
2. *If a rumor of sickness arises, it will be reported directly to me.*

**The order is defensible, and this is the lifeblood of this quest.** It reads like a border governor's border order; Aren reads it that way too, and she may be right. The table cannot say *"this man knew about the sickness in advance"* — it can only be uneasy. The sickness came to @[Meridia](entity:location/Meridia) after the order, but there is no record anywhere that would show it.

**The order is @[Lord Commander — Varhan](entity:npc/Lord Commander — Varhan)'s cover.** The first point ties the castle's hands, the second brings the news not to the institution but straight to him. Together they make Votumar a deaf tower.

**The first point makes the table a courier.** Aren cannot send a soldier to Lucid Triton — it is two days away. She can send civilians.

**If the @[Sealed Letter](entity:adventuring-gear/Sealed Letter) falls into Varhan's hands**, the table lays what it knows, where it knows it from and who it is in front of the enemy — and Aren's name is at the bottom of the letter. Taking the letter to the Assembly is not an option written on the card but something the table can find.

**Sending a soldier is Aren's own breach.** Civilian clothes obey the letter of the order, not its spirit; if it comes out, this is Treason against the Will, and Aren does it knowingly.

**If Aren is missed or turned against them, the line does not die.** @[Castle Clerk — Nerion](entity:npc/Castle Clerk — Nerion) enters a petition in the ledger; the institution is entered through writing. It wins no ally and it is slow, but the door does not close.

mapping.name: The Missing Count
mapping.description: The count in the castle's supply storehouse does not add up. The shortfall is not large — a few sacks, some coal, a roll of strap leather — but it is spread over two months and no one can say when it began. @[Forgemaster — Torvun](entity:npc/Forgemaster — Torvun) wants it closed before count day comes.
mapping.objective:
**Goal: find where the shortfall comes from.** What is done once it is found is the table's.

Torvun cannot look personally. In Votumar, noticing a shortfall means **reporting** it, and what is reported enters the ledger; once a sack of flour enters the ledger it is no longer a sack of flour, it is a Treason against the Will file. A stranger keeps no ledger — that is why Torvun gives them the job.

**What is at hand:** Torvun's own supply ledger (handed over if asked) · the records room of @[Castle Clerk — Nerion](entity:npc/Castle Clerk — Nerion) · the watch ledger of @[Gate Commander — Nevra](entity:npc/Gate Commander — Nevra) — what went out through the gate. Putting the three ledgers side by side is **Investigation DC 13**; asking, listening and going around the garrison folk require no roll.

## When this job leaves the table

- **When the shortfall is closed** — by finding who took it, by putting the goods back, or by the table covering it out of its own pocket;
- **When it is reported** — the person or the shortfall, whichever is reported;
- **When count day comes.** Torvun takes the shortfall on personally, and does not tell the table.

---

## Cards in this quest

**Place:** @[Votumar](entity:location/Votumar)

**NPCs:** @[Forgemaster — Torvun](entity:npc/Forgemaster — Torvun) · @[Castle Clerk — Nerion](entity:npc/Castle Clerk — Nerion) · @[Gate Commander — Nevra](entity:npc/Gate Commander — Nevra)

**Neighboring chain:** @[The Last Written Order](entity:quest/The Last Written Order). This job is not its prerequisite; it opens a small window onto the same two months.
mapping.reward: No cash — in Votumar trade is done not for profit but for supply. What Torvun can give is the forge: armor and weapon repair, straps, buckles, whatever is needed, overnight and free. And a name in the castle to stand guarantor for a stranger.
mapping.secrets:
**The shortfall has two causes, and both are true.**

**Someone really is taking.** One of the forge apprentices, once a week, in small and pitiful amounts. The reason is a family among the garrison folk; who they are is **the DM's**, and this card writes no name.

**The other is not taking but not writing.** For two months a release of goods was given by word of mouth and never entered any ledger. What has made the taking invisible for two months is not theft but **that gap**: the line that would show the loss was never written.

**This is what the table chooses — whether to report the person or the gap.** If it reports the person, an apprentice comes before the Laws of Honor and Oath. If it reports the gap, the shortfall looks like @[Forgemaster — Torvun](entity:npc/Forgemaster — Torvun)'s failing, and Torvun already blames themself. The third way is silence, and that is a decision too.

**This job is a quiet rehearsal.** Without anyone saying it, the table learns through a sack of flour that *"nothing has been written here for two months"*. The same two months stand behind @[The Last Written Order](entity:quest/The Last Written Order) too.

mapping.name: What the Stones Know
mapping.description: At the continent's far north lives a tribe that reads the sickness not from rumor but from nature. Going to Radenhall, getting past the path, and listening to what has been known there for months.
mapping.objective:
At the continent's far north, in the forest ringed by coastal mountains, the @[Wardens of the North](entity:lore/Wardens of the North) read the rot directly from nature. @[Radenhall Courtyard](entity:location/Radenhall Courtyard) is a 4–5 day journey from @[Lucid Triton](entity:location/Lucid Triton), and a single narrow path leads down inside.

## Who points the way to Radenhall

| Carrier | What they know |
|---|---|
| @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar) | That a tribe that reads nature lives at the continent's far north |
| @[Sindri](entity:npc/Sindri) | That the recipe for the @[Sherbet of Resistance](entity:adventuring-gear/Sherbet of Resistance) came from the north, from the druids |
| @[Wardens of the North](entity:lore/Wardens of the North) | A character with druid or nature knowledge has heard of the tribe |

## Open doors

| Door | Its keys |
|---|---|
| **The path** | @[Path Scout — Addluin](entity:npc/Path Scout — Addluin) turns back everyone who wants to cross, once. Two keys, one is enough: convincing him their purpose is good · speaking of the rot |
| **The Courtyard** | @[Eldest Druid — Halder](entity:npc/Eldest Druid — Halder): where the rot began and which way it is walking (@[Welcome in the Courtyard](entity:scene/Welcome in the Courtyard)) |
| **The sherbet** | Both the recipe for the @[Sherbet of Resistance](entity:adventuring-gear/Sherbet of Resistance) and the trade for it are here; the one who brews it is @[Healer — Iven](entity:npc/Healer — Iven). Gold is not taken; what is asked in return is the DM's |

## What can happen here

- **The druid can sense the sickness.** If one of the characters has been infected, the druid may sense it. Whether she senses it, and if so when and how she says it, is the DM's.
- **Lateness.** There are no rumors about the sickness here, because everyone already knows. No one came to ask.

## When this job leaves the table

- When what the druid tells has been listened to;
- Or when the table turns back from the path, or never goes north at all. Radenhall is not a required stop.

---

## Cards in this quest

**Scene:** @[Welcome in the Courtyard](entity:scene/Welcome in the Courtyard)

**Places:** @[Radenhall Courtyard](entity:location/Radenhall Courtyard) · @[Lucid Triton](entity:location/Lucid Triton) · @[Healers' Barracks](entity:location/Healers' Barracks)

**NPCs:** @[Eldest Druid — Halder](entity:npc/Eldest Druid — Halder) · @[Path Scout — Addluin](entity:npc/Path Scout — Addluin) · @[Healer — Iven](entity:npc/Healer — Iven) · @[Bard — Tamsin](entity:npc/Bard — Tamsin) · @[Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar](entity:npc/Border and Trade — Orvan Sancar) · @[Sindri](entity:npc/Sindri)

**Item:** @[Sherbet of Resistance](entity:adventuring-gear/Sherbet of Resistance)

**Rules and institutions:** @[Wardens of the North](entity:lore/Wardens of the North) · @[Blight — Infection](entity:curse/Blight — Infection) · @[The Silent Shrines](entity:lore/The Silent Shrines)

**Neighboring quests:** @[Where They Came From](entity:quest/Where They Came From) · @[Chasing the Rumor](entity:quest/Chasing the Rumor). The single list of everything: @[Index](entity:lore/Index).
mapping.reward:
The map of the rot in nature: where it began and which way it is walking. By trade, the @[Sherbet of Resistance](entity:adventuring-gear/Sherbet of Resistance), or its recipe.

The map is not a record: the druid's word is written in no guild ledger. Whether it is the hard proof @[Where They Came From](entity:quest/Where They Came From) wants comes out in the Assembly.
mapping.secrets:
**The Wardens have known for months.** They read the rot not from rumor but from the soil and the trees. The druid does not say how long she has known: *"A long time."*

**The druid's word comes from an Unwritten place.** It may be part of the proof Orvan is looking for, but in the world of records the word of an Unwritten place carries no weight. Orvan knows this too.

**No lock.** No other card gives the map of the rot, but the job runs without that map too.
mapping.dmNotes:
Do not play this job like a reward. An answer sits here, and beside the answer, how late it already is.

The card list is at the bottom of the quest's own page. The other chains and the place/character cards: @[Index](entity:lore/Index).

mapping.name: The Masked Job
mapping.description: The @[Military Law Guild](entity:lore/Military Law Guild) has bought a house on one of the upper terraces of @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr) and is setting up a room for itself in the harbor; building work has begun on its upper floor. The @[Customs Governor](entity:npc/Customs Governor) does not want that room to open, and he has a job to give to faces no one knows.
mapping.objective:
**Goal: bring the small chest in the house's cellar to the governor, then burn the house.** The order is the governor's condition: the chest must come out before the fire.

The offer is carried by @[The Governor's Deputy](entity:npc/The Governor's Deputy); the governor gives it himself, in his office, with the door closed. No one forces anyone, and the offer can be refused.

## Open doors

| Door | Its keys |
|---|---|
| **No one recognizes them** | The masks the deputy gives · night · the narrow street (the neighbors look but do not recognize) |
| **Getting into the house** | The front door · up the scaffold on the left wall to the upper floor · the shuttered windows. The deputy describes the layout of the @[Military Law Chamber](entity:location/Military Law Chamber) |
| **The chest** | The cellar hatch is in the hearth hall on the ground floor. The lock: thieves' tools **DC 15** · the key on the @[Head Watchman](entity:monster/Head Watchman)'s belt · breaking it **Strength DC 15**, noisy |
| **Burning it** | The walls are stone, the rest wood. The tar buckets and the timber stack upstairs make the fire grow |
| **The watchmen** | Fighting, slipping past, or luring them outside: @[The Night Worksite](entity:encounter/The Night Worksite) |

## When this job leaves the table

- **When the chest reaches the governor and the house has burned** — the job is done;
- **When the chest never reaches the governor** — if the table kept it or opened and read it, a lever against the governor is now in the table's hands;
- **When the table refuses the offer or abandons the job halfway.** Whether the governor looks for other hands is the DM's.

---

## Cards in this quest

**Places:** @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr) · @[Customs House](entity:location/Customs House) · @[Military Law Chamber](entity:location/Military Law Chamber)

**NPCs:** @[Customs Governor](entity:npc/Customs Governor) · @[The Governor's Deputy](entity:npc/The Governor's Deputy)

**Encounter:** @[The Night Worksite](entity:encounter/The Night Worksite) — @[Site Watchman](entity:monster/Site Watchman) · @[Hired Cutlass](entity:monster/Hired Cutlass) · @[Head Watchman](entity:monster/Head Watchman)

**Institution cards:** @[Military Law Guild](entity:lore/Military Law Guild) · @[Border and Trade Guild](entity:lore/Border and Trade Guild)

**Neighboring chain:** none. This job is a prerequisite for nothing; but the papers in the chest touch the ledger of the @[Customs House](entity:location/Customs House).
mapping.reward:
**50 gold per person and an item.** The DM decides what the item is. The deputy pays the gold when the job is done; the governor gives the item with his own hand.

No receipt, no paper, no signature. There is nothing the governor has written about this job.
mapping.secrets:
**The governor's trouble.** A policing guild opening a room in the harbor means a second eye beside the customs ledger. The governor shows loads unloaded short as complete in the ledger (@[Customs House](entity:location/Customs House)), and the bundle in the chest is the proof of it.

**What is in the chest.** A bundle of weighbridge slips: on each, a ship's load as weighed on the weighbridge, and on a paper pinned beside it the same ship's figure in the ledger. The two do not match. To both his deputy and the table the governor says only *"something of mine"*. A character with the @[Archivist](entity:background/Archivist) background reads the bundle at a glance; anyone else sees with **Investigation DC 12** that the two columns do not match.

**Why strangers.** In Elymsyr everyone knows the governor's men. No one knows faces just off a ship; the mask completes the rest.

**The price of the fire.** Arson is a grave crime, and the one who writes up this crime is the @[Military Law Guild](entity:lore/Military Law Guild) itself. If a mask falls, or a watchman sees a face, that face enters that guild's ledger. The deputy does not know whoever is caught; the governor has never seen them.

**Death.** The watchmen are not guild members but hired men. But a dead watchman turns the job from arson into murder, and the governor does not want the dead. Whether he cuts the reward is the DM's.

mapping.name: Sorting Satchel
mapping.description:
A compartmented bag of stiff, oiled leather, worn over the shoulder. Inside are seven narrow compartments; a letter is punched into the mouth of each. The flap closes with two straps, and the straps' brass buckles are forged in the shape of a key, in the way archive officials recognize. The bag smells of old paper and beeswax.

**Use:** permission to read in archives other than Occulus. When the official at an archive door sees the bag, they understand its bearer has come for work, not curiosity, and let them in.

*SRD equivalent: `Case, Map or Scroll`.*

mapping.name: Ledger Primer
mapping.description:
A thick, heavy book. The corners of its leather binding are darkened by fingerprints, its spine resewn in two places. On every page an abbreviation, a stamp or a classification mark is drawn, and opposite it what it means is written in small, neat letters. In the margins are the notes of several generations of archivists.

**Use:** reading the language of ledgers. Anyone who looks at a ledger sees the lines; someone who knows this book also sees why an abbreviation is there, which office a stamp belongs to and why a column was left empty.

See @[The Banner Register](entity:lore/The Banner Register).

*SRD equivalent: `Book`.*

mapping.name: Banner Index
mapping.description:
A narrow, tall book. Its pages are divided by office names, and a colored leather tab is sewn onto the edge of each section: red for customs, green for the healers, grey for military law. A dried bay leaf has been placed between the pages.

**Use:** finding which document is kept in which office. Asking the right question at the wrong desk is the same as never asking; the index shows the right desk.

*SRD equivalent: `Book`.*

mapping.name: Caftan of Rank
mapping.description:
A long caftan of heavy, dark cloth. Its collar and cuffs are embroidered in silk according to the house's rank; someone who can read the embroidery tells at a glance which house and which step the wearer belongs to. It makes no sound when walking; when you sit, its folds fall back into place on their own. It has taken on the smell of cedar from the chest.

**Use:** decides who will speak in a room. The word of the one wearing the caftan is heard before the word of the one who is not.

*SRD equivalent: `Clothes, Fine`.*

mapping.name: Student's Notebook
mapping.description:
A spellbook with a locked brass cover. On its first page the stamp of the Wizards' Guild is printed. On the margin of the pages, every time the book is opened, a small, inkless date mark appears on its own. The student has the key to the lock; the master has the spare.

**Use:** entry to the library of the @[Wizards' Guild](entity:lore/Wizards' Guild).

**Price:** the date marks in the book show when the student studied what, and the one who reads these marks is the student's master.

*SRD equivalent: `Spellbook`.*

mapping.name: Cargo Hook
mapping.description:
An arm-length cargo hook of wrought iron. Its wooden handle is darkened and polished by rope and sweat. Its point has been blunted on purpose: for catching a sack, not for piercing. Its owner's notches are cut into the base of the handle.

**Use:** work and fellowship among workers on the wharves. No one asks the name of someone who holds the hook right on the pier; the day wage is paid in the evening.

*SRD equivalent: `Grappling Hook`.*

mapping.name: Logbook
mapping.description:
A thick ledger whose pages have swollen with salt and damp. In it are courses, harbors put into, dates, wind notes, and short warnings jotted beside each harbor: *pier rotten*, *harbor master wants a bribe*. A ship's name is carved into its cover.

**Use:** course knowledge and the right to put in at harbors. At a harbor this logbook takes the place of the captain's identity: it shows where they came from and where they are going.

*SRD equivalent: `Book`.*

mapping.name: Sherbet of Resistance
mapping.description:
A palm-sized bottle of green glass, its mouth sealed with red wax. The sherbet inside is dark brown and cloudy. When the wax is broken a smell of bitter root and pine resin spreads; the taste stays on the tongue for a long time.

**The only known protection against the sickness.** When drunk, for **24 hours** it gives **+8** to Sickness Score rolls: both the exposure roll (CON DC 12) and the daily sickness roll (CON DC 13). It does not cure the sickness; it only makes it harder to catch. See @[Blight — Infection](entity:curse/Blight — Infection).

**Who makes it:** a licensed physician, someone with druid knowledge, or someone who works with an alchemist's kit. **Clean water** and the right herb are needed. The recipe's homeland is @[Radenhall Courtyard](entity:location/Radenhall Courtyard): the @[Wardens of the North](entity:lore/Wardens of the North) know the sherbet, make it and give it in trade; the recipe is learned there too.

It is scarce. In the city it is sold dearly by licensed physicians; in the provinces it cannot be bought with money, it is made.
mapping.dmNotes: The +8 is high on purpose, because the sherbet is scarce: a new bottle does not easily replace one that is drunk. If you hand out the sherbet freely, the only decision left in hand loses its meaning too.

mapping.name: Sealed Letter
mapping.description:
A folded report, sealed at its edge. Thick castle paper, its edge cut clean, its fold sharp. On the back the Silver Shield's tower shield is pressed into white wax; at the edge of the wax it carries a second small stamp saying it was signed as acting authority. On the front, a single line: *To the Lord Commander, by hand.* The smell of new wax and ink not yet dry has settled into the paper; pressed with a finger where it is folded, it is still warm.

**Use:** in @[Lucid Triton](entity:location/Lucid Triton), someone carrying the sealed letter of a military governorate does not wait in line. The doorkeeper does not ask a name, he opens the door — the bearer is not the letter's addressee but is on its way.

**A seal breaks once.** A letter with a broken seal opens no door, and having broken a seal that came out of a castle under the Laws of Honor and Oath stays with the bearer.
mapping.dmNotes:
@[Deputy Lord Commander — Aren](entity:npc/Deputy Lord Commander — Aren) gives it if she is persuaded (@[The Last Written Order](entity:quest/The Last Written Order)). Inside is a dry account of what was seen in @[Silverwater](entity:location/Silverwater) and Aren's acting signature; there is no accusation, there is a request — an order to the castle.

The letter's addressee is @[Lord Commander — Varhan](entity:npc/Lord Commander — Varhan), and this card's real weight is there: if it is delivered by hand, the Faceless gets the news.

mapping.name: Guild Seal
mapping.description:
A heavy seal ring of silver. The guild's sign is carved in reverse into its flat face; pressed onto wax it comes out the right way round. Old red wax remains in the grooves.

**Use:** lodging in the guild's houses, credit from the guild's merchants, and the right to ask names. A sealed person can ask in a room who the other person is, and is expected to get an answer.

*SRD equivalent: `Signet Ring`.*

mapping.name: Guild Badge
mapping.description:
A coin-sized brass badge worn on the lapel of a coat. The guild's sign in relief on it; its edges softened from frequent polishing.

**Use:** shows membership even while the ring stays in the pocket. A doorkeeper who sees the badge asks no questions; an argument about to start at a door ends when the badge is seen.

mapping.name: Family Seal
mapping.description:
A thick, heavy ring of gold. The house's sign is carved on its face, and around the sign the house's name is written in fine letters. The ring's inner edge has thinned from being worn for generations.

**Use:** doors open with the house's name. But the name brings obligations too: whoever carries this ring carries the house's debts and enemies as well.

*SRD equivalent: `Signet Ring`.*

mapping.name: Forged Seal
mapping.description:
A seal ring hard to tell from the real thing. Silver plating, brass beneath; one corner of the plating slightly worn. The carving is good, but a jeweler's loupe shows that the line between two letters is too sharp.

**Use:** a false identity. It opens a door as quickly as a real seal.

**If caught, it is a crime.** Using a forged seal counts as a crime committed against the Common Will (@[Courts of Honor](entity:lore/Courts of Honor)).

*SRD equivalent: `Signet Ring`.*

mapping.name: Barracks Tag
mapping.description:
A palm-sized silver tag hung around the neck on a thin chain. On one face the shield sign of the @[Order of the Silver Shield](entity:lore/Order of the Silver Shield), on the other the soldier's name and unit engraved. Warm from being worn against the skin.

**Use:** food, bed and passage in the Order's barracks. A soldier who shows the tag goes hungry in none of the Order's barracks.

The tag is also used as a holy symbol, but what it carries is not a line but a **record**: it says the oath was sworn before witnesses and entered in the ledger. A paladin who leaves the Order leaves their tag behind — they lose their power, not their name.

*SRD equivalent: `Emblem (Holy Symbol)`.*

mapping.name: Seal of Command
mapping.description:
A seal ring of silver and, in a leather pouch, a cake of white sealing wax. The Order's shield and rank lines are carved on the face of the ring. The Order's orders are sealed with this white wax.

**Use:** passage without question through the Order's gates, and knowledge from within the Order. A paper sealed with this seal is not a letter but an order.

*SRD equivalent: `Signet Ring + Sealing Wax`.*

mapping.name: The Sealless Ring
mapping.description:
A thick ring of gold carried in the hidden pocket of Kromanna's clothes. It is forged in the shape of a seal ring, but its face is flat: the sign once carved there has been filed away. The file marks are still bright.

Finding it requires searching her and **Investigation DC 15**. Kromanna does not show it of her own accord.

**Looking closely:** the seal face was not broken but flattened by filing. The gold on the filed surface is still bright yellow; the rest of the ring has taken on the dull color of years. This work was done recently.

**There is no stamp on it at all.** No assay stamp, no master's mark, no house seal. In Meridia a jeweler strikes their stamp on their work: the stamp is a signature. Someone who does not strike one is either outside the guilds, or has left their name behind.

In Meridia a seal ring is worn openly. This ring was being hidden.
mapping.dmNotes:
Finding this ring is not required; if missed, the story still moves on.

Do not confuse it with the two wedding bands in the cabin: the bands carry the real names (@[Questioning at the Cabin](entity:scene/Questioning at the Cabin)), this ring points to the harbor. Two separate locks, two separate doors.

The one who filed the ring is @[Enamel](entity:npc/Enamel). But no one in the city can point to her, because there is no stamp to follow. The only thing @[Kildrak Ferrun](entity:npc/Kildrak Ferrun) can give is a direction: good work without a stamp, that is, a workbench outside the guilds, that is, a harbor.

@[Where They Came From](entity:quest/Where They Came From).

mapping.name: Archivist
mapping.description:
You grew up among dusty shelves, by lamplight, reading ledgers others had written. You know where a document is kept, what an abbreviation means, which desk to put a question to. Your fingers are never fully clean of ink.

**Your items:** the @[Sorting Satchel](entity:adventuring-gear/Sorting Satchel) gets you into archives other than Occulus. The @[Ledger Primer](entity:adventuring-gear/Ledger Primer) lets you read the gaps in a ledger. The @[Banner Index](entity:adventuring-gear/Banner Index) shows where each document is kept.

**Your price:** the guild you work for knows where you are. When called, you are expected to go.
mapping.dmNotes:
Archivists are the provincial clerks of the @[Border and Trade Guild](entity:lore/Border and Trade Guild).

**Where this character stands out (none of it requires a roll):**

- The customs ledgers of @[Elymsyr](entity:location/Elymsyr): which ship did not arrive, which load was unloaded short.
- The watch ledger of @[Gate Commander — Nevra](entity:npc/Gate Commander — Nevra) in @[Votumar](entity:location/Votumar): an *order* column staying empty for two months is impossible, and an archivist sees it at a single glance.

mapping.name: Guild Member
mapping.description:
You are a member of a guild: you started as an apprentice at a workbench or in a writing office, and today you carry a rank. You have a bed in the guild's houses and credit with its merchants.

**Your items:** the @[Guild Seal](entity:trinket/Guild Seal) grants lodging, credit and the right to ask names. The @[Guild Badge](entity:trinket/Guild Badge) shows your membership even while the ring is in your pocket.

**Your price:** the guild's business comes before your own. If you do not go when called, you may lose your rank.
mapping.dmNotes:
The Guild Seal and Guild Badge are the character's starting items. Because the background card's inventory field does not hold this kind of item, add them to the character by hand.

**Something that requires no roll:** on sight, recognizes @[Velvet](entity:npc/Velvet) on the wharf as the man of a great institution.

mapping.name: Guild Scion of Rank
mapping.description:
You are the child of a house: your family holds a guild's seal. You grew up in a big house, with good teachers, better prepared for the examinations than anyone. The second half of your name opens doors.

**Your items:** the @[Family Seal](entity:trinket/Family Seal) opens doors with the house's name. The @[Caftan of Rank](entity:adventuring-gear/Caftan of Rank) decides who will speak in a room.

**Your price:** your face is recognized. Few people carry your family's seal, and your family's enemies recognize you too. Hiding who you are is hard.
mapping.dmNotes:
The Family Seal is the character's starting item. Because the background card's inventory field does not hold this kind of item, add it to the character by hand.

**Something that requires no roll:** on sight, recognizes @[Velvet](entity:npc/Velvet) on the wharf as the man of a great institution. The seat holders in the Assembly know the character's house.

mapping.name: Magic Guild Student
mapping.description:
You are a student at the academy of the @[Wizards' Guild](entity:lore/Wizards' Guild). Your days were spent in the library, under a master's eye, in study halls that smell of sulfur and ink. For you magic is a profession: with its steps, its examinations and its license.

**Your item:** the @[Student's Notebook](entity:adventuring-gear/Student's Notebook) gives entry to the guild's library.

**Your price:** a student is under supervision. Your master knows of your notebook, and an unpermitted spell stays as a line in your record.
mapping.dmNotes:
Origin feat: *Magic Initiate*, from the **Wizard** list.

**Alchemist's kit.** Healing potions cannot be bought with money in the provinces, they are made; so is the @[Sherbet of Resistance](entity:adventuring-gear/Sherbet of Resistance). That is why this character can be very useful at an unexpected moment.

One of the characters who can sense the magical trace in the cabin with Arcana DC 13.

mapping.name: Guild Agent
mapping.description:
You do a guild's work that it does not name: reading a letter on the road, listening behind a door, looking like someone you are not. Your master tells you what to do, not why to do it.

**Your item:** the @[Forged Seal](entity:trinket/Forged Seal), a false identity. If you are caught, it is a crime.

**Your price:** you have two masters. The guild's interest comes before your companions, and one day you will have to choose between them.
mapping.dmNotes:
The Forged Seal is the character's starting item. Because the background card's inventory field does not hold this kind of item, add it to the character by hand.

**Something that requires no roll:** on sight, recognizes @[Velvet](entity:npc/Velvet) on the wharf: someone of their own trade.

mapping.name: Dockworker
mapping.description:
You grew up with sacks on your shoulders and rope in your hands, on piers where no one asks your name. You no longer notice the smell of salt, tar and fish. You know by eye which ship put in when, which load is heavy.

**Your item:** the @[Cargo Hook](entity:adventuring-gear/Cargo Hook), work and fellowship among workers on the wharves. Someone who holds the hook right on the pier is quickly hired.

**Your price:** your word counts at no official door. Your name is not written in any guild's ledger.
mapping.dmNotes: **Where this character stands out:** @[The Wharf](entity:location/The Wharf). The workers soon take them in; they do not talk on the first day, they talk on the second.

mapping.name: Ship Captain
mapping.description:
You are a ship's captain, or once were. You held the helm in storms, bargained with harbor masters, found enough bread for your crew. Your hands are calloused from rope, your skin darkened by the sun.

**Your item:** the @[Logbook](entity:adventuring-gear/Logbook), course knowledge and the right to put in. At a harbor it takes the place of your identity.

**Your price:** a ship is a burden: debt, crew, harbor fees.
mapping.dmNotes: Bargains not as a passenger but as a colleague with @[Captain Caelynn](entity:npc/Captain Caelynn) and @[Captain Holg](entity:npc/Captain Holg) at @[The Wharf](entity:location/The Wharf), and with @[Captain — Maren](entity:npc/Captain — Maren) at the @[Lower Wharf](entity:location/Lower Wharf).

mapping.name: Paladin Soldier
mapping.description:
You are a soldier of the @[Order of the Silver Shield](entity:lore/Order of the Silver Shield). You were raised in Votumar's sandy courtyard, inside the shield wall, your shoulder pressed against the shoulder of the one beside you. You know how to stand silent, how to wait for orders, how to carry a shield's weight for hours.

**Your item:** the @[Barracks Tag](entity:trinket/Barracks Tag), food, bed and passage in the Order's barracks.

**Your price:** your uniform is recognized. The people are wary of the institution, and the Order expects obedience from you.
mapping.dmNotes:
The Barracks Tag is the character's starting item. Because the background card's inventory field does not hold this kind of item, add it to the character by hand.

In @[Votumar](entity:location/Votumar) and @[Argenfon](entity:location/Argenfon) doors open to them on their own. If they leave the Order, they lose their food, their bed and their tag together.

mapping.name: Paladin Officer
mapping.description:
You hold rank in the @[Order of the Silver Shield](entity:lore/Order of the Silver Shield). You used to stand inside the shield wall; now you stand in front of it and give orders. You put your orders in writing and seal them with white wax.

**Your item:** the @[Seal of Command](entity:trinket/Seal of Command), passage without question through the Order's gates and knowledge from within the Order.

**Your price:** rank means reports. Not reporting something you saw also counts as a crime.
mapping.dmNotes:
The Seal of Command is the character's starting item. Because the background card's inventory field does not hold this kind of item, add it to the character by hand.

**Something that requires no roll:** on sight, recognizes @[Velvet](entity:npc/Velvet) on the wharf as the man of a great institution.
