mapping.name: Clockwork Soul
mapping.description:
Your power comes from the absolute order of Mechanus: the realm of interlocking gears that turn forever. An ancestor, a moment of birth, or a cause never known bound a piece of that order to you.

Such a sorcerer's magic is not fire or lightning but **correction**: it erases excess, completes what is lacking, pulls deviation back into line.
mapping.flavor_description:
The gear of Mechanus always turns at the same speed, whatever the rest of the multiverse does. You are part of that speed: flattening what chaos bends, putting back a balance that has broken, is your reflex.

Some bearers count this a duty, some a disease. Both do the same thing: wherever they sit down, things begin **to be set right**.

features.name: Clockwork Magic
features.description:
The following spells are always prepared for you and do not count against the number of spells you know: **Alarm · Protection from Evil and Good.**

At each tier, you can replace **one** of the spells gained at that tier with another **abjuration** or **transmutation** spell from the sorcerer, warlock or wizard list.

features.name: Restore Balance
features.description: **Reaction.** When a creature within 60 ft is about to roll a d20 with advantage or disadvantage, you cancel the advantage **or** disadvantage. Uses equal to your proficiency bonus; regained on a long rest.

features.name: Clockwork Magic — Level 2
features.description: **Aid · Lesser Restoration** are added to your always-prepared spells.

features.name: Clockwork Magic — Level 3
features.description: **Dispel Magic · Protection from Energy** are added to your always-prepared spells.

features.name: Bastion of Law
features.description: **Action.** Spend 1–5 sorcery points; give yourself or a creature within 30 ft **d8 ward dice** equal to the points spent. While taking damage, the warded creature spends and rolls as many dice as it likes, and the total is subtracted from the damage. Lasts until your long rest or until the dice run out; one ward at a time.

features.name: Clockwork Magic — Level 4
features.description: **Freedom of Movement · Death Ward** are added to your always-prepared spells.

features.name: Clockwork Magic — Level 5
features.description: **Greater Restoration · Wall of Force** are added to your always-prepared spells.

features.name: Trance of Order
features.description: **Bonus action**, 1 minute: attack rolls against you cannot have advantage, and on your d20 rolls a 9 or lower counts as a 10. 1 free per long rest; then 5 sorcery points.

features.name: Clockwork Cavalcade
features.description: **Action.** In a 30 ft cube you heal by sharing out a total of 100 hit points, repair damaged objects, and end spells of 6th level and lower. 1 free per long rest; then 7 sorcery points.

mapping.dmNotes:
*Clockwork Soul* (Tasha's Cauldron of Everything) — content and levels the same as the original; the subclass opens at 1st level.

**The only deviation:** at the 7th-level tier **Death Ward** is given in place of *Summon Construct*; Summon Construct is not in SRD 5.2.1. If you want to trim it, put *Stone Shape* in its place.

mapping.name: Drakewarden
mapping.description:
You have formed a mystic bond with a drake. The scaled predator that appears at your side when you call becomes your companion, your mount and your weapon; as it grows, the bond grows too.

The drake carries an essence — acid, poison, cold or lightning — and as the bond deepens, that essence mixes into the damage, resistance and breath of you both.
mapping.flavor_description:
**No flight.** Neither the drake nor you ever has wings at any level, and neither of you flies. All of this world's pressure is built on **passage** — the customs wharf, the single narrow path, the watchtowers, the blockade. A flying mount would bypass that pressure entirely.

**No dragons.** The drake is not a dragon but a `beast`: it does not breathe fire, the fire essence type cannot be chosen, and in place of the Draconic language the original text grants, Primordial is given.

features.name: Draconic Gift
features.description: You learn the **Thaumaturgy** cantrip (it counts as a Ranger cantrip and does not count against the number of spells you know) and you learn the **Primordial** language. You choose your drake's **essence type**: acid, poison, cold or lightning.

features.name: Drake Companion
features.description: As an **action** you summon the drake within 30 ft. 1 free per long rest; after that, a spell slot of 1st level or higher. It shares your initiative, acts after you, and takes Dodge if not commanded.

features.name: Bond of Fang and Scale
features.description: The drake becomes **Medium** and can carry you **on land**. Its bite adds +1d6 essence damage. **You** become resistant to the essence type you chose. *(No wings, no flight.)*

features.name: Drake's Breath
features.description: **Action.** You or the drake exhale essence in a 30 ft cone: Dexterity saving throw (DC = your spell save DC), **8d6** essence damage, half on a success. 1 free per long rest; after that, a slot of 3rd level or higher.

features.name: Perfected Bond
features.description: The drake becomes **Large** and continues to carry you on land. Its bite adds another 1d6 (+2d6 in total). Drake's Breath becomes **10d6**. **Reflexive Resistance:** while within 30 ft, when one of you takes damage you use your reaction to grant resistance to that damage — uses equal to your proficiency bonus, regained on a long rest. *(No flight.)*

mapping.dmNotes:
*Drakewarden* (Fizban's Treasury of Dragons) — content, levels and all numbers the same as the original. Deviations:

- **Flight was removed entirely** — no wings at 7th level and no flying mount at 15th, and nothing was put in their place. The subclass is a notch weaker than the original, and on purpose.
- The **fire** essence type was removed from the list; the drake is not a `dragon` but a `beast`, and **Primordial** is given instead of Draconic.

If your table finds the loss too heavy, there is one dial: add the line **"the drake cannot be knocked down"** at 15th level.

mapping.name: Oath of Will
mapping.description:
Your oath was not sworn to a god. It was sworn before witnesses, entered in the ledger, and it stands as long as it is not broken.

On this continent asking a god for something is a gamble (@[Rule Deviations](entity:lore/Rule Deviations)), and the paladin orders accepted this three centuries ago and stopped asking. What remains is smaller and more reliable: a word given, and a body that keeps it.

The oath-sworn does not heal, does not bless, does not work miracles. **They find and they hold.** What the order taught them is not prayer: reading a ledger, following a trail, and not giving up a line until someone comes.
mapping.flavor_description:
**Nothing this oath grants requires the calling roll.** The features below and the oath spells are not asked of a god; they come from the oath itself. In return, every divine spell you additionally prepare from the paladin list is subject to the roll in @[Rule Deviations](entity:lore/Rule Deviations). Your hand is **narrow but reliable**.

**If the oath is broken.** The order's text is a little different in every castle; the only condition that does not change is *a word given is kept*. For an oath-sworn who knowingly breaks their oath, everything on this page **stops working for one long rest**. There is no permanent loss — the order itself is still debating this.

**The Barracks Tag is not an antenna but a seal** (@[Barracks Tag](entity:trinket/Barracks Tag)): it says the oath was sworn and who witnessed it. A paladin who breaks from the order loses their power, not their name.

features.name: Weight of the Oath
features.description: Your **Strength** score **increases by 1** (to a maximum of 20). You gain proficiency in the **History** and **Investigation** skills.

features.name: Oath Strike
features.description: When your melee weapon attack hits, you can spend a spell slot to deal an extra **2d8 force** damage; **+1d8** per slot level above 1st, to a maximum of **5d8**. **+1d8** if the target is a Blighted creature. Once per turn. *Replaces Divine Smite.*

features.name: Oath Spells
features.description: This spell is **always prepared** for you, does not count against the number of spells you prepare, and **requires no calling roll**: **Comprehend Languages.**

features.name: Oath Vow: Hold the Line
features.description: **Channel Divinity.** Action; until the end of your next turn, you and your allies within 10 ft roll exposure saves with advantage.

features.name: Oath Spells — 2nd tier
features.description: **Locate Object · See Invisibility** are added.

features.name: Unbroken Word
features.description: Your allies within 10 ft (you included) roll with advantage every saving throw that would give a Sickness Score. At 18th level the range becomes 30 ft.

features.name: Oath Spells — 3rd tier
features.description: **Nondetection · Clairvoyance** are added.

features.name: Oath Spells — 4th tier
features.description: **Locate Creature · Arcane Eye** are added.

features.name: Untiring Oath
features.description: You cannot be frightened. In addition, on damage that would drop you to 0 hit points you stay at 1 hit point — once per long rest.

features.name: Oath Spells — 5th tier
features.description: **Legend Lore · Scrying** are added.

features.name: Vowbound
features.description: Bonus action, 10 minutes: your auras extend to 30 ft and your attacks against Blighted creatures have advantage. Once per long rest.

mapping.name: School of the Bulwark
mapping.description:
The least loved and most often called branch of the Wizards' Guild.

On this continent asking a god for help is a gamble (@[Rule Deviations](entity:lore/Rule Deviations)) — divine healing is asked for anew each time, and most of the time it does not come. The @[Wizards' Guild](entity:lore/Wizards' Guild) noticed this gap three centuries ago and solved the problem from the other end: **if a wound cannot be closed, it must not be allowed to open.**

A graduate of the School of the Bulwark does not throw fire, does not raise the dead, does not read the future. They enter a room, raise an invisible wall in front of their friends, and stand there until that wall falls apart. In the guild's own words: *"We do not heal. We make it unnecessary."*
mapping.flavor_description:
**Nothing this school grants requires the calling roll.** Both the Bulwark and the Countermage are arcane power — not something asked for anew with every use, but a craft learned once. The roll in @[Rule Deviations](entity:lore/Rule Deviations) binds the Cleric, the Warlock and the Paladin's divine spells; it does not bind the wizard.

At the table this means something very concrete: **for a group without a divine healer, you are the only reliable line against damage.** If the Cleric's *Cure Wounds* does not hit 19, nothing happens; your bulwark rolls no die, it just stands.

The guild does not count this a virtue, it counts it insurance. Graduates of the School of the Bulwark are posted to caravans, mines and behind the front — not so they will be heroes, but so that **no one dies**.

features.name: Bulwark
features.description:
**Once per long rest.** When you cast an **abjuration** spell of 1st level or higher by spending a slot, **if you wish** you raise a **Bulwark** on the back of that spell — it costs no action, you make the decision.

Capacity `2 × wizard level + Intelligence modifier`; the bulwark takes damage coming at you. While the bulwark stands, every abjuration spell you cast writes **level × 2** hit points to the bulwark (automatically, at no extra cost).

**When its hit points drop to 0 the bulwark breaks**, you take the leftover damage, and no new one can be raised **until a long rest**.

features.name: The Guild's Book
features.description:
When you choose this school, **two abjuration spells of 2nd level or lower** are added to your spellbook for free. After that, **each time a new spell slot level opens**, one more abjuration spell is added (you cannot choose from a level you have no slots for).

In addition, **Shield** and **Protection from Evil and Good** are always prepared for you and do not count against the number of spells you prepare.

features.name: Extend the Bulwark
features.description:
**Reaction.** You redirect damage coming at a creature you can see within 30 ft to your Bulwark. The creature takes the excess damage; the bulwark waits at 0 hit points.

No limit on uses — the limit is the bulwark's hit points.

features.name: Countermage
features.description:
**Counterspell** and **Dispel Magic** are always prepared; they do not count against the number of spells you prepare.

If the target of *Counterspell* passes its saving throw, **the slot is not spent**. When *Dispel Magic* requires an ability check, you add your **proficiency bonus** to the check.

features.name: Resistance to Magic
features.description: You are **resistant to all damage** from spells, and you make **every saving throw** against a spell's effects **with advantage**.

mapping.dmNotes:
**Deviation flag — this subclass is not in the SRD.** It is a subclass unique to Aegis, **written from scratch** inspired by the classic *abjuration* tradition; it is not a translation of any third-party text. The reason is the world's own rule: because @[Rule Deviations](entity:lore/Rule Deviations) ties divine healing to a roll, the group needs a reliable line against damage, and that line has to be arcane.

**2024 compatibility.** The subclass opens at **3rd level**, features come at the **3 / 6 / 10 / 14** tiers — exactly the same as SRD 5.2.1's subclass skeleton. The abjuration traditions of the old 2014 shape (2nd level) are not used in this world.

**Balance notes.**
- The bulwark's capacity is ~13 hit points at 5th level, ~24 at 10th, ~38 at 17th. Feeding pushes this up somewhat, but you are looking at **one bulwark per fight**: once the bulwark breaks it does not come back until a long rest. So this is not a tap but **an insurance policy that opens once a day**. Even if the group has no healer, it is not enough on its own, and this is deliberate.
- **When to raise it** is the player's decision: a bulwark raised early melts under small hits, a bulwark raised late may never have been raised. That is the card's game.
- *Extend the Bulwark* is unlimited but spends a **reaction**: once per round. That is the real limit, not a counter.
- The "slot is not spent" clause at the 10th-level tier is only for *Counterspell*, not for *Dispel Magic*.
- The always-prepared **Shield / Protection from Evil and Good** at the 3rd-level tier is an addition the classic tradition does not grant; it was put in so that the card gives something visible in the app and the bulwark can be raised on the first round. If you want to trim, this is the first clause to remove.

**Tell the player:** the bulwark **does not raise itself** and **is one a day**. If no abjuration spell is cast, there is no bulwark; after it breaks, there is none until a long rest. Half of this card, *Extend the Bulwark* included, depends on the bulwark.

mapping.name: Drake
mapping.alignment_note: Bound to the bond, not to a master.
mapping.ac_note: scale armor — 14 + the bonded ranger's proficiency bonus
mapping.language_note: Does not speak. Understands what the bonded ranger says.
mapping.immunity_note: Immune to the essence type chosen when it is summoned (acid, poison, cold or lightning).
mapping.description: > Dog-sized, low and broad. Its back is covered with hard olive-green scales, its belly a light grey. Its eyes are horizontal slits; when it turns its head its neck does not move, its whole body turns. Its breath is heavy and hot, but what comes out of its mouth is not fire.
mapping.traits_md:
**Scaling.** Its stats grow with the bonded ranger's level:

- **AC** = 14 + proficiency bonus
- **Hit points** = 5 + (5 × Ranger level); number of hit dice equal to Ranger level, d10
- **Bite** = +3 + proficiency bonus to hit, 1d6 + proficiency bonus damage
- **Size** = 3rd lvl Small · 7th lvl Medium · 15th lvl Large
- **Speed** = 40 ft at every level

**Saving throws:** proficient in Dexterity and Wisdom — DEX +1 + proficiency bonus, WIS +2 + proficiency bonus.

**It does not fly.** It has no wings at any level.
mapping.dmNotes: This card is not an enemy but a player's companion. It acts on the bonded ranger's (@[Drakewarden](entity:subclass/Drakewarden)) turn, after them; if not commanded, it takes Dodge.
